# Mission Guidance: Kazma Agent Framework

## Project Overview

Kazma is a multi-platform AI agent framework with a LangGraph supervisor brain,
swarm orchestration, cross-platform dispatch (Telegram/Discord/Slack/Web/TUI),
and an OpenAI-compatible LLM provider layer. What Kazma is and can do, on one
page (read it before describing or promoting Kazma):
`docs/docs/guide/what-is-kazma.md`. See `docs/docs/guide/architecture.md`
(Docusaurus docs under `docs/docs/`) for the full system architecture and
`CHANGELOG.md` for recent work. Binding industrial audit (waves 0–8 shipped):
`docs/audits/AUDIT_DEEP_2026-09-01_EXEC.md`. Historical production audit:
`docs/audits/AUDIT_PRODUCTION_READINESS_2026-07-21.md`. System map:
`docs/ARCHITECTURE_AND_SYSTEM_MAP.md`.

## Package Scope

All packages are in scope. There is **no** `kazma-memory` package (retired;
V2 memory lives in `kazma_core.memory`).

| Package | Path | Purpose |
|---------|------|---------|
| `kazma-core` | `kazma-core/kazma_core/` | Agent runner, LLM provider, swarm engine, model registry, config store, IDE service |
| `kazma-gateway` | `kazma-gateway/kazma_gateway/` | Platform adapters (Telegram/Discord/Slack), agent handler, slash commands, `/ide` commands |
| `kazma-ui` | `kazma-ui/kazma_ui/` | FastAPI web app, IDE page, swarm panel, settings, SSE chat, static JS/CSS |
| `kazma-tui` | `kazma-tui/kazma_tui/` | Textual-based TUI dashboard + IDE editor screen |
| `kazma-cli` | `kazma-cli/kazma_cli/` | `kazma` CLI (`serve`, `migrate`, `ask`, ACP) |
| `kazma-skills` | `kazma-skills/kazma_skills/` | Native skill manifests + implementations |

## Critical Subsystems (READ BEFORE MODIFYING)

### 1. Provider/Model Resolution (`kazma-core/kazma_core/model_registry.py`)
- `get_client(model)` auto-corrects provider/model mismatches at runtime
- `set_active_model()` switches BOTH model AND provider via `find_provider_for_model()`
- Never change one without the other or the LLM call goes to the wrong API endpoint
- **The client class comes from the provider's declared `api_style`**
  (`kazma_core/provider_adapters.py`, `build_client`, the one constructor
  every `ModelRegistry` path calls): `google`→`GeminiProvider`, `anthropic`→
  `AnthropicProvider`, `azure`→`AzureProvider`, `bedrock`→`BedrockProvider`,
  else (`openai`) the generic `LLMProvider`; a provider's style is in
  `providers.capabilities`. The generic `LLMProvider` always sends
  `Authorization: Bearer` to `/chat/completions` — it CANNOT reach
  Anthropic-native (`/messages`), Azure (`api-key` header + `api-version`),
  or Bedrock (SigV4). Adding a non-Bearer provider means a new class + a row
  in `provider_adapters._ADAPTERS` + its `api_style` in the capability table,
  not just a preset.
- A provider with no usable key is replaced by one that has a key in
  `get_client()` — and that is announced, never silent; provider keys are
  install-scoped so it does not happen for a key that is there. Both in §38.
- **Where Spaces is enforced, a model is also the person's** (S2-03, §70):
  `get_client(None)` and `resolve_live_client` give work for a person their
  own model (`spaces.person_models.model_for_work`), and every provider
  class's `chat`/`chat_stream` asks `_person_call` first: it refuses a model
  the person may not use (`_refuse_a_model_not_allowed`) and returns the
  client carrying the person's own key, when they keep one (S2-04), to
  which the method hands the whole call. A new provider class does the
  same (or hands the call to `super()`).

### 2. Platform Isolation (`kazma-gateway/kazma_gateway/agent_handler/`)
- The LangGraph state NEVER contains `chat_id`, `user_id`, or `message_id`
  as keys of its own.
- These live in `SessionStore` and are restored via `_build_target_id()` on reply
- **One declared exception, the `_gateway` routing block** (2026-11, FA-151):
  `agent_handler/store.py` and `send_message.web_gateway_block` write
  `thread_id`, `display_name`, `platform` and `delivery_target` -- the
  platform-prefixed address a reminder is booked to (§16B) and an expired
  approval is answered at (§30E2) -- and nothing else. A fork's block keeps
  none of the three platform ids even from an older checkpoint
  (`time_travel._SNAPSHOT_PLATFORM_IDS`). Gate:
  `tests/test_gateway_routing_block.py` (a planted `chat_id` key as the
  negative control).
- Breaking this leaks platform IDs into the graph and corrupts sessions
- `SQLiteSessionStore._ensure_db` publishes its connection only after pragmas,
  table creation and migrations finish. Publishing before those awaits lets
  another request's fast path query a missing table. Failed/cancelled setup
  closes the unpublished connection; `close` shares the initialization lock.
  Gate: `TestConcurrentSerialization.test_concurrent_first_use_waits_for_schema`
  (old initializer fails deterministically), plus setup failure/close cases.

### 3. LLM Tool Fallback (`kazma-core/kazma_core/llm_provider.py`)
- Some providers (NVIDIA NIM) reject tool definitions with 404 "Function not found"
- The code retries without tools automatically when this is detected
- Never remove the `status_code == 404 and "function" in detail.lower()` branch

**LLM error classification — `transient` flag (do not flatten):**
- `LLMError(..., transient=True/False)` classifies every failure raised by
  `LLMProvider.chat()`. Transient = network (Connect/Timeout/**ReadError**/
  RemoteProtocol) + 429; permanent = 4xx content/schema + UnicodeEncode.
- The supervisor retry loop (`graph_supervisor.py:_call_llm_with_retry`) ONLY
  retries `LLMError` when `transient` is True — permanent errors fail fast.
  `httpx.ReadError` (mid-stream drops) MUST stay transient, or
  "stopped-thinking" forced-finalization returns. The graph is split:
  `graph_builder.py` wires nodes; `graph_supervisor.py` is the supervisor
  LLM call; `graph_tool_worker.py` is HITL + commitment; `graph_respond.py`
  is `respond_node`. Do not "fix retry" inside `graph_builder.py`.
- `friendly_llm_error()` prefixes all messages with `⚠️` and gives an
  actionable hint — never change it to return a bare string, or failures
  get mistaken for normal model replies again.

**Turn-failure surfacing — never synthesize over a broken turn:**
- When the supervisor's LLM call fails after retries, it sets
  `SupervisorState.turn_failed=True` + `error_message` (NOT a fake answer).
- `respond_node` (`graph_respond.py`) checks `state.get("turn_failed")` and
  MUST skip its synthesis LLM call when True — synthesizing a plausible
  answer over a failed turn was the root cause of the "model stopped thinking"
  symptom.
- Keep the `turn_failed` guard in `respond_node` and the `transient` flag
  on `LLMError`; removing either reintroduces silent forced-finalization.

**Bare tool-argument text is ambiguous, never executable** (2026-10-09):
`agent/answer_quality.py` detects a small literal object matching an available
tool's schema for ONE model recheck within the turn budget. The declared
`SupervisorState.tool_argument_rechecks` resets on a fresh turn, not an approval
resume. The reminder is call-local system guidance; it must not replace the
user's active goal/language or accumulate in checkpoints. Retry the original
conversation, discarding the rejected candidate: replaying it as a synthetic
assistant turn loses thinking metadata and strict providers reject it. Never guess a tool
name or execute the parsed text: it may be requested JSON or a dictionary
example. Actual calls still go through the normal tool worker and HITL.
Answer guidance joins source grounding at the LLM boundary (synthesis too).
Gate: `tests/test_answer_quality.py`, including the original fragment without
recovery as a negative control, bilingual reads, requested data and auto-denial.
The terminal reply also wins over a longer prefix-matching stream in
`turn_document.split_stream_and_final` and its JavaScript mirror. A recheck
can stream a JSON object twice; choosing the longer text corrupts the saved
answer even though `done.content` is correct. Gate: terminal reply authority,
durable presentation and browser TurnDocument tests. No final text means a
partial turn keeps its stream; paused narration stays in its own part.
Gateway completion delivers this finalized text without cultural prefix/suffix
rewriting: it can corrupt requested JSON, one-sentence replies and language.
The shared turn runner owns terminal persistence and post-turn memory; do not
re-close or re-merge the completed checkpoint in the gateway. Cultural prompt
guidance and pure-greeting fast paths remain. Gate: `tests/test_gateway_terminal_answer.py`.
The HTTP subscriber persists terminal text before yielding `done` and must
not flush its accumulated tokens on a later cancellation. The pump's final
write alone is insufficient: subscriber flushes can race it. Gate:
`test_sse_chat.test_disconnect_flush_cannot_overwrite_observed_terminal_reply`
(cancellation while awaiting another frame, before and after done).
Active attachment extraction and its working-memory anchor preserve full
paths (`turn_input.py`): a basename is a display name, not a second path to
read. Same-named files in different folders remain separate. Gate:
`tests/test_attachment_path_identity.py` (old basename matcher as control).

**One-paragraph output requests** (`agent/answer_format.py`, 2026-10-09):
`respond_node` applies the check after plan-fence normalization and before
terminal delivery/post-turn memory. Only explicit latest-user EN/AR requests
count; quoted, fenced, negated, conflicting and historical instructions do
not. Plain prose changes paragraph separators only. Code, lists, tables,
blockquotes, JSON and multiline quoted literals remain intact. Headings may
get ONE quiet, tool-free formatting call (15 s, 4096 output tokens, 16000 input
characters), on the turn's resolved provider. Accept only unchanged wording
and order, with exact quoted/inline-code spans; never execute returned tool
calls. Account the call through the existing LLM ledger. Preserve the original
on failed/unsupported repair, and skip ALL formatting on `turn_failed`.
This is a conservative layout safeguard, not arbitrary format compliance.
Gate: `tests/test_answer_format.py` (real graph, old boundary as negative
control, bilingual prose, protected blocks, no extra prose model call,
tool-free retry, streaming silence, deadline, cancellation and ledger).

**Verbatim JSON copies** (`agent/json_echo_format.py`, 2026-10-09):
At the same terminal boundary, direct latest-user EN/AR requests to return
only a supplied JSON object verbatim may lose an enclosing JSON fence and
surrounding prose. Require an exact textual match to the user's literal: no
serialization, guessed values, tools or extra LLM call. Unsupported requests,
conflicting suffixes, quoted/historical instructions, duplicate keys,
non-JSON constants, multiple blocks and changed object text stay untouched.
The failed-turn and assistant-tool-call guards apply before repair. This
targets literal copies, not arbitrary JSON generation or general compliance.
Gate: `tests/test_json_echo_format.py` (original H04-ar fence/prose failure,
EN/AR, real respond boundary, data fidelity and no execution).

**Telegram code delimiters** (`kazma_gateway/telegram_format.py`, 2026-10-09):
Markdown-to-HTML conversion recognizes line-based fences and matching maximal
backtick runs for inline code. A bare ``` in explanatory prose must not steal
the next inline opener and expose underscored names to italic parsing. Preserve
fenced code whitespace and escape content before styling. The shared converter
serves normal chat and swarm output; Slack/Discord keep their original Markdown.
Gate: `tests/test_telegram_format.py` (old matcher as negative control, EN/AR,
mixed delimiters, real gateway preparation and HTML send path).
Web's separate `streaming.js` renderer uses the same inline-run rule and stashes
code before styles, links and images. Gate: `tests/js/test_markdown_render.js`.

**Vision capability routing (`kazma-core/kazma_core/vision_capability.py`):**
- `is_text_only(model)` / `is_vision_capable(model)` classify by allow/deny
  lists (deny wins; unknown models are NOT downgraded — fail-open).
- `analyze_image` (`tools/vision_analyze.py`) uses the active model if
  vision-capable, else auto-selects a configured vision model via
  `get_vision_client(registry)` (one-off client, no active-profile change),
  else returns a clear actionable error BEFORE any API call.
- `build_user_content()` (`gateway/agent_handler/attachments.py`) takes
  `vision_capable` and, for text-only models, downgrades chat images to the
  `[Attached: … — use file_read to open: …]` stub instead of `image_url`
  (text-only providers like DeepSeek reject `image_url` with a 400).

**Strict local chat templates — system messages MUST stay at the head:**
- Local OpenAI-compatible servers with strict Jinja templates (LM Studio /
  llama.cpp Qwen3) return HTTP 400 `System message must be at the beginning`
  when any `role: system`/`developer` message appears AFTER the first user
  message. Kazma injects such notes mid-stream (INTENT ENGINE plan notes,
  iteration budget nudges, mission patches), so checkpointed history
  naturally contains them — a plain reload+send 400s on every turn.
- `hoist_system_messages()` (`llm_provider.py`) is applied to the messages
  payload inside `LLMProvider.chat()` — the single OpenAI-compatible path
  (LM Studio, Ollama, OpenAI, DeepSeek, …) shared by all transports. It
  moves system/developer messages to the head (order preserved, no-op when
  already ordered) and keeps assistant/tool adjacency intact. NEVER remove
  this call from `chat()`.
- New mid-stream system-note injection sites are covered by the hoist — but
  never add a second LLM-call path that bypasses `LLMProvider.chat()`.
- Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock have their own `chat()` implementations
  that handle system messages natively — do NOT hoist there.

### 4. Swarm Handoff Cycle Detection (`kazma-core/kazma_core/swarm/engine.py`)
- **Handoff is reachable from shipped workers** (Swarm audit SW-E13, owner
  decision D6: a product feature). The LLM worker (`InProcessWorker`) offers
  its model `handoff_to_worker(worker, reason, task?, context?)`
  (`swarm/handoff.py`) whenever the engine dispatches it: `dispatch_worker`
  binds a `HandoffOffer` (the registered workers and the autoscaler's
  templates, never the worker itself, and the cycle guard at this point of the
  chain). The call raises `HandoffRequest` out of `dispatch()`
  (`except HandoffRequest: raise` before its catch-all) to `_handle_handoff`.
  The tool is the worker's, never the registry's (the main agent, the MCP
  server and cron never see it); it has a `TOOL_TIERS` tier (`write`) and a
  side-effect profile (`delegate`), and approves nothing: the target's tools
  ask the bus as any worker's (§7B). A refused call (unknown worker, no
  reason, beside other tool calls, a worker scope without `delegate`, the
  guard) is the tool's answer and the worker finishes the task itself.
- `_handle_handoff()` accepts `_visited: dict[str, int]` and `_depth: int`
- These thread through `_dispatch_worker_by_name_all` -> `_dispatch_worker` -> `_handle_handoff`
- Max depth is 5 (a hop at depth 5 is refused: four hops, five runs); removing the guard causes infinite recursion on A->B->A cycles
- Workers can be revisited up to `MAX_VISITS=2` times: each runs at most twice in a chain, so A->B->A and A->B->A->B run and B's hop back to A is refused
- Visit counts are tracked per worker IDENTITY (`_handoff_identity`): a pool
  instance counts as its template, since a hop to a template spawns a new
  instance each time (counting instance names, only the depth stopped a
  template ping-pong). A target name resolves like a pattern's
  (`_resolve_worker`: registered, else spawned from the template).
- Every ending of `_handle_handoff` releases the source's in-flight count
  (`_release_handoff_source`): the guard's refusal left it busy for good.
  The target keeps the dispatch's metadata, task id and workspace
  (`build_handoff_context`, with or without a blackboard); the hop is the
  task's `handoff` event (the Swarm page's chain) and `kazma_swarm_handoffs_total`.
  Gate: `tests/test_swarm_handoff_tool.py` (a scripted model end to end; the
  guard removed and instance counting as negative controls).

### 5. Circuit Breaker Half-Open (`kazma-core/kazma_core/swarm/reliability.py`) + ReliabilityRegistry (`reliability_registry.py`)
- `_probe_in_flight` flag ensures only ONE dispatch passes through half-open state
- Both `record_success()` and `record_failure()` reset it
- Never remove this flag or concurrent calls bypass the probe semantics
- ReliabilityRegistry (P2-1 refactor) owns all breaker/retry/timeout/validator state
- **An outcome names its admission** (Swarm audit SW-E11, 2026-10-14).
  `admit()` / `check_or_raise()` return a `BreakerAdmission(generation,
  probe)`; every change of state bumps `generation`. An outcome from an older
  generation, or any outcome but the probe's own while a probe is in flight, is
  stale: counted (`stale_outcomes`), never applied. A dispatch admitted before
  the trip closed a half-open breaker while its probe still ran. Callers pass
  the admission (`record_success(admission)`); one without it cannot resolve a
  probe. Shared breakers write by compare-and-set: never over a newer
  generation. A dispatch is one in-flight count whatever its retries
  (`SwarmWorker.in_flight`); the autoscaler never reaps an instance with one in
  flight (SW-E12). Gate: `tests/test_swarm_boundaries_and_signals.py`.

### 6. TaskStore WAL Mode (`kazma-core/kazma_core/swarm/task_store.py`)
- SQLite uses WAL + `busy_timeout=5000` for concurrent read/write
- Schema auto-migrates on init (ALTER TABLE for new columns on existing DBs)
  through `kazma_core.db.sqlite_columns.add_missing_columns` -- every SQLite
  store does (2026-09-30): read `PRAGMA table_info`, add what is missing, let a
  real failure raise; only another process adding the column first is
  tolerated. The old `try: ALTER ... except Exception: pass` hid a locked or
  read-only database until every later query failed with "no such column".
  Gate: `tests/test_sqlite_column_migrations.py` (no SQLite `ADD COLUMN`
  outside the helper; Postgres `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent and
  exempt -- and never swallowed: it aborts the transaction it runs in).
- Worker filter uses `json_each()` not `LIKE` for exact matching

### 7. HITL Approval Gates (3 execution paths + 1 registry — all must stay wired)
There are **three independent HITL execution paths** and **one decision
registry** (§30). Breaking any execution path creates an unattended-danger-tool
gap. Minting a second gate from `LocalToolRegistry.execute` on the web/chat
path (H-8) reopens ghost cards. Decision truth = `hitl_gates.db`; execution
truth = LangGraph checkpoint. Surfaces render; they never infer Approved.

**A. Graph interrupt() — single-agent chat (Web SSE + Telegram/Discord/Slack)**
- `graph_tool_worker.py:tool_worker_node` calls LangGraph `interrupt()` for
  danger tools (wired from `graph_builder.py` closures — do not look for the
  gate body in `graph_builder.py`)
- Gate is active ONLY when `hitl_config` is passed to `build_supervisor_graph()`
- Required build sites: `agent_runner.get_streaming_graph()`, `agent_runner._ensure_graph`,
  and `app.py` startup recompile into `_graph_holder`. Omitting HITL on any site =
  dormant gate on that path.
- Resume: `graph.ainvoke(Command(resume=…), config)` via `POST /api/approve/{thread_id}`
  (SSE — the Web SoT), or gateway `/hitl approve|deny {thread_id}`. The
  WebSocket takes no approvals: it refuses `approve_tool` (§31 D).
- State persists in the checkpointer — paused turns survive restarts
- Gateway approval notification throttles reset at a fresh operator request
  (`graph._handler_body`, before building its new state), never at an approval
  resume. Identical args can represent a new deliberate operation after a
  refusal/expiry; keeping the old three-minute mute created an invisible real
  Telegram gate (2026-10-09). Within-turn duplicate/burst suppression remains.
  Gate: `tests/test_gateway_approval_card_retry.py` (all three transports,
  unchanged throttle as negative control, resume and other-thread isolation).
- Double-gating prevention, for ONE call (Swarm audit SW-S01, 2026-10-14):
  the graph binds `_graph_hitl_gate_ctx` / `_hitl_approved_ctx` to the tool it
  decided about (`safety/call_authority.py`: `call_authority(var, tool)`), and
  that call's first execution consumes it (`claim_call_authority`). Work the
  call starts -- `dispatch_swarm`'s task, a thread, another tool -- finds it
  spent and asks the bus; detached starters run in `detached_context()`. The
  old step-wide booleans travelled through `asyncio.create_task`'s context copy,
  and a swarm worker's `file_write`/`send_message` ran with no card anywhere.
  §30's "decision truth = hitl_gates.db" holds for detached swarm work and the
  bus too: a bus request is a gate row (mechanism `swarm_bus`) with the human
  actor and its own `timeout`/`cancelled` endings.

**B. Swarm bus — `/swarm` + IDE `LocalToolRegistry.execute` path**
- `tool_registry.py:execute()` calls `safety.check()` (async) for danger tools
- `check_sync()` is **fail-closed** (default): blocks danger tools when no real
  bus adapter is present. `allow_headless_danger=True` is the test/dev escape hatch
- Canonical floor, ON by default since audit 2026-09-16 F-5: CANONICAL is always
  unioned into the effective `require_approval_for`, so Settings/YAML cannot
  narrow below it. `KAZMA_HITL_CANONICAL_FLOOR=0` is the warned opt-out. (It
  was an opt-in `=1` from 2026-08-19; docs describing it that way are stale.)
  The drift warning repeats every 15 min either way.
- Bus adapters: `TelegramBusAdapter`, `DiscordBusAdapter`, `SlackBusAdapter`
- App wiring: **one** adapter if only one platform; **`FanOutBusAdapter`** when
  multiple are configured. NullBus = internal-only / fail-closed danger.
- **One request, one decision** (`swarm/shared_approvals.py`, Swarm audit
  Stage 1, 2026-10-14; replaces Wave 6 H-12's tri-state vote). `check()` opens
  the request under a freshly minted id bound to the tool and an arguments hash
  -- never an id from the tool's arguments (SW-S02: one click approved every
  later call carrying that `task_id`). Every platform's card shows every
  argument, bounded and marked when cut (`swarm/approval_card.py`, SW-S03), and
  waits on ONE shared row (`swarm.approval.<id>` in the settings store,
  compare-and-set). The first human decision on any platform decides it -- an
  Approve, or a Deny, which is final (owner decision D7) -- and every card shows
  that outcome (SW-S05). The request's deadline is the only one: `timeout` and
  `cancelled` are outcomes, never a deny (SW-S04). Do not bring back per-adapter
  timers or votes. This is still **not** web `claim_gate`.
- H-9: `is_danger_tool()` is `safety.hitl.approval_floor()`, the floor
  `requires_approval()` uses (SW-S11: it gated only `danger`/`unsafe`, so an
  unclassified tool passed the bus)
- Approval buttons: `shared_approvals.decide_from_button(data, actor=,
  platform=)` from each platform's click handler; no adapter instance is needed,
  and a decision that cannot be recorded is a WARNING with the actor
  (`kazma_swarm_failures_total{site="approval_resolve"}`). The gate row records
  the human who pressed. Gate: `tests/test_swarm_bus_approvals.py`.
- **The Web dashboard answers the same request** (SW-S03, 2026-10-14). Every
  card carries `approval_card.web_link(id)` (`ApprovalRequest.web_link`, shown
  before the code block): `/swarm?approval=<id>` on `KAZMA_PUBLIC_URL`. The
  Swarm page's panel (`swarm_panel/routes_approvals.py`: GET for any signed-in
  user, `POST .../decide` admin) shows `shared_approvals.describe(id)` -- the
  whole call from the gate record, the card's hash, the state -- and decides
  with `resolve(..., platform="web")`. `describe` answers only a `swarm_bus`
  gate: a chat approval is not that page's to show. The id comes from the
  template (`data-approval-id`), never `location.search` (a soft navigation runs
  the script first). A `swarm_bus` gate is never a "twin" of another
  (`hitl_gates._lookup_live_gate`, `_supersede_pending_twins`): two identical
  calls asking at once are two requests; matched as twins, the second's outcome
  was recorded on the first's row. Gates: `tests/test_swarm_approval_page.py`,
  `tests/e2e/test_swarm_approval_panel.py` (EN/AR, reached by soft navigation).

**C. Pipeline checkpoints — swarm PIPELINE tasks** (separate from A and B)
- `engine.py:_handle_pipeline_checkpoint` + `approve_checkpoint`
- Every ending of a task goes through `SwarmEngine._finalize_task`: it saves
  the task, tells the panel, and (`_close_open_checkpoint`) closes a paused
  pipeline's checkpoint — entry, auto-reject timer, gate row. Cancel skipped
  the close and left Approve on cancelled tasks. Code that sets a terminal
  status itself must be declared in `tests/test_swarm_paused_task_endings.py`
  with how it covers those three.
- A pipeline paused before a restart is restored as a PAUSED in-flight task
  (`_active_tasks`, Swarm audit SW-E09: the history is an LRU, and an evicted
  restored pipeline could not be cancelled and came back paused at every boot);
  paused tasks do not count against admission. `reject_checkpoint`
  decides "already finished?" BEFORE the handler runs — the handler marks the
  shared task failed, and judging after it left restored rejects unsaved
  (2026-09-25: four `200`s, still paused at the next boot).

**An always-ask tool takes a one-time approval only** (2026-10-16).
`ALWAYS_HITL_TOOLS` (X writes, and `request_path_access`) are never skipped
by YOLO or a grant, so their card offers Approve once / Deny only: the
interrupt carries `always_ask`
(`graph_tool_worker`; `yolo_allowed` is no marker -- it is also false wherever
YOLO is off for the install), every hop to the page passes it (the SSE frame,
the socket card, the pending-approvals items, the client copies), and the
chat card and the approvals panel drop "Allow tool". The approve route
refuses a `tool` or `yolo` answer for one before anything is claimed or
resumed (409 `one_time_only`, the gate stays pending), and `grant_tool`
never stores one (`hitl_grants.one_time_only`). Live 2026-10-16 an "Allow tool
(session)" click on an x_post card -- beside a tip saying grants cannot skip
the tool -- approved THAT call and published a post the owner read as "it
will still ask me before posting". Gates: `tests/test_always_ask_one_time_only.py`
(the route without the refusal as control), `tests/e2e/test_always_ask_one_time_approval.py`.

**A folder-access request always asks** (2026-11-01, the owner's decision):
on 2026-10-26 a YOLO window let `request_path_access` run with no card (the
daily digest's "ran without asking" found it), and a path grant widens what
every file tool may read or write for the session. It is on
`ALWAYS_HITL_TOOLS` (and `swarm/safety._ALWAYS_HITL_FALLBACK`, the same
list). It is not public: its card keeps the ordinary header and says it asks
every time (chat apps: `ASKS_EVERY_TIME`; web: `chat.hitl_tip_always`), and
`tests/test_public_action_cards.py` declares it in `NOT_PUBLIC`. **A YOLO
window is not a gate that is off:** `get_hitl_config` gives `enabled: False`
under YOLO and `yolo: True` when the gate is otherwise on, and the tool worker
shows an always-ask tool's card there. It refused every always-ask tool under
YOLO as a disabled gate ("Re-enable safety.hitl.enabled"), X posts too; a gate
the operator turned off still refuses them. Gate:
`tests/test_folder_access_always_asks.py` (the old list and the config without
`yolo` as negative controls).

**A fetch after outside text asks, narrowly** (2026-11-11, the owner's
decision; `safety/outside_text_fetch.py`, the one decision). `read_url`,
`crawl_site` and `web_search` are read tier, so text a turn read could send
data out in a URL. Once a turn has read outside text -- a tool result inside a
data fence (`prompt_fence.holds_fence`: only the fence helpers write one), or
a user message quoting a fenced document -- a call that fetches a URL
(`FETCH_URL_FIELDS`, an MCP tool's `url`-like argument) asks ONLY when its
host was named neither in the user's latest message (outside its fences; a
swarm task's prompt) nor in a search result of the same turn
(`SEARCH_TOOLS`, read with `serp.extract_urls_from_search`), and is not
`KAZMA_PUBLIC_URL`'s host. An ordinary one-time card; YOLO and standing
grants skip it (`hitl.standing_approval`, said by `note_ran_without_asking`);
its note says why (`card_notes` code `outside_fetch`, `safety/card_notes.py`
`NOTE_TEXT` = catalog `chat.hitl_note_outside_fetch`, EN/AR). Both chokes
ask it: the chat graph's split (`graph_tool_worker`, state in the declared
`SupervisorState.outside_text`, updated after each step, kept across an
approval pause, reset by `initial_supervisor_state` and by the supervisor at
iteration 0) and `LocalToolRegistry.execute` (a swarm dispatch binds
`outside_text_scope` around the worker with its prompt; the registry asks
`SafetyMiddleware.check` with `force_danger` and `card_notes`). A new
fetching tool is declared in
`FETCH_URL_FIELDS` or `NOT_FETCHES`. Gate: `tests/test_outside_text_fetch.py`
(a real graph and scripted model; the graph without the check as the
control).

**A task a turn starts, a page it saved, a page its history keeps**
(2026-11-15, the defensive check before the independent review: a sub-agent's
goal counted as the user's words, so a delegated fetch to an attacker's host
ran with no card). A task started after outside text carries the turn's state
(`delegation_state`): a sub-agent's goal, a swarm task's prompt, a handoff's
task and a scheduled task's stored prompt are the model's words, never the
user's. The task starts read, and only the real user's hosts
(`OutsideText.user_hosts`) and the turn's search hosts count as named. The
chat tool worker binds `turn_scope` (a snapshot from before the step); a swarm
dispatch binds `outside_text_scope(prompt, inherited=, context_text=)`, and
the innermost scope wins. Carriers: `SubAgentManager.spawn`, `dispatch_swarm`
metadata, `HandoffRequest` (via `dispatch_helpers.with_outside_text`), and the
cron column `outside_text` (cleared by a prompt the owner edits on the page).
`DELEGATIONS` names every DELEGATE and SCHEDULE tool. A call that fetched an
address and ran marks the turn read whatever it returned; `READS_OUTSIDE`
names the readers with no address argument. A file Kazma saved from the web
(`research_files.SAVED_FROM_WEB_FIRST_LINES`) comes back fenced from
`file_read` and `file_search`, and from `shell_exec` and `python_exec`
(2026-11-16: `cat`, `grep -r` or a snippet's `open()` returned it raw) when
the output holds a saved page's first line, or a file the command names or a
folder it walks (`shell_paths.read_paths`), or a path a snippet's string
names, is or holds one (`research_files.any_saved_from_web`; gate
`tests/test_saved_page_fenced_everywhere.py`). At iteration 0, after stub and trim, a fenced
tool result or user message in the kept history, or the Knowledge block,
makes the turn read; Kazma's own system notes do not; hosts the kept history
named stay named. Fence markers in disguise (spaced, fullwidth, zero-width,
Unicode dashes, DeepSeek's tokens) are redacted on a folded copy
(`_fold_for_markers`, `_FOLDED_MARKER_RE`), `filter_injection` reads it too,
and `_SENTINEL_RE` is linear. Hosts from search results still count as named
(the owner's call). Gates: `tests/test_outside_text_delegation.py`,
`tests/test_fence_marker_variants.py`, `tests/test_regexes_stay_linear.py`.

**A draft is published only after the user has seen it, on a card that says
it publishes** (2026-10-16, the same incident: "check the metrics" saved a
draft and asked to post it 2 s later, in that turn, and the card was approved
as part of the reading). `safety/commitment/proposals.bind_turn` names the
running turn (thread + `created_at`, the effect journal's turn scope) in
`tool_worker_node` before the commitment gate; `save_proposal` stamps the
draft with it (`saved_turn`); `_resolve_proposal_backed_post` refuses a draft
stamped with the running turn, or stamped with no turn running
(`drafted_this_turn`), telling the model to show the draft (its text is in the
refusal) and post after the user answers. An unstamped draft (a page, an older
build) is not judged. The card names the public action
(`safety/public_actions.PUBLIC_ACTIONS`, catalog `chat.hitl_public_<tool>` and
`_btn`, chat.js `_PUBLIC_ACTION_LABELS`: one list, held to the public ones of `ALWAYS_HITL_TOOLS`):
"Publish to X — public, can't be undone", the post first and whole, **Post now**
-- on the chat card (which keeps that title on every pending render,
`data-pending-title`), the approvals panel and the chat apps, whose keyboards
take `approve_label` and drop "Approve for task" (`task=False`), and whose
`/hitl approve_task` on an always-ask gate approves nothing. Gates:
`tests/test_proposal_seen_before_publish.py`, `tests/test_public_action_cards.py`,
the e2e above (two turns, real graph, browser EN/AR; all fail on the old code).

**X Studio drafts from the operator's reference documents** (2026-10-26,
`x_api/references.py`). `connectors.x.drafting.reference_files` (Settings → X,
up to three text files, 40,000 characters together) are read whole at every
Generate: the drafter gets them fenced as the facts its posts may state, the
fact check as evidence a claim can cite (`evidence.source_hold` accepts
`kind: reference_file`, bound to the file and the hash of the text read, dated
by the file's last change). A file that cannot be read stops the draft before
any model call. For posts about Kazma itself the reference is
`docs/docs/guide/what-is-kazma.md`. Gate: `tests/test_x_drafting_references.py`
(brief-only drafting as the negative control). **Chat drafts through the same
pipeline**: `x_draft_posts` (x-publisher skill, write tier) runs `draft_posts`
and saves under the running turn (`saved_turn`, so never published in it);
product knowledge and `save_proposal`'s description send X post writing there
(`tests/test_x_draft_posts_tool.py`). **A post has its own length**
(`connectors.x.drafting.post_length`, full by default,
`reply_style.with_post_length`; replies keep the reply length;
`tests/test_x_post_length.py`).

**X model calls turn hidden reasoning off** (2026-10-26). `deepseek-flash`
thinks by default and its reasoning counts against `max_tokens`: an X check
given 1,800 tokens got 1,800 reasoning tokens and no answer, reported as
"invalid JSON". `x_chat` passes `reasoning="off"` when the client's
`can_turn_off_reasoning()` is True; `LLMProvider._chat_payload` then sends
DeepSeek's `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` -- to DeepSeek's own API only
(an unknown field can be refused elsewhere; providers with their own `chat`
never get the argument). A refused switch is retried once without it. A
verifier reply cut off at its limit is `_VerifierCutOff`, never "invalid
JSON". Gate: `tests/test_x_reasoning_off.py`.

**The whole X API, from X's own spec** (2026-11-17; live, asked on WhatsApp
for new followers, the agent opened x.com in the browser).
`x_api/x_api_operations.json` is X's OpenAPI spec reduced
(`scripts/x_api_catalog.py --write`, one operation a line);
`x_api/operations.py` is the one answer to what each is: `read`, `stream` (read at
most 60 s / 100 events), `write`, or `refused` with the reason (posting and
deleting a post go through `x_post` / `x_delete_post` and their drafts and
gate; media upload is `x_upload_media`; an answer that is a credential, a
file body). `x_api/api_call.prepare` checks every call before it is sent:
path values against X's pattern and `_PATH_BREAKERS`, declared query values
only (type, enum, range), declared body fields only, required ones, 64 KiB.
Tools: `x_api_operations` and `x_api_read` (read tier; one read from the X
read budget, the answer fenced), `x_api_act` (danger, `ALWAYS_HITL_TOOLS`, a
public action "Act on X with your account", CRITICAL so no swarm worker
runs it; a refusal from X is `KnownEffectError`, an unknown outcome says so),
`x_upload_media` (chunked, alt text; `media_ids` on `x_post` /
`x_schedule_post`). Three sign-ins (`x_api/auth_tokens.py`, chosen in
`operations.AUTH_ORDER`): the OAuth 1.0a keys, Sign in with X (OAuth 2.0 PKCE,
`x_api/oauth2_sign_in.py`, `/api/x/oauth2/*`; the verifier rebuilt from the
state with `KAZMA_SECRET`, never stored; used only with the scopes the
operation lists; refreshed before its two hours end; its tokens are
`CREDENTIAL` in `settings_restore`) and the app's Bearer token. Settings → X
→ The whole X API. A secret setting is cleared with `delete`, never an empty
write (the store refuses it: X's Disconnect left the four keys in place until
this day). Gate: `tests/test_x_api_operations.py` (every operation
classified, the shipped catalog equal to the script's rendering, hostile path
values, the sign-in end to end with another browser refused, the old
Disconnect's empty write as the control).

**Danger tool list SoT (must stay one list):**
- **Canonical:** `kazma_core.safety.hitl.CANONICAL_DANGER_TOOLS`
- **YAML:** `kazma.yaml` `safety.hitl.require_approval_for` (parity-tested by
  `tests/test_agent_skills.py::TestHitlWiring::test_yaml_parity` and
  `tests/test_hitl_wiring.py` — the tests compare SETS; `hitl.py` groups the
  tools thematically while the YAML list is alphabetical. Add a new danger
  tool to BOTH or the tests fail)
- **Settings UI / ConfigStore:** `safety.require_approval_for` — consumed by

- **Swarm bus:** `swarm/safety.py` `_EXTENDED_DANGER` is a materialized copy of
  CANONICAL with identical contents (CANONICAL is a tuple, so it cannot be the
  same object — spawn tools only if on CANONICAL)
- **MCP tools:** `classify_mcp_tool()` name patterns (write/exec/delete → danger).
  Gate is in `UnifiedToolExecutor.execute()`

**Diagnosis map (multi-path “X relates to Y”):** `docs/docs/ops/diagnosis-map.md`

### 8. ConfigStore Singleton + Atomicity (`kazma-core/kazma_core/config_store.py`)
- Uses WAL + `busy_timeout=5000` (like all other SQLite stores)
- Process-wide singleton: `get_config_store()` — all components MUST use this, not `ConfigStore()` directly
- Multi-key writes MUST use `batch_set()` for atomicity. `transaction()` is
  SQLite-only (on Postgres its `_get_conn()` refuses) and no product code
  calls it: do not add a caller (audit 2026-10-26 AUD-079)
- **`atomic_update` on Postgres locks the key itself first**
  (`pg_advisory_xact_lock` on `_ATOMIC_UPDATE_LOCK_PREFIX` + key, for the
  transaction; 2026-11-18, the Spaces S1-10 review). `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`
  locks nothing while the row does not exist: two processes' first updates
  of a key each read nothing and the second replaced the first. A
  read-modify-write belongs INSIDE the updater: a read before
  `atomic_update` loses what another process wrote in between. Gate:
  `tests/test_atomic_update_first_write.py` (real Postgres, two stores; the
  raw `FOR UPDATE` order as the control).
- Never construct `ConfigStore()` in gateway/core code — use `get_config_store()`
- **`self._lock` covers the live statement, and `close()` must take it too.**
  Every read/write holds the lock across `_get_conn()` *and* the statement
  that follows. `close()` did not, so it freed sqlite's native handle under a
  thread already inside `sqlite3_step` — a use-after-free, which on Windows
  is a bare `access violation` with no traceback that no `try/except` can
  catch. It killed a full pytest run at 19% on 2026-09-20: the memory
  worker's session-purge cadence read the `auth` category on a pool thread
  while the per-test fixture closed the same store. **Any new method that
  touches `_conn` holds `_lock` for as long as the statement is live.**
  A read after a close is fine — `_get_conn()` reopens lazily.
  Repro: `tests/test_config_store_close_race.py`.
  `_stored_raw` holds that same RLock through its native SELECT too, including
  dict/secret preparation before `batch_set` enters its transaction (2026-10-11).
  A cache-only lock exposed SQLite API misuse/corrupted reads under concurrent
  acquisition first writers. Gate: `tests/test_config_store_raw_read_lock.py`,
  including the original lock boundary as a traced-statement negative control.
- Background cadences do not run under pytest:
  `worker_bootstrap.background_schedulers_enabled()` is False there (override
  with `KAZMA_TEST_BACKGROUND_SCHEDULERS=1`). One switch for all eight
  schedulers — the purge was simply the one that got caught.
- **A snapshot answers a key stored nowhere as `get` does** (2026-11-13):
  `ConfigStore.snapshot(prefix)` walked kazma.yaml with `{}` as each missing
  level's default, so `snapshot(k).get(k)` answered `{}` for a key held in
  neither the database nor the YAML, and the crawl journal read a removed
  job as a broken row ("journal unavailable": CI, a library deleted as its
  crawl ended). A prefix the YAML does not hold is now absent from the
  snapshot. The journal also deletes an evicted job's revision key before
  its row (`crawl_jobs._forget_job_keys`): between the two deletes, the row's
  key read back as its child merged in. Gates:
  `tests/test_config_store_snapshot.py`, `tests/test_knowledge_crawl_journal.py`
  (the old walk and the old delete order as controls).
- **A write drops only what it can change in the read cache**
  (`ConfigStore._invalidate_key`, 2026-10-01): the key, its ancestors (`get`
  merges a missing key's children, so `a`'s cached view holds `a.b`) and its
  descendants. Every `set`/`batch_set`/`delete` cleared the WHOLE cache,
  misses included, so any write anywhere -- the heartbeat, a session stamp --
  sent the next read of every setting back to the database (on Postgres a
  round trip, often from the event loop). A raw `transaction()`,
  `reset_all()` and a YAML reload still clear everything (their keys are not
  known). `tests/test_config_store_cache_scope.py` (the full clear as the
  negative control).
- **GET nested vault walk is resolve-only.** `_resolve_vault_value` decrypts
  `vault://` pointers inside dicts/lists. Lazy-migrate of plaintext secrets
  is **only** for the exact string key `get()` was called with. Nested
  `api_key` fields inside `providers.list` must not share
  `cfg:providers.list.api_key` — that ping-ponged `vault.store` on every
  registry read and stalled SSE (2026-09-08 `_No response received._`).
- **A changed shipped default declares whether installs follow**
  (`kazma_core/config_defaults.py`, 2026-09-29). The first boot copies every
  merged shipped/local YAML value into the database (`reconcile_from_yaml`, through
  `shipped_settings`) and a stored value wins, so a default changed later
  never reached an install that had booted before it -- the live install
  still held four lifecycle events after the fix, and ten older shipped
  values (a read-only audit that day; most no longer read). A
  `RetiredDefault` (key, every old value, date, why) makes installs follow:
  at boot a stored value equal to an old one becomes today's, ONCE per entry
  (`system.config.retired_defaults`), so an owner who picks it again keeps
  it. `NEW_INSTALLS_ONLY` keeps the old value, with the reason. Never
  "follow" by equality with no declaration: the live `agent.language: ar`
  equals an old default and is read. Gate:
  `tests/test_shipped_config_defaults.py` (kazma.yaml against
  `tests/fixtures/shipped_config_defaults.json`; `python
  scripts/shipped_defaults.py --write` refreshes it and refuses an
  undeclared changed value).
- **First boot seeds merged YAML, retirement reads shipped defaults**
  (`reconcile_from_yaml`, 2026-10-06): local provider/model choices must
  survive a restart (the fallback followed the active workspace then; it no
  longer does, §62). Seed missing keys through
  `load_merged_yaml` and `shipped_settings`, including local-only files;
  existing rows retain precedence. Check declared retirements against raw
  shipped defaults BEFORE seeding, so a fresh local choice equal to a retired
  value is not mistaken for an old stored default. No valid shipped mapping
  means no retirement. `tests/test_config_reconcile_local.py` covers both
  SQLite and real PostgreSQL, plus the workspace reload that exposed it.

### 9. SwarmEngine Module Structure (P2-1 refactor — 3 extractions)

The original 1878-line `engine.py` god class was split into focused modules.
SwarmEngine remains the central orchestrator with thin delegates for backward
compatibility. **All public API methods and constructors are unchanged.**

| Module | Responsibility | When to open it |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| `engine.py` | Dispatch, handoff, task lifecycle, worker registry | Always — the orchestrator |
| `reliability_registry.py` | Circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, validators, concurrency | Configuring per-worker reliability |
| `phonebook.py` | WorkerRegistry summon + the fenced memory context of `dispatch_by_name` (which runs through `dispatch()`) | Topology/DAG worker lookup |
| `checkpoint_manager.py` | HITL pipeline checkpoint state, timeout auto-reject, persistence | Pipeline pause/resume logic |
| `shared_approvals.py` / `approval_card.py` | A bus approval request's one decision; the card's text | Swarm-bus HITL (§7B) |
| `limits.py` | Input, pause and parallelism limits | A new task field or limit |
| `task_model.py` | A task's own model call outside a worker (the Refiner, a synthesis): ledgered, accounted, bounded | A new model call in a pattern |
| `semantic_router.py` | Semantic routing: Kazma's embedder, exact comparison, the measured floor | Routing by meaning |
| `single_operator.py` | The multi-user refusal (decision D1) | A new swarm surface |

**Rules after refactor:**
- New reliability features go in `reliability_registry.py`, not `engine.py`.
- **The engine owns every run** (Swarm audit Stage 2-3, 2026-10-14):
  `_run_owned` registers it before its first await, one run per task id; the
  RUNNING row is an admission compare-and-set (`TaskStore.admit`, `generation`
  and `run_id`); `persist_task` follows one transition table (a finished
  status is never left, an older generation's write is refused and kept as
  `orphan_results`). An interrupted run records `interrupted_by` and
  `execution_outcome` (`none_invoked` / `unknown` with `invoked_tools`) from
  its effect tracker; an uncertain result is stored `failed`; retrying an
  unknown outcome needs `acknowledge_unknown`; a resumed pipeline skips its
  journaled steps. Task writes run in threads, one task's in order
  (`_persist` / `_flush_writes`); the admission write is the first of them,
  and a stop that lands during it is the run's interruption like any other
  (`_stopped_at_admission`, 2026-10-15: the SQ01 24-hour soak found a
  shutdown leaving five tasks admitted, with RUNNING rows, and never ended).
  An approval stopped during its admission write has resumed nothing: the
  checkpoint is offered again and its auto-reject armed again
  (`_approval_stopped_at_admission`, decided by the write's own outcome:
  admitted, its RUNNING row goes back to PAUSED; failed, the PAUSED row
  stays; refused, another run's task is left to that run; an outcome not
  known in time keeps the claim, and the next start decides from the row).
  Gates: `tests/test_swarm_owned_lifecycle.py`,
  `tests/test_swarm_interrupted_effects.py`, `tests/test_swarm_stop_at_admission.py`.
- **A store fault never becomes a stored-looking success** (Swarm tracker
  SQ04, 2026-10-15). A task write the store refuses for a reason that passes
  (lock, busy, database away: `_store_error_passes`) is tried again
  (`_WRITE_RETRY_WAITS`); a run whose ending never landed is reported
  `failed` with `unsaved`/`store_error`/`result_status` to its caller, the
  engine's record and the stream (`_unsaved_ending`; the row stays RUNNING and
  the next start holds it unknown). An approval whose admission write fails
  resumes nothing (`_admit_to_store(must_record=True)`, `503
  approval_not_recorded`): resumed, a crash would offer the checkpoint again.
  **A new task runs only with its RUNNING row** (2026-10-15): the admission
  write is tried again the same way, and one that still fails refuses the
  task, nothing run (`_store_refused`: `task_store_unavailable`, retryable,
  the slot freed, counted `running_row`; the dispatch route answers 503 with
  Retry-After, the Swarm page words it in its language). It used to run with
  no RUNNING row, so a crash in it left effects no recovery could see. The
  refusal is the task's ending in this process only (history and stream, so a
  background dispatch's page hears it); dispatching the same task again runs
  it. A refused attempt whose write landed before its connection was lost is
  our own row (same `run_id` and generation): admitted. A durable dispatch
  that never ran is finalized (`durable._not_run`). Lost writes are counted
  (`task_write`, `step_journal`, `worker_metric`, `breaker_read`,
  `breaker_persist`, `breaker_lease`). Harness: `scripts/swarm_chaos.py`;
  gate: `tests/test_swarm_chaos.py` (each fix's old code as its negative
  control, the run-anyway admission included; the Postgres cases
  `@pytest.mark.postgres`).
- **A shared breaker never takes an older state** (SQ01 soak, 2026-10-15):
  an outcome changes the breaker under its lock and shares it in a second
  step, so a refresh between the two read the generation before;
  `refresh_from_shared` takes a NEWER generation's state only, and from the
  same generation only its counters and settings (never its state or open
  time). The soak harness test failed 2 runs in 10 on it. Gate:
  `tests/test_swarm_breaker_shared_refresh.py` (the old refresh as control).
- **The durable path (Temporal) runs the engine's own run, where it was
  admitted** (Swarm tracker SQ03, SW-E16, 2026-10-15; rules in
  `swarm/durable.py`'s docstring). One workflow per run (`kazma-swarm-<id>`,
  `-g<generation>` for an approved resume, which takes the durable path too);
  its one activity is scheduled on a queue only the admitting process polls
  (`activity_queue`) and runs only for a run registered and waiting there,
  in the run's own context, the body being `SwarmEngine._run_admitted` (or
  `_resume`) -- the same deadline, watchdog and endings as in process (one
  deadline owner). Temporal's limits come from the same budget
  (`engine.task_budget`, `durable.activity_timeouts`) and sit after the
  engine's own end of the run; one Temporal does fire, or a cancel or
  terminate made through it, is settled in the run (`durable._settle`:
  `deadline`, `worker_lost` or `temporal_cancel`, with `execution_outcome`).
  Never retried (`maximum_attempts=1`: the worker's own retries run inside,
  under §30 G). A stop stops the work here first, then cancels the
  workflow. A heartbeat every `HEARTBEAT_EVERY_S` lets Temporal call a dead
  process's worker lost; the workflow worker keeps no cache (no sticky
  queue), so a restarted Kazma settles that workflow at once; the activity
  uses TRY_CANCEL (the SDK cannot evict a workflow waiting on a cancel).
  The workflow's result is a summary (no prompt or output); the task store
  holds the result, and a run whose work ended does not wait past
  `WORKFLOW_CLOSE_WAIT_S` for Temporal (counted `durable_workflow`). A first
  run of a pipeline journals its steps too, so a killed process's task is
  held unknown naming the step it stopped in. Gate:
  `tests/test_swarm_temporal_durable.py` on Temporal's time-skipping test
  server (a real child process killed mid-step; the old activity body, the
  old ending, the worker's own context, the in-process resume and no
  heartbeat/journal as controls). The test server does
  not skip time while an activity is scheduled or running: those limits run
  short and real there.
- **Swarm failures are loud and counted** (SW-E14): lost evidence or a lost
  decision is a WARNING and `kazma_core.metrics.record_swarm_failure(site)`
  (`kazma_swarm_failures_total{site}`). A catch-all handler in `swarm/` or the
  bus adapters that stays below WARNING is declared with its reason in
  `tests/test_swarm_boundaries_and_signals.py::_QUIET_HANDLERS`. Each worker
  result is counted once in the worker metrics (`_finalize_task`).
- **A deadline on work keeps the work in its caller's task** (2026-11-11):
  the run (`_run_admitted`), a dispatch (`TimeoutGuard.execute`), a pattern
  step, a consult, a worker's tool call and a scheduled fire's turn are
  bounded by `asyncio.timeout`, never `asyncio.wait_for`. On Python 3.11 (CI's
  and the live install's) `wait_for` ran the work in a task of its own, and a
  second cancel of the caller (a shutdown after a stop) left it running after
  the run had ended: Linux CI's Swarm soak saw a worker with a dispatch in
  flight after the engine stopped, and the Scheduled soak's clock could not
  see a fire's turn. 3.12's `wait_for` already ran it in the caller's task.
  Every other `wait_for` in `swarm/` and `cron/` is declared with why it bounds
  no work: `tests/test_work_deadlines_stay_in_the_task.py` (a copy of 3.11's
  `wait_for` as the negative control, on every Python).
- **A worker's text reaches a model fenced** (SW-S10): `check_swarm_task`,
  pipeline and handoff hand-ons, the synthesis prompt, the Refiner. Same gate
  file (`_RESULT_TEXT_ONLY` declares the stored-result builders).
- **The Refiner's report and every synthesis are the task's** (SW-E15,
  decision D8: fixed, 2026-10-15). A pipeline that succeeded (first run or
  resume) is refined by one model call: the report is the result's
  `synthesized_output`, the last step's output stays `aggregated_output` and
  every step's stays in `worker_results`; a failed or partial one is not
  refined. Every model call the swarm makes for a task outside a worker -- the
  Refiner, a fan-out or consult synthesis -- goes through
  `swarm/task_model.call_task_model` (`resilient_chat`: retries, failover,
  the per-call ledger with the task's id as `thread_id`; bounded output and
  deadline; the watchdog counts the Refiner as one more pipeline step), and
  its tokens and cost join `total_tokens` / `total_cost`
  (`PatternExecution.synthesis_tokens` / `synthesis_cost` into
  `_finalize_task`). A Refiner that cannot answer leaves the unrefined result
  with a WARNING and `kazma_swarm_failures_total{site="refiner"}`, never a
  stand-in report. Gates: `tests/test_swarm_refiner.py` (no direct `.chat(`
  in `swarm/` outside `worker.py`, the old Refiner as its control).
- **Semantic routing has one embedding space** (SW-E10, decision D8: fixed,
  2026-10-15). `swarm/semantic_router.py` embeds the task and each worker
  profile with Kazma's embedder (`memory.embedder.get_embedder`) and compares
  them exactly in the process -- no vector store, no default embedding
  function, no other model (gate). A profile matches only when it stands out
  from the others (`MATCH_FLOOR`, measured with bge-m3 on
  `tests/fixtures/swarm_routing/`, `scripts/swarm_routing_bench.py`; the
  nearest worker with no floor is the negative control); otherwise keywords
  route, and the autoscaler takes what nothing matched. In a thread, within
  `routing_engine.SEMANTIC_DEADLINE_S`; an embedder that is missing, failing,
  slow or busy routes by keywords, said once at WARNING
  (`site="semantic_routing"`). A DISPATCH stores in `task.workers` only the
  worker that ran; the candidates are in `metadata.routing_diagnostics`.
  Changing a profile's text, the dataset or the embedder's model needs the
  vectors recorded again (`scripts/swarm_routing_bench.py vectors`). Gate:
  `tests/test_swarm_semantic_routing.py`.
- **`/api/swarm/*` has one role table** (`kazma_ui/swarm_panel/route_roles.py`,
  SW-S07): GET is any signed-in user, everything else admin, enforced by the
  routers' `RoleCheckedRoute`. On an install with platform users every swarm
  surface refuses (`409 swarm_single_operator`, decision D1). Gate:
  `tests/test_swarm_route_roles.py`.
- **Bus posts are mention-safe** (SW-S13): every Discord and Slack bus post and
  edit goes through `_post_message` / `_patch_message` / `_update_message`,
  which apply the chat adapters' `sanitize_outbound` (and Discord's
  `allowed_mentions: {"parse": []}`).
- **A tool long by design gets its time** (`graph_helpers.LONG_RUNNING_TOOLS`,
  2026-10-31): every tool call is bounded at `agent.tool_timeout_seconds`
  (120 s, a hung tool's bound), and `run_research_pipeline` and
  `knowledge_ingest_site` get at least 1,500 s, `crawl_site` 900 s (the turn's
  budget still bounds the turn; a disabled bound stays disabled). Cut at 120
  s, a deep research from chat never finished: live, a Kuwait history paper
  became a page-by-page search by the model
  (`tests/test_long_running_tool_timeout.py`).
- **`check_swarm_task` waits for the result** (`wait_seconds`, default 60,
  at most 90: below the 120 s tool timeout), answering the moment the task
  finishes. Answering "still running" at once, with "poll every few seconds"
  in its description, had the chat model poll three times in two seconds;
  the stagnation guard ended the turn 3.8 s into a 36 s task (live
  2026-10-20). Gate: `tests/test_check_swarm_task_waits.py` (no wait as the
  negative control).
- **A wait is progress, not a loop; a finished task goes back to its chat;
  `/unrestricted` reaches the worker** (2026-11-14, live: a 15-minute data
  task from an `/unrestricted` Telegram chat ended "partial" on the third
  90 s wait, the worker ran out of 40 rounds, and no one sent its result).
  `check_swarm_task`'s "still running" answer begins
  `tool_loop_breaker.STILL_RUNNING_PREFIX`, and `stagnation_signatures`
  leaves such an answer out of the stagnation window -- only from a tool in
  `WAITING_TOOLS`; the task's time limit and the turn's budgets still bound
  it. `SwarmEngine._finalize_task` calls
  `swarm.chat_delivery.deliver_finished_task` for every ending but a pause: a
  task whose `source_platform` is the chat app of its `source_delivery_target`
  (Telegram, Discord, Slack; a web turn's target is the operator's Telegram,
  so not sent) is sent there after `HANDOVER_GRACE_S`, unless the chat's turn
  read the result (`note_result_handed`); past `INLINE_MAX_CHARS` the result
  is a Markdown file. Under `/unrestricted` (`agent.unrestricted`:
  `is_unrestricted`, recorded on the task as `unrestricted` and bound around
  the worker by `worker_dispatch` with `unrestricted_scope`) the task's time
  limit is one to six hours, the worker gets `UNRESTRICTED_WORKER_ROUNDS` and
  reads `UNRESTRICTED_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS` of each tool result. The forced
  report at the round limit turns hidden reasoning off. It lifts no safety
  gate (always-ask tools, outbound allowlist, protected keys, denylist) and
  not the browser's network isolation, which is the install's
  `KAZMA_BROWSER_NETWORK_MODE` (one shared browser, not a chat's). A message
  that is a template with blanks still in it (`turn_input.unfilled_blanks`:
  `<FILL IN ...>`, `[FILL IN]`, `{{name}}`, EN/AR) gets "ask, don't guess"
  in its latest-message note. Gate: `tests/test_unrestricted_swarm_runs.py`
  (the old window and planted look-alikes as negative controls).
- **The task store** strips NUL from every Postgres parameter
  (`_pg_execute`) and runs SQLite at `synchronous=FULL` (the RUNNING row is
  crash evidence, SW-E16); worker-metric days follow the task retention.
- **The concurrency soak** (SQ01): `scripts/swarm_soak.py` is the soak harness
  (a real engine on a private SQLite store, scripted workers, bursts, outages,
  cancels, `auto` tasks and restarts; checks every cycle from the task store's
  own status log), held by `tests/test_swarm_soak_harness.py`. Its first
  trial found shutdown's `stop_all_runs` returning before the tasks it
  stopped were written (the writes run in threads), so a process that exited
  then left the next boot to record a failure of unknown outcome; it now
  waits for them, bounded (`_flush_stopped_writes`, a WARNING and
  `site="shutdown_write"` when one is left), and the soak counts one left as
  a violation. `--duration` is seconds of LOAD: the time a restart takes is
  added (one that waits out the stop grace for a task ignoring its stop took
  12 s of the test's 24 s run and left the breaker no window to recover in).
- `engine.py` public methods are thin delegates — the real logic lives in the extracted modules.
- The de-facto public attrs (`_workers`, `_active_tasks`, `_task_handles`, `_metrics_collector`) remain on `SwarmEngine`.
- Constructor signature is unchanged — test fixtures work without modification.

### 10. IDE Subsystem (`kazma-core/kazma_core/ide/`)

The IDE is a transport-agnostic coding backend (Web, TUI, all chat platforms).
It is the **single source of truth** for file/exec/git/swarm operations on a
workspace. Three new modules; understanding their interaction is essential.

**A. Workspace root resolution — ONE ladder (binding SoT)**
- Public API: `kazma_core.workspace.binding.resolve_active_root()` (also
  `file_write._get_workspace` / `configure_workspace` for compat).
- Used by: all `file_*` tools, IdeService, workspace UI API, env_context.
- **Resolution precedence:** per-task `workspace_scope` ContextVar →
  **active WorkspaceStore row** → `configure_workspace()` pin →
  `KAZMA_WORKSPACE` env → `{data_dir}/workspace` default sandbox. A fresh
  store seeds its first active row from `KAZMA_WORKSPACE`, else the working
  folder when it is a project, else the default sandbox: the row then
  outranks the variable, so a guess seeded over it kept the guess (2026-11,
  §56).
- **Binding bus:** `WorkspaceStore.set_active_workspace` →
  `notify_root_changed(root)` → pin tools + MCP rebind for
  `workspace_bound` servers (`${KAZMA_ACTIVE_WORKSPACE}` in command).
- MCP filesystem must NOT stay on a static `kazma-data/workspace` fossil
  after Switch Repo / clone. **Nor in storage** (2026-10-02): every read and
  write of the MCP store passes `mcp_servers_store._canonical_server` (a
  workspace-bound server is marked `workspace_bound: true`, and an old
  sandbox path in its folder argument goes back to the placeholder;
  `mcp_rebind.is_legacy_sandbox_arg` knows each spelling, the bare
  `kazma-data/workspace` included). The live settings held a pre-placeholder
  copy that won over kazma.yaml's by name, the MCP page showed it, and the
  next MCP edit wrote it over kazma.yaml. The page shows the command as it
  runs (`KazmaAgent.get_mcp_servers`). `tests/test_mcp_servers_store.py`
  (identity canonicalizer as the negative control). Storage holds
  configuration only: `_canonical_server` drops the runtime fields
  (`_RUNTIME_FIELDS`: status, connected, tool counts...), which `upsert`
  wrote into kazma.yaml for every server.
- **Every MCP server Kazma ships runs an exact version** (2026-11, supply
  chain). kazma.yaml ran `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` through
  `npx -y` with no version: each start ran whatever npm served. kazma.yaml,
  the catalog and `mcp_servers_store.SHIPPED_PACKAGE_VERSIONS` name one
  version (held equal, the catalog held to the registry record). The first
  boot copied kazma.yaml's list into the settings store, which wins by name,
  so installs follow two ways: a store still holding that copy takes today's
  at boot (`config_defaults` retires `mcp.servers`), and any stored command
  naming a shipped package bare is pinned by `_canonical_server`
  (`_pinned_command`), which every read and write passes; a version the
  owner wrote stays. Gate: `tests/test_mcp_shipped_servers_pinned.py` (every
  npx/uvx command in a shipped config pinned; the old kazma.yaml line, the
  canonicalizer without the pins and the boot without the declaration as
  negative controls).
- **The running server never writes kazma.yaml's MCP servers**
  (2026-10-02): it is a tracked file, and every page's MCP change left the
  live checkout modified, so a `git pull` touching kazma.yaml refused to
  merge (the swarm templates' lesson, §14). Writes go to the settings store
  (`mcp.servers`) and config.raw; a kazma.yaml server removed from a page is
  named in `mcp.removed_servers` (written in the same `batch_set`) and left
  out of the merge, and adding it again clears it. The one write left is
  `move_plaintext_secrets` swapping typed secrets for pointers
  (`_write_everywhere(rewrite_yaml=...)`, the file's own list kept). Gate:
  `test_only_the_secrets_mover_rewrites_kazma_yaml`
  (`tests/test_mcp_servers_store.py`).
- **The manager's connect pins, and keeps failures per server**
  (`AsyncMCPManager.connect_from_config`, 2026-10-02). A workspace-bound
  config no caller pinned (no `_resolved_workspace`) starts on the active
  workspace, read off the loop; the reconnect sweeper and Settings' Test
  passed the stored config and started the filesystem server on the literal
  placeholder. A call changes `connection_errors` only for its own servers:
  boot connects one server per call, each call cleared them all, and the
  sweeper -- which retries what is named there -- never retried an early
  failure. A stop drops the server's entry; the text is `redact_secrets`'d.
  One Start/Stop: `KazmaAgent.start_mcp_server` / `stop_mcp_server`, for
  the MCP page, Settings' switch (saved AND applied now) and `/config tools
  toggle` (run on the server loop from the resolver's thread). One "is it
  on": `mcp_servers_store.server_enabled`. `tests/test_mcp_servers_live.py`.
- **Per-task scope guard (deep-audit 2026-08-19):** MCP rebind is
  PROCESS-GLOBAL — a per-task `workspace_scope` does NOT rebind servers.
  `mcp/manager.py:execute_mcp_tool` fail-closes with an actionable error
  when a per-task scope targets a different root than the bound MCP root
  (kill-switch `KAZMA_MCP_SCOPE_GUARD=0`). Per-workspace MCP instances
  remain future work.
- Path-traversal protection: `IdeService.resolve()` does a string-level
  `normpath` `..` check + containment backstop (symlink/junction-aware).
- **A relative path an agent tool is given means the active workspace**
  (`binding.resolve_tool_path`), the directory `shell_exec` runs in — never
  the server process's CWD. Every file tool, `check_path_access` and the
  skill tools resolved against the CWD until 2026-09-26; it only looked
  right because the live workspace IS the install folder. After a Switch
  Repo, `file_read("README.md")` read the install's README. Gate:
  `tests/test_tool_paths.py` (every tool that builds a path from its own
  parameter, behavioural runs from a CWD holding a same-named decoy).
  `file_delete` refuses the workspace root and its ancestors. The SQL tools
  (`sqlite_query`, `execute_db_query`, `inspect_db_schema`) joined them on
  2026-10-02 (`database_client._checked_sqlite_file`): their path parameter
  is `db_uri`, which the gate's name pattern did not match, and they opened
  it with `sqlite3.connect`, which was not on its list of openers; both are
  now.
- **File tools keep a file's own line endings**
  (`tools/text_newlines.py`): read exact, write `newline=""` in the file's
  existing style; a new file takes the platform default. Text mode turned
  every patched LF file into CRLF on Windows, and the checkpoint rollback
  wrote CRLF files back as `\r\r\n`. Tests: `tests/test_text_newlines.py`
  (bytes, both styles).
- **A checkpoint restore writes only a file the checkpoint holds**
  (`FileCheckpointStore._held_file`, 2026-10-01): the whole-file and the
  per-hunk reject (`restore_one`, `restore_hunk`) both take the file through
  the checkpoint's own list and `check_path_access(..., "write")`, and keep
  its line endings. `POST /api/ide/checkpoints/{id}/restore-hunk` wrote any
  path the request named, itself, in text mode. The review diffs exact text
  (`hunks.file_diff`, the one diff for review and restore, so a hunk index
  means the same hunk in both) and lists a file created after the checkpoint.
  `tests/test_ide_checkpoint_hunks.py`.

**B. HITL routing — no parallel write/exec path**
- All mutating/exec IDE operations (`write_file`, `apply_patch`, `delete_file`,
  `run`, `run_file`, `git`) delegate to `LocalToolRegistry.execute()` via
  `IdeService._call_tool()`. The HITL gate lives in `tool_registry.py:execute()`
  (§7B). Never call the underlying tool functions directly from the IDE layer.
  Prefer `file_apply_patch` for edits to existing files (not whole-file write).

**C. Awareness injection — `ide/env_context.py`**
- `build_env_context()` resolves workspace root, repo slug (from WorkspaceStore
  cache or `git remote`), branch, GitHub auth, and available tools into a
  markdown block.
- It is the turn's `environment` note, current, ONE copy a call: the web
  transport adds it (`sse_chat/` package, voice), and the supervisor builds it
  at iteration 0 for a turn that arrives without one -- the chat apps, a
  scheduled task, a child graph (`graph_supervisor`,
  `graph_helpers._ensure_environment_note`). Workspace switches take effect at
  the next turn (a turn note since 2026-09-29, §43). It is never part of the
  base prompt: `agent_runner.py` baked the block it saw at server start into
  the base prompt until 2026-11-15 -- a second copy on the web, and the chat
  apps' only copy, stale after Switch Repo. Every dispatched worker prompt
  gets its own (`worker.py`). The IDE chat's open file is its own turn note
  (`source="ide_context"`), never glued to the question.
- `IdeService.send_to_swarm()` attaches the env block to the task `context` —
  never drop this or workers lose workspace awareness. It awaits the
  threaded `build_env_context` (2026-10-02): it ran the blocking builder (two
  git probes of up to 4 s, a store read) on the event loop "on purpose" from
  2026-08-27. `_build_env_context_sync` is a loop-stall helper now, so no
  async code calls it again (`tests/test_ide_send_to_swarm.py`).

**D. Per-task workspace targeting — `ide/workspace_scope.py`**
- `workspace_scope(workspace_id)` is an async context manager backed by a
  `ContextVar`. `worker_dispatch.py` wraps `worker.dispatch()` in it when a
  `SwarmTask` carries `workspace_id`.
- `_get_workspace()` consults the scope FIRST, so concurrent tasks can target
  different repos. `SwarmTask.workspace_id` (None = global active workspace)
  propagates through `SwarmDispatchContext.metadata`.
- `ContextVar` propagates across `await` points within one asyncio task;
  `asyncio.create_task` copies the context (var travels with it).

- **Approval resumes keep the turn's workspace** (2026-10-07):
  `agent.turn_workspace.turn_workspace` captures the resolved root at turn
  entry into the declared `SupervisorState.workspace_root`. Both UI entry
  points (`turn_runtime.invoke_turn` / `astream_events`) and core `_ainvoke`
  use it. A `Command` reads that checkpointed root and restores a path scope
  for execution; the approval request's context and global active row cannot
  redirect a paused turn. A new turn captures the current scope afresh;
  `/compact` maintenance keeps the checkpoint's root instead.
  Legacy checkpoints without the root, invalid roots and missing directories
  fail closed with a public instruction to start a fresh turn. Never infer a
  legacy root from a pending tool's arguments. Gate:
  `tests/test_turn_workspace_resume.py` (reopened SQLite saver, both entries,
  concurrent scopes, exactly one effect, old unscoped resume as negative control).

**E. Repo identity — `WorkspaceStore` persistence**
- `stores/workspaces.py` has repo-identity columns (`repo_url`, `owner`,
  `repo`, `default_branch`, `is_github`) added via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`.
- `repo_for(root_path)` returns cached identity (avoids `git remote` per turn);
  `set_repo_identity()` persists it. `env_context` prefers the cache.
- Native GitHub tools (`git_github_manager/tools.py`) use the shared
  `GitHubClient` (OAuth→PAT→env token) via lazy import, with env-var fallback
  for headless mode. Don't revert to `os.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN")`-only.
- **An empty list from GitHub is not "none".** GitHub filters an endpoint
  to what the token may read (a fine-grained token without "Issues" gets
  `[]`, not a 403), so `github_list_issues` checks an empty answer against
  the repository's `open_issues_count` and says the token may lack the
  permission; on the live install the agent reported "no open issues" over
  #20 (2026-09-28). Pull requests are dropped BEFORE the list is cut.
  `tests/test_github_list_issues.py`.

**E1b. Git history has read-only tools** (2026-10-19): `git_log` (count up
to 100, path, oneline) and `git_diff` (uncommitted, a commit or a range,
path, stat) beside `git_status`, read tier, git run with the tool child
environment and `core.fsmonitor` off, output fenced (commit messages are
whoever committed them). With host shell off and the Python sandbox refusing
subprocess, "git log -3 --oneline" had no way to run on live (Telegram).
`tests/test_git_read_tools.py`.

**E2. A project's files are what its repository keeps**
(`workspace/project_files.git_project_files`, 2026-10-02): tracked files
plus untracked ones `.gitignore` does not exclude, for the agent's
`file_search`, the code index and the Workspace page's recent files. Git
runs with `tool_child_env()` and `core.fsmonitor` off. `None` = walk: no
work tree, git missing, or the folder itself ignored and named as the path
(the default sandbox inside the install's checkout). The search and the
index walked every folder off a skip list: on the live install (workspace =
install folder) a 4.7 GB clone, ignored by `.gitignore`, took one search
13.9 s and could take the code index's whole 4,000-file budget. The three
walks also share ONE skip list (`GENERATED_DIRS`; they kept three), and the
repository ignores `AppData/`. `tests/test_project_files.py` (the old walk
as the negative control; the lists compared by identity). The code index and
the security report (§49) read `project_files.iter_project_files` (git's list,
else a walk; never a generated or dot folder); the search keeps its own walk
because it searches `.github`.

**F. Transports**
- Web: `/ide` page + `/api/ide/*` router (`ide_api.py`); file-aware AI chat
  reuses `/api/chat/stream` (no parallel path).
- TUI: `editor.py` `EditorScreen` (pushed from `files.py`).
- Chat: `/ide` slash commands in `commands.py:_try_ide_command`, wired in
  `graph.py` after the swarm intercept.

- Follow existing Kazma code style (type hints, docstrings, logging)
- Use `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` pattern
- Use `from __future__ import annotations` for type hints
- Keep modules focused (one concern per file)
- Python: compile-check with `py_compile` before committing
- JavaScript: syntax-check with `node --check` before committing
- Never use `&&` or `||` in PowerShell commands; use `;` and `$LASTEXITCODE`

### 11. Self-Improvement Soul Store + Prompt Fence (`kazma-core/kazma_core/skills/self_improvement.py`)

The self-improvement engine persists "Soul deltas" (LLM-generated system-prompt
refinements derived from untrusted conversation/tool output) and re-injects
them into every future system prompt. Two invariants must hold:

**A. Storage is ConfigStore-backed, NOT a free-standing JSON file.**
- The supervisor/main-agent Soul lives in `get_config_store()` under key
  `self_improvement.agent_evolution` (a dict `{"agents": {<id>: {soul, history}}}`).
- `_load_agent_evolution` (a read) and `_update_soul` (every change) go
  through ConfigStore — do NOT reintroduce a direct `path.write_text` write
  (the old `agent_evolution.json` was non-atomic and corruptible on
  crash/concurrency).
- Every change is one `atomic_update` with the read inside the updater
  (across processes); `_agent_evo_lock` orders this process's own changes
  (and the legacy migration). Both are required (S1-10 review, 2026-11-18:
  a read before the write lost another process's lesson).
- A one-time migration (`_migrate_legacy_evolution_if_present`) moves any
  pre-existing `agent_evolution.json` into ConfigStore and renames it
  `.migrated`. Leave this in place.
- Swarm *worker* deltas live on `WorkerRegistry` (`WorkerEntry.system_prompt`),
  not here.

**A2. A turn teaches only what memory would keep** (2026-11, FA-212).
`close_turn` is the one hand-off (`learn_from_finished_turn`, beside the
memory hand-off): never a failed turn, a turn or chat the forget ledger keeps
out, a refiner that could not answer (no template line), or a lesson longer
than `_MAX_DELTA_CHARS` (refused, never cut). The cap keeps whole lessons
(`_lessons` / `_render`). Gate: `tests/test_lessons_only_from_kept_turns.py`.

**A3. A turn teaches only on a signal, and a lesson is merged** (2026-11,
the memory framework audit's F13, decision 12). Every finished turn used to
cost one more model call, and the Soul's twelve slots let twelve routine
turns push out a real correction. `learn_from_finished_turn` now reads the
turn first, with no model call (`skills/lesson_signal.read_signal`): a
**correction** of the previous answer, a **recovered failure** (a tool that
failed, then a later call of the same turn that worked, read from the
state's `tool_results`) or the user's **feedback** ("from now on...", "too
long", "المرة الجاية...", "اختصر ردودك"), from the user's own words
(`memory.own_words`, quoted spans out), English and Arabic read alike (the
Arabic phrases folded as the text is); no signal, no refiner. The chat
refiner (`analyze_and_apply_chat_turn`, `_refiner_prompt`) is shown the
turn and the lessons the space's Soul holds, each in a data fence, and
answers one line: NOTHING, SAME n, REPLACE n or NEW (`_read_refiner_reply`;
anything else teaches nothing). A lesson is merged: it takes the place of
the one it replaces and of any that says the same (`_same_lesson`: folded
equal, or content words overlapping 80 %), and its history entry names
where those came from (`also_from`), so forgetting any of those turns takes
the merged lesson back (`forget_lessons_from`). The refiner searches no
memory any more. A swarm worker's refiner may answer NOTHING too. Gates:
`tests/test_lessons_on_a_signal.py` (twelve routine turns keep a
correction; the old rule, a lesson from every turn, loses it to the twelve
slots: the control), `tests/test_paired_languages.py` (the signal pairs).

**B. Every injected Soul delta MUST go through the prompt fence.**
- `kazma_core/safety/prompt_fence.py` provides `is_override_delta()` (rejects
  injection markers like "ignore prior instructions") and
  `format_untrusted_block()` (wraps content in a `<kazma:data untrusted>`
  fence telling the model the text is observation data, NOT instructions).
- Deltas are checked at creation time (`_analyze_success`/`_analyze_failure`)
  AND at apply time (`_auto_apply`/`apply_agent_mutation`) — defense-in-depth.
  Never inject a delta via the old `"Apply these refinements to your behaviour:"`
  framing; always use `format_untrusted_block(evo, source="self_improvement")`.
- **One place adds the main agent's Soul: the supervisor**, at the start of
  every turn on every surface and every install
  (`graph_helpers._ensure_space_lessons`: every other `self_improvement` note
  the call holds is dropped, one current fenced copy added), and it cuts a
  Soul baked into a base prompt (`self_improvement.without_baked_soul`).
  Nothing bakes one (`agent_runner` did, read once at start: stale after the
  first new lesson), and the transports (`sse_chat/`, gateway `graph.py`,
  `voice_turn.py`) add none: the model saw it twice (S1-10 review,
  2026-11-18). The swarm worker (`worker.py`) fences its own. Gate:
