  `tests/test_lessons_per_space.py` (one copy through the real supervisor
  graph; the old base prompt with the cut taken out as the control).
- Kill-switch `KAZMA_SELF_IMPROVEMENT=0` is checked live (not just at init) on
  both the chat/supervisor path and the swarm worker path.

### 12. Time Travel Replay (`kazma-core/kazma_core/time_travel.py`)

The time-travel subsystem saves the `SupervisorState` after supervisor
iterations to `<data dir>/snapshots.db` (SQLite WAL). Hardened to the
2026-10-13 audit (TT-01..TT-12, tracker
`docs/plans/TIME_TRAVEL_INDUSTRIAL_HARDENING_GOAL.md`). Every restore, fork
and approve test runs on the real graph and saver of `tests/_tt_graph.py`
(the product SQLite saver; Postgres when a throwaway database is set).

**A. The recorder must be wired into ALL graph-build sites.**
- `SnapshotRecorder` is created once per agent (`agent_runner.py` via
  `create_recorder(config=...)`) and passed to `build_supervisor_graph(...,
  snapshot_recorder=...)` at all 3 call sites: the run graph
  (`_ensure_graph`), the streaming graph (`get_streaming_graph`), and
  child graphs (`build_child_graph`); also the app.py post-startup recompile
  and `kazma_core/cli/ask.py`. If any site omits the recorder, that path stops
  capturing snapshots silently. The server registers it as the process's
  recorder (`set_process_recorder`); the chat apps, the slash resolver and the
  forget fan-out use `process_recorder()` (they each built their own).

**B. One source of truth, one identity (TT-01).** The database only: no
in-memory copy (it keyed `(thread_id, iteration)`, disagreed with SQLite and
kept serving cleared steps). A step is addressed by its snapshot id;
`iteration` restarts every turn and is a step number inside a turn. Rows carry
`turn_key` (the turn's `created_at`), `turn_index` (user messages held, the
memory turn number), `seq` (capture order), `message_count`, `nbytes`,
`truncated`; an older file is backfilled from its own JSON at open. Restore,
fork, detail and compare take the id on every surface (the chat apps accept
its first 8+ characters, `resolve_ref`); listings group turns then steps
(`replay_routes.group_steps`). Retention evicts by capture order.

**C. Capture (TT-06, TT-11).** `graph_builder._supervisor` calls
`time_travel.capture_after_supervisor` (one function: the test graph runs the
same path): off the loop, never failing the turn, thinned in a long turn
(`_capture_due`: every step to 20, every 10th after, always the last), and
stamping `snapshot_id` only when the durable write succeeded (`capture`
returns None on failure; `kazma_time_travel_capture_total{result}`). The
step's insert and its eviction are ONE write transaction
(`SnapshotStore.enforce_bounds(record, insert=True)`, the only call
`capture` makes): a crash or an error leaves the step stored with its
eviction, or not at all, and None means nothing was stored. As two
transactions (`save`, then `enforce_bounds`) a kill between them left the
turn one step over its cap until its next capture (31 of 30, found by the
TT-G3 soak, 2026-10-15); `save` alone is for seeding a store in tests.
Gate: `tests/test_time_travel_capture_atomic.py` (a real child killed inside
and after the transaction; the two transactions as the negative control; no
product code writes a step any other way). Budgets
are enforced in SQLite on every capture, oldest first: per step
(`max_snapshot_bytes`, 2 MB: a larger state is stored cut with
`_time_travel_truncated` and can be read, never restored or forked), per turn
(`max_per_turn`, first and newest), per chat (`max_snapshots`,
`max_thread_bytes`) and in total (`max_global_snapshots`, `max_total_bytes`).
Read failures raise `SnapshotStoreError`: 503 `store_unavailable` on the
routes, a plain sentence in the chats -- never "no steps saved".
`maintain_snapshots` VACUUMs only when a quarter of the file and 8 MB are
free, then truncates the WAL the VACUUM wrote through (`_truncate_wal`), and
reports sizes as the file plus its WAL and shared memory (`_disk_bytes`):
with the recorder's connection open the WAL kept the rewritten file's size,
and the "reclaimed" it reported was not the disk's (found by the TT-G3 soak,
2026-10-15). A prune that did not stick is an ops alert
(`time_travel.prune_not_sticking`); the run has a firing-ledger signature.
The long soak (TT-G3) is `scripts/time_travel_soak.py`: a restart per cycle
on private stores, 2,000-iteration turns, every restore/fork/forget path,
injected faults and kills, these budgets checked after every cycle
(`tests/test_time_travel_soak_harness.py`, with planted violations). A soak
reads a process's peak memory through `soak_report.peak_rss_bytes` (its own
peak: `VmHWM` on Linux), never `ru_maxrss`, which on Linux keeps the parent's
size from before the child's exec -- a cycle child of a 1 GiB pytest process
read 1 GiB on Linux CI (2026-11-10; gate in `tests/test_soak_report.py`).

**D. Restore and fork are one service (`kazma_ui/thread_rewind.py`, TT-02,
TT-04, TT-G1).** Every surface calls `rewind_thread` / `fork_thread`: the
page's routes (the TUI uses them), the chat apps' `/replay <step>` and
`/fork <step>` (`_handle_replay` / `_handle_fork` in gateway `graph.py`; the
slash resolver answers `list`, `compare`, `clear` and returns None for a
step). Under the thread's mutation lock a restore refuses 409 `turn_running`
(a registered turn, or the lock held by another task) and 409
`approval_pending` naming the cards (registry or live interrupt; decision
D11: nothing is settled behind the human), writes a turn-boundary state
(`turn_boundary_payload`: nothing pending, tool chains sanitized,
`SCRATCHPAD_CLEAR` first, written `as_node="respond"` so `next == ()`), takes
the later turns back from memory (`rewind_memory`, D2), from the transcript
(`_transcript_cut`: the chat-store rows after the step) and from Time Travel
(the steps saved after it), bumps the thread's rewind generation, journals
`thread_rewound` (every tab reloads; never replayed) and writes an audit row
(`kazma_core/time_travel_audit.py`, `time_travel_audit.db`, refusals too). A
fork records a chat app's owner first, off the loop (`record_thread_owner`
returns False and logs WARNING; a failure refuses the fork), writes the
boundary state under the new id, and saves a projected chat row (questions
and answers only) with a catalog title (`replay.fork_title`). Do NOT
overwrite `active_thread.{sender}` on a fork. Gates in
`tests/test_time_travel_rewind.py`: only `thread_rewind` calls
`apply_snapshot_to_thread`; every product function that calls
`aupdate_state`/`adelete_thread` holds `thread_locks.thread_mutation` or is
declared.

**D2. A rewind rewinds memory** (Memory audit M09, 2026-10-13, decided with
TT-03: memory is rewound, not kept). `/undo`, `/edit`, a restore
(`apply_snapshot_to_thread`) and abort call `memory.forget.rewind_memory`
after they write: the turns they took back -- episodes, the agent's notes,
facts -- are forgotten under every key and tenant that holds them, journaled,
with ledger rows from the old questions (a deferred write, the deep pass and
turn reconcile from the unchanged transcript do not bring them back); a fork
touches the original chat's memory not at all. The deep pass applies facts
only while its turn is still remembered (`_apply_if_still_remembered`). The
transforms are `agent/rewind.py`. Gate: `tests/test_memory_rewind.py` (each
rewrite through a real LangGraph graph, recall after; the rewrite alone as
the negative control; every product function calling `.aupdate_state(`
calls `rewind_memory` or is declared not a rewind).

**E. One per-thread checkpoint-mutation lock (`kazma_ui/thread_locks.py`,
TT-04).** Task-reentrant, per loop, bounded. Gateway turns and commands
(`cmd_lock`), the approve route (`_approve_lock_for`), the web abort, `/reset`
and chat delete, the dashboard delete, and the start of a web turn take it.
A web turn reads the checkpoint before its stream starts; it starts the graph
under the lock only if the thread's rewind generation is unchanged (else it
answers `replay.turn_after_restore` and runs nothing).

**F. The approve route resumes only a live interrupt, keyed (TT-02,
§30 B2).** `next` without an interrupt is a 409 (it was "still try resume"
with a gate-less security command: the restored step's denied call ran); a
card the registry knows as another gate is a 409
(`hitl_gate_bridge.gate_names_interrupt`); there is no gate-less fallback.
`build_resume_command(..., interrupt_id=)` keys every approval and deny
resume by LangGraph's interrupt id (web route, gateway `/hitl`, timeout
auto-deny, supersede, CLI): a resume whose interrupt is gone resumes nothing.
Gate: `test_every_approval_resume_is_keyed_by_its_interrupt`.

**G. Delete and Forget reach the steps (TT-05).** Chat delete
(`sse_chat` delete route), forgetting a chat (`forget_chat`), a user's Forget
of a memory (`forget_episode`, by "user": the chat's steps from that turn on,
under every key) and `/replay clear` on every surface go through
`forget_thread_snapshots` / `forget_turn_snapshots`; a rewind's own
`forget_episode(by="rewind")` leaves the steps to the restore. Registered in
`memory_stores.EXTERNAL_STORES`. `snapshots.db` is `machine` in
`store_registry` (not carried in a bundle) and in `NOT_BACKED_UP` (the
universal backup leaves it out): a copy elsewhere would bring back deleted or
forgotten chats. `/reset` keeps the steps (documented).

**H. The web chat answers `/replay` and `/fork` without the model**
(`kazma_ui/sse_chat/_time_travel.py`, 2026-09-28), in the page's language:
the saved steps (plural forms) and a link, `/replay?thread=<id>`, that
`replay.js` opens on that chat's timeline; `/replay clear` deletes the steps.
Before, the text reached the model. `tests/test_web_time_travel_command.py`.

**I. `/api/replay/*` is mounted when the app is built** (2026-10-01), and
reads the recorder and the graph per request (`create_replay_router(
recorder_getter=, graph_getter=)`): 503 `time_travel_unavailable` until
startup makes a recorder. A model switch rebuilds the graph, which a router
given one at mount time never saw. `tests/test_replay_router_getters.py`.

**J. Settings reads the live recorder (TT-08):** `max_snapshots`,
`max_global_snapshots` and `limits` are public properties;
`/api/settings/time_travel` reports them and the live retention, so "restart
required" clears after a restart. **Migration (TT-09):** `path_rewrite`
rewrites JSON-escaped Windows paths (`C:\\Users\\...`) both ways, converts the
path's rest to the target's separators, and keeps a JSON row whose rewrite
would not parse. Gates: `tests/test_time_travel_bounds.py`,
`tests/test_time_travel_identity.py`.

**K. Off the loop, and every surface driven (TT-Q1).** Building a recorder
(`create_recorder` reads the settings store), the process recorder, the
fan-out deletes, the owner record, the fork's chat row, the web chat's reply
and the audit store are loop-stall helpers (`_LOOP_STALL_HELPERS`; Time Travel
is a `_CROSS_MODULE_AREAS` area). The chat apps' real handler and the TUI's
commands list, restore and fork on the fixture graph
(`tests/test_time_travel_surfaces.py`); the page, reached by the sidebar, in
English and Arabic, a restored chat, and a failed step list shown as an error
are `tests/e2e/test_time_travel_page.py` (run explicitly: `fast_test` skips
`tests/e2e`).

### 13. Proxy Provider Addon (`kazma-core/kazma_core/proxy/`)

An opt-in, pluggable scraping proxy so `read_url` / `crawl_site` / `web_search`
can route through a configured proxy (anyip.io first). Acquisition is
**local-only by default** (2026-10-10): `web_acquire.policy` requires
`KAZMA_ACQUISITION_MODE=local_first_with_remote_fallback` AND `proxy` in
`KAZMA_ACQUISITION_REMOTE_PROVIDERS`. Stored proxy settings alone cannot
authorize that route. HTTP clients always disable ambient environment proxies.

- **Proxy resolution is fail-closed (2026-10-11).** `proxy/config.py` reads one
  live category snapshot per route; nested provider reads share it. Only an
  absent/default `none` selects direct routing. Unknown providers, failed config
  or initialization, missing credentials, unresolved vault pointers and invalid
  routes raise typed `proxy_routing_error`; never substitute `NullProvider`.
  An account change takes effect on the next resolution. Settings Test resolves
  once off-loop and probes that exact URI under policy, admission, a 15-second
  deadline and a 128-byte decoded response cap. No raw credentials in errors.
- **The DDGS SDK runs in `web_acquire/search_sdk.py`'s isolated child**, with
  proxy/account environment stripped, explicit route via stdin, a 30-second
  process-tree deadline and bounded memory/output. DDGS_PROXY otherwise overrides
  an explicit proxy. Never mutate process environment around SDK calls. Search
  admission and cancellation retain ownership until child cleanup joins; no next
  backend after cancellation. Other synchronous search backends still require
  hard whole-request containment. Gates: `tests/test_proxy_routing_safety.py`,
  `tests/test_search_sdk_worker.py` and real Chromium proxy-refusal coverage.
- **`get_scraping_client()` (`client.py`) is the single injection point.** The
  scraper builds its `httpx.AsyncClient` via this factory, not `httpx.AsyncClient`
  directly. It injects `proxy=` when configured + rotates UA from
  `USER_AGENT_POOL`. Adding a new fetch path = use this factory.
- **Scraping-scoped ONLY.** The proxy is never applied to LLM API calls — those
  use the separate `http_pool.py`. Never wire `get_scraping_client` into the LLM
  provider path, or provider API keys would route through a third party.
- **Adding a provider** (anyip.io, BrightData and Oxylabs are registered) =
  one class under `proxy/` + one line in `registry.py::_PROVIDERS` + one
  Settings dropdown option. The scraper
  talks to the `ProxyProvider` interface, not to any provider directly. Don't
  hard-code a provider into `read_url.py`.
- **`proxy.password` auto-vault-encrypts** via the existing
  `is_sensitive_config_key` rule.

### 14. Swarm Autoscaler (`kazma-core/kazma_core/swarm/autoscaler.py`)

Dynamic worker creation: when a task with `workers=["auto"]` has no matching
registered worker, the autoscaler spawns one from `swarm_templates.json` so the
swarm works with zero pre-registered workers.

- **`engine.get_autoscaler()` is a lazy singleton.** It loads
  `swarm_templates.json` once on first access. The dispatch fallback that calls
  `maybe_scale()` is in `dispatch_inner.py` — it only fires on
  `NoCapableWorkersError`, never when a named worker is requested or when routing
  succeeds. Do not call `maybe_scale` from elsewhere.
- **`swarm_templates.json` ships production templates** (coder/researcher/generalist)
  with `model`/`provider` left EMPTY so best-model selection (`models/selection.py`)
  fires at dispatch. Do not assume `swarm_registry.json` is the only worker source.
- **The worker registry is a data-dir store** (`registry.default_registry_path()`:
  `<data dir>/swarm_registry.json`, 2026-10-01). It was
  `Path("swarm_registry.json").resolve()` at import -- the process's working
  directory: no backup copied it, and a test run inside an install wrote the
  install's. An older build's file there (or at the install root) is moved in
  once and renamed `.migrated` -- never into a temporary data dir (a test's
  subprocess has no conftest pin, and its install root is the checkout the
  tests run in); writes are atomic; every change and every read of the
  entries holds the registry's lock (route threads write while the swarm
  reads on the loop). `tests/test_worker_registry_store.py`. A migration
  bundle carries it, and the operator's templates, even with `--no-assets`
  (§18, `store_registry.DATA_DIR_ENTRIES`).
- **"Finished" is one list** (`swarm.task.TERMINAL_STATUSES` / `is_terminal`,
  2026-10-02): the engine (finalize, approve, reject), the task store's
  retention and the task stream all ask it. The stream kept a copy without
  `cancelled`, so a cancelled task's stream never ended. **A finished task's
  stream ends with `task_completed`** whatever the bus remembers
  (`swarm_sse._final_event`, from the stored result): the Swarm page's
  client reconnects on every close, and the bus forgets a task at a restart
  and at cleanup -- a deploy left cards counting through ten reconnects.
  `tests/test_swarm_task_stream_ends.py`; what the page reads off a result
  must be a `TaskResult` field (`tests/test_swarm_page_result_fields.py`:
  the pipeline view and Play mode read `synthesis`/`response`, which no
  result has).
- **`matches_task` uses word-boundary token matching** (not raw substring). When
  adding expertise tags to a template, pick whole words — the tag `code` would
  not match "barcode" (intentional). The template using the most of its words
  wins (`WorkerTemplate.match_score`, each word once); file order (specialist →
  general) breaks a tie, then the catch-all (2026-11-15: first-match gave a
  research task mentioning Python to the coder; `tests/test_swarm_template_choice.py`,
  the yes/no rule as the control). A language's name is context for
  `classify_prompt` (`_CODING_CONTEXT`), never coding work alone.
- **Best-model-per-task** (`models/selection.py`): spawned workers classify their
  prompt (`models/router.py::classify_prompt`) and pick the best available model
  (user `models.defaults.<kind>` → heuristic → active). The selection never
  mutates the active profile. Env-lock (`KAZMA_MODEL`) always wins.
- **Handoff cycle guards (§4) still apply** to auto-spawned instances — they are
  regular `InProcessWorker`s once spawned, counted as their template, and a
  handoff may name a template (an instance is spawned for it). Idle-reap after 5 min;
  `record_activity` refreshes the timer, and an instance with a dispatch in
  flight is never reaped (`SwarmWorker.in_flight`, SW-E12). Instances are named
  `<template>-pool-<boot tag>-<n>` (a new tag each start, so an earlier run's
  shared breaker is never inherited); a reaped instance's shared breaker keys
  are deleted.
- **The Swarm page offers "auto"** in both worker pickers, chosen by default
  when nothing is registered, and the status says "On demand" when templates
  exist and nothing runs (`/api/swarm/status` `templates`). Until 2026-09-28
  the page refused to dispatch without a registered worker and said "Stopped"
  over a swarm that answered through the API in 3 s.
  `tests/test_swarm_auto_worker.py`.
- **A template with `catch_all: true` takes any `auto` task no other template
  matches** (the shipped `generalist`). Matching is by the prompt's words:
  "In one sentence: what is idempotency?" matched nothing and failed with "No
  capable workers" (2026-09-28). The shipped file is found from the install
  containing the package (`_default_templates_path`), never the CWD; the
  operator's edits are saved to `<data dir>/swarm_templates.json`, which then
  replaces the shipped list -- writing them into the tracked file left a
  modified checkout that `git pull` refuses.
- **An idle instance takes the next task before a new one is spawned**
  (`AutoScaler._take`, for `maybe_scale` and `spawn_by_name`, 2026-10-15): no
  dispatch in flight and no task already handed to it. A handed-out instance
  is claimed (`_claims`) until its dispatch begins (`record_activity`; its
  in-flight count covers it from then) or its breaker refuses it, else for
  `_CLAIM_S` (60 s); a claimed instance is never reaped. The router matches instances by
  their template's words, so before this a task the catch-all took never
  reached an existing catch-all instance: each spawned a new one up to the
  bound, then failed "No capable workers" until the idle ones were reaped (the
  SQ01 soak found it). Gate: `tests/test_swarm_autoscaler_reuse.py` (never
  reuse as the negative control). An open breaker is not dodged by spawning:
  its instance is reused and refuses, as the breaker means (a lingering claim
  as the control).

### 15. V2 Memory Worker & Schedulers (`kazma-core/kazma_core/memory/worker_bootstrap.py`)

The V2 cognitive engine has a background maintenance tier: a durable task
queue drained by a worker, plus **eight** fire-and-forget asyncio scheduler
loops started from `start_memory_worker()`. These were the subsystem that
silently lost its backup/export runs (the routines existed but nothing called
them) — read this before touching the background memory path.

**A. `start_memory_worker()` is the single boot entry — it starts EVERY
scheduler.** Called from `app.py` startup (wrapped in try/except so it
can't block boot). It registers handlers + `start_worker()` + all
`_start_*_scheduler()` calls in that function. If a new scheduler is added,
register/start it HERE or it will never run (the exact gap that previously
left backups/export inert). Current boot list:

- `_start_macro_sleep_scheduler()`
- `_start_backup_export_scheduler()`
- `_start_reconsolidation_scheduler()`
- `_start_commitment_gc_scheduler()`
- `_start_session_purge_scheduler()`
- `_start_daily_digest_scheduler()`
- `_start_firing_ledger_scheduler()`
- `_start_restore_drill_scheduler()`

**B0. A job's wait is counted from its last run, never from boot.** The live
install restarts several times a day; a scheduler that sleeps a whole
interval from process start never runs there. The daily digest was not sent
once in the week to 2026-09-28, and the backup sweep, skipping a fresh backup
at boot, waited six hours from boot (a nine-hour gap). Long jobs stamp their
last run (`observability/cadence.py`, the ledger and drill their own keys)
and sleep only the rest of the interval. `tests/test_scheduler_cadence.py`
boots every scheduler `start_memory_worker` starts on a virtual clock with
its job due in 30 minutes and fails unless it runs within 40; a new
scheduler needs a case there.

**B. Distinct cadences (do not collapse them):**
- **6h `macro_sleep`:** rule-based tier demotion/promotion (TTLs,
  importance, access) and archival (`macro_sleep.py:run_macro_sleep`).
  First sweep 60s after boot. **Archival is cold storage, never deletion**
  (2026-09-26): `_ARCHIVE_EPISODE_SQL` moves the tier and fills an empty
  summary with a stub; the question, the answer and the vector stay, and
  no statement may set episode text to NULL (gate in
  `tests/test_memory_nothing_lost.py`). Only rows stale on BOTH clocks are
  archived (created past the TTL *and* not recalled within it — every chat
  turn is importance 1 and can never be promoted, so the recall clock is
  what keeps an in-use memory). Recall searches every tier in
  `vector_engine.RECALLABLE_TIERS`; an archived hit ranks just behind an
  equally matching active one (`memory.v2.archived_recall_weight`, 0.98 --
  2 % off its evidence score, a tie-breaker, never a reason to lose it), and
  a recalled archived memory returns to episodic at the next sweep. Moves reach the state mirror; a remote vector
  index is re-tagged, never told to delete. There is no decay score:
  `compute_retention` was removed 2026-09-23 (per-second λ, no reader).
- **6h backup/export** (`_BACKUP_EXPORT_INTERVAL_HOURS = 6`, not 24):
  enqueues `native_backup` + `nightly_export` + `native_pg_backup` →
  native `sqlite3.backup()` of both memory DBs (`backup.py`) + JSONL/GraphML
  dumps (`export.py`) + a filtered `pg_dump` of Kazma's Postgres
  shared-state tables (§21). First sweep 120s after boot. Kept separate
  from macro_sleep so a slow disk on backup can't stall decay. The export is
  a portable text snapshot, whole (2026-10-13, Memory audit M30): no vector
  column, other bytes as base64 (it wrote Python `b'...'` literals), every
  table paged through (the audit log stopped at its newest 20,000 rows), a
  count per piece; a piece that fails fails the task (`_ExportResult.failed`,
  M20 -- failures were logged at DEBUG and counted done).
- **Lifecycle failures are seen** (2026-10-13, Memory audit M20): the
  schedulers enqueue through `worker_bootstrap._enqueue_checked` (a refused
  task is a WARNING and the ops alert `memory.enqueue_failed`; the result was
  ignored, and a broken `memory_ops.db` stopped every cadence while health
  showed an empty queue). Vector repair and recovery let a locked or busy
  database reach the runner (they reported it as nothing to do); the runner
  logs it at INFO for two passes, WARNING from the third, and every sweep's
  last outcome is in memory health (`sweeps`, `sweep_health()`), with the
  queue's oldest pending and running ages and each task type's last success
  (`queue`). Three failed passes in a row degrade health (`sweep_failing`).
  Gate: `tests/test_memory_lifecycle_signals.py`.
- **24h reconsolidation:** `global_reconsolidation` (dedupe + re-embed of
  beliefs, subject-hash partitioned).
- **15-min commitment GC:** TTL expiry + tiered retention (§20). Every
  sweep on this cadence is one entry of `_MAINTENANCE_SWEEPS`, in this order:
  commitment GC, artifact GC, HITL-gate TTL, the retention of decided gates,
  tool receipts, finished task ledgers, model calls (§56), ended YOLO
  windows -- `safety/yolo.py`; a pre-TTL flag with no end time counts as
  ended, it had kept one live chat's approvals off since July --, memory
  task-queue purge, swarm task retention — `swarm.task_retention_days`,
  default 30, 0 keeps all —, pipeline log retention, swarm approval rows,
  run incident retention (§52), checkpoint retention (§41), the supervisor
  watch (§39), the document worker broker (§19 E1), guard dependencies
  (§39), malware signatures
  (§19 E), dependency advisories (§57), model failover drill (§38), provider
  health (§60), erased space keys (§70, S4-07), forget convergence (§15I), memory vector repair, memory recovery,
  retired knowledge promotions and memory turn reconcile (§15F), memory
  text fill (§15F), memory mirror sync (§15K), memory graph sync (§15K2), weekly topic summaries (§15J), entity count repair
  (§15L) and knowledge vector repair (§24F, last), run by ONE isolated
  runner so a failing sweep never stops the rest -- and is logged at WARNING
  (it was DEBUG: a sweep failing every pass is a feature that is off). A new periodic cleanup is a
  new entry there, never a new loop (`tests/test_swarm_task_retention.py`).
- **Session purge, daily digest, weekly firing ledger, restore drill:**
  started here too; do not assume "the four original loops" is the set.
All `enqueue_task(...)` loops: the durable worker drains the actual work, so
a failed enqueue cannot kill the cadence and a failed handler is
retried/bounded by the queue.

**C. Handler registration is idempotent via separate module-level flags.**
`register_v2_handlers()` guards on `_registered` (macro_sleep /
entity_merge / micro_consolidation); `register_backup_export_handlers()`
guards on `_backup_export_registered` (native_backup / nightly_export /
native_pg_backup). The underlying `register_handler()` is a plain dict
assignment (idempotent overwrite), but the flags avoid re-churning on
re-boot / repeated calls and let the backup handlers register
independently of the core V2 set.

**D. The durable queue lives in `memory_ops.db` (`task_queue.py`).** Bounded
retries: `max_attempts` (6 for a memory write, `MEMORY_LANE`; 3 for
maintenance) then dead-letter (`status='failed'`); stuck `processing` rows
past 300s are reclaimed. Per-task short-lived SQLite connections (no WAL
contention with chat reads on `memory_state.db`). `enqueue_task` is
best-effort and never raises. Since 2026-10-13 (Memory audits M12, M13):
- **A failed attempt waits its backoff** (`next_attempt_at`, `_retry_delay`:
  30 s, x4 each time, at most an hour). It went back to `pending` at once:
  three attempts in three polls, so a ten-minute provider outage
  dead-lettered every deep pass of it.
- **A dead letter is kept until the operator retries or clears it** (the
  Memory page's queue): `purge_completed_tasks` deletes completed rows only.
  One dead letter degrades memory health (`status_detail: dead_letters`) and
  raises the ops alert `memory.dead_letter`. They were deleted after a week,
  and health (five or more) cleared itself.
- **A failure is a failure.** `dual_write.write_episode` says `written`,
  `refused` (the user keeps the turn out) or `failed`; a failed write raises
  `EpisodeWriteFailed` in the post-turn pipeline, counts `mirror_fail`, and
  the live thread hands the turn to the queue (`post_turn_memory`) -- the
  None was ignored and the turn counted `ok`. The deep pass tells "the model
  is unavailable" (`belief_extractor._llm_extract`: no client, or the call
  raised -- retried, `deep_pass_failed`) from "it answered with nothing"
  (done); an outage ended as a heuristic-only "done", never redone.
- **A lane claims no more rows than it has free slots, and memory writes
  have their own lane** (`MEMORY_LANE`: post-turn memory, the deep pass,
  entity merges, summary rebuilds). The worker claimed eight and ran two:
  a row that waited past the stuck threshold was claimed again and ran
  twice, and a pg_dump or a restic check held up a user's turn.
Gate: `tests/test_memory_queue_retries.py` (each with its negative control:
the ignored None, the one-None extractor, no backoff, the old purge, the old
batch-claim loop, one lane).
- **A handler that fails says why** (2026-11-20): `return
  failed_because("...")` (`task_queue.failed_because`, always False) puts the
  reason in the task's `error_log`, which the Running work card, the
  Dashboard's incident (its bell text is `name: reason`, `runs.notify`) and
  the Memory page's queue show; a reason given in a worker thread is kept, and
  it is masked (`redact_secrets`). A bare `return False` recorded "handler
  returned False": live 2026-11-19 a failed Postgres dump copy said nothing
  more. Gate: `tests/test_task_failure_reasons.py` (no registered handler
  returns a bare False, a planted one as the control).

**D2. No slow call under a memory write lock; one vector per row** (2026-10-13,
Memory audits M14, M15, `memory/vector_write.py`). No embedding, Postgres
mirror, graph or vector-index call runs inside a memory SQLite write
transaction, `belief_mutation._mutation_lock` or the episode writer's lock:
a fact was embedded inside the mutation's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` under the
process-wide lock (every belief write waited on one embedder call, up to two
minutes), the superseded fact's graph delete and mirror tombstone ran there,
and `macro_sleep` made a Postgres round trip per archived fact inside its
transaction. Now `mutate_belief` writes the vector after the commit
(`_store_belief_vector`), the superseded edge and tombstone after it too, and
`macro_sleep` unmirrors after its commit. A row's vector is embedded ONCE
(`encode_vector`, no lock held), written by one guarded `UPDATE`
(`write_local_vector`: no vector yet and the row still holds what was embedded;
it commits only a transaction it began), and sent to the remote index only
(`index_remotely` through `backends.get_remote_vector_backend`, taken back out
if a forget landed meanwhile). An episode was embedded twice, the second write
ran on the shared connection without the lock or the tier guard (a forgotten
memory got its vector back), and `LocalSqliteVectorBackend.upsert` committed
the caller's transaction; no memory writer upserts through it now. Recall's
access bump waits at most 50 ms for the write lock and keeps its counts when
the database is busy (`recall.flush_access_bumps`, written by the next recall
or `macro_sleep`) -- it waited the full busy timeout (5.54 s measured) on the
turn path and dropped them. Gate: `tests/test_memory_io_outside_locks.py`
(a probe in every embed, mirror, graph and vector hook used by
`belief_mutation`, `macro_sleep`, `hygiene`, `forget` and the episode writer
finds the database free and no memory lock held; one embedding per write; the
forget race; a gate on local upserts; each with its negative control).

**E. The split-DB design is load-bearing.** `memory_state.db` (hot reads:
beliefs, episodes, entities, procedural DAGs) is isolated from
`memory_ops.db` (cold writes: task queue, audit log) precisely so background
consolidation/backup writes don't WAL-contend with chat recall reads. Do
not merge them or route queue writes at the primary DB.

**F. Every memory findable (2026-09-26, `docs/plans/MEMORY_NOTHING_LOST_PLAN.md`).**
Measured on live that day: meaning search compared episodes inside an
unordered `LIMIT` slice (the 60 newest of 300 were never searched), facts
inside the 400 "most important", fact meaning search ran only when keywords
came up short, and archiving had erased 76 memories.
- **A memory keeps all of its text** (2026-11-19, the owner: "Keep more,
  so find a way or a workaround to keep all text"; `memory/limits.py`, the
  one home of every length memory holds itself to). Every episode writer
  cut: 4,000 characters of a turn's question and of its answer
  (`dual_write.episode_row`, `turn_reconcile`), 2,000 of the summary, 8,000
  of a swarm result (`swarm_bridge`), 16,000 of a turn waiting in the queue
  (`consolidator._defer_turn_memory`). Now every writer stores through
  `limits.episode_text`: whole, up to `EPISODE_TEXT_MAX` per field (2 MiB,
  the web chat's request body limit: a safety ceiling nothing reaches; one
  past it keeps its start with a WARNING). Ids are unchanged (they hash the
  first 512/200 characters). **Old rows still match**: code that finds a
  turn's row by its text compares `limits.turn_key` (the first 4,000
  characters, stripped) -- turn reconcile's "already stored" count, the
  forget ledger's key (`forget.question_sha` hashes `question_key`), the
  weekly summaries' copy key; the archive's copies are matched in either
  form (`forget._scrub_legacy_copies`), the legacy-copy rule by prefix as
  before, and recovery (`rehydrate`) reproduces the old writers with
  `LEGACY_*`. Compared whole, every long turn already in memory was written
  a second time. **The cut text comes back** (`memory/text_fill.py`,
  maintenance entry "memory text fill", after turn reconcile): a turn's row
  (`e_`) whose question or answer is exactly 4,000 characters, not
  forgotten, not yet marked, is filled from the chat store and its spool
  (`chat_history.conversations_for`, which now returns each copy's tenant;
  another space's copy is never read in) when the row holds exactly the
  chat text's start and its id is that turn's -- one such text, or it is
  left; the forget ledger is asked inside the write's transaction;
  compare-and-set on the text read and the tier; the full-text index and the
  mirror outbox follow through their triggers; the vector is written again
  only when its text changed. Each row is marked once (`text_fill`: filled,
  whole, unavailable) and memory health counts them (`findability.cut_text`,
  with the swarm results and summaries no chat can fill). **Meaning search
  covers the start of a long memory** (`EMBED_TEXT_CHARS`, 4,000: the vector
  is what it always was), **keyword search all of it**. **Passages** (the
  memory plan's W5 + W1b, 2026-11-22, `memory/passages.py`, behind
  `passages.in_use()`, off):
  vectors of about 256 tokens (`limits.PASSAGE_TOKENS`, whole sentences, 32
  overlapping) of what a memory's own vector misses -- every side but the
  vector's, and the vector's own past `EMBED_TEXT_CHARS` -- in
  `episode_passages` (memory id, space, side, offsets, vector, model; no
  text). Triggers on `episodes` take them with a row's delete, a forget, a
  text change and a move of space (with the switch off they cost an insert
  nothing and a forget about 3 µs: the plan's W5); the writer fills them
  after its own vector (`write_passages`: vectors first, then a
  compare-and-set on the text), the vector repair sweep fills older memories
  (`fill_passages`, 200 a pass, behind the switch), the benchmark's seeding
  fills its stores (`benchmark.fill_passages_whole`, refusing a store
  missing any). **They never lift a memory's meaning**: counted as
  max(vector, best passage) they lost answers and precision on Kazma's
  benchmark and no threshold the plan's rule allows recovered them (the
  plan's W5 has the numbers; the main session's decision: no cosine lane of
  their own). **They bring the reranker's candidates** (W3, below): the
  memories whose best passage is among the question's nearest are read
  beside that passage, and the block shows the stretch a memory was kept by
  (`display_at(anchor=)`, W1b). Gate: `tests/test_memory_passages.py`
  (EN/AR; the writer off, a stale write and a forget as controls).
  **Relevance: a cross-encoder decides what is shown** (the memory plan's
  W3 + W2, 2026-11-22, `memory/reranker.py`, `recall._by_relevance`, behind
  `reranker.in_use()`, off: **not accepted** -- under the plan's rule no
  floor keeps every answer on the four stores with either model, and the
  reference model is several times the latency budget; the plan's W3 has
  the numbers): inside `_rank_by_evidence`, the
  one ranking of every path, the shipping model (`reranker.MODEL`, pinned,
  local files only, no remote code) reads the question beside the best 20
  candidates by today's evidence and every memory a passage brought (a
  memory's start and its passage's stretch, the better counting), a few
  pairs at a time until the recall's budget (`reranker.BUDGET_S`, all kinds
  together) ends; the probability it answers is a logistic fit of the
  evidence and the model's score together (`reranker.CALIBRATION`, per kind,
  fitted on the benchmark's first set by `scripts/memory_rerank_calibrate.py`),
  and a memory is shown at or above the kind's floor and within its gap of
  the best (`_RERANK_*_FLOOR`, `_RERANK_*_GAP`). What the budget left unread
  keeps today's rule, ranked after what was read, and the recall says so
  (`RecallResult.rerank`: "whole" / "partial"); no model on disk is today's
  rule (said once, tried again after ten minutes). Facts are not reranked
  (`_RERANK_KINDS`: their calibrated probability ranked no better than the
  evidence). Measurements replay the model's recorded scores
  (`memory_bench.py rerank-scores`, not committed while the reranker is
  off; `benchmark.ReplayReranker` refuses a pair it lacks).
  Gate: `tests/test_memory_rerank.py` (EN/AR, both recall paths, a scripted
  model; today's rule, no floor, the budget ended and passages alone as
  controls).
  **Shown bounded, read whole**: the recall block shows a memory with its
  own bounds -- **room by rank** (the memory plan's W1a, 2026-11-22,
  `recall._room_by_rank`, `episode_text.display_at`), **for the
  conversations recall rates strong only** (a "possibly related" one keeps
  the fixed bounds, `_roomy`: the block grows only where recall is fairly
  sure it holds the answer): the best of them up to `RECALL_LEAD_SHOW`
  (1,500) characters, every other `RECALL_OTHER_SHOW` (500), each side cut
  around the stretch holding the
  most of the question's words (`query_terms.word_term`: search's reading,
  folded, the article and one-letter prefixes, a light plural); when that
  stretch is not the side's start, the side's opening sentence comes first
  (up to `RECALL_KEEP_OPENING`, 120 characters, at most half its room),
  then " … " and the stretch -- a memory often names its subject first --
  unless the stretch shown alone would begin inside the opening; when the
  block's budget would leave a line out the others give way first (to
  `RECALL_OTHER_LEAST`), then the best (to `RECALL_LEAD_LEAST`). **The
  budget is the whole block's** (`max_tokens`, 1,500 from the supervisor):
  rules, speakers note, fence and lines, counted as the context trim counts
  (`summarizer.estimate_text_tokens`, Arabic at about 2.5 characters a
  token). Until 2026-11-22 it bounded a quarter of the lines' characters,
  so the frame and Arabic's shorter tokens fell outside it and a block
  passed 1,500 (`tests/test_recall_block_budget.py`, Arabic counted as Latin
  as the negative control). Recall
  keeps each conversation's first `RECALL_FOCUS_READ` characters a side
  and how much more it holds (`_keep_sides`, in the asker's tenant); a
  follow-up joined to its turn and another member's turn keep recall's
  line (`_roomy`), and a hit with no sides is shown at `RECALL_SHOW_*` as
  before. Gate: `tests/test_recall_room_by_rank.py` (the fixed bounds, the
  block without the ladder, a raw word reading, the stretch alone and a
  plain opening rule as negative controls) --
  and, when it leaves some out, a note in the
  memory's language naming how many characters and `memory_read("<id>")`
  (`episode_text.more_note`); `memory_search` and the probe show up to
  `MEMORY_SHOW_MAX` (1,500); `memory_read` (read tier, fenced, the caller's
  tenant, `memory/episode_read.py`) reads one whole, `MEMORY_READ_PAGE`
  characters a page, and a page never ends in whitespace (the data fence
  drops a block's trailing whitespace: cut at a fixed size, the pages joined
  back lost a space at each boundary); the Memory page's list and probe offer
  "The whole memory" folded (`GET /api/memory/v2/episodes/{id}/text`), only
  for a memory the preview cut -- the list route says how much (`more`,
  from `display_parts`; guessed from the two lengths, a short memory of
  several lines read as "N more"). Model inputs stay
  bounded: the deep pass reads `DEEP_PASS_QUESTION`/`DEEP_PASS_ANSWER`
  (1,500/800), weekly summaries 400/600 per turn. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_keeps_all_text.py` (every writer, a long turn through
  the real code; old cut rows matching; the fill, the ledger, the race,
  another space's chat; the bounded views and the reader; a long turn end
  to end -- stored by the live writer, found by the real `recall` by a word
  only its end holds, shown bounded with the note, read back whole by
  `memory_read`, every character; no slice of a memory's text in memory
  code whose bound is not a `limits` name -- the old cut put back through
  `limits`, the old cut lines and fixed-size pages as the negative
  controls), and in a browser by the sidebar, EN/AR,
  `tests/e2e/test_memory_page_browser.py` (the list's fold reads a long
  memory to its last word; a short one of several lines has none).
- **Exact meaning search, every row** (`vector_engine.py`):
  `vec_distance_cosine` in SQL over every comparable row (same size, same
  model; NULL/'' version = legacy same model), NumPy chunked fallback, zero
  vectors excluded, read-only (no temp tables). Gate: no `LIMIT` in a
  candidate fetch unless it orders by distance.
- **Facts** (`recall._recall_beliefs`): meaning search always runs, over
  every current fact; ranking is §15G's evidence, with the belief thresholds.
- **Vector repair** (`reembed.run_vector_repair_pass`, 15 min, ~20 s): no
  vector, wrong size or another model's vector -> re-encoded in place,
  newest first; with nothing to repair it never loads the model.
  `global_reconsolidation` calls the same function.
- **Recovery of erased rows** (`rehydrate.run_rehydrate_pass`, 15 min):
  sources are earlier backups of the memory DB (a same-row copy whose text
  reproduces the stub), the chat store + spool and checkpoint history
  (`chat_history.py`, both backends), `noted` beliefs, `memory_store` tool
  calls (resumable scan). Anything but a backup must
  reproduce the episode id (`dual_write._episode_id` /
  `swarm_bridge.bridge_episode_id`) AND the stub (`_archive_stub`, checked
  against the old SQL). Sources must agree or nothing is restored; text is
  never overwritten; an unreadable source leaves the row pending (an outage
  is never a verdict). Verdicts live in `metadata.rehydrated` /
  `metadata.rehydrate`; memory health shows them (`memory_findability`).
- **Every turn reaches memory** (item H): `kazma_ui.turn_runtime.close_turn`
  -- the closer every transport runs -- hands a finished turn (graph
  terminal, not paused, and the `_post_turn_memory` record's turn index
  equal to the state's) to `consolidator.remember_turn`, once per turn.
  Nothing else calls it or `_schedule_post_turn_memory` (gate in
  `tests/test_memory_every_turn.py`). Until 2026-09-26 only the gateway
  handler did, so no web chat turn reached memory from 2026-08-08.
  `extract_turn_texts` pairs a question with ITS answer (it used to take the
  previous turn's when there was none); the episode `turn_number` is the
  turn index (`user_turn_index`), not the iteration count that made a
  repeated question collide into one memory.
- **A poison turn is set aside** (2026-10-13, Memory audit M27): a
  reconciled turn whose fact extraction fails `_FACT_ATTEMPTS` (3) passes in
  a row is marked `metadata.facts_failed` (a WARNING names it) and the facts
  cursor moves on; the count rides the reconcile state (`fact_attempts`). A
  locked database is never a verdict: it raises to the runner. One failing
  turn used to keep the cursor before it for good. The embedding rebuild
  (M28) loads the model first and re-encodes in place (a row keeps its old
  vector until the new one is written; it NULLed every vector and committed
  before the model loaded), and takes its pre-rebuild copy again each time
  (it kept the first one forever). `macro_sleep`'s tier moves are
  compare-and-set on the tier and last touch it read (M29: a forget during
  the sweep had its "forgotten" overwritten; `moves_skipped` counts them).
  Gate: `tests/test_memory_lifecycle_cas.py`.
- **Turn reconcile** (`turn_reconcile.run_turn_reconcile_pass`, 15 min, ~60
  s): every chat-store turn older than 10 minutes without an episode gets
  one, with its own time, through `mirror_episode`. Then the turns it wrote
  get their facts as a live turn does -- the heuristic pass at once, the LLM
  deep pass queued (`micro_consolidation`, at most `_DEEP_PER_PASS` = 60 a
  pass) -- at the turn's own time (§15H; a rowid cursor, `facts_after`).
  Repeated questions are counted, erased-row stubs count as present, and the
  cursor passes only settled sessions. On live it found 1,004 of 1,174 chat
  turns missing. **The cursors live in `memory_state.db`**
  (`memory_reconcile_state`, `turn_reconcile.read_state`, 2026-10-14): in
  the settings store a restored older memory database met a cursor already
  past the chats changed since its backup, and their newer turns were never
  memories again. Without the row (an older build's database, an older
  backup) every chat is read once. `memory.backup.restore_memory_backup` --
  the Memory page's restore -- copies the backup over the live file, then
  applies the forget journal and runs turn reconcile at once (forgets made
  since came back until the next 15-minute pass). Gates:
  `tests/test_memory_restore_drill.py` (RPO/RTO at any size,
  `KAZMA_TEST_MEMORY_RESTORE_DRILL_TURNS`; the cursor of after the backup as
  the negative control). `scripts/memory_soak.py` is the soak harness
  (private stores, a process per cycle, killed cycles, restores; checks every
  cycle), held by `tests/test_memory_soak_harness.py`.
- **Knowledge Library text is injected, never written into memory** (Memory
  audit M04, 2026-10-13). The supervisor copied up to two injected chunks a
  turn into the chat's memory (`promote_kb_hits_to_episodes`, setting
  `memory.v2.promote_kb_to_episodes`, on by default), inline in the async
  node -- a chat-store read, an insert, embeddings, the vector index and the
  Postgres mirror on the loop -- as `user_text="[Knowledge: ...] ..."`:
  crawled text recalled as history, grouped into summaries as the user's,
  and kept after its library was deleted. The promotion, its setting and
  Settings toggle, and recovery's library source are gone; the maintenance
  sweep "retired knowledge promotions" (`forget.retire_knowledge_promotions`)
  empties the copies an earlier build left -- no ledger row, the library
  keeps the text. `mirror_episode` is a loop-stall helper. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_kb_never_in_memory.py` (a real supervisor call that
  injects library text under a loop SQLite/embedder tracer: no memory write;
  recall shows none; the old call on the loop as the tracer's control; the
  retirement; nothing writes the old source).
- **Nothing repoints live memory** (item I): no product code rebinds a
  `kazma_core.paths` function or resets the shared `dual_write` writer
  (`_reset_mirror` is a test helper; gate in `tests/test_memory_every_turn.py`).
  The Dashboard's golden eval did both inside the live server, so any turn
  written during -- and, through the writer left on its temp file, after --
  a run was stored in a file nobody read. It now seeds and recalls on a
  private database (`recall(conn=...)`), refuses the live one, and runs off
  the event loop.
- **Nothing stranded in a table recall does not read** (item J,
  `memory/legacy_tables.py`): a one-off operation on 2026-08-02/03 (never
  committed) moved 329 episodes into `episodes_archive`, which no code
  reads. The recovery sweep puts each back as a cold (`archived`) memory --
  own id, text, vector, tenant, time -- skipping an id `episodes` holds and
  a text the tenant already holds; the legacy table is left as it is. Health
  counts what is still stranded. `entities_archive` stays archived (junk
  nodes and 200-character truncations of memories held in full).
- **Conversation history has one reader** (`memory/chat_history.py`): the
  past-chats fallback and the recovery read Postgres `kazma_chat_sessions` or
  SQLite `sessions`, overlaid with the save spool (`paths.chat_spool_db`, the
  web UI's rule too), tenant-filtered, scored in SQL over every session. The
  fallback used to open only the SQLite file -- on Postgres a July leftover.

**G. Recall injects what the question is about -- and nothing when nothing is
(Stage 2, 2026-09-26, plan §5 R1/R2/R4/R7, S4/S5/W3).** Recall used to
rank-fuse its channels and always return its top five: on live, 77 of 77
recalls injected exactly "5 beliefs, 5 episodes", and on the retrieval
benchmark no unanswerable question got an empty result and three facts in
four injected were noise.
- **One ranking, every path:** `recall._rank_by_evidence` scores every
  candidate -- local and Postgres-primary, episodes and facts -- on its
  meaning similarity ABOVE the question's background (the mean of meaning
  ranks 4-15, blended with a 0.5 prior below five samples: bge-m3 puts
  almost everything at 0.45-0.65, so an absolute cosine cannot tell "about
  this" from "near this") plus the share of the question's content words it
  holds. Below the floor nothing is injected; behind the best by more than
  the gap, nothing either; below "strong" it is shown as "(possibly
  related)". Thresholds per kind (`_evidence_rules`), each from a sweep on
  the benchmark (the comments say what each end cost). With no comparable
  vector for any candidate, words decide alone: at least half the question
  (`_WORDS_ONLY_FLOOR`). A keyword-only candidate is judged by meaning too:
  its stored vector locally, `VectorBackend.similarities` on the
  Postgres-primary path (every backend implements it). Never add a path
  that ranks by position again -- `tests/test_memory_relevance.py` replaces
  the ranker with rank fusion and every path must break.
- **Content words** (`memory/query_terms.py`): EN + Gulf/MSA stopwords,
  Arabic folded (`documents.arabic.fold_for_search`) with the article and
  one-letter prefixes handled, light plurals, whole-word prefix matching
  (`mentions`: "out" is not in "about"), an underscore separates words (as
  in FTS5). The FTS query, the mirror searches, the past-chats fallback and
  coverage all use it. A words-only search needs half the question: the
  mirror top-up (which also never re-adds a row the local database holds --
  local recall already judged it) and the past-chats fallback (more than
  half), which now actually runs, whenever recall comes back empty.
- **Facts:** candidates are content-word matches, the nearest facts by
  meaning, the facts extracted from the turns episode recall found
  (provenance: `source_session`/`source_turn`, never a substring bridge),
  and the graph walk's head. The access-count "rotation" penalty is gone: a
  fact asked about often is not demoted for it (R4). Display de-slugs the
  subject ("platform team owns ...").
- **The model sees the question AND the answer (R3, 2026-09-27).**
  `memory/episode_text.py` is the one home of an episode's texts:
  `display_text` ("User: ... / Assistant: ..." when both sides exist; one
  side is shown as it is -- a swarm result must not read as something the
  user said) is what the injected block and the tool/probe outputs show
  (`metadata["display"]`, read through `recall.shown_text`); `match_text`
  (summary, else question, else answer) stays what recall compares,
  de-duplicates and seeds the graph walk by -- used for those, the display
  changed which memories were kept and precision fell; `embed_text` keeps
  the vector question-first. Embedding the answer too was built and
  measured, and not adopted: with every threshold re-swept, precision fell
  in four benchmark categories (fact 0.71 -> 0.65, multi 0.89 -> 0.78, noise
  0.61 -> 0.57, paraphrase 0.66 -> 0.65) and answer-only questions gained
  nothing (their words are in the answer, which keyword search and coverage
  read). Gate: `tests/test_memory_episode_text.py::test_every_episode_text_comes_from_one_place`
  (no "summary first" choice outside that module; ids and dedupe keys take
  the question first and are exempt).
- **"Remember this" in either language (W4).** `memory/remember_request.py`
  is the one detector: English phrases as before, Arabic (MSA and Gulf:
  تذكر، لا تنسى، احفظ، سجل عندك، خلك فاكر، حط في بالك ...) compared folded
  and as whole words with an optional و/ف prefix -- "تذكرة" (a ticket) is
  not "تذكر". It promotes the turn to the recall tier (`episode_row`) and is
  a durable cue (`is_filler_turn`: "تذكر هذا" is eight characters).
- **Write-path details** (2026-10-13, Memory audit M26): English "remember"
  phrases match whole words, and one right after "do/did you" is a question
  ("Can you denote that" matched "note that" and became a recall-tier
  memory); `dual_write.mirror_belief` (no caller, past the trust gate, the
  ledger and supersede) is deleted; a single-valued fact's current value is
  the newest, and extra current rows are closed at its start; the deep pass
  marks its episode (`metadata.deep_pass`, `_DEEP_PASS_VERSION`) and a
  second task for it does nothing; the embedder singleton is built once
  under a lock. Gate: `tests/test_memory_write_path_items.py`.
- **A single value stays single whatever the writer labels it** (2026-11,
  the memory framework audit's F7, `belief_mutation._classify_predicate`,
  `_survivor`). Kazma's own class (`kazma_classifies`) wins over the caller's
  label: the agent's memory tools label a fact "set" by default, and an
  agent's `lives_in Tokyo` labelled a list stood beside the user's own
  London, past the trust gate. The class is read from the name's words
  (`belief_mutation._kazma_name`, as `predicates` compares names): "live_in",
  "in_lives" or "is_name" labelled a list slipped past an exact-name class.
  Of several current rows of a single-valued
  fact, the newest the user said stays (else the newest), and a newer row
  from a lower source closes where it began. On names a person holds several
  of (`_LISTABLE`: works_at, active_project, current_role) a list labelled by
  the user's own words stays a list, and stays whole until a write that may
  replace the user's value replaces all of it; every other single-valued name
  holds one value whoever labels it. **A plural name is a list**
  (`_names_a_list`, the security review of F1's second half, 2026-11-18):
  "names", "favorite_foods", "colors_favorite" put Kazma's one-value thing in
  the plural and are written as a set; "lives_in" and "works_at" keep their
  verb's "s", and "the_name" or "is_name" is still `name_is`. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_kazma_class_wins.py` (the label first, keeping the
  newest, the exact-name class, no listable names and no plural rule as
  negative controls).
- **A list stays a list** (2026-10-19, `belief_mutation._established_kind`).
  The extractor labels each fact's type; a single-valued label on a predicate
  the subject keeps as a list (current `set` rows) is written as one more
  entry, and the "extra current rows" close never takes a list entry --
  unless Kazma itself classifies the predicate (`kazma_classifies`: the
  functional and state lists, `favorite_*`, the rotating current facts).
  Live, `user noted "test codeword is ..."` labelled functional superseded one
  of the owner's notes and closed 57 more. `scripts/memory_reopen_lists.py`
  (`memory/list_reopen.py`; `size`, then `apply --db --yes`, copy first)
  reopens entries closed that way, one audit row each. **"Forget" in chat
  forgets the turn too**: `memory_invalidate(forget_source_turn=true)` runs
  `forget.forget_belief_source` -- the fact's source turn through
  `forget_episode(by="user")`, as the Memory page's Forget -- or recall found
  the turn and the next turn learned the fact again. A value that names one
  thing (`forget._distinctive_value`: one token of 6+ characters with a
  digit, `-` or `_` -- a codeword, an order or phone number) is forgotten in
  every memory of the tenant that holds it: Kazma's own later answers quoting
  it kept it, and a new chat recalled one. A plain word is never swept.
  **"Forget everything that mentions X"** is `memory_forget_mentions(text)`
  (`forget.forget_mentions`, danger tier, 4+ characters): everything of the
  tenant holding the text -- memories, facts current, ended or archived (in
  their subject, predicate or value), weekly summaries, entities it names
  with their merges and groupings, changes, legacy rows, queued turns --
  matched by `memory/mention_match.py` (both sides folded as search folds:
  case, Arabic letter forms and marks; an id also by its slug; Kazma's own
  names for the person and itself never a mention). "About me" is searched
  and named (`about_me_holds_it`), never edited. Journaled (kind
  `mentions`: ids only, an entity's id hashed). `memory_search`
  ranks the best few matches, so forgetting its hits one by one left 5 of 7
  (live). It also removes every self-improvement lesson holding the text
  (`self_improvement.forget_text`, the Soul and its history: a lesson quoted
  the codeword into every prompt), and a forget keeps its own turn out of
  memory (`forget.keep_turn_out`, the ledger row the writer asks first: the
  request "Forget every memory that mentions X" was written as a memory of
  X) -- **only when the user's own words ask to forget**
  (`memory/forget_request.is_forget_request`, 2026-11-22, the memory plan's
  finding 16: English and Arabic, a polite question too, read through
  `own_words(questions=True)`, so never a "forget" in a quote, someone
  else's words or a text to translate). A model that retires an old memory
  on its own in a turn that states a new fact ("I moved to Porto",
  "انتقلت إلى بورتو") keeps that turn: it is an update, and the quick pass
  writes the new fact (live, the move was kept out and no new home was
  written). Gate: `tests/test_forget_only_when_asked.py` (a real supervisor
  graph and `close_turn`, EN/AR; every forget keeping its turn out as the
  negative control). A lesson never quotes the task (it appended "Task context: '<the
  user's message>'"). The memory tool also takes a
  memory id (`e_...`, from `memory_search`) and forgets that memory, and an id
  it cannot find is refused before anything is done (`RefusedBeforeEffect`):
  the model passed memory ids the first day, and "not found" was recorded as
  an unknown effect that failed the turn. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_list_stays_a_list.py` (the old write and invalidating
  alone as negative controls).
- **Small talk is kept, never recalled (W5).** `episode_text.is_small_talk`:
  the whole message is small talk by its words, never by length ("Pixel's
  age?" is short and a question). A greeting, thanks or goodbye with a reply
  under 1,000 characters (live greeting replies ran to 531, median 141); an
  acknowledgement ("ok", "yes", "تمام") only with a reply under 200 -- it is
  often the go-ahead for a report. Every episode candidate path of recall
  (local, Postgres-primary, mirror top-up) leaves it out; the row stays. A
  small-talk MESSAGE looks nothing up: `recall` returns empty at once and
  `search_transcripts` (the past-chats fallback an empty recall runs) too.
  **Extraction's filler check follows the same rule** (2026-11, the memory
  framework audit's F8): `belief_extractor.is_filler_turn` asks
  `episode_text.is_small_talk_words` after the durable cues. A message of
  twelve characters or fewer was filler by its length, and "I'm diabetic",
  "Call me Sam", "No, Lisbon" and "عندي سكري" reached neither pass. **Small
  talk is read by whole phrases** (the security review of F1's second half,
  2026-11-18): a message is nothing but `_SMALL_TALK_PHRASES` (longest
  first), the words that may follow one (`_SMALL_TALK_TAILS`: "thanks
  man", "شكرا حبيبي"), laughter and pauses -- never every WORD small talk,
  which made "I am a man", "I am Sure", "I'm Kazma" and "no it will do"
  filler. The phrases include the replies a person answers and goes ahead
  with ("نعم", "لا", "ايوه", "كمل", "يلا", "خلاص", "ان شاء الله", "go ahead",
  "yes please", "sounds good", "I'm good"). A message past `_FILLER_MAX`
  (400 characters) is never filler, and the cues read no further. A filler
  turn queues no deep pass (one model call): the
  post-turn path and turn reconcile ask `is_filler_turn` before queueing
  `micro_consolidation`. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_short_statements.py` (the length rule and the
  word-by-word rule as negative controls), the write scenarios' `short` category, and
  `tests/test_filler_queues_no_deep_pass.py` (tasks counted through the real
  post-turn function; every function queueing a deep pass asks, or is
  declared; the path without the check as the control).
- **The graph walk reads the seeds' neighbourhood (R5).** It loaded the
  tenant's most important facts (800 at the defaults) and walked those: a
  fact below the cut was out of reach however close to the question.
  `recall._belief_neighbourhood` reads the facts around the seeds hop by hop
  (one round past the walk's radius, so the edges between its outermost
  nodes are there); the seeds come from every entity name. Same graph as
  before whenever the old cut held everything.
- **Recall has a deadline and embeds the question once** (2026-10-13, Memory
  audit M16). `recall()` wraps the body (`_recall`) with a per-recall memo
  (`_QUERY_MEMO`): each text is embedded at most once, a failure included
  (a failed embedding was tried by every channel, four times a recall), in a
  bounded daemon thread (`_embed_within`, two in flight at most) waited on
  until `memory.v2.recall_deadline_s` (default 5 s). Past it, or with the
  embedder failing, recall answers from keywords and sets
  `RecallResult.degraded`; `memory_search` then says the search was
  incomplete, never "No relevant memories found.". Both embedders carry a
  circuit breaker (`embedder._EmbedderBreaker`: 30 s doubling to ten
  minutes, no call and no log while open, one log line per opening) shown in
  memory health (`embedder`, `status_detail: embedder_unavailable`). Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_recall_deadline.py` (negative controls: the body
  without its memo or deadline, a breaker that never opens).
- **Recall reads the question's text, bounded** (2026-10-13, Memory audits
  M17, M25). The supervisor's latest user text is
  `turn_input.extract_latest_user_text(messages, image_marker=False)`: the
  text parts only. It was `str(content)` -- on a photo turn the Python repr of
  the parts, base64 included (recall embedded 200,125 characters and built a
  6,029-term keyword query; the language lock and the router read it too).
  `recall()` reads at most `_QUESTION_MAX_CHARS` (2,000: the start and the
  end of a long paste), the keyword query and the graph walk's seeds at most
  `_QUESTION_MAX_TERMS` (32) words, each once. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_question_bounds.py` (a photo turn through the real
  supervisor node; recall at 2,000 words within twice 20 words on a seeded
  store; the bounds lifted as the negative control).
- **Hybrid vector search merges (R8).** `HybridVectorBackend.search`
  returned the remote index's hits alone whenever it had any, so a memory
  not yet in the remote index was invisible to meaning search. Both are
  searched and merged by id; the local store's score wins (it is the source
  of truth).
- **The block carries the dates Kazma holds** (2026-11-20, framework audit
  F2 step 1, part C2). `recall` ends with `recall._date_hits`: each turn
  gets its day (`said_on`, from the candidate's `at`), each fact the month
  it became true (`since`, its `valid_from`), and a functional or state
  fact the value it replaced with its months (`before`, read through
  `supersedes_id` in the fact's tenant; a forgotten value, `object = ''`,
  is never shown). In the operator's zone (`_memory_zone`:
  `resolve_cron_zone`). `_dated_line` puts them BEFORE the text ("[since
  Oct 2026] user lives in London; before that: Paris (May 2026 to Oct
  2026)"), after the reading tag, one line. No model, no new storage; a
  read that fails leaves the dates out with a WARNING. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_recall_dates.py` (recall without the dating step as
  the negative control). **A changed value names the conversations that
  said it** (2026-11-23, the memory plan's W4): on a fact line with
  `before`, each value is followed by "(memory e_...)" of the turn that
  stated it (`recall._stated_in`: the fact's `source_session` /
  `source_turn`, in the asker's tenant, a turn recall could still show), so
  the model can open it with `memory_read`; an unchanged fact names none.
  Gate: `tests/test_memory_changed_value_sources.py` (EN/AR; the line as it
  was as the control). **A change waiting for the user's yes is shown
  beside its fact** (2026-11-22, the memory plan's finding 17): the same
  step reads the newest open pending change on each shown fact
  (`recall._waiting_changes`, `changes.PENDING`, state open: a decided or
  expired change is not shown, another tenant's never) and `_dated_line`
  ends the fact's line, inside the fence, with `WAITING_CHANGE` and the
  value ("user lives in Lisbon; changed, not confirmed yet, to: Porto") or
  `WAITING_ENDED`; a recall rule outside the fence says to give both
  values and ask. A bare move is put to the user as a question (finding
  15), and recall showed only the held home: the real-use suite run twice
  after finding 16 answered "Where do I live now?" with the old home in 3
  of 4 language-runs. A store from before the change log shows its facts
  as before. Gate: `tests/test_memory_waiting_change_in_recall.py` (the
  real quick pass, `recall` and block, EN/AR; recall reading no change as
  the negative control).
- **A fact is found by a question in either language** (2026-11-22, the
  memory plan's finding 10). A fact's words are Kazma's English name for it
  ("user lives in بورتو"): an English question matched the name ("live",
  worth the whole fact floor) and an Arabic one no word of it, so "وين أسكن
  الحين؟" found the user's home once in four real-use runs. The words each
  fact kind is asked with, in both languages and one sense only, live
  beside `fact_names.KINDS` (`ASKED_WITH`; a favourite's kind words from
  `arabic_facts.favourite_kind_words`; `NOT_ASKED_BY_WORDS` names a fact
  meaning alone decides, with why): recall's word coverage reads them beside
  the fact's own words (`recall._belief_candidate`, `asked_words`), and the
  fact lane's keyword search (local and Postgres-primary) is asked for the
  kinds a question names (`_belief_search_words`, `kinds_asked`). The Arabic
  words for "now" (الحين, الآن ...) are not content words, as English "now"
  is not (`time_words`, part F's non-content handling); "these days",
  "هالأيام" stay content in both. The fact's vector is unchanged (W3
  measures what this table gives). Measured: the gate 36/42 -> 42/42 (every
  loss an Arabic question); Kazma's benchmark hit rate and MRR unchanged,
  precision 0.4872 -> 0.4828 (q1008 "كم صرفنا لحد الحين؟" shows one more
  turn: its answer held "الحين", a word it no longer counts); the speakers
  set and the small store unchanged. Gate: `tests/test_memory_fact_languages.py`
  (`benchmark.run_fact_languages`: five facts told by the real quick pass in
  each language, stores of one and five, asked in both, bge-m3's recorded
  vectors, `scripts/memory_bench.py fact-languages-vectors`; a word in
  another sense shows none; every predicate a quick pass writes has words in
  both languages or a reason; today's rules as the negative control, which
  lose Arabic questions only). **City and home ask where the user lives
  only when said of the user** (2026-11-22, the main session's decision
  after the real-use suite's "أي مدينة صارت بيتي هالفترة؟" found no fact):
  `fact_names.ASKED_AS_MINE`, `kinds_said_of_the_user`. English says it in
  the phrase ("my city", "my home", "home for me", "I call home"), Arabic in
  the word ("مدينتي", "بيتي", "ديرتي" after a question word or a verb of
  becoming). The word must be the thing asked, in both languages: never a
  word describing another ("my home Wi-Fi", "عنوان بيتي"), a place
  something is in ("in my home", "في بيتي") or another kind of city ("my
  favourite city", "مدينتي المفضلة"). "Which city is the capital", "the home
  page", "مدينة الملاهي" and "بيت الشعر" ask nothing. Such a question reads
  those words as "live" in the fact lane (`asked_as_mine`, for its kinds
  and its word coverage), and the asker's own fact of that kind is kept
  whatever its evidence (`recall._named_facts`, `_rank_by_evidence`'s
  `named`, both fact lanes; `_ASKER_ENTRY` is `user` or the member's
  entry). Words alone were not enough: bge-m3 puts "What is my city?" below
  an unrelated question's background for "user lives in Porto", and a
  fact's coverage weighs 0.06. A named fact clears no cut, so the
  benchmark's edge margin counts it as `benchmark.NAMED_MARGIN`. Measured:
  the 28 city/home rows of the fact-languages set 3/28 -> 28/28 (words alone
  7/28), the precision rows show no fact; Kazma's benchmark, the speakers
  set and the small store do not move (a first version showed the home for
  the small store's abstain question q805, "What is my home Wi-Fi network
  called?": hence the rule that the word is the thing asked).
- **One fact, one predicate name (W6, `memory/predicates.py`).** The
  extractor names predicates freely; under two names a single-valued fact is
  never superseded (live 2026-09-27: "daily_tweet_cap" 16 and
  "tweet_daily_cap" 8 both current). Names that are the SAME WORDS (order,
  filler words and a plural "s" aside) are one name: `mutate_belief` writes a
  new fact under the name its subject already uses for those words and type
  (`canonical_predicate`, inside the mutation lock, so the trust gate still
  decides), and reconsolidation retires what is stored twice
  (`merge_same_word_predicates`: latest statement among equal sources; where
  the user's word and an inference disagree, both stay -- the extractor labels
  the user's own later words "inferred", so either choice is wrong). Never by
  meaning: bge-m3 puts "grok_next_reset" / "grok_personal_next_reset" (two
  accounts) at 0.94, above most true pairs. Names a word apart are the
  extractor's to avoid: the deep pass is given the names in use
  (`predicate_vocabulary`) and told to reuse them, and to skip one run's
  status and internal ids. Measured and gated in
  `tests/test_memory_predicate_names.py`.
- **Measured, not asserted (R7):** `kazma_core/memory/benchmark.py` seeds a
  private database the product's way -- turns via `episode_row`, facts via
  `mutate_belief(private=True)`, which keeps every write in that database (no
  state mirror, graph or remote vector index), and (v3) weekly
  summaries as `topic_summaries` stores them, a summary answering when it
  stands for an answering turn -- and asks the real `recall()`. CI replays bge-m3's recorded vectors
  (`tests/fixtures/memory_bench/vectors.npz`); `thresholds.json` is a
  ratchet stamped with the dataset version: `python scripts/memory_bench.py
  lock` raises it and refuses to lower it, `lock --rebaseline` is for a new
  dataset version only. A change to the dataset's texts needs `vectors`
  re-recorded with the real model. The Dashboard's golden eval seeds facts
  the same way; a case marked `needs_meaning` is skipped without an
  embedder and must pass with one. **Dataset v5 (2026-10-14, Memory audit
  M24)** adds a second set of 40 questions (`SECOND_SET`: no threshold is
  swept on it; the builder refuses one that repeats a tuning question; a
  `mixed` category asks across languages), scored apart
  (`report["second"]`, gated as `second.*`). **It is not held out**
  (renamed 2026-11-20, benchmark audit R8, the owner's decision 4): two
  decisions were taken by looking at it and it is gated in the same lock,
  so it stays gated as a second check, and only a sealed set (another
  session's questions, scored on request) may be called held out
  (`test_nothing_calls_the_second_set_held_out`: the page, the guide, the
  builder and the benchmark's docstring; the old words as the negative
  control). **The sealed set** (2026-11-20, R8, decision 4;
  `docs/plans/MEMORY_SEALED_SET.md`) is written by a session that does not
  build or tune recall, as `tests/fixtures/memory_bench/sealed_questions.json`.
  CI checks its shape only (`sealed_problems`: 8 questions or more in each of
  `SEALED_CATEGORIES`, Arabic in each but keyword, every gold id in the
  dataset, no repeat of a question the benchmark asks), never its scores:
  `scripts/memory_bench.py sealed --look "why"` is the only way it is scored
  (its question vectors recorded with the real model once, in
  `sealed_vectors.npz`), every look is logged in the lock's `sealed` section
  (date, reason, commit, the file's hash, the scores) and kept by every
  `lock`, and a look with `--decided` spends the set until its questions are
  new. The page prints the last look apart. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_benchmark_sealed.py` (a planted set; a test that scores
  the sealed file as the negative control). An extraction benchmark
  (`benchmark_data/extraction.json`, `run_extraction_benchmark`: 40 turns
  EN/AR/mixed; the heuristic pass in CI, the model's deep pass from
  recorded replies, `tests/fixtures/memory_bench/extraction_llm.json`,
  recorded with `scripts/memory_extraction_record.py --out <fixture>
  --limit N` run by an install's own Python (it loads that install's
  `.env`; `memory_bench.py` stays env-free) -- it costs a call a turn and
  asking; a turn with no recording is an error, never "the model was
  down"). **Dataset v3 asks what part C2 changed** (2026-11-20,
  `memory_bench.EXTRACTION_C2_TURNS`, ten turns EN/AR, `new_in: 3`): a
  fact's start from the turn's day, the turn before read for context only,
  a held fact replaced, a fact ended, planted text kept out. A gold fact
  names what it asks (`since`, `replaces`, `ended`) and the model's pass
  scores it per language (`dated`, `replaced`, `ended`; `_score_c2`); a
  fact said to have ended finds only an ending (`_value_matches`). A drift
  check leaves out, named (`llm_waiting`), the turns added after its
  recording's `extraction_version`. A relabel is a file holding every
  locked reply (`reply_hashes`), re-keyed or extended. **The recording**
  (2026-11-20, the owner's yes): deepseek-flash, all 40 turns of v3, 5
  askings each, 200 calls; the file says what the provider counted
  (`usage`: 307,945 prompt tokens, 259,712 of them cache hits, 31,740
  completion tokens, 21,916 of them reasoning; no price known to Kazma)
  and names the message each turn was asked (`asked`, which a drift check
  replays by after a later message form, `_reply_key`). The recording of
  2026-10-15 is kept as `extraction_llm_2026-10-15.json`: the Spaces R3
  study and the 2026-11 audits' evidence measured it. Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_benchmark_c2_turns.py` (answers with no start,
  replacement or ending, and a scorer that ignores `ended`, as negative
  controls). **Scored by value since 2026-11**
  (dataset v2, benchmark audit R1): per pass and language `found` (a gold
  fact's whole value -- equal, or whole words of it -- under its subject, or
  the relation from the other side, under any name that does not turn it
  around: a negative or past name finds only a negative or past fact),
  `named` (of those, under a listed name), `right` (kept facts not unwanted:
  a turn's `extras` are true, its `avoid` entries are never right and find
  nothing; the name is scored apart) and `quiet`; the old strict reading
  stays in each row as `recall`/`precision`, ungated. **A recording says
  what it is** (`_recording_identity`: its replies' hash, model, provider,
  date, askings, the system prompt's hash) and a recording of another prompt
  is refused (`StaleRecordingError`, also at replay time); a message the
  recording holds no reply for is its own failure, never "the model is
  down". The gate and the lock compare the locked prompt hash too: the same
  replies relabelled as another prompt's are refused, flag or not, also
  when they are keyed by another message (`replies_sha256`, the replies
  alone, `_same_replies`). **Several askings a turn** (benchmark audit R2,
  2026-11-20): a recording holds a list of replies a turn; every asking is
  scored, a score is the total over the askings (`_total_over_askings`) and
  its spread two standard errors of theirs (`_spread`, kept in the lock as
  `spread`); a new recording is locked only with `ASKINGS_STANDARD` (5)
  askings a turn and a finished recorder (`memory_bench._new_recording_problems`);
  the write scenarios replay the first asking. The recorder
  (`record_llm_extraction`, `scripts/memory_extraction_record.py --out PATH
  --limit N`) asks through the product's own `_llm_extract`, every turn's
  first asking before any second, saves after every reply with the usage
  the provider reported (`usage`) and the message each turn was asked
  (`asked`), continues its file without asking again what it has, and
  stops at its call limit (`complete`: false). Gates: `tests/test_memory_extraction_record.py`, the
  askings cases in `tests/test_memory_benchmark.py` (today's one-reply file
  refused as a new recording, the first asking alone as the controls). The lock
  (`_extraction_lock`): the quick pass is a ratchet; the model's pass
  compares exactly on the same recording, a new recording is locked only with
  `lock --new-recording "why"` and replaces the old scores exactly (written
  in `recordings`), no recording is a failure, and `lock --rebaseline`
  resets the extraction part when its dataset version changes. Gates in
  `tests/test_memory_benchmark.py`, each with its negative control (a
  renamed extractor keeps `found`; "Keep nothing" as the prompt is refused;
  the old max-of-two floor). **A prompt change waits for its recording,
  declared** (2026-11-20, framework audit part C2: its prompt changes land
  first and are recorded once, with the owner's yes). `lock --prompt-changed
  "why"` writes `extraction.pending_recording` (the prompt and message form
  it waits for, the recording it replaces, each change dated with its
  reason; `memory_bench._declare_prompt_change`); until a recording of
  today's prompt ends it, `benchmark._check_recording` answers `previous` and the
  model's pass and the write scenarios replay the old recording by turn
