source (`/home/user/kazma`) has its workspace root and data dir baked into
stored text. Before the swap the importer rewrites them, in the staged
copies, to the target's (`build_path_map`: the source workspace root and the
source data dir, each to the target's; `migration/path_rewrite.py`), in
exactly these columns (`importer._PATH_REWRITE_TARGETS`):
`workspaces.root_path` (exported as `workspaces.db`, merged into
`settings.db` after the swap); `sessions.messages` (`chat_sessions.db`) and
`spool.payload` (`chat_sessions_spool.db`); in `memory_state.db`
`entities.metadata_json`, `episodes.user_text`, `episodes.assistant_text`,
`episodes.summary_text`, `episodes.metadata_json`, `beliefs.object`,
`beliefs.metadata_json`, `procedural_dags.preconditions_json`,
`procedural_dags.dag_steps_json`, `procedural_dags.postconditions_json`; in
`memory_ops.db` `memory_audit_log.reason`,
`memory_audit_log.state_before_json`, `memory_audit_log.state_after_json`;
`cron_jobs.prompt` (`cron.db`); `agent_artifacts.value`
(`agent_artifacts.db`); `task_ledgers.goal`, `task_ledgers.next_action`,
`task_ledgers.steps`, `task_ledgers.findings` (`task_ledgers.db`). The
import report counts the rows changed per database (`rows_rewritten`).
Nothing else is rewritten: `config.yaml` is imported as exported, the
document store holds no paths, and time-travel snapshots (`snapshots.db`)
are not carried at all, so none of their columns is rewritten (2026-10-14,
Time Travel audit TT-05: a copy elsewhere would bring back chats the owner
deleted or forgot; §12, `store_registry`: `machine`). Three correctness
properties: (1) `PathMap` is ordered **longest-source-first** so
`/home/u/kazma` doesn't partially rewrite `/home/u/kazma-repos/ShipX`; (2)
substitution is byte-level substring on the column text (NOT a JSON parse --
paths appear anywhere), of the forward-slash form, the backslash form AND
the JSON-escaped Windows form (`C:\\Users\\...`, every backslash doubled
inside a JSON column; TT-09: a Windows-source migration left those paths on
the old machine), whose rest is written in the target's separators (`/` for
a POSIX target, still escaped for a Windows one); a match is anchored at
path boundaries, so no false positives (`/home/u/kazma-backup` is not
`/home/u/kazma`, `barcode` ≠ `code`); (3) a row that parsed as JSON and
whose rewritten text would not keeps its original text and is counted in a
WARNING (`_parses`). Gates: `tests/test_path_rewrite.py`,
`tests/test_time_travel_bounds.py` (both directions with the old rewrite as
the control; this list against the importer's). Workspace root rewrite also
fires `notify_root_changed()` so MCP rebinds.

**C. Import is atomic — never corrupt the target mid-flight.** The importer
(`migration/importer.py:import_bundle`) stages to `kazma-data/.migrate-staging-<ts>/`,
verifies, path-rewrites the *staged* copies, backs up the live DBs to
`.migrate-backup-<ts>/`, then swaps staging → live one file at a time via
`rename`. Any exception before the swap leaves live data untouched; the
staging dir is preserved on failure. `verify` runs as a dry-run inside every
import and is available standalone. **A kept staging dir expires**
(2026-11-11): the next import removes one older than `STALE_STAGING_S` (30
days), never one a running import marks as its own (`IN_USE_MARKER`, written
by `mark_working_folder`, taken off by `import_bundle` however the run ends;
`_working_folder_in_use` keeps a folder whose mark it cannot read or rule
out). It was swept with `max_age_s=inf`, kept forever. Gate:
`tests/test_failed_import_staging_expires.py` (the old age as the control).

**What restoring the old Kazma after the PC reset taught it** (2026-11-19):
- **`kazma migrate import` holds Kazma itself.** It runs the whole check
  first as a dry run (a bundle that would be refused never stops Kazma),
  stops Kazma through its guard once no chat turn runs (`setup._MoveHold`,
  the database and engine moves' hold, under `_IMPORT_PAUSE_REASON`),
  imports with `server_stopped=True` (the heartbeat the server stamped in
  its last minute is no live server: the gate refused the owner for two
  minutes after their own pause), and starts Kazma again whatever the
  outcome (invariant C left the data as it was). `--force` imports
  without the hold, as before. A bundle it cannot read is one sentence
  (`_refuse_unreadable`), not zipfile's traceback.
- **The vault status said at the end is the one after the import**
  (`_say_key_written`: `replaced`, or `set` for an install with no key).
  It printed the pairing read before the swap: "mismatch ... Re-run with
  --reset-vault-key", after that flag had written the right key.
- **The document list follows the bundle** (`_document_list_plan`, step
  2b, before anything changes). A bundle carries `data/documents.db` only
  when its source kept the list in SQLite; on an install whose list follows
  Postgres the import said "documents.db not installed" and 29 documents
  came back with no list. Now the setting unset or `auto` gets
  `KAZMA_DOCUMENTS_METADATA_BACKEND=sqlite` written into `.env` (and the
  process) before the store is restored, said in the output; named
  `postgres`, the import stops, nothing changed.
- **Every sync Postgres pool is closed before Python exits**
  (`postgres_pool.close_at_exit`, one `atexit` handler): on Python 3.14
  psycopg_pool's `__del__` cannot join its threads at shutdown, and every
  `kazma` command that touched Postgres ended with "Exception ignored ...
  PythonFinalizationError". Checked on the owner's 3.14 install (a plain
  pool as the control).
Gates: `tests/test_migrate_import_after_reset.py`,
`tests/test_migrate_cli_holds_kazma.py`, `tests/test_pools_closed_at_exit.py`
(each with the old behaviour as its control).

**Scope — SQLite + Postgres (v2).** The bundle always carries the SQLite
files (vault, memory, cron and the other stores `store_registry` carries —
these are SQLite even under a Postgres backend). When the source is Postgres, it ALSO carries a
``data/postgres.dump`` produced by ``pg_dump -Fc`` containing the
shared-state tables (settings, chat sessions, checkpoints, swarm tasks).
The exporter reads via the backend-agnostic data-access layer for the
SQLite portion and shells out to ``pg_dump`` for the Postgres portion.

**Postgres dump/restore discovery — ``pg_bridge.py``.**
``resolve_pg_dump()`` / ``resolve_pg_restore()`` try, in order: (1) the
binary on PATH, (2) ``docker exec ${KAZMA_DB_CONTAINER:-kazma-db} <bin>``
(the common Docker-deployment default — the DB container has the client
tools even when the host doesn't), (3) raise ``PgToolNotFound`` with a
clear install hint. Override the container name with ``KAZMA_DB_CONTAINER``.

**Target-backend matching on import.** The importer checks the target
backend: if Postgres, it ``pg_restore`` the dump (``--clean --if-exists``
idempotent; schema self-recreates, target DB can be empty) into
``KAZMA_DATABASE_URL``, then proceeds with the SQLite-file restore +
path-rewrite of the staged SQLite stores (B). If the target is SQLite but the
bundle has a Postgres dump, it **aborts with a clear error** rather than
silently importing partial data (the SQLite files alone lack chat history,
settings, checkpoints that live in Postgres). No SQLite↔Postgres content
translation is attempted — the bundle is source-backend-shaped.

**Bundle layout:** `manifest.json` (version, source OS/host, per-file sha256,
vault-key fingerprint, table counts, source workspace root), `meta.env`
(vault key + public url), `config.yaml` (ConfigStore.export_yaml — secrets
are `vault://` refs, not plaintext), `vault.db` (encrypted, under `data/`),
every other SQLite store `store_registry` says a bundle carries, under
`data/` (`bundle_store_names`, plus the `checkpoints_<tenant>.db` family
members present), `data/postgres.dump` (only when the
source was Postgres — custom format, restored via pg_restore), `pathmap.json`,
and verbatim `assets/`: every other entry of the data dir that
`store_registry.carried_in_bundle` says travels (2026-10-01) -- the swarm's
worker registry and templates even with `--no-assets`; attachments,
documents, exports, images, the default workspace and the operator's own
files otherwise. It was five hand-listed folders, so the workers, the
workspace and everything the agent wrote into the data dir stayed behind.
The import asks the same question of every name the bundle holds (a bundle
cannot plant `install_id`, backups or a database), keeps a target file it
replaces in `.migrate-backup-<ts>/files/`, and fails on a file it could not
restore; an export that could not read a file records it and `verify`
refuses the bundle.

**Key files:**
- `migration/bundle.py` — `Manifest`, `KazmaBundle`, `verify()`, `sha256_file`
- `migration/path_rewrite.py` — `PathMap`, `build_path_map`, `rewrite_paths_in_sqlite`
- `migration/vault_pairing.py` — `check_vault_key`, `sync_vault_key`
- `migration/exporter.py` — `export_bundle()`
- `migration/importer.py` — `import_bundle()`, `ImportReport`
- `kazma-cli/kazma_cli/migrate.py` — CLI dispatch (`kazma migrate export|verify|import`)
- `memory/backup.py:backup_one()` — the WAL-safe SQLite copier reused by the
  importer's pre-swap safety backup (promoted from `_backup_one`).
- Document store export/import is also wired — see §19 F3 and
  `migration/exporter.py`. What travels follows where the document CATALOG is
  (`documents.backup.installed_document_backends`: the running service, else
  the configured backends, so the CLI sees a Postgres store too): a SQLite
  catalog as `documents.db` + the content it references; a Postgres catalog as
  `data/postgres.dump` + every content file it references (copied after the
  dump: a superset); a Postgres catalog beside a SQLite queue is refused by
  name. The export records a refusal or a missing referenced file under
  `_document_store`, and `verify` refuses the bundle. A document restore that
  fails on import fails the import (2026-10-13, DOC-A7/A8).

### 19. Document Intelligence (`kazma-core/kazma_core/documents/`)

Durable document platform (phases 0–10), hardened 2026-10-13 against the
Documents audit (tracker `docs/plans/DOCUMENTS_INDUSTRIAL_HARDENING_GOAL.md`,
F01–F10 / Q01–Q05; an independent review and the 48–72 h soak are still
open, and the default `process` worker profile is not qualified for hostile
documents, E). Docs SoT:
`docs/docs/guide/document-intelligence.md`, phases
`docs/docs/guide/document-phases.md`, security
`docs/docs/security/document-security.md`, ops
`docs/docs/ops/document-processing.md`.

**A. Two boundaries — do not invent a third path.**
- **Durable public boundary:** `DocumentIngestionService` — Web
  `/api/documents/*` (`documents_api.py`), native `document-platform` tools,
  gateway `/documents`/`/docs`, TUI `DocumentsPanel` (through the Web API).
  Tenant/actor ACL, capacity, audit, jobs, index.
- **Execution boundary:** `DocumentService` — sniff/parse/OCR/render inside
  an isolated worker (a bounded subprocess, or a per-job container: E).
  Durable workers call it; chat
  `agent_handler/attachments.py` may call it for **transient** fenced excerpts
  only (not a second durable store).
- Gateway/UI **must not** import `documents.parsers`, `documents.ocr`,
  `documents.renderers`, `parser_worker`, `mutation_worker`, etc.

**B. Job state machine (canonical).**
`received → quarantined → validating → ready_to_parse|ocr_required →
parsing|ocr_running → normalizing → indexing → verifying → ready`
(+ `retry_wait`, `rejected`, `cancelled`, `dead_letter`). Do not reintroduce
generic PENDING/ACCEPTED/PROCESSING labels in product code or docs.

**B2. Intake admission is durable; a partial publication is undone only by
its owner or after its owner is PROVEN dead.**
`documents/admission.py` reserves pending queue and tenant rate/byte budgets in
the job backend before durable ingestion reads bytes. SQLite uses a short
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; Postgres locks the one `document_intake_mutex` row
(`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`). No DB lock is held
during streaming. Declared lengths are enforced before CAS publication; unknown
lengths reserve the intake maximum and reconcile actual bytes. Replay is checked
before fresh admission. Retries reserve a slot and require write ACL on a live
document. A published job closes its reservation. Since 2026-10-13 every
reservation records its OWNER (install, host, pid, process start time) and,
before any metadata write, the ids it publishes under; the rows it creates
carry its `intake_token`. A failed intake rolls its own rows back
(`_abandon_own_intake`). At start and every minute while the workers run
(`_sweep_stranded_intakes`), `_recover_stranded_intakes` claims (CAS) and
rolls back intakes whose owner is provably dead (same install and host, pid
gone or reused) or restored from a backup. An owner that cannot be proven dead
(another host, an unreadable process) holds a LEASE: it renews
`heartbeat_epoch` every quarter of its own `lease_seconds`
(`documents.intake.lease_seconds`, default 300, stored on the row) while the
intake runs, and is taken over only once that has lapsed. The takeover FENCES
it: `jobs.enqueue(intake_fence=)` creates the publishing job only in a
transaction that finds the reservation still active and still the caller's,
under the admission mutex the claim also takes, and a claim refuses a
reservation whose job exists. A fenced owner removes the rows tagged with its
token (`_discard_tagged`) and answers `intake_taken_over` (409); the sweep
removes what a fenced owner wrote and left, for a day after the takeover
(`fenced_epoch`). A legacy row (no owner or no heartbeat: a build without the
fence) is never taken over and is reported (`stranded`, readiness
`document_intake_reservations_stranded`; a remote intake renewing its lease is
not stranded). Never add age-only expiry without the fence. The Web route
answers every budget BEFORE reading the body (`precheck_upload`; F08 below).
Gates: `tests/test_document_admission_hardening.py`,
`tests/test_document_crash_recovery.py` (a real child killed after each of 7
intake stages and inside 4 job stages, SQLite and real Postgres),
`tests/test_document_intake_lease.py` (a real child on "another host",
paused, taken over and resumed; without the fence it publishes over the
takeover, without the sweep its rows stay), the real-Postgres races in
`tests/test_document_jobs_pg_idempotency.py`, and the opt-in
`tests/test_document_intake_lease_containers.py`
(`KAZMA_TEST_CONTAINER_LEASE_DRILL_IMAGE`): the stale owner in a real other
container -- frozen with `docker pause`, or cut off the network -- is taken
over on the database's clock and fenced when it returns; with its renewals
blind the fence alone refuses it; blind and unfenced it publishes (control).
**A stop waits for the sweep, and this process's own leftovers are taken
back** (2026-11-08, the drill VM's 48-hour soak, which restarts the service
in one process). The sweep's pass runs in a thread, and cancelling its task
did not stop it: `close()` took the database away under it ("could not be
rolled back (ProgrammingError)"), and the intake it had just claimed named
this process as owner, so every later sweep here skipped it as running until
the process exited. `stop_workers` now sets the sweep's stop flag and waits
for the pass (`wait_then_cancel`, 30 s), which stops between intakes; and
`admission.is_live` -- the tokens `reserve` hands out until `finish`, and the
one a sweep is rolling back (`holding`) -- tells an intake this process is
working on from one it left: a "self" owner not live is rolled back like a
dead one. Gate: `tests/test_document_intake_sweep_stop.py` (the old stop and
the old "self is always running" rule as controls).

**B3. Admission, scratch and claims are bounded and fair** (2026-10-13, F08).
The Web upload refuses a declared length past the limit, a disabled platform,
a disk whose free space minus the incoming file is below the floor, a full
queue, a tenant cap or a spent rate window before reading a byte, and holds
one of `documents.capacity.max_concurrent_uploads` spool slots (per process)
while receiving. Spools, staged copies and parser/operation run directories
live under the storage root: the floor measures them and GC sweeps what a
crash left (`retention._sweep_scratch`). A worker stage below the floor is
retried (`storage_full`), never started. Postgres metadata enforces the tenant
blob quota (an advisory lock per tenant serializes check and insert). Claims
are fair across tenants (`jobs.fair_claim_order`: fewest running first, then
by when the job became ready, so a retry does not jump the queue), on both
backends. The ten JSON routes (`/import`, `/generate`, `/merge`, `/convert`,
`/split`, `/fill-form`, `/redact`, `/index`, `/unindex`, `/search`) read their
body through `documents_api._json_body`: a declared length past 2 MiB is
refused unread, an undeclared one is cut off at the cap, malformed or
too-deep JSON is a 422. FastAPI's `Body(...)` parsed any size into memory
before a route could look at it; never take a document route's body that way.
Gates: `tests/test_document_upload_admission.py` (body-read counter,
the old route as its control), `tests/test_document_claim_fairness.py`,
`tests/test_document_quota_both_backends.py`,
`tests/test_document_json_body_cap.py` (`Body(...)` as its control).

**B4. Every job read names its caller** (2026-10-13, F05). `job_status`,
`job_events`, `jobs_for_document`, `cancel_job` and `retry_job` take a required
`actor_id`; `ingestion.SYSTEM_ACTOR` (not a string) is for code that already
authorized the read. A missing actor is refused -- it used to mean "no check".
An unreadable job reads exactly like an unknown one on the Web routes, the
agent's tools and the gateway (no existence oracle; a replay by another actor
is `idempotency_conflict`). `/api/documents/ops/audit` is admin-only. A
nameless caller is refused before the lookup, whether or not the job exists,
and cancelling needs write access, as a retry does (2026-10-15, the Q04
defensive check: read was enough). Gate:
`tests/test_document_job_read_matrix.py` (signature gate with its control).

**B4b. The asker, in the asker's space** (Spaces S1-12, 2026-11-18; it
replaced DOC-A3's one stand-in principal, `operator`). A document's tenant is
its space and its owner the account that ingested it. The page, chat
`/documents` and the agent's tools ask one function,
`documents.principal.surface_scope`, and act as the scope's asker: Spaces
enforced, the bound scope (its asker must be a member; none bound refuses,
`NO_SPACE_REFUSAL`); one operator, the owner's account in the bound tenant;
platform users without Spaces (the older multi-user mode), as before -- the
page acts as each user's name, chat and the agent refuse
(`MULTI_USER_REFUSAL`, D1). Members of a space share it:
`DocumentIngestionService.grant_member_access` gives the asker an `owner` ACL
row on the space's documents it lacks (granted by each document's owner,
audited `grant_member`, ownership unchanged, re-checked at most once a minute
per space and member, at once after a new document in this process); that is
also how documents made before Spaces (owned by `operator`, `auto-cookie`,
`agent`) reach the owner's account, with no step to run. The grant is made
through the built service: the agent's tools build it first
(`_ensure_service`, then `_scope(svc)`), so the first call of a process, or
of a turn during boot, already reads them. Chat `/documents` reads the tenant
its own turns run in (`_chat_document_scope`: memory's
`resolve_tenant_id`, the one the turn's state and the agent's tools carry):
with a retired memory mode stored, `telegram` or the sender, until Spaces is
enforced or the owner presses "Use one memory" (S1-09's rule); a rule that
cannot be read (a settings outage) means the owner's space, as before, with
a WARNING. The run
supervisor's buttons use `owner_actor` (the owner's account,
single-operator only) until S1-21. `surface_scope`, `owner_actor` and
`grant_member_access` are loop-stall helpers. No surface passes a literal
actor. Gates: `tests/test_document_spaces.py` (one real intake through the
page and the agent, seeded documents for the rest; the old `agent`
principal resolved through the tool's own scope path, older documents with
no grant, a grant through the installed service during boot, the first
chat rule on a retired memory mode and a literal actor as controls), the
matrix's Documents cases (`tests/_document_space_cases.py`).

**B4c. Each space's files in its own folder, once Spaces is enforced**
(Spaces S1-12). A space's folder is `storage.space_folder` (the root for the
owner's space, so an install's documents never move; `spaces/<id>` for any
other). Content is read and written only through
`ContentAddressedStorage.for_space(tenant)` (`SpaceStorage`); the
install-level object has no content call.
- **Before enforcement nothing changes** (`storage.writes_folder`): every
  tenant writes to the root, as before Spaces -- the older multi-user mode's
  tenants and a retired memory mode's (`telegram`) too -- so a chat finds its
  documents where it always did, a backup has the shape it always had, and an
  older build reads every file. Once enforced, each space writes to its own
  folder.
- **Reads look in both places** (`storage.blob_rels` / `manifest_rels`): the
  space's folder, then the root.
- **The root keeps every tenant's files in this release** (a revert reads the
  root only): GC's root folder keeps every live reference of any tenant (its
  recheck asks any tenant; a catalog row with no tenant name is kept there
  too), and `spaces/<f>` keeps only its own tenants'
  (`repository.gc_marks_from_rows` gives references per tenant,
  `gc_is_live_reference(tenant_ids=)`). Removing a copied space's root copies
  is a later step, after S1-33.
- **The copy** (`documents.space_files.copy_into_space_folders`, at start,
  only while enforced) checks every tenant at every start and copies what a
  space's folder lacks, a file an older build wrote during a revert included.
  Journal `.space-files.json`: `copying` recorded before, `moved` after; each
  file digest-checked and renamed into place; a stop or crash resumes. A
  reference whose id names no file, a tenant with no name, a file that cannot
  be read or does not match its digest is a WARNING and the copy goes on
  (an ERROR at every start would trip the deploy's log check).
- **Backups and the export record each file where the live store keeps it**
  (`backup._held_rel`, `backup_pg.held_paths`); a verify accepts either place.
  So a backup taken before enforcement has the old shape; one taken after
  holds `spaces/...` paths, which an older build cannot verify. An import
  drops the journal (the next start re-checks).
Gate: `tests/test_document_space_files.py` (a store writing the space folders
before enforcement, one folder for every tenant once enforced, and the first
collector that let the root forget a copied tenant, as controls).

**B6. One status per error code** (2026-10-13, DOC-A4/A9).
`documents_api._STATUS_BY_CODE` answers every route: writes off, an unavailable
required scanner and `worker_isolation_*` are 503 with `Retry-After`
everywhere (writes-off was 422 on the action routes; the scanner 400). The
upload precheck asks `malware_blocks_intake` before reading the body. Every
body goes through the 2 MiB reader (`_json_body`, `_optional_json_body` for
delete); no route calls `request.json()`/`body()`/`form()`. Gates:
`tests/test_document_api_statuses.py`, `tests/test_document_json_body_cap.py`.

**B5. Outages are retried; only content is rejected** (2026-10-13, F07). A
required malware scanner that is unavailable, a full disk (`storage_full`), a
locked or unreachable metadata store (`metadata_unavailable`, SQLite or
Postgres: `errors.infrastructure_errors`) go to the queue's finite retry
budget, then dead-letter -- never REJECTED. (At upload, a required scanner
that cannot run refuses the upload with `malware_scanner_unavailable`; nothing
is published.) A store error while recording a
stage's outcome leaves the job leased for lease recovery and never ends the
worker loop. Gate: `tests/test_document_fault_transitions.py` (old handling as
the negative-control witness).

**C. Config is ConfigStore-nested.** Primary keys are
`documents.intake.*`, `documents.limits.*`, `documents.ocr.*`,
`documents.workers.*`, `documents.capacity.*`, `documents.retention.*`,
`documents.gc.*`, `documents.security.*`, `documents.indexing.*`,
`documents.quotas.*`, `documents.render.*` and `documents.storage_root`, plus
rollout `documents.enabled` / `shadow` / `default_authoritative`. Prefer
`get_document_config()` live reads. Legacy aliases exist for a few keys only
(`documents.intake_max_bytes` / `intake_max_files`,
`documents.worker.lease_seconds` / `max_retries`,
`documents.shadow_mode`, `documents.authoritative_by_default`,
`documents.limits.max_uncompressed_bytes`) — do not invent
`documents.max_pages` style flat keys without wiring aliases. A default
coordinator captures one strict immutable policy per operation
from `ConfigStore.snapshot("documents")` (one SELECT, no per-key TTL). Share its
`DocumentPolicy` with execution, render, capacity, knowledge and GC layers; never
refresh a shared mutable config during an operation. Explicit configs stay fixed.
Worker tasks must detach startup's ContextVar and capture again per stage.
Unavailable/invalid live policy refuses execution; rollout never enables writes
on a settings outage. Remote parsing still checks live denial before each upload.
Storage root, committed-reference quota, worker concurrency/lease/heartbeat and
queue retry timing are constructed-resource settings: pin them until coordinator
reconstruction and report configured/effective differences in readiness `policy`.
Intake version metadata and parsed manifests record the effective policy hash.
Backup/migration resolve the installed CAS root (`get_document_storage_root`),
never a pending proposed root, and offline resolution does not create a service.
Backup and migration take their path from where the catalog is
(`backup.installed_document_backends`, F3); a fallback SQLite database never
stands in for a Postgres catalog.
A new document Postgres table goes in `db.pg_backup.KAZMA_PG_TABLES` (gate:
`tests/test_pg_backup.py::test_kazma_pg_tables_covers_document_ddl`, which reads
the DDL) AND in `backup_pg.DOCUMENT_PG_TABLES` (gate since 2026-10-13, DOC-A13:
`tests/test_document_pg_tables.py`, the DDL and a started store on real
Postgres, both directions). The Postgres store's backup and restore are F2;
RPO/RTO on deployment hardware and store sizes remain open.
Every `DocumentConfig` field has a reader outside `config.py` (DOC-A2: eight
settings were read, validated and acted on by nothing -- `fence_llm_content`,
`allow_encrypted_documents`, `allow_external_render_resources` among them --
and were removed; none was shipped in kazma.yaml, so no stored default to
retire). Gate: `tests/test_document_config_fields_read.py`.
Gates: `tests/test_document_live_policy.py`, `tests/test_config_store_snapshot.py`.

**D. Multi-replica honesty.**
`jobs_pg.py` can claim jobs with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` when
Postgres is configured. The job queue is on Postgres whenever Kazma's backend
is (`KAZMA_DOCUMENTS_JOBS_BACKEND=sqlite` keeps it local). Document
**metadata** (documents/versions/blobs) follows the job backend when
`KAZMA_DOCUMENTS_METADATA_BACKEND` is unset or `auto` -- so it is on Postgres
by default on a Postgres install -- `postgres` forces `repository_pg.py` and
`sqlite` keeps SQLite; either Postgres store needs the pool up. Readiness
must report single-replica for metadata **whenever the SQLite backend is
active** — never claim multi-replica HA from the availability of the Postgres
path alone, only from the backend actually in use. Single-replica is a
fact, not a degradation: `status` is `degraded` only when a configured
backend is not the one serving (`*_fell_back_to_sqlite`); a SQLite backend
chosen in `.env` is `ready` with `metadata_multi_replica: false`
(`tests/test_document_operations_phase9.py::test_readiness_status_means_a_configured_backend_is_serving`).
The live Documents page said "Storage: degraded" in red over a deliberate
SQLite choice (2026-09-28).

**E. Fence + security honesty.**
LLM-visible document text goes through untrusted fences
(`source="document"` or chat `document_attachment`), the document intent
handler's "reorganize this document" prompt included (it put it in raw
until 2026-10-15; the unreached document pipeline was removed 2026-10-27,
audit AUD-075; `tests/test_document_text_fenced_to_model.py`,
the unfenced prompt as control). Auto-index is **off** by
default. Redaction UI confirm is Web-only; API/tools can redact under ACL.
**Malware:** `documents/malware.py` runs on quarantine via
`scan_if_configured` (`auto`/`on`/`off` + fail-closed). Uses system
`clamscan`/`clamdscan` only — no third-party upload of document bytes.
Sandbox, `KAZMA_DOCUMENT_WORKER_ISOLATION=process` (default): scrubbed env;
Windows Job Object memory/CPU-rate/process limits with fail-closed parser
start -- the worker starts SUSPENDED and is resumed only once the job holds it
(DOC-A12, 2026-10-13: a venv's `python.exe` is a launcher, and a job assigned
a moment late held only the launcher, so the first run of every process ran
uncapped while reporting "enforced"); the CPU cap is `cpu_cores=1`, sized by
`security.process_budget.job_cpu_rate` (CpuRate is a share of the WHOLE
machine: the old 100*100 was no cap). Every Job Object assignment in product
code holds a suspended child (gate `tests/test_job_objects_hold_suspended_children.py`,
`code_exec` too; busy-worker and memory-hog measurements with the old launch
as controls in `tests/test_document_sandbox.py`); Unix memory/CPU-time
`setrlimit` (no process-count limit). It confines
no filesystem/network access; readiness says `hostile_document_profile:
unqualified`. `container` (2026-10-13): both worker call sites (service
parser, operations mutation/renderer) branch to
`worker_container.run_container_worker` -> the broker
(`documents/worker_broker.py`, stdlib-only), the ONLY holder of the Docker
socket -- never mount it into Kazma. One container per job under one fixed
policy (no network/mounts, read-only root, tmpfs, cgroup limits, caps
dropped, uid 10001); the broker attests it from inside the image before
serving -- the exact uid and gid and an empty capability bounding set too
(2026-10-15: any non-root uid passed, and the bounding set was read and never
checked). Inputs/outputs are digest-checked bundles (`worker_bundle.py`); the
output is untrusted. No fallback to `process`; an invalid mode refuses every
run; a crash with no stream is `parser_result_missing`, as locally. Never
block the output pump on a kill: an attached container whose stdout backs up
cannot be killed (Docker 29). In container mode the four readiness factories
(`get_parser_registry`, `get_renderer_registry`, `get_mutation_registry`,
`get_ocr_health`) answer from the image's own capability report, as live
views, never from host packages; the broker refuses to serve without it. A
broker that is not ready answers the retryable `worker_isolation_unavailable`
(a full one `worker_isolation_busy`), never a permanent engine error. The
image reports a fingerprint of its document code: readiness says
`image_code_matches: false` and `document_worker_image_outdated` when the
image was built from other code than Kazma runs (rebuild it:
`scripts/document_worker_image.py build`; the guard's broker switches by
itself, E1). The image carries no Docling and no httpx: local salvage is not part
of the container profile, and remote parsing stays in the Kazma process (K).
It carries the neural OCR engine (G4) and its models: the `ocr-models` build
stage (hash-locked `deploy/document-worker/ocr-models.txt`, CPU PyTorch) runs
`scripts/ocr_models.py install`, only `/models` reaches the final image
(`KAZMA_OCR_MODEL_DIR=/opt/kazma/ocr-models`, read-only, verified at build),
and `parser_container_request` points the parse at that copy -- the host's
model directory is never sent. The capability report names both OCR engines
(`ocr.engines`); an older image's report without them reads neural as absent.
**The image's locks keep up with Kazma's own** (2026-11-11): the engines'
direct pins (`deploy/document-worker/requirements.in`) are versions `uv.lock`
holds, and no package either hash lock holds is below a floor pyproject.toml
declares or a recorded advisory's fix; the engines hold no httpx, Docling or
torch. The locks had kept Pillow 12.3.0, pypdf 6.19.0, brotli 1.2.0 and, in
the build stage, filelock 3.32.3 and setuptools 83.0.0 -- 72 advisories --
after Kazma's own environment had moved past each. Gate:
`tests/test_document_worker_locks.py` (the old locks as the control). A new
lock needs the image rebuilt.
`security.execution.container_required` refuses the `process` profile
(`worker_isolation_required`; unreadable policy refuses too) -- checked where
Kazma starts a worker, never inside one. Gates:
`tests/test_document_worker_container.py`; real Docker
(`KAZMA_TEST_DOCUMENT_WORKER_IMAGE`, CI job `Document worker container
profile`): `tests/test_document_worker_container_docker.py`.
Rendering engines: a readiness probe imports exactly what its render path
uses -- WeasyPrint 70 (the locked floor) removed `default_url_fetcher`, and
every HTML->PDF job failed while the engine read "ready". The renderer's
fetcher (a `URLFetcher` subclass) allows only `data:` and files inside the
approved asset folder (`tests/test_weasyprint_renderer.py`). Every LibreOffice
call goes through `binaries.run_soffice_cli`, which kills the whole process
tree on timeout and bounds the last wait: `subprocess.run(timeout=)` waited
without a limit for the pipes soffice.bin still held and hung the
certification, and the legacy Office parser still called it that way until
2026-10-15 (`tests/test_soffice_call_bounded.py`: the old call as its control,
the legacy parser, and a gate -- no product module naming LibreOffice starts a
process itself, two probes of other programs declared).

**E1. Which profile runs is the admin's setting; the guard runs the broker**
(2026-10-15). Live that day: the install required containers, documents ran
in `process`, no broker ran -- the container profile needed three `.env`
lines and a hand-run process -- and every document was refused.
- **One answer for the profile** (`worker_container.worker_isolation_mode` /
  `isolation_selection`): `KAZMA_DOCUMENT_WORKER_ISOLATION` wins when set
  (the environment's floor); else the setting
  `security.execution.document_worker_isolation` (`process`/`container`,
  Settings -> Documents, `PUT /api/settings/documents` `worker_isolation`,
  validated by `settings_validation`); none saved is `process`. Under
  `security.` so `config_save` refuses it, and a restore never changes it
  (`KEY_RULES` credential class: an older backup must not move documents out
  of containers). An unreadable setting refuses (`document_policy_unavailable`),
  never guesses `process`.
- **A worker never reads settings**: every worker entry point (`main` of the
  parser, mutation and renderer workers, and `worker_entry`) calls
  `worker_process.mark()` first, and the profile is then `process` (its own
  engines). The local profile scrubs the worker's environment, so a settings
  read there would open the default data folder's store. A new worker entry
  point marks itself (`test_every_worker_entry_point_marks_itself_first`).
- **Kazma asks the guard** (`documents/broker_supervision.py`): it writes
  `want` and the broker URL it uses to `KAZMA_GUARD_BROKER_REQUEST_FILE` --
  at boot (`start_broker_requests`, in a thread), on a profile change (a
  ConfigStore change listener that publishes on a retained thread of its own,
  `_drain_publishes`) and on the maintenance sweep "document worker broker";
  only when the decision changed. An unreadable profile leaves the request
  standing. A URL that is not the guard's (a `.env` broker) means the guard
  runs none. Readiness reads the guard's record back (`supervisor_report`:
  `guard`, `old_guard` -- `document_broker` missing from `guard_features` --,
  `external`, `none`).
- **One step that fixes it**: `worker_isolation.action` (`isolation_action`)
  is a `code` the pages word from the catalog (`documents.isolation_action.*`),
  an English `message` and the `command` to run; the Documents page shows it,
  Settings -> Documents offers *Use the container profile* when the install
  requires containers. Never tell the owner to edit `.env` for what a setting
  decides.
- **The image is named by its build inputs** (`documents/worker_image.py`,
  stdlib-only, loaded by the guard by path): the Dockerfile, its
  `.dockerignore`, the requirements and every file of `kazma_core` the build
  context sends, CRLF-insensitive -> `kazma-document-worker:src-<16 hex>`.
  `test_the_tag_covers_exactly_what_the_build_sends` holds the walk to the
  `.dockerignore`. `scripts/document_worker_image.py build` builds and labels
  it (`io.kazma.document-worker-image.source` / `.documents-code`); never make
  a boot build an image. A build then removes the builds of other code
  (`_prune_older`, `--no-prune` keeps them): this code's, what the broker
  serves or asks for, the newest other one (a revert finds it) and one a
  job's container still uses are kept, a refused removal is said and never
  fails the build. Every build used to stay, one per deploy: 34 (about 7.7
  GB) on the live engine by 2026-11-14 (`tests/test_document_worker_image.py`,
  `--no-prune` as the control). The broker serves the newest labelled build while
  the tag asked for is missing (`--fallback-to-newest-built`, status
  `image_fallback`/`image_source`) and exits 6 to switch, idle, once it
  appears. Readiness: `image_current: false` or `image_fallback` is
  `document_worker_image_outdated`; one ops alert per build
  (`documents.worker_image_outdated`, stamped
  `system.documents.worker_image_alerted`).
- **Broker exit codes** are the guard's vocabulary: 2 cannot start, 3 policy or
  no engines, 4 no image (`_NoWorkerImageError`), 5 no Docker engine
  (`_DockerEngineUnavailableError`, `check_engine` first), 6 newer image, 7 the
  TCP address cannot be listened on (a test bind, first, before attesting). The
  broker handles the guard's CTRL_BREAK (SIGBREAK) and SIGTERM, also while it
  attests, and removes its job containers on the way out.
Gates: `tests/test_document_worker_profile.py`, `tests/test_document_worker_image.py`
(the CTRL_BREAK stop with an unhandled one as control),
`tests/test_guard_document_broker.py`; real Docker (opt-in
`KAZMA_TEST_DOCUMENT_WORKER_IMAGE`): `tests/test_document_broker_guard_docker.py`.

**E2. A deleted document is never still searchable** (2026-09-28).
`DocumentService.delete_document` takes the document out of every library
that holds it (`DocumentKnowledgeAdapter.libraries_holding`, the one answer,
also shown on the Documents page) BEFORE the tombstone; a library it cannot
leave stops the delete (`document_unindex_failed`, naming the library) so a
retry can finish it. It used to swallow the failure and archive a document
chat could still quote. The whole sequence, from reading the libraries to the
tombstone, holds the document's publication lock (an index published in
between survived the delete), and with no knowledge adapter (Knowledge failed
to start) a document the store records as indexed is not deleted (it was
tombstoned and stayed searchable; 2026-10-15).
`tests/test_document_library_membership.py`.

**E3. One PDF active-content policy, applied only inside the worker**
(2026-10-13, F01). `documents/pdf_policy.assert_pdf_safe` walks the object
graph (not page streams or extracted text), bounded at 100,000 objects and
depth 128, and refuses script (JavaScript, XFA), actions that run, open,
submit or fetch outside the document (Launch, remote GoTo, SubmitForm,
ImportData, renditions, rich media, sound, movie), embedded files (a bare
`/EF` without `/Type` too) and links that are not absolute http, https or
mailto (`file:`, UNC and relative targets leak credentials when opened).
A `/GoTo` or `/Thread` with an `/F` file specification is a remote go-to by
another spelling and is refused too (Q04 FIND-01, 2026-10-15: the independent
review found it passed as navigation). Action and key names are matched
case-insensitively (OBS-02), as the sniffer's regex is. Navigation inside the
document and web links stay. A graph it cannot read, or
one past its budget, is refused, never passed. It runs on intake (`sniff`), on
every mutation input and output (redaction opened its source before the
policy until 2026-10-13) and on every PDF Kazma renders (LibreOffice,
WeasyPrint, ReportLab), always in the worker. No PDF library opens a PDF in
the server process: the document intent handler reads through
`DocumentService` (a removed pipeline used to fall back to fitz exactly
when the worker had refused a file), and structural preflight and
local salvage run in the worker too. Gates:
`tests/test_pdf_openers_stay_in_workers.py` (any PDF-library opener outside
the worker-side modules fails, except declared checks of a PDF Kazma itself
just generated; the old reader as its control), `tests/test_document_pdf_policy.py`
(real inert PDFs: each denial, navigation and web links kept, shared indirect
`/URI`, the call-site matrix through the real worker),
`tests/test_document_worker_preflight.py`.

**F. Multi-replica backends.**
Jobs: `jobs_pg.py` when Postgres. Metadata: `repository_pg.py` when the
metadata backend resolves to Postgres (D) and the pool is up. GC is
backend-agnostic: `retention._mark` dispatches to `repository.gc_mark`, which
both backends implement, so mark/sweep runs on Postgres metadata -- in fact
only since 2026-11 (FA-205): the Postgres mark read its rows by position and
failed every pass (`repository_pg._cell` reads by name), and an install whose
catalog is SQLite sweeps the orphan rows a Postgres catalog left
(`retention._sweep_idle_catalog`). The old
`gc_postgres_metadata_sql_port_pending` skip is gone and
`tests/test_leftovers_except_g.py` asserts it stays gone. Audit works on both
backends.

**F2. A Postgres store is backed up as ONE point in time** (2026-10-13, F06).
`documents/backup_pg.py`: a REPEATABLE READ transaction exports its snapshot,
reads the blob/manifest references inside it, PINS them (`.backup-pins`; GC
re-reads pins before each delete), and `pg_dump --snapshot` dumps the document
tables while that transaction stays open; the files are copied with
checksums. The scheduled document backup takes this path whenever the
installed store is on Postgres. A restore goes only into an EMPTY database and
storage root, re-checks every table's row count against the snapshot, expires
the dead source's leases and marks its unfinished intakes `restored` (rolled
back at start). The knowledge index is a separate store (library chunks in
the settings store, vectors in Chroma): restore reports `reindex_required`,
and every worker start runs `DocumentIngestionService.reconcile_index` once,
which re-publishes each version the store records as indexed but no library
holds, from its own manifest, as the owner, through `index_document_ir`. Each
is re-checked under the document's publication lock
(`DocumentKnowledgeAdapter.publication_lock`, striped per tenant and
document; index and unindex hold it), so an unindex is never undone. A
missing library, a superseded version or a missing manifest is reported,
never invented; chunks the store does not record are reported and removed
only with `index --apply --prune`. Operator: `scripts/document_pg_backup.py`
(`backup`, `verify`, `restore`, `index`). Gates:
`tests/test_document_pg_backup_restore.py` (real Postgres, private databases;
a dump outside the snapshot is caught by the row-count check),
`tests/test_document_backup_pins.py`, `tests/test_document_reindex_after_restore.py`
(both backends; without the re-check an unindex is undone), and the opt-in
`tests/test_document_pg_restore_drill_scale.py` (`KAZMA_TEST_RESTORE_DRILL_DOCUMENTS`).

**F3. Backup, export and import follow the CATALOG** (2026-10-13, DOC-A6/A7/A8).
`backup.installed_document_backends()` is the one answer: the running
service's repositories, else the configured backends (a CLI has no service;
asking only the service exported a Postgres store as its empty local
`documents.db`). Postgres catalog -> coordinated backup (F2); its files travel
in a migration bundle, the catalog in `data/postgres.dump`. SQLite catalog
beside a Postgres queue -> the SQLite snapshot, with quarantine->originals
promotions read from the queue after the snapshot and kept in the manifest
(`promoted_versions`, read again by `verify_document_backup`); the jobs
backend alone used to pick the coordinated backup, which read a catalog that
was not there. Postgres catalog beside a SQLite queue (a fallback) ->
`UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE`, by name. Backups are written under a `.…partial` name
and renamed when complete. A failed document restore fails `kazma migrate
import`. Restoring BOTH Postgres backups into one database: the whole-database
dump first, then `restore --replace-document-tables` (drops the dump's older
document tables only after the backup verifies and the storage root is empty).
Gates: `tests/test_document_backup_shapes.py`,
`tests/test_document_pg_restore_order.py` (both wrong orders as controls),
`tests/test_document_backup_restore_hardening.py`.

**F4. The Postgres audit is append-only too** (2026-10-13, DOC-A1). Trigger
`document_audit_guard` (function `kazma_document_audit_guard`) refuses every
UPDATE and every DELETE outside a transaction the retention prune marks
(`SET LOCAL kazma.document_audit_prune`); the prune runs in bounded batches on
Postgres (it called the SQLite connection, `None` there, and the table grew
forever). `pg_dump -t` carries a trigger but not its function: every restore
creates `db/pg_backup.KAZMA_PG_FUNCTIONS` first, and any trigger function in
product code must be declared there. Gate: `tests/test_document_audit_pg.py`
(old prune, no trigger and no function step as controls).

**G. Certification.**
`scripts/certify_documents.py` (`documents/certification.py`) +
`tests/test_document_certification_phase10.py` + `hostile_corpus.py` /
committed `tests/fixtures/documents/hostile_manifest.json`. Keep CLI gates and
pytest groups honest (architecture/a11y/crash matrix are pytest). The report
runs what it names: the hostile corpus, a bounded performance smoke, engine
readiness, rollout, the isolation profile configured NOW (`process` is
CONDITIONAL and never reported as confined; `container` passes only attested
and with a current image), the fidelity corpus (G2) and a real SQLite backup,
verify and restore. Postgres multi-replica, metadata multi-replica, a 48-72 h
soak and an external security review are NOT RUN, `default_ready` stays
false, and `--soak` is an extended smoke, never a soak
(`tests/test_document_certification_honesty.py`). The soak harness is
`scripts/document_soak.py` (Q03: private SQLite stores unless `--use-env`,
restarts and killed intakes, fails on a job left unfinished, a reservation
left pending or scratch left behind); a two-minute pilot is not the soak.

**G2. Fidelity is measured on a versioned corpus** (2026-10-13, F09/Q02).
`documents/fidelity.py` builds EN/AR/bilingual cases with Kazma's own engines
(DOCX, PDF, HTML, OCR from a rasterized page) from a ground-truth spec and
measures the real parser: word recall, segment recall, order, exact numbers,
table cells, page honesty, alignment, CER/WER, punctuation. Floors and release targets are
declared per corpus version in `tests/fixtures/documents/fidelity_thresholds.json`;
the `qualified` list must match the measurement. Change the corpus = bump
`CORPUS_VERSION` and re-lock (`scripts/document_fidelity.py --lock`, which
never lowers a floor within a version). Version 2 adds long documents (EN/AR,
many pages), two columns from another producer (MuPDF Story), wide wrapping
tables and a degraded scan. A segment counts as recovered only when its
words come back together (`_SPAN_SLACK`): words in order but interleaved with
another column are not. Alignment judges every line that shows its side
against its segment's direction by `arabic.direction_of`, the engines' own
per-block rule. Version 3 adds `*-ocr-table`, an OCR page with its ruled
table; the OCR reference text is the whole page, table included. Version 4
(2026-10-15) puts the page furniture the renderer drew (the Arabic route's
brand footer, read from the rendered PDF: `_drawn_furniture`) into the OCR
reference: without it a perfect reading scored CER 0.114 on `ar-ocr`. The OCR
cases are measured per engine (`fidelity.OCR_ENGINES`: `tesseract`,
`neural`), each with its own floors and `qualified` list under
`ocr_engines.<engine>`; a case another engine read (a fallback) fails the
test and is refused by `--lock`, and a lock keeps the floors of an engine not
installed where it runs. Version 5 (same day) measures `punctuation`: each
ground-truth word's following marks against the marks after the word it
aligns to, where either has one (wrong, dropped and added marks are errors;
a mark inside a number is `number_recall`'s); release target 1.0. Every
other metric reads words, so the live install's "placed under review:"
passed them all. Not qualified, each with its reason in the
thresholds file: with Tesseract `ar-ocr`, `ar-ocr-table` (no Arabic-Indic
digits, lines dropped) and `en-ocr-degraded` (3.75 read as 3:75: a speck
above the decimal point; a full stop it adds mid-line). With the neural
engine every OCR case qualifies, punctuation included (G4: the speck rule,
EasyOCR's second readings, the marks and punctuation rules, the final-mark
vote). A re-lock keeps the file's `notes` and
`measured_on`: a note for a case that now qualifies is removed by hand. Certification runs the
corpus and reports the actual isolation profile and backends (F10). Gate:
`tests/test_document_fidelity.py`.

**G3. Scanned pages: tables cell by cell; real scans measured opt-in**
(2026-10-13, from a real 300 dpi copier scan of an Arabic booklet).
`ocr/tesseract._parse_tsv` reads Tesseract's TSV with `quoting=QUOTE_NONE`: a
word OCR reads as starting with `"` opened a CSV quoted field that swallowed
every later row, so a page's "text" held other rows' coordinates (one line of
14,386 characters) and lost words. `ocr/tables.py` (Pillow only) finds ruled
grids and reads each cell (`TesseractProvider.recognize_region`, psm 6/7); when
`eng` is installed, a cell with no letters, or one read below 0.5 confidence,
is read again as digits only (`eng`), and that reading wins only at
confidence >= 0.75. The page's lines inside a table become one `TABLE` block (`extractor: ocr-grid`, cells right to left
for an RTL table). Rules the scan taught, each gated with the old rule as its
control: a ruling line is ONE continuous stroke (a joined Arabic baseline is
as dark as a rule on average, and cut text lines in half); a cell is >= 3 %
of the page wide (the strips of a page border made every boxed section a
"table"); the line cut follows the page's paper (pale tinted grids). At most
600 cells and 120 s a page: past either, the tables already read are kept and
the rest keep the page's own reading; a cell that fails to read drops the
table pass for that page (`documents.ocr.tables`, default on, Settings →
Documents). Measured on the scan: a contents table's numbers 22 % -> 91 %,
its rows kept together 3 % -> 56 % complete, 6 of 6 searches on the right
page. Tesseract did not read Arabic-Indic digits in any font measured (fast or
best `ara` model, `script/Arabic` fast or best, any segmentation mode): the
installed `ara` model's character set holds one of the ten (٠) and neither
Arabic separator. The neural engine (G4) does. Gates: `tests/test_document_ocr_tables.py`,
`tests/test_document_ocr_phase5.py` (the quote with the old quoting as
control), `test_ocr_without_the_table_pass_fails_the_floor`, and the opt-in
`tests/test_document_real_scans.py` (`KAZMA_TEST_REAL_SCANS_MANIFEST`: a
manifest outside the repository names each scan by path and SHA-256, the
pages, the numbers, symbols and single terms each holds -- never page text --
the searches and the floors; without it the test skips). Since 2026-10-15
each engine is held to its own floors there (`floors_by_engine`), with a long
worker time limit so every page stays with the engine asked for.
**Every Tesseract call names its thread budget** (2026-11-13,
`ocr.tesseract._thread_limit`): `OMP_THREAD_LIMIT` is the caller's
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` (1 in the document worker), else 1. The sandbox passes a
child only the variables it names, so Tesseract started a thread per CPU it
could see (32 here) whatever the worker's CPU limit. Measured in the document
worker image (Tesseract 5.5, libgomp), eight reads four at once: 4.8-6.0 s
unlimited against 2.5-3.2 s at `--cpus=1`, 1.0 s against 0.6 s at `--cpus=4`;
never slower. Gate: `tests/test_tesseract_thread_limit.py` (through the real
sandbox; the old request, which passed no limit, as the control).

**G4. The neural OCR engine** (2026-10-15, Q02: Arabic and Arabic-Indic
digits). `documents.ocr.engine`: `auto` (default; the neural engine when its
packages and models are installed where documents are parsed, else
Tesseract), `neural` (the same, with a document warning when Tesseract read
it), `tesseract`. Validated on every write (`settings_validation`, and the
Documents settings route asks it): an engine the policy cannot read would
stop every document job. `ocr/pipeline.select_ocr_provider` is the one
choice. `ocr/neural.py` runs four models on ONNX Runtime in the document
worker, never in the Kazma process: PP-OCRv5 detection; boxes of one line
joined (gap <= 1 line height: per-word crops gave stray characters), cut to
their ink; EasyOCR `arabic_g1` reads each line (`english_g2` a line without
Arabic, and English-only pages); each word without a digit is voted on with
PaddleOCR's PP-OCRv5 Arabic recognizer and Tesseract's words on the page --
the two agreeing, or PaddleOCR at >= 0.9 alone, replace EasyOCR's word; a
number is always EasyOCR's. EasyOCR's own second reading of a letter it
doubted (>= 0.1, a letter of the same bidi class) is a reading too: another
reader that reads it makes two (the table page's "ربالأ", ب 0.74 / ي 0.26,
is Tesseract's "ريالاً"). The vote is over letters: a word's punctuation is
EasyOCR's (PaddleOCR drops a full stop), and a space read before a full
stop or comma goes (EasyOCR reads the gap a font leaves after a final ف as
one). EasyOCR writes no harakat (its Arabic list leaves them out) and draws
the tanween over an alef as a hamza ("ريالأ"): where another reader read the
same letters with harakat on that side of that letter, those stand, unless
a reader read EasyOCR's hamza too; a mark only another reader saw is never
added (Tesseract writes "الشماليٍ"). Before a line is read, ink smaller than
the line's own pen (area under half the stroke squared, no side longer than
a stroke) is removed from its box, unless it continues past the box: on the
degraded scan a speck beside the decimal point read "3.75" as "3,75"
(specks 1-3 px of area; the smallest real mark, a blurred full stop, 6). A
"," or "." between Arabic-Indic digits is put back as ٫/٬ by a number's
grammar (`arabic.arabic_number_separators`, both engines: neither EasyOCR
`arabic_g1` nor Tesseract `ara` can write those marks). A line's last mark
is two readers' (`_vote_final_mark`, after the letter vote): EasyOCR says
THAT a mark is there (it wrote one after the last word, or gave one >= 0.1
past its last character: `Reading.beyond`), Tesseract's reading of the same
word -- same folded letters -- says WHICH, when it is ONE mark; on an Arabic
line Tesseract's "," is a comma of either form (`ara` has no "،": EasyOCR's
form if it read a comma, else "،"). A mark Tesseract alone reads is never
added, none is removed, a number's own marks are never touched. English
pages read Tesseract only when a line ends in a mark to vote on. Measured
on 176 generated lines (EN/AR, clean and degraded; the live install read
"placed under review:"): English 61 -> 83 of 88 right, 22 -> 0 wrong;
Arabic 70 -> 74, 6 -> 3 wrong; 0 marks added; no probability threshold on
EasyOCR alone separates "." from ":" (the right mark second at 0.07-0.40).
Left: a mark EasyOCR reads as a letter ("!" as "l", Arabic "." as "ء") --
its own second reading there is mostly under 0.1, so no two readers agree.
Not adopted: a crop margin (EasyOCR's own 0.1 of the height) read English
line-final full stops right but added full stops to Arabic headings that
have none. A drawn line goes to logical order by
`parsers.pdf_rtl.logical_line`, never a recognizer's `get_display` (which
leaves "30-09-2026" reversed). The page pass skips the lines inside ruled
tables (`skips_table_regions`; `tables.table_regions` is `read_tables`' own
grid finder) and the page is read again in full when a table was not read
cell by cell. Near the worker's time limit (`apply_ocr(deadline=)`, 0.8 of
`documents.workers.timeout_seconds` from the parser worker's start) the
remaining pages go to Tesseract, said on the document (`tesseract_from_page`):
one core makes it ~15 s an Arabic text page, 30-45 s with ruled tables. The
digits-only cell pass keeps an English reading only at EasyOCR's own score >=
0.75 (an English reading of an Arabic-Indic number is confident by character).
Models (`ocr/neural_models.py`): every source pinned by URL, size and SHA-256
(Apache-2.0), installed by `scripts/ocr_models.py install` (EasyOCR's PyTorch
weights converted to ONNX and checked against PyTorch; without torch it
converts in a `uv run --isolated` environment) into `KAZMA_OCR_MODEL_DIR` or
`<data dir>/models/ocr` (`store_registry`: `models`, rebuilt, not backed up)
with a `manifest.json`; the worker uses them only when every file matches it.
The service tells the worker where they are (its environment is scrubbed).
Runtime packages are the `ocr` extra (onnxruntime, opencv-python-headless,
pyclipper, numpy). Measured against Tesseract, PaddleOCR (native and ONNX),
EasyOCR alone, tessdata_best and the 2-reader combinations:
`docs/plans/DOCUMENTS_INDUSTRIAL_HARDENING_GOAL.md` (Q02). Gates:
`tests/test_document_ocr_neural.py` (each rule with its control; the
end-to-end readings need the models and skip without them),
`tests/test_document_ocr_reading_rules.py` (separators, punctuation, second
readings, marks, specks, a line's last mark; the old rules as controls, and
end to end on the corpus's table page, clean page and degraded scan, the old
rules re-run on the same model outputs), `tests/test_document_fidelity.py`, `tests/test_document_real_scans.py`, and in
the image `test_the_neural_ocr_engine_reads_inside_the_container`.

**G5. A long scan is OCR'd a few pages per run; a stopped call stops its
worker** (2026-10-22: a 54-page Arabic scan sent to the chat, ~35 s a page
on one core with the neural engine). The worker takes `ocr.max_pages` and
names the rest in `ocr.deferred_pages`; `DocumentService.ocr_in_batches`
reads them in further runs, each sized from the seconds a page has taken. A
durable job reads every page (`parse_ingested_blob`, progress through
`documents/ocr_progress.py` into `job_status`'s `progress`); a tool call
(`read_with_ocr_budget`, `ocr_transient_within`) reads what fits in
`tool_ocr_budget()` and names the rest (`ocr_continuation_note`). A chat
attachment's excerpt is the text layer only (`text_layer_sync`, `ocr.disable`):
it OCR'd the whole scan for five minutes before the model saw the message.
Every async `DocumentService` worker call goes through
`documents/cancellation.run_cancellable`: a cancelled await sets the run's
cancel signal, the broker exchange closes its connection (the broker removes
the container) and the local sandbox kills the tree -- timed-out tool calls
left their OCR containers running and each retry shared the CPU with them.
Gate: `tests/test_document_ocr_batches.py` (the one-run parse, a read without
a cancel check and the old excerpt as negative controls). `document_convert` to
Word or Markdown of a document read by OCR exports that text
(`DocumentIngestionService._ocr_text_payload`), never the scan's images.
`document_convert` and `document_redact` save their artifact under
`<data dir>/documents` and name the path for `send_file`
(`document_platform/tools._saved_copy`, through `resolve_artifact_blob`'s
ACL): an `artifact_id` alone is something no agent tool takes, and the model
hunted the disk for the file and remade it (2026-10-22). Gate:
`tests/test_document_convert_saves_a_file.py`.

**H. Arabic / RTL — one module, one shaping pass, one fold.**
`documents/arabic.py` is the ONLY home for Arabic text policy. Do not
reintroduce a codepoint-block regex, a second shaping routine, or a
call-site-local normalization.

- **Direction** is decided by Unicode **bidi class** (`R`/`AL`), never by a
  block regex — the regex missed Hebrew/Syriac/Thaana/N'Ko and Arabic
  Extended-B, and counted harakat and Arabic-Indic digits as letters.
  `is_rtl_dominant` has **no** "any RTL char near the start" escape hatch; that
  clause made the threshold dead code and flipped English reports to RTL.
- **`shape_arabic` vs `rtl` are different questions.** `rtl` is "lay the page
  out right-to-left"; `shape_arabic` is "this contains complex script, a visual
  engine must shape it". `PdfEngine.render` gates the DOCX→LibreOffice route on
  **`shape_arabic`** — gating it on `rtl` stranded every mixed-language
  document on the degraded reportlab path.
- **Shape once per paragraph.** `arabic.shape_spans()` resolves bidi embedding
  levels over the whole paragraph, splits styled spans at level boundaries,
  applies UBA rule L2, and only then reshapes. Never call the shaper per
  markdown span: that reorders each fragment internally, emits them in logical
  order, and renders the sentence inside-out with the spaces eaten.
- **Search folding is applied on BOTH sides.** `fold_for_search` feeds the
  `folded` column of `knowledge_chunks_fts` at index time AND the query at
  search time (`knowledge.py:fts_search`). A fold on one side only is worse
  than none. SQLite's `unicode61` treats harakat (`Mn`) as separators, so
  vocalized Arabic indexes as single letters without this.
- **PDF lines with right-to-left script are re-read glyph by glyph**
  (`parsers/pdf_rtl.py`, 2026-10-13). PyMuPDF reverses such a line
  character by character, which turned numbers drawn left to right around
  ("١٢٣٤٥٦٧" -> "٧٦٥٤٣٢١") and swapped the letters of ligature glyphs ("في" ->
  "يف"); Arabic table cells came out fully reversed. Glyphs come from
  `page.get_texttrace` (a ligature's extra characters carry glyph -1, in
  logical order); only right-to-left runs are reversed, as whole glyphs. A
  block's base direction comes from its layout when a line shows it (Kazma
  sets RTL paragraphs against the right margin), else `is_rtl_dominant`. An
  RTL table's columns are read right to left. Digits after Arabic letters are
  ARABIC numbers to the bidi algorithm (W2): "-" does not join them (W4) and
  a space between two of them is right-to-left (N1), so "في 2026-09-30" is
  drawn "30-09-2026 يف" and a table row's numbers right to left. Each number
  cluster's reading is the one `arabic.visual_order` (python-bidi) draws as
  the page shows; with none, the left-to-right reading stands. A gap wider
  than half a font size is a word break; a zero-advance glyph that is not a
  mark is a misread mark (LibreOffice maps a tanween to "/") and is dropped.
  OCR words get the same rule: `arabic.number_in_logical_order` puts a
  separated number read off an Arabic line back in logical order (the TSV
  parser applies it with the paragraph text before the word), and
  `arabic.arabic_number_separators` puts back the ٫/٬ an OCR reader wrote as
  "," or "." between Arabic-Indic digits (a group of other than three digits
  follows a decimal separator; before exactly three it stays as read:
  thousands or fils). OCR readings only: a text layer's marks are the
  page's. Gates:
  `tests/test_document_pdf_rtl.py` (round trips laid out by python-bidi
  itself; without the check the date reads back reversed),
  `tests/test_document_number_order.py`,
  `tests/test_document_ocr_reading_rules.py` (the separators).
- **`to_logical()` runs in `parsers/common.IRBuilder.add_page`**, before limits,
  quality assessment and chunking. It NFKC-folds Arabic presentation forms back
  to base letters so a legacy visual-dump PDF is recovered without OCR. Pages
  whose character *order* is also reversed still fail the quality gate and
  still escalate — that is the correct remaining OCR case.
- **Fonts are chosen by verified coverage** (`documents/fonts.py`), not by first
  path that exists. An RTL job requires presentation-form cmap coverage
  (`U+FB50-FDFF` / `U+FE70-FEFF`); base-block coverage renders tofu.
  `_setup_fonts` raises `DocumentRenderError` rather than emitting a blank
  Arabic PDF behind a warning string.
- **IBM Plex Sans Arabic (OFL) is vendored** in `documents/assets/fonts/`
  (Regular + Bold + `OFL-IBM-Plex.txt`) so generated documents match the web
  UI and the Docusaurus docs on Windows, macOS and the container. Amiri
  remains a naskh fallback if Plex is removed. `KAZMA_DOCUMENT_FONT_DIR`
  overrides the directory. Precedence: **Plex wins both directions** when
  present; Amiri only for Arabic jobs if Plex is absent; system fonts last.
  Do not revert to "bundle-for-Arabic, system-for-Latin" — that split
  restyled English documents away from the product face. The OFL text must
  keep travelling with the fonts.
- **HTML exports inline the pinned font** as a data URI
  (`documents.render.embed_html_fonts`, default on) so an Arabic export renders
  the same wherever it is opened. That costs ~850 KB per Arabic file; the flag
  exists for deployments that serve these over the wire. English exports are
  never affected. DOCX names `THEME["font_latin"]` / `THEME["font_arabic"]`
  (both IBM Plex Sans Arabic); LibreOffice uses only the system's fonts and
  its profile's, so every rendering conversion (the PDF route,
  `renderer_worker._libreoffice`) copies the bundle into the profile's
  `user/fonts` first (`fonts.give_soffice_the_bundled_fonts`). Until
  2026-10-18 nothing did, and the document worker image installs no Plex:
  every Arabic PDF the container profile rendered was DejaVu Sans with Noto
  Serif for Latin (live: the owner's tweet archive). Gate:
  `tests/test_document_archive_layout.py` (the opt-in
  `KAZMA_TEST_DOCUMENT_WORKER_IMAGE` case converts in the real image with and
  without the bundle).
- **The images and CI carry the system deps.** `fonts-noto-core` (the Naskh
  faces ship inside it; `fonts-noto-naskh-arabic` is not a Debian/Ubuntu
  package, and naming it failed the image build and CI's Tests job),
  `libreoffice-writer` (`-nogui` in the worker image), `tesseract-ocr` with
  `-ara` and `-eng` -- in the
  application image (`Dockerfile`), the document worker image
  (`deploy/document-worker/Dockerfile`) and CI, which checks `fc-list` for
  Naskh. Removing them does not fail a test — it silently returns the platform
  to blank Arabic PDFs, and makes `tests/test_docx_rtl_visual.py` skip instead
  of run.

**I. Direction is per BLOCK, not per document.**
`DocProfile.direction` is the *document* base direction — margins, section,
chrome, gutter. `DocProfile.block_direction(text)` resolves each block on its
own, and every engine must use it for content: `w:bidi` per paragraph (DOCX),
per-block style alignment (PDF `_styles_for`), a `dir` wrapper on the blocks
that differ (HTML).

A document is not required to be all one language. A bilingual archive, a
report quoting Arabic sources, minutes with two languages — resolving direction
once for the whole document means whichever language loses the ratio has every
one of its blocks aligned backwards. This was reported from a real generated
tweet archive: 35% Arabic, so the document resolved LTR and every Arabic tweet
was left-aligned with no `w:bidi` at all. Nudging the ratio would simply have
inverted the bug onto the English blocks.

Blocks with no strong directional character — a divider rule, a bare number, a
date — inherit the document direction rather than defaulting to LTR. The DOCX
LTR branch must stamp `w:bidi val="0"` explicitly: in an RTL document the
Normal style and the section both carry bidi, so silence is not neutral.

**J. One type scale, enforced by measurement.**
`theme_cs_size()` is the complex-script optical size and **every** engine must
apply it: DOCX via `w:szCs`, HTML via `_css`, PDF via `_build_styles`. The PDF
engine was the odd one out for a long time — it used the Latin `body_size` for
Arabic, so the same document was set at 11pt one way and 16pt the other and
paginated to 6 pages versus 13. Same rule for `line_height` vs `line_height_ar`
and for table cells (`theme_cs_size(10)`).

RTL tables must read right-to-left in every format: `w:bidiVisual` (DOCX),
`dir="rtl"` (HTML), and an explicit column reversal in the PDF engine, which
has no bidi table model of its own. **Which tables are RTL is the table's own
language** (`DocProfile.table_direction`, 2026-10-20), and a cell with no
letter ("29 – 32") takes its table's direction (`block_direction(text,
neutral)`): an English table in an Arabic document was mirrored and its
ranges read "32 – 29", and the agent dropped the house style for hand-written
HTML to get a readable table. `convert_document` says it converts an existing
file in its own styling and that reports are made with `generate_pdf` /
`generate_docx`. Gate: `tests/test_document_table_direction.py` (through real
LibreOffice; the document's direction as the negative control).
**An HTML file converted to PDF is in the house style** (2026-10-20,
`renderer_worker._house_style_html`): its content -- headings, paragraphs,
lists, tables, `dir` marks -- in `HtmlEngine.render_html_body`'s themed shell
(brand face embedded, heading bars, table style), its own fonts, colours,
presentational attributes and CSS dropped, the page breaks it asked for kept;
`convert_document(keep_source_style=true)` keeps a file's own design, only
when the user asks. The agent made a bilingual report as its own HTML four
times (DejaVu/Noto), and memory then held the file, so every later request
converted it again. The house CSS ends paragraphs and lays out tables by each
block's own direction (`text-align-last: start`, no `direction` on `table`):
an English section of an Arabic report was set right to left. Gate:
`tests/test_document_html_house_style.py`; checked in the worker image on the
live file. The printed page carries the DOCX engine's chrome
(`HtmlEngine.page_chrome_css`: the short brand on top, the brand and the page
number at the bottom, on the reading-start side, as `@page` margin boxes),
and a Latin run in right-to-left text is marked (`arabic.isolate_ltr_runs` on
the text nodes, `_isolate_latin_in_rtl`): "50 °C" in an Arabic note drew
"C° 50". Everything in the house face (the owner's word, "house every
thing"): paragraphs written as list items ("▪ <b>Summer:</b> ...") become a
list (`_house_lists`), and a bullet or check symbol the face lacks is drawn
as the house draws it (`_house_symbols`: ■ ▪ ● ◆ ► ▸ ○ □ as •, ✔ as ✓) --
they fell back to DejaVu. A generated document's list bullets too
(`DocxEngine._house_bullets`): every bullet level is "•" in the house face;
the template's levels named Symbol and LibreOffice drew them in OpenSymbol,
the one face of the first house-style report that was not the house's. Gate:
`tests/test_document_house_bullets.py` (real LibreOffice, the PDF's embedded
faces; the template's levels as the negative control). **Arabic bold and
italic** (`DocxEngine._complex_script_emphasis`): every `w:b`/`w:i` in the
body and styles gets its `w:bCs`/`w:iCs` twin, which is what draws Arabic
bold; only Arabic runs of right-to-left paragraphs had it, so a bilingual
title's Arabic half and an Arabic list's bold lead-ins came out regular. And
a bilingual title's halves in either order are one heading
(`heading_text.headings_equivalent`): the title was drawn twice (live
2026-10-20). Gate: `tests/test_document_bilingual_title_and_arabic_bold.py`
(real LibreOffice; the engine without the twins as the negative control).

**A DOCX carries the house fonts** (2026-10-22, `engines/docx_fonts.py`):
`DocxEngine` embeds the bundled IBM Plex Sans Arabic (regular, bold) after
every save -- obfuscated font parts, `w:embedTrueTypeFonts` -- because a DOCX
only names its fonts, and a device without Plex drew the owner's OCR'd booklet
in another face. A file that cannot take them is still written (WARNING).
Gate: `tests/test_docx_embeds_house_fonts.py` (Word 16's own encoding as a
fixture; the engine without the step as the negative control).

**Every font slot of every Office file names the house face** (2026-11-11,
`engines/office_fonts.py`). Live 2026-11-10 the owner: a deck "has the font
set to the Kazma font but displays it as Arial". A DrawingML run has three
slots and Arabic is drawn from `a:cs`; python-pptx's `font.name` writes
`a:latin` alone, so Arabic fell to the template theme (Calibri, an empty `cs`,
`script="Arab"` = Times New Roman / Arial), and so did everything that
inherits in every Office format: the caret at a line's end, a new text box or
cell, Word's heading styles (Times New Roman for Arabic, measured in Word),
the notes page, the master's bullets (Arial). Now: each PPTX run, paragraph
default (`a:defRPr`) and end mark (`a:endParaRPr`) names IBM Plex Sans Arabic
in `a:latin`, `a:ea` and `a:cs` (`house_text_properties`, the one helper); the
themes (`house_theme`: latin/ea/cs and `script="Arab"`, other scripts
dropped), the master's `p:txStyles`, `p:defaultTextStyle`, the layouts and the
notes master (made even with no notes) too (`PptxEngine._house_package`);
bullets are `a:buChar` "•" in the house face, hanging on the paragraph's
reading side, never typed into the text. A PPTX paragraph takes its own
direction (`block_is_rtl`, the footer the deck's) and its text one run per
script with its `lang` (`arabic.script_runs`: in PowerPoint a mixed run drew
its spaces on the wrong side of the Arabic words as `en-US`, or moved the
full stop as `ar-SA`). The deck embeds the face (`engines/pptx_fonts.py`:
`p:embeddedFontLst`, `ppt/fonts/fontN.fntdata` as uncompressed Embedded
OpenType 0x00020001, which PowerPoint loads -- checked with a renamed copy of
the face no machine has). DOCX: the theme, `w:docDefaults` and every style's
`w:rFonts` (`styles.xml`, `stylesWithEffects.xml`) name it with no theme
reference, and the font table lists only the faces the document names
(`DocxEngine._house_package`). XLSX: the stylesheet's first font -- the
Normal style a new cell takes -- names it with no theme scheme, and the theme
is the house theme (`XlsxEngine._house_workbook`); Excel cannot embed fonts.
Code keeps its monospace face and formulas Cambria Math (DOCX/HTML), and DOCX
direction marks their face (above). Word's PDF names ArialMT for one
invisible glyph: the tab after a list bullet (no font maps U+0009; a plain
Word document does the same). Gate:
`tests/test_office_files_name_the_house_face.py` (English, Arabic and
bilingual files in every format through `renderer_worker._generate_*`; every
slot of every XML part resolved through theme references; each run, end mark
and bullet of the slides and notes; the embedded faces equal to the bundle;
PDF and HTML faces; LibreOffice draws the deck and workbook in the house face
only; the engines with these steps taken out, and a planted Segoe UI and
mixed run, as negative controls). **Office's Protected View loads no embedded
font, and garbles a face installed for one Windows user** (measured 2026-11-12,
the owner's machine: IBM Plex Sans Arabic in the user's own font folder):
PowerPoint draws Arabic in it as wrong glyphs and Word shows Arial until Enable
Editing. A python-pptx deck with no embedded font garbles the same way; one
naming Arial or a face installed nowhere draws correctly. It is the install,
not the file: do not change the engines for it (the guide's "Office's
Protected View"). Setup installs the bundled faces for all users and retires
a per-user copy (`kazma_core.house_font_install`; the fonts part of
`kazma setup system`/`install`; `tests/test_house_font_install.py`, the old
"bundled with Kazma" check as the negative control). The one document font
stays IBM Plex (the owner's decision, 2026-11-12): Calibri, Segoe UI and Dubai
display in Protected View, but Microsoft's terms let Kazma ship none of them
for its PDFs and HTML. **A document built by hand in code goes to
its generator** (`agent/raw_document_guard.py`, asked by the tool worker
before a `python_exec`/`code_exec`/`shell_exec` call runs): reportlab or
fpdf -> `generate_pdf`, python-docx -> `generate_docx`, a new openpyxl or
xlsxwriter workbook -> `generate_xlsx`, python-pptx -> `generate_pptx`. The
owner's Arial deck of 2026-11-10 was python-pptx run that way: the guard
knew no PowerPoint library and named `generate_pdf` for everything. Gate:
`tests/test_raw_document_guard.py` (the old marker list as control).

**A ReportLab PDF draws every letter, and bold is bold** (2026-10-31,
`documents/glyph_fallback.py`). The house face has no Latin Extended-A or
Additional (ā ḥ ṣ ẓ ḍ ṭ ʿ ʾ: every scholarly transliteration of Arabic), and
ReportLab draws a letter its face lacks blank: live, a Kuwait history paper
read "Kāẓima" as "K ima" and the agent stripped the transliteration from its
own paper. `GlyphFallback` wraps each such run in a face whose cmap has it (a
wide-Latin sans the machine has, else the bundled Amiri), in every paragraph
(`paragraph_class`), table cell (`cell`) and contents entry; ReportLab's
`<font>` resets bold, so a run inside `<b>` names the bold face. The house
face is registered as a family (`addMapping`, italic mappings first): inline
`**bold**` came out regular in every ReportLab PDF before. Gate:
`tests/test_pdf_glyph_fallback.py` (the markup without the fallback and the
font without the family as negative controls).

**A ReportLab table's cells wrap inside the page** (2026-10-31,
`rich_render.ltr_table_cells`, used by the body's Markdown tables and
`PdfEngine._add_table` for left-to-right tables). A plain-string cell is drawn
on one line at its natural width: live, the Kuwait paper's chronology ran
past both page edges, a date ran into its event ("c. 3000 BCE onwardDilmunite")
and `**1752**` kept its asterisks, and the agent rewrote the table as a list.
Cells are Paragraphs with inline Markdown; columns keep their natural width
when the table fits, else narrow columns keep theirs and wide ones share the
rest (at least 48 pt). Right-to-left and shaped Arabic tables keep their own
path. Gate: `tests/test_pdf_table_cells_fit.py` (plain cells as the negative
control).

Headings carry keep-with-next (`w:keepNext`/`w:keepLines`/`w:widowControl` in
DOCX, `_keep_headings_with_body` → `KeepTogether` in PDF, `break-after: avoid`
in HTML) so a heading is never the last thing on a page. Paragraph widows and
orphans are off (`allowWidows=0`/`allowOrphans=0`, `orphans: 3`/`widows: 3`).

**A Markdown source keeps its shape** (2026-10-18, the same archive):
`rich_render.parse_rich_blocks` keeps a hard line break (two trailing spaces
or a backslash) as `\n` in a paragraph's or quote's text, and the engines
draw it (DOCX a `w:br`, ReportLab line by line, so an Arabic paragraph's lines
