are not reversed; HTML through `markdown`) -- a tweet's lines ran into one
justified paragraph. A quote is upright (Arabic has no italic face; LibreOffice
slanted it), in muted ink, with a bar on its own reading side, kept on one page
with the paragraph that introduces it. A section's heading level is its `#`
count relative to the shallowest heading below the title
(`renderer_worker._build_model_and_profile`; every section was level 1). A
heading's bar sits on the heading's own reading side (`_edge_bar`, which also
keeps `w:pBdr` in schema order). A divider is a rule, never a row of "─".
Table cells are compact and vertically centred. **In a right-to-left block a
left-to-right run that holds a Latin letter is marked with LRM on both sides**
(`arabic.isolate_ltr_runs`, applied by `DocxEngine._isolated` to body runs,
headings and cells): "10 · 2026-10-05 — 15:15 UTC · <id> — محذوفة" came out
in reverse group order around "UTC"; the strong mark makes the run's digits
and separators left to right (W7). The sentence punctuation right after
the run's last letter (`. ! ? , ; :`, `_LTR_TRAILING_PUNCT`) is inside it: an
English sentence ending an Arabic paragraph drew its full stop on the far
side of the next line (2026-10-20, `tests/test_document_english_sentence_in_arabic.py`).
A run of digits alone is NOT marked:
"في 2026-09-30" drawing "30-09-2026" (W2) is the Arabic convention, read right
to left as the date, and the PDF and OCR readers (§19H) read it back by that
rule -- marking it broke the fidelity corpus. An attached `@ # $` (or `+ -`
before a digit) joins its run. **Every direction mark is drawn in a face that
has its glyph** (`DocxEngine._give_direction_marks_a_face`, the last step
before saving: each mark its own run in `fonts.direction_mark_family`, Amiri;
none bundled, the marks are dropped). IBM Plex Sans Arabic has no glyph for
any mark, and LibreOffice draws a missing mark with the face's space glyph:
the PDF's text map then named every space of the bold face U+2066 (the first
version used LRI…PDI in Plex runs, deployed for an afternoon: copied text lost
its spaces, and Kazma's reader failed on the page). `to_logical` strips the
marks when Kazma reads a PDF back. And a block
`to_logical` shortened is no longer taken for a limit cut
(`IRBuilder.add_page`): every block after the first one holding an RLM or an
isolate was dropped from a parse, silently. Gates in
`tests/test_document_archive_layout.py`: the LibreOffice word-order test (no
marks as the control), the text read back from the real LibreOffice PDF (its
spaces, the heading in order, a table once; the morning's isolates as the
control), the bidi-mark parse (the old check fails it).

**Kazma reads past the faults LibreOffice writes into a text map, and reads a
table once** (2026-10-18, the same archive read back by the agent, which took
the duplicate for a rendering defect and tried to "fix" it). `pdf_rtl`: a
direction mark with a visible advance is the space it was drawn with; a digit
or Latin letter of no width is a misnamed mark (Plex's shadda as "8"/"3"); a
Latin letter under `_KASHIDA_EM` (0.15 em) is a misnamed kashida ("G"); Arabic
letters of no width stay (a ligature's parts). A letter glyph's text keeps the
marks it names only where a mark glyph is drawn on it (`_drop_undrawn_marks`):
LibreOffice 24.2 (Ubuntu 24.04, Linux CI 2026-11-10) names "ريالاً"'s tanween
glyph "#" and puts the tanween into the lam-alef ligature's text, so every
lam-alef read "لاً" (the footer's "الاصطناعي" with a tanween).
`arabic.visual_order` drops
isolates (python-bidi asserts on them; the whole page's reading failed). The
PDF parser finds the tables first and reads a single-column page's text
around them (`pdf_layout._segments_around_tables`): each table once, where it
stands; a table's cells were also page text. Gates:
`tests/test_document_pdf_text_map_faults.py`, `tests/test_document_pdf_rtl.py`.
**Reading Kazma's own bilingual PDF back** (2026-10-20: the agent read a
house-style PDF as broken and dropped the house style): a kashida glyph with
no name (U+FFFD, narrower than 0.15 em) is no text; table cells are left out
of column detection (a table is read from its grid), and two sides are
columns only when they stand side by side (`_side_by_side`: short Arabic and
English lines stacked one above the other made a "second column", which put
a title's last word after the paragraph and read the table twice); on a
single-column right-to-left page each block is read once
(`_without_contained`), top to bottom (`_reading_order`); a number-only cell
of a right-to-left table runs right to left ("٤٣ – ٤٦", `text_in_rect(...,
base="R")`); a cell's wrapped lines are one value; and a left-to-right line
whose brackets read inside out ("Avg high )°C(": one glyph draws "(" in an
English cell and ")" in an Arabic one, and the text map names it once) is set
right. Gate: `tests/test_document_table_direction.py` (a bilingual PDF made
through real LibreOffice and read back). **Table cells are read from the
glyphs on every page** (`pdf._logical_table(rtl_page=False)`: left to right,
PyMuPDF's text only for a cell the glyphs leave empty): on the all-English
page PyMuPDF's table reader put the "fi" ligature's "i" after the next glyph,
and Kazma quoted its own cell as "frist rains" (test 18, live 2026-10-20).
Gate: `tests/test_document_pdf_ligature_cells.py` (PyMuPDF's reader as the
negative control).

`tests/test_document_layout.py` measures all of this against a rendered PDF
with PyMuPDF rather than grepping the source — every defect it covers was
invisible at the code level and obvious on the page. Do not weaken it to source
assertions.

**K. Third-party parse egress is opt-in and audited.**
`extract_salvage.try_remote_parse` uploads the ORIGINAL document bytes to
LlamaParse/Reducto. It requires `documents.security.remote_parse` (default
**off**); an API key in the environment is not consent. Local Docling salvage
is `documents.security.local_salvage` (default on), inside the bounded parser
worker, along with structural preflight. Every remote attempt requires a
durable `egress` audit row carrying immutable job identity before upload,
with separate success/failure events; a context-scoped recorder prevents
cross-tenant attribution. Actor, request digest and OCR intent belong to the
job, not a deduplicated version. Consent is rechecked at each provider attempt.
A failed provider is audited (`failure`) and the next configured one is tried,
after the live policy is read again (until 2026-10-13 the first failure
re-raised and the fallback never ran). Both providers use one client
(`_provider_client`): no ambient proxy environment, no redirects (an upload is
never re-sent elsewhere), decoded answers capped at 32 MiB
(`remote_parse_response_limit`). Remote parsing runs in the Kazma process
(`DocumentService`), never in the worker; local salvage runs only in the
worker (every other caller passes `allow_local=False`, gated in
`tests/test_extract_salvage.py`), and a remote parse that is refused or fails
is a WARNING naming the error type (it was DEBUG). Transient excerpts lack durable egress scope and cannot upload remotely. The legacy
`KAZMA_REMOTE_PARSE=0` / `KAZMA_DOCLING=0` env switches remain as an additional
veto only — they can turn a tier off, never on. Gates:
`tests/test_document_egress_hardening.py`, `tests/test_document_egress_pg.py`
(the same rules on real Postgres metadata, jobs, audit and settings),
`tests/test_extract_salvage.py`.

**L. Pictures in generated documents** (2026-11-12, the owner's request).
`generate_pdf` / `generate_docx` place a Markdown image on a line of its own
(`![caption](path)`) where it stands; `generate_pptx` takes a slide's `image`
and `image_caption`, drawn beside the slide's text on the side opposite its
reading start, or across the slide when it has no text. One grammar for both
processes, standard library only: `documents/image_refs.py` (a fenced code
block is text; an image inside a sentence is refused, never dropped).
- **The Kazma process decodes nothing** (`documents/image_inputs.py`,
  `DocumentImages`): an address is refused naming `download_image`; a path is
  read under the file tools' rule (`resolve_in_scope(..., "reads")`) or is in
  Kazma's own `images`/`attachments` folders (absolute, checked on its text
  before it is resolved, strictly); its first bytes must be a PNG, JPEG, GIF
  or WebP (`image_type`, also `vision_analyze`'s sniff); at most `MAX_IMAGES`
  (40: the container takes 64 files a job), `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`,
  `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`. Each is copied as `image-NN.<ext>` into a folder of the
  call's own (removed when the call ends) and the reference rewritten, so the
  worker never sees a path; every refusal is `RefusedBeforeEffect`. A Markdown
  file's relative path means its own folder first.
- **The worker cleans before any engine reads** (`documents/image_clean.py`,
  `renderer_worker._cleaned_images`, for generate pdf/docx/html/pptx):
  `Image.open(..., formats=ALLOWED_FORMATS)` only (never EPS: Ghostscript),
  `MAX_PIXELS` with the bomb warning as an error, EXIF orientation applied,
  sRGB through its profile, `MAX_SIDE`, rebuilt from pixels alone (no EXIF,
  GPS, text chunks, comments or trailing payload), saved under `images/`
  beside the output -- never into `assets/`, which `_verify_assets` checks
  again after the render. `ImageRejected` is `WorkerError("invalid_image")`;
  the tool appends the user's file name (`DocumentImages.explain`).
- **Placement** (`renderer_worker._add_body_with_figures`, `_figure_width`:
  6.5 in wide at most, 8 in tall, never above its 96 dpi size): centred, the
  caption under it in its own direction, kept on one page. A picture that was
  approved and cleaned and cannot be embedded fails the document (the engines'
  block loop `DocumentRenderError`); a legacy `images` payload naming no
  approved picture is still skipped.
- **`download_image`** (`tools/image_download.py`, write tier, in
  `FETCH_URL_FIELDS`): one GET through `fetch_public`, judged by its bytes,
  saved under `<workspace>/downloads/images`, never over an earlier file.
Gates: `tests/test_document_images.py` (each hostile file beside what the raw
file carries: GPS, a polyglot, a bomb, an EPS; placement in PDF, Arabic PDF
through LibreOffice, Word and PowerPoint; the tools; the builder without the
split as the negative control), and in the worker image
`test_pictures_are_cleaned_and_placed_inside_the_container`
(`KAZMA_TEST_DOCUMENT_WORKER_IMAGE`).
### 20. Commitment Layer (`kazma-core/kazma_core/safety/commitment/`)

A policy gate between the LLM and durable mutations. Kazma resolves intent
against memory BEFORE acting — the CoPilot incident class (model invents a
date, schedules it, overwrites the user's real belief) is blocked at both the
schedule layer and the memory layer. Full plan + Phase-0 exit report:
`docs/plans/INTELLIGENT_AGENT_COMMITMENT_LAYER.md`,
`docs/plans/COMMITMENT_PHASE0_EXIT_REPORT.md`. **All phases shipped**: 0–2
(core + gate + store + TTL/GC), 3 (semantic clarify/confirm interrupt card),
4 (remind + cancel_job + exec/outbound/config resolvers), 5 (swarm scope-token
default + MCP classification), 6 (autonomy modes), 7 (soul confirm gate), 8
(docs + metrics). Default-off kill-switches on every enforcement layer.
**Fail posture (deep-audit 2026-08-19):** authorization-engine EXCEPTIONS on
semantic tools fail CLOSED at both chokes (a broken policy engine must not
free-fire the remind/exec classes); the layer kill-switch and
import-unavailable degradation stay fail-open (treated as layer-off).

**A. Two `authorize_effect` choke points + an independent memory-side gate.**
- `agent/graph_tool_worker.py:tool_worker_node` — the single-agent chat path;
  the gate runs BEFORE the security HITL split so it can rewrite args first.
- `agent/tool_registry.py:LocalToolRegistry.execute` — the IDE/swarm path
  (mostly audit-only — remind/cancel_job decisions need graph context — but
  the exec denylist / outbound allowlist / config protected-key resolvers DO
  enforce here).
- `memory/belief_mutation.py:_mutate_functional` — the memory corruption half
  is gated by its OWN source-trust check (a fact the user stated yields only
  to the user's own words, `memory.provenance.may_overrule`), NOT by an
  `authorize_effect` call — two independent defenses, by design.

**B. The decision mapping (§3.4). `authorize_effect` returns one of:**
- `allow` (+ optional `rewritten_args`): for the remind act, the gate anchors
  the relative phrase to a memory event and **rewrites the tool args to the
  memory-correct fire_at**: an aware ISO instant computed in the operator's
  zone (`cron.timezone`, §16G), never a naive time read as UTC. A recurring
  timing is never rewritten, and a recurring request ("every day at 9")
  booked as a one-off is denied (Scheduled audit SCH-E03, E05, 2026-10-14).
  `edit_scheduled` is its own act (`edit_job`): the caller's own jobs only,
  and the new timing through the same resolver. For exec, the denylist blocks catastrophes before
  the HITL card. For config, protected keys are denied. For outbound, the
  target allowlist is checked.
- `clarify` / `confirm`: a real interrupt card fires on the unified HITL bus
  (kind=semantic_clarify/confirm) with discrete options. Per-option buttons
  render on Web (chat.js + sidebar), Telegram, Discord, and Slack. Resume
  applies the chosen `slots_patch`. The existing Approve/Deny buttons map to
  best-option / cancel via `build_resume_value`.
- `deny`: blocked with a clear error; no card. The tool worker returns it
  as a `policy` refusal and the model goes on (2026-10-20: it was
  `terminal`, the clarify-card outcome, and a sandbox-refused `python_exec`
  ended a report turn before `generate_pdf`; gate
  `tests/test_policy_deny_keeps_the_turn.py`, the terminal outcome as the
  negative control).
- Audit-only: read tools, `mutate_fs` (containment in `IdeService.resolve`),
  `delegate` (HMAC trust at skill-load).

**C. Invariants — removing any reintroduces the incident class:**
- **Source-trust gate** (`_mutate_functional`, and the history path): a fact
  the user stated may NOT be superseded by a lower-trust source. Kill-switch:
  `cfg.v2.functional_supersede_requires_user_assert`. **The provenance
  ladder** (`memory/provenance.py`, Memory audit M03, 2026-10-13):
  `user_explicit` -- the user's own channel only (the Memory page, a chat
  command, or a memory tool on a turn whose latest user message asks to
  remember AND holds 80 % of the stored words); `user_stated` -- the user's
  literal statement read by the heuristic pass from their own message;
  then `system_tool`, `agent_asserted` (a memory tool the user did not ask
  for) and `llm_inferred`. A `user_*` fact yields only to `user_*`, in its
  own turn too (the model pass's same-turn correction was removed by rule A
  of F1's second security review, 2026-11-18; §15H's entry on a model's
  reading).
  Until then `memory_store` / `memory_link_entities` wrote `user_explicit`
  for anything the model chose (a fetched page, an email), unscreened, and
  the user's own words were `llm_inferred`: the model's fact blocked the
  user's correction. The tools now screen (`filter_injection`,
  `is_override_delta`; refused, nothing stored) and answer
  `user_fact_stands` when a write would replace the user's fact -- the user
  corrects their own facts. Gate: `tests/test_memory_provenance.py` (the
  R02 witnesses inverted, EN/AR remember requests, the injection corpus,
  the same-turn rule, the old gate as negative control, every product site
  writing `user_explicit` declared as a user channel). The rows the old tools
  wrote are relabelled by `scripts/memory_relabel_provenance.py`
  (`memory/provenance_relabel.py`, 2026-10-15; `size` names ids, never
  values; `apply --db --yes` copies to `<db>.pre_relabel` first): a
  `user_explicit` fact a memory tool's note names (or, before notes named
  their chat, holds its value within seconds) or that names a chat turn
  becomes `agent_asserted`, unless the Memory page edited it, an operator
  action named it, or its turn asked to remember those words (today's rule);
  the page's links and the V1 backfill are left. One audit row per fact; the
  live run is the owner's. Gate: `tests/test_memory_relabel_provenance.py`.
- **Rewrite-on-allow**: the gate's fire_at wins over the model's args — do not
  let the original (possibly wrong) `timing` reach the scheduler for remind.
  The fire_at is one instant in the operator's zone, and a recurrence is kept
  as the user asked, never turned into one fire
  (`tests/test_cron_timing_model.py`).
- **Exec denylist**: catastrophic commands (`rm -rf /`, fork bombs, `curl|sh`,
  `dd of=/dev/`, `mkfs`, shutdown, `chmod 777 /`) are denied BEFORE the HITL
  card. Safe commands pass through (HITL still applies).
- **Config protected keys**: `safety.*`, `agent.commitment.*`,
  `notifications.lifecycle.*` cannot be mutated by the agent (self-protection).
- **Outbound allowlist**: when `agent.commitment.outbound_allowed_targets` is
  configured, unknown targets → clarify with the allowlist.
- **Swarm scope default** (`worker_dispatch._do_dispatch`): when
  `swarm_scope_enforce` is on, dispatched workers are capped at semantic_tier
  HIGH (deny exec/outbound/config/identity CRITICAL) + denied_acts=
  {soul_delta, identity, config_change}. Default ON since 2026-08-15 (intent-engine auto-dispatch) — opt-OUT via the env/ConfigStore kill-switch.
- **Soul confirm gate** (`apply_agent_mutation`/`_auto_apply`): when
  `soul_requires_confirm` is on, soul deltas are held until confirmed via
  `POST /api/commitment/soul/{cid}/confirm`. Mint-wired at both apply callers.
  Config default is off; **auto-ON in production / multi-user** unless the
  operator set the key explicitly (`get_commitment_config`).
- **Fail-open + kill-switch**: `KAZMA_COMMITMENT_ENABLED=0` disables the whole
  layer. Every enforcement layer has its own default-OFF flag. (Engine
  *exceptions* on semantic tools fail closed at both chokes — see the §20
  header; only the kill-switch/import-degradation paths fail open.)
- **Conservative auto-store**, **No late approve**, **GC cadence** — as before.

**D. Components (`kazma_core/safety/commitment/`, and `kazma_core/safety/side_effects.py`).**
- `safety/side_effects.py` — the single SoT registry: tool → `ToolEffectProfile`.
  Parity-tested. Unregistered mutators fail-closed (tokenized). MCP tools
  (`mcp__*`) route through `classify_mcp_tool_effect`.
- `authorize.py` — `authorize_effect` (the policy gate) + `EffectDecision` +
  the act resolvers: `_resolve_remind_act`, `_resolve_cancel_job_act`,
  `_resolve_edit_job_act`, `_resolve_exec_act` (denylist+cwd),
  `_resolve_send_outbound_act` (allowlist), `_resolve_config_change_act`
  (protected keys).
- `relative_time.py` — `resolve_remind` (EN+AR). G2-measured (0 false-allow)
  on one-off requests; recurring requests (EN+AR) are measured by the
  Scheduled corpus in `tests/test_cron_timing_model.py`, not by G2.
- `store.py` — `Commitment` + ops-SQLite tables + TTL/GC + tiered retention +
  `list_pending_soul()` (the confirm queue).
- `constraints.py` — `is_commitment_enabled` + `load_constraint_beliefs` +
  `cron_pending_jobs` (for the cancel_job resolver).
- `config.py` — `get_commitment_config` (the ONE config reader).
- `scope.py` — `ScopeToken` + `swarm_scope` (ContextVar) +
  `default_worker_scope()` + `is_act_within_scope()` (the privilege guard).
- `resume.py` — `build_resume_value()` + `is_semantic_kind()` (maps
  Approve/Deny → option/cancel for semantic interrupts on every platform).
- `_commitment_resolve_gate()` in `graph_tool_worker.py` — the extracted gate
  (Phase 2.5 SRP). Called from `tool_worker_node`.
- **Operator API**: `kazma_ui/commitment_api.py` —
  `GET /api/commitment/soul/pending`, `POST .../{cid}/confirm`, `POST .../{cid}/reject`.
- **Metrics**: `kazma_ui/metrics.py` exposes
  `kazma_commitment_decisions_total{decision=...}` + `kazma_commitment_pending`.

**E. Modes + kill-switches.**
- Modes (`agent.commitment.mode` / `KAZMA_COMMITMENT_MODE`): strict |
  balanced (default) | autonomous | yolo.
- Kill-switches (all default OFF / layer default ON):
  `KAZMA_COMMITMENT_ENABLED` (layer, default on),
  `KAZMA_COMMITMENT_SWARM_SCOPE_ENFORCE` (default ON since 2026-08-15),
  `KAZMA_COMMITMENT_SOUL_REQUIRES_CONFIRM` (default off; auto-ON in
  production / multi-user unless explicitly set),
  `KAZMA_AUTO_STORE_BELIEFS` (default conservative).

**Tests:** 15+ test files (`tests/test_commitment_*.py` +
`tests/test_side_effects.py`) — corpus/G1/G2, store+GC, authorize, clarify-card
interrupt+resume, tool_worker gate, scenarios (7), act resolvers, modes, scope,
soul, cancel_job, config. Run:
`python -m pytest tests/test_commitment_*.py tests/test_side_effects.py -m "not slow"`.

### 21. Postgres Shared-State Backup & Schema Assurance (`kazma-core/kazma_core/db/pg_backup.py`)

Scheduled `pg_dump` backups + boot-time schema verification for the tables
Kazma owns in Postgres. Built after the 2026-08-14 incident where a second
app pointed at the shared `kazma` database dropped Kazma's tables
(checkpoints / settings / chat sessions / document jobs) and there was no
scheduled PG backup to restore from.

**A. `KAZMA_PG_TABLES` is the single SoT of which tables Kazma owns.**
The list lives in `kazma_core/db/pg_backup.py` (not here — this file will
drift). It includes LangGraph `checkpoints*`, shared-state
(`kazma_settings`, `kazma_chat_sessions`, `kazma_swarm_tasks`,
`kazma_swarm_worker_metrics`, `kazma_platform_users`, `kazma_web_sessions`),
document jobs (`document_jobs`, `document_job_events`), document intake
ownership and admission (`document_intake_reservations`,
`document_intake_mutex`, §19 B2), **and** the document catalog from H-13
(`documents`, `document_blobs`, `document_versions`, `document_artifacts`,
`document_acl`, `document_tombstones`, `document_chunks`,
`document_audit_events`), and the memory mirror (`kazma_episodes`,
`kazma_beliefs`, §15K: recall's store when Postgres is the primary, and the
only copy of what other replicas wrote; boot requires them only when memory's
state backend is Postgres, `pg_backup._required_pg_tables`). A new shared-state PG table MUST be added to that
Python list or it silently stops being backed up
(`tests/test_pg_backup.py::test_kazma_pg_tables_covers_document_ddl` reads the
document stores' DDL). This dump does not carry the document store's content
files; a document store on Postgres is backed up as one point in time with its
files by `documents/backup_pg.py` (§19 F2).
The dump is deliberately table-filtered — never a whole-DB dump — so a
shared database neither leaks foreign-app data into Kazma's backups nor
restores over another app's tables. `hitl_gates.db` is SQLite (single-process
like the turn journal), not this list.

**B. Dump pipeline (6h loop, `worker_bootstrap.py`).**
The backup/export loop enqueues `native_pg_backup` when
`pg_backup_enabled()` (live-checked: Postgres backend + `backups.pg.enabled`
config + `KAZMA_PG_BACKUP_ENABLED` env kill-switch). The handler
(`_handle_native_pg_backup`) runs `perform_pg_backup()` in a worker thread:
dump via `migration/pg_bridge.dump_database(tables=KAZMA_PG_TABLES)` to a
`.tmp` file, validate the `PGDMP` magic, atomically rename into
`{kazma-data}/backups/pg/pg_shared_<epoch>.dump`, then prune to
`backups.pg.retention` (default **3** local staging dumps; restic keeps
history. Env `KAZMA_PG_BACKUP_RETENTION`).
Failures return False so the durable queue retries (max 3) then
dead-letters; a failed dump never leaves a valid-looking file behind.

**C. Boot-time schema verification (fail-open, never blocks boot).**
`app.py:_on_startup` calls `verify_required_pg_tables(pool)` when PG is
active. Missing tables → CRITICAL log naming the missing tables + the
restore command (`python scripts/pg_backup.py restore --latest`); the
server still boots (SQLite-side features work) but chat/settings/document
history is broken until restored. A pool failure returns None = "unknown",
not "all present".
**Dropped, or added by this build?** (2026-10-14.) The check runs before
the stores start, on purpose (a store recreates a dropped table empty and
would hide the drop), so a table a newer build adds is missing too until its
store creates it: the first boot of the Documents hardening told the owner to
restore a backup over two tables that had never existed. Every check records
the Kazma tables it finds in `<data dir>/pg_tables_seen.json` (beside the
install, so a lost Postgres cannot lose the record; `machine`).
`report_missing_tables` calls a missing table on the record dropped
(CRITICAL, restore command) and one never seen new (INFO; WARNING with no
record yet), and `recheck_new_tables` looks for those again a minute after
start (still missing: WARNING). Gate: `tests/test_pg_tables_seen.py` (the
live boot as the witness, the old rule as the negative control).

**D. Operator CLI (`scripts/pg_backup.py`).**
`backup` (one-shot dump now), `restore --latest|--file <name> [--dry-run]`
(via `pg_bridge.restore_database`, `--clean --if-exists` — only the dumped
tables are touched), `list`. Loads the `.env` python-dotenv finds walking up
from the script's folder (not the CWD); never prints the DSN userinfo.

**E. Config is live-read, never raises** (mirrors `get_hitl_config`):
ConfigStore keys `backups.pg.enabled` / `backups.pg.retention`; env
kill-switch `KAZMA_PG_BACKUP_ENABLED=0`. Tests:
`python -m pytest tests/test_pg_backup.py`.

**E2. The dump must find its tools without PATH's help.** `pg_dump` usually
runs inside the DB container through `docker exec`, and a Docker Desktop
update dropped the CLI from the system PATH on 2026-09-25 — every dump after
it failed while Docker and the container were fine. The docker CLI is found
by `kazma_core.docker_cli.find_docker_cli()` (`KAZMA_DOCKER_BIN`, PATH,
Docker's install folders), never `shutil.which("docker")` alone
(`tests/test_docker_cli_discovery.py` gates it). The tools of the Postgres
`kazma setup postgres` installed (its record's `bin_dir`,
`pg_bridge._installed_tool`) come after PATH and before any container: after
the move to the service (2026-11-06) `KAZMA_DB_CONTAINER` still named the
old container, and a dump through it read that container's stale database.
Boot checks the tool
(`pg_dump_tool_problem`, ops alert `backup.pg_tools`), and a failed dump's
alert carries its reason (`last_pg_backup_failure`), redacted. Putting the
folder back on PATH then needs only `kazma_guard.py --reload`: the server
adopts PATH entries the OS settings gained since the guard started (§38).

**E3. Schema setup takes no table lock it does not need**
(`kazma_core/db/pg_schema.py`, 2026-10-13). Postgres takes `ALTER TABLE ...
ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`'s ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock -- and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT
EXISTS`'s SHARE lock -- BEFORE it looks for the column or index (measured: the
ALTER waits behind `pg_dump`'s read locks, both wait behind any open writer).
Every store sent them at every start, so starts deadlocked each other (a
4-writer restore drill, in the intake store's constructor), and a start during
a dump waited for the whole dump with every query on the table queued behind
it -- the core schema's 5 s timeout then failed the pool. `ensure_schema`
takes one transaction-scoped advisory lock every Kazma schema setup shares,
and sends a `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE INDEX` or `ADD COLUMN` only when the
catalog says it is missing; any other `ALTER TABLE` is refused. Every
Postgres DDL site uses it: the core schema, the swarm task store, the memory
mirror and pgvector table, and the document jobs, catalog and intake stores.
Gate: `tests/test_pg_schema_setup.py` (no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` sent
outside it, the old shapes as control; on real Postgres each store's setup
completes under a held dump lock and an open writer, and fresh starts at the
same moment both succeed -- the direct statements wait and collide).

**F. Universal backup — "never left anything behind"**
(`kazma_core/backup/universal.py`). One unified backup that backs up
literally everything: every `*.db` in `kazma-data/` (WAL-safe via
`sqlite3.backup()` API), every non-DB dir (attachments, document-store,
workspace, exports, vectors — via `_robust_copytree` that skips ephemeral
files like LibreOffice cache). It does **not** run a second `pg_dump`.
It **records whether `native_pg_backup` is fresh** (`_pg_dump_state`); a
stale/missing dump is a failed item in the manifest, not `"ok": true`.
Produces `manifest.json` + retention-capped (default 7). Wired into the
6h `native_backup` handler (auto) +
`POST /api/backup/now` (manual, background task) + Settings → Backup tab
(animated progress bar polling `GET /api/backup/status` every 2s).
Delete/archive/download: `DELETE /api/backup/{name}`,
`POST …/archive` (zip), `GET …/download`. The per-file copy MUST be robust
(`_robust_copytree`) — `shutil.copytree` aborts on one vanishing file and
loses the entire `document-store`. Do NOT revert to `copytree`.
**Old offsite copies are deleted after each successful upload** (2026-11-03,
the owner had deleted eleven 344 MB zips by hand). `_offsite_sync` runs
`_prune_offsite` on the path that made the copy -- the native provider's
`list_backups` / `delete_backup` (every provider in `cloud_sync.py`, each
page of a listing, a bad name refused before any request) or `rclone lsf` /
`rclone purge --drive-use-trash=false` (a folder per copy) -- keeping the
newest `backups.offsite.keep` (`offsite_keep`, default 7; `0` keeps every
copy; Settings -> Backup -> Keep cloud copies). Names are the backup's
epoch (`_NATIVE_COPY` / `_RCLONE_COPY`); a listing that fails, is not whole
or lacks the copy just uploaded deletes nothing (`_old_copies` raises); a
copy already gone is done; deletes stop at `_PRUNE_BUDGET_S` and the rest
wait for the next run. The answer joins the offsite result (`pruned`,
`prune_error`, `prune_left`), never fails the backup, and a `prune_error`
raises `backup.offsite_prune_failed` (warn) before the fallback check in
`_alert_on_backup_gaps`. Deletes are for good, never to a trash. Gates:
`tests/test_offsite_retention.py` (a trusting rule deleting from a stale
listing as the negative control), the provider cases in
`tests/test_cloud_sync.py`.
**A copy in a folder the owner chooses** (2026-11-20, the owner's item;
`kazma_core/backup/folder_copy.py`, Settings -> Backup -> "A copy on another
drive"). Another drive, a USB disk or a network share holds a restic
repository (`<folder>/kazma-restic`, `restic_repo.repo_paths()["folder"]`,
also in `configured_repos`, so the Postgres dump's copy goes there too):
every universal backup is copied into it, encrypted with Kazma's restic
passphrase, its repository made on the first copy
(`restic_repo._folder_repo_made`). Settings `backups.folder.enabled`,
`.path` (absolute, never inside the data folder: `folder_copy.path_problem`)
and `.keep` (the newest N of each kind, `--keep-last`; 0 keeps every copy;
the nightly restic maintenance applies it, `folder_copy.keep_policy`), each
with a `settings_validation` rule. A folder that is not there is never a
failed backup: `note_presence` says it once (`backup.folder_missing`, the
runtime mark `system.backups.folder_missing_since`) and its return once
(`backup.folder_back`). Routes: GET/PUT `/api/settings/backup/folder`, POST
`.../test` (writes and removes one probe file; free space, same disk as the
data, restic, passphrase) and POST `.../browse` (the page's folder picker;
never a network path: listing one connects to its host). Gates:
`tests/test_backup_folder_copy.py` (real restic; the copy without making the
repository, the notice without its mark and the maintenance with the default
policy as negative controls), `tests/e2e/test_backup_folder_browser.py` (by the
sidebar, EN/AR, the picker, a refused save, Test).
**The folder's rules hold for every name a path can have** (2026-11-21, the
SonarCloud review of the Test). `folder_copy.path_problem` answers one of
`folder_copy.PATH_PROBLEMS`, and the save refuses every one of them (it
named two and kept a path with any other): a device path (`\\.\`, `\\?\`,
`\??\`: a named pipe, a raw disk) is refused on its text before anything
opens it (`remote_paths.device_path_reason`; a plain `\\server\share` is a
folder, choosing one is the feature); "inside the data folder" is judged by
the real path AND by each folder's identity (`folder_copy._identity`: volume
and file id), since `\\?\C:\...` and a loopback share
(`\\localhost\C$\...`) resolve to themselves; the walk up stops at the first
folder that does not answer (`folder_copy._not_made_yet`: an offline share
waits out a network timeout per question); "the same disk" is the volume
(`st_dev`), never the drive letter. Gate:
`tests/test_backup_folder_path_rules.py` (the Test, the save and a stored
path; every code worded by the page in both languages; the old rule, the old
save and the drive-letter check as negative controls; the loopback share
where this account can reach it).

**Every copy of a live SQLite database is one step, through one helper**
(`kazma_core.db.sqlite_snapshot.snapshot_copy`, 2026-10-13, Memory audit M19):
the universal backup, the native memory backup (`memory/backup.backup_one`,
also the migration importer's pre-swap copy), the embedding rebuild's
pre-copy, the memory restore route and the X shadow script. A batched copy
(`pages=N`) restarts whenever the source is written: the native memory
backup -- the declared restore source -- finished only in a quiet window (778
restarts in two seconds). Gate: `tests/test_sqlite_snapshot.py` (the copy
finishes under a writer every 2 ms; `pages=100` as the negative control; no
`.backup(` call outside the helper).

**G. Postgres as an OS service** (resilience plan A1,
`kazma_core/postgres_service.py`, `kazma_cli/setup.py`). A database in a
container dies with Docker Desktop, which starts only when someone signs in
(live 2026-11-04: eleven hours). `kazma setup postgres` installs Postgres 16
with the OS's package manager (winget, Homebrew, apt, dnf; WSL as its distro)
as a service that starts at boot and restarts on failure, `listen_addresses =
'localhost'`, creates `kazma` and the `kazma_app` role (`kazma_app_role.sql`),
turns on WAL archiving, writes `KAZMA_DATABASE_URL` into `.env` (never
printed, restricted) and records it in `<data dir>/setup_record.json`.
**Kazma's own driver first** (the drill VM, 2026-11-06: the address went into
an environment without psycopg, and the server waited ten minutes on a
database that was fine): when `postgres_pool.driver_missing()` says so, the
plan's first step installs the `postgres` extra (`setup._extra_requirements`,
read from the package's metadata) with `uv pip install --python
<sys.executable>`, which adds and never removes; a second run on a set-up
service does it too, and a failed install writes no `.env`. `--check` reports
the driver. A missing driver is `PostgresDriverMissing`: the pool raises it
at once, says it once at ERROR, its `reason` reaches the boot wait, the guard
and the settings error (`DRIVER_MISSING`, what to run), and it is never an
outage (`driver_missing` on the error, read first by
`availability._outage_one`); a driver installed while the boot waits is found
at the next try (import caches cleared). Gates:
`tests/test_postgres_driver_missing.py`, the driver cases in
`tests/test_setup_postgres.py` (the plan without the step as the negative
control). No
password on a command line (the Windows installer's throwaway one aside,
replaced at once through psql's stdin); the superuser's is kept in
`<install>/.kazma/postgres_superuser.pass` (a Kazma secret file). `--check`
and `--dry-run` change nothing; a second run repairs and never reinstalls;
`--move-from-container NAME` switches Kazma in ONE run (`setup._MoveHold`):
Kazma stopped through its guard once idle, the container's data copied in
(`backup/pg_move.py`: dump inside the container, `pg_restore` as
`kazma_app`, every Kazma table's row count compared), `.env` written, the
memory backends' own addresses that name the container repointed through
the vault (`setup._repoint_memory_backends`: the mirror has no fallback to
`KAZMA_DATABASE_URL`), Kazma started on the new server and seen signed in
there, the container stopped and kept. Live 2026-11-06 the first move copied while Kazma kept writing to
the container and said "reload when idle": the next restart would have
started Kazma on a copy missing everything since. A second run replaces an
earlier copy only when Kazma never started on it (`pg_move._replace_refusal`:
its `system.lifecycle.last_boot_epoch` not newer than the container's,
nothing connected; `postgres_service.empty_database_steps`, after the dump),
and after a failed copy into an emptied database `.env` names, Kazma stays
stopped. Gates: `tests/test_postgres_move_switch.py` (the old setup fails
all 16), and on real Postgres `tests/test_resilience_postgres.py`.
`kazma doctor` checks the service from the record; the guard watches it
(`DatabaseServiceWatch`: starts a stopped service once per outage, pages once
at five minutes, once on recovery). A state `sc` refuses ("Access is
denied": a guard without admin rights, the user-level task) is unknown and
the port decides -- read as stopped it paged a running database down; a
refused start is said once with the fix (2026-11-11). An S4U boot task of an
admin account runs with its full token whatever its run level (measured on
the drill VM), so `--install`'s boot task keeps `Highest`. Gates: `tests/test_setup_postgres.py`
(every package manager faked; a password on psql's command line as the
negative control), `tests/test_guard_database_service.py`.

**G2. Postgres 18, and moving an install to it** (2026-11-13,
`kazma_core/postgres_upgrade.py`, `kazma_cli/postgres_upgrade.py`).
`postgres_service.PG_MAJOR` is 18: a new install gets 18, and every name
that held 16 takes the major (`service_name`, `bin_dir_for`, `setup_plan(...,
major=)`, `empty_database_steps`). **A repair keeps the major the record
names**: `_setup_postgres` repairs the record's installed service (16 on an
install made before), never installs 18 beside it, keeps the record's history
fields, and signs in with the stored superuser password (a repair used the
installer's throwaway, which no installer had set). `kazma setup postgres
--upgrade` moves an install: 18 installed beside 16 on a spare port
(`postgres_upgrade._free_port`, from 55432) with the role and the password
Kazma already uses; Kazma held through its guard (`_MoveHold`, its own
reason); `copy_database` (the new major's `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` as
`kazma_app`, one transaction, every public table's count and every sequence
compared; an earlier copy replaced only by `pg_move._replace_refusal`'s
rule); the switch (`switch_steps`: the new server's port written ON DISK,
`postgres_service.port_step` -- never through a connection -- then the new
stopped, the old stopped and off the boot list, the new started on the old
port, checked to answer as 18 and to sign Kazma in); the record (new server,
the old under `previous`), Kazma started and seen signed in, the first base
backup taken. `.env` and the memory backends' addresses do not change.
Every stage is journaled first (`setup_record.json` `postgres_upgrade`);
the record names the server about to be on the port before any server stops,
and the guard's `DatabaseServiceWatch` leaves the service alone while the
journal says `switching` (at most `DBSVC_UPGRADE_HOLD_S` =
`postgres_upgrade.SWITCH_HOLD_S`), so the watch never starts the old one. A
failed copy starts Kazma again on the old server; a failed switch is undone
(`undo_steps`: the new stopped, off the boot list and back on its spare
port; the old back on the boot list and started); a run killed in the switch
is undone by the next run first. Gates: `tests/test_postgres_upgrade.py` (a
fake Windows machine whose services keep their own ports and states: the
order, each failure, a killed switch, the repair rule, each platform's
switch; the run without the undo as the negative control),
`tests/test_postgres_upgrade_real.py` (real 16 and 18 servers, opt-in
`KAZMA_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_BIN`; a partial restore as the control). Drilled end to
end on the Windows drill VM (`scripts/postgres_upgrade_drill.py`: 16 set up by
the code before, seeded, upgraded, 12 checks; passed 2026-11-13,
`docs/audits/evidence/postgres_upgrade_drill_2026_11_13.json`). Its first runs
found three faults, each fixed with a test: the Postgres setup's runner lacked
the winget package-list repair (`setup._do_setup_step`), uv was looked for on
PATH only (`kazma_core/uv_cli.py`, `find_uv`: also `~/.local/bin`, where setup
puts it; a uv environment has no pip), and the finish waited for a Kazma that
was not running.
**Compose deployments** (`kazma_core/postgres_compose_upgrade.py`,
`scripts/pg_compose_upgrade.py`): `docker-compose.postgres.yml` and
`docker-compose.ha.yml` run 18 on a volume of its own (`kazma_pgdata18`,
mounted at `/var/lib/postgresql`, the 18 image's layout), with 16's
`kazma_pgdata` mounted read-only at `/kazma/pg16` only so the db entrypoint
refuses an empty 18 while a 16 database is there (exit 78, naming the
script; `KAZMA_PG_UPGRADING=1` lets the script's own start through): a
`docker compose up` after a pull never starts Kazma on an empty database.
The script dumps from the 16 container, or, when compose already replaced it,
from a temporary 16 server on the 16 volume (`OLD_IMAGES`); keeps the 16
container's definition in a journal beside the compose file (owner only: it
holds the password), because compose finds a service's container by labels
and removes the old one; restores into 18 and compares; any failure removes
the 18 container and its volume and makes 16 again from the kept definition
(`engine_move._create_args`). Gate: `tests/test_postgres_compose_upgrade_real.py`
(a real compose project, opt-in `KAZMA_TEST_PG_COMPOSE_UPGRADE=1`: the refused
`compose up` as the negative control, both sources, a planted restore failure
put back and then moved).

**H. WAL archiving and point-in-time restore** (A2,
`kazma_core/backup/wal_archive.py`). `archive_mode = on`, `archive_timeout =
300`, each segment copied by the OS's own copy then renamed (the server's
service account cannot run Kazma's Python). The maintenance sweep "WAL
archive" reads `pg_stat_archiver` (a failing archiver, or none archived for
15 minutes, pages `backup.wal_archive_stale`), takes a weekly base backup
(`pg_basebackup -Ft -z -X fetch`, two kept, a failed one leaves no folder),
prunes the WAL the older one no longer needs, and sends new segments and base
backups offsite (`pgwal-*`, `pgbase-*`, in order; a failed upload stops the
pass). **Each major has its own archive, base backups and offsite names**
(2026-11-13): `wal_archive.default_archive_dir(platform, major)`,
`default_base_dir(major)`, `offsite_tag(major)`, named by the record
(`base_backup_dir`, `offsite_tag`; empty on an install made before 18, which
keeps its folders). A new major numbers its segments from the start again on
the same timeline: beside 16's base backup the prune took every 18 segment
for older than that backup's start (the shared folder is the negative control
in `tests/test_postgres_upgrade.py`). `kazma restore postgres --to TIME --into DIR` lays the newest base
backup taken before TIME (`wal_archive._base_before`; a time without a zone is
this machine's) into a new folder set to replay to TIME; the live database is
never touched. It took the newest base whatever TIME was, and Postgres cannot
replay a base back to a time before it was taken. A TIME before a move to a
newer major is restored from the server it replaced
(`wal_archive.generation_for`: the record's `previous`, its archive, base
backups and programs). **Every value the restore writes into
`postgresql.auto.conf` goes through `wal_archive._conf_string`** (backslashes
and quotes doubled): the file's reader takes a backslash as an escape, and
written plain the Windows copy command read `copy
"C:ProgramDataKazmapg_wal_archive-18%f"` -- no point-in-time restore on Windows
had ever replayed past its base backup (found 2026-11-14 restoring the owner's
first 18 backup into a scratch folder). Gate:
`tests/test_setup_postgres.py` (retention, the archiver's numbers, restore and
its base, offsite order; the written file read back with Postgres's own
quoting rules, the plain writer as the negative control),
`tests/test_wal_restore_real.py` (opt-in `KAZMA_TEST_PG_UPGRADE_BIN`: a real
cluster archiving with the product's command, its base backup, rows before and
after a moment, the restore holding exactly the rows before it with archiving
off; the plain writer cannot replay on Windows),
`tests/test_resilience_postgres.py` (the archiver's numbers, outage or query
error and the move from a container, on a real Postgres; a row lost in the
move as the negative control).

**G3. The data folder: the database and the engine off Windows' own drive**
(2026-11-21, `kazma_core/data_folder.py`, `kazma_core/data_folder_move.py`).
The 19 Nov PC reset lost the database: setup put it in `C:\Program
Files\PostgreSQL\18\data`, its WAL archive in `C:\ProgramData\Kazma` and the
engine's disk in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kazma\engine`, while the install folder
(`.env`, `.kazma`, the dumps) was on another drive. Windows only.
- **One folder, chosen once, recorded** (`data_folder` in
  `setup_record.json`; `kazma setup data-folder D:\Kazma` or `kazma setup
  install --data-folder D:\Kazma`; a drive alone, `D:`, means `D:\Kazma`):
  `postgres-<major>\data`, `postgres-<major>\wal_archive`,
  `postgres-<major>\base`, `engine` (`data_folder.Layout`). Every later run,
  a repair and an upgrade (`postgres_upgrade.Upgrade.new_data_dir`) read it.
  Each folder is restricted before anything is in it, inherited rights
  removed (`data_folder.prepare_steps`: a second drive's root lets every
  signed-in user change files): SYSTEM and the administrators, the
  service's account on the data, Kazma's account (by SID, `whoami /user`) on
  the base backups and the archive.
- **Refused before anything changes** (`data_folder.folder_problem`): not
  Windows, not a full local path, a share or device path, characters the
  archive command, the installer or a service's command line cannot take
  (letters, digits, spaces, `. _ - ( )`), Windows' own drive, a drive that is
  not fixed, a `subst` drive, inside Kazma's install or data folder, too
  little free space (a new install: `FRESH_FREE_BYTES`; a move: what moves
  plus `MOVE_MARGIN_BYTES`).
- **A new cluster** is made there by the installer (`setup_plan(data_dir=)`:
  `--datadir`), its archive and base backups beside it; the record keeps
  `data_dir` (`PostgresRecord.data_dir`), and a step that writes the port
  names the folder (`port_step(..., data_dir)`, `Step.data_dir`), never
  Program Files.
- **After a reset** (the service gone, the data kept: `data_folder.
  kept_cluster_major`) setup attaches it (`setup._reattach_steps`): the
  installer's own empty cluster under Program Files (left, unused), the
  service pointed at the kept one (action `point_data_dir`: `-D` through
  `Win32_Service.Change`, the folder given to the service's account, its
  `archive_command` set on disk), then the settings and the role signing in
  with the kept database's superuser password (refused when
  `<install>/.kazma/postgres_superuser.pass` is lost). The engine's kept `ext4.vhdx` is
  registered in place (`wsl --import-in-place`, the new account granted on
  it: WSL attaches as this account, a new one after a reset). So after a
  reset `setup.cmd` is all it takes.
- **The move of an installed part** (`kazma setup data-folder FOLDER`,
  `data_folder_move.move`; `kazma setup install --data-folder` adds it as a
  step): Kazma held through its guard (`_MoveHold`), every stage journaled
  first (`data_folder_move` in the record), a part that fails put back
  (`_put_back`), a run that died put back by the next (`recover`), Kazma
  started again and seen ready. The database: the service disabled (no
  guard of any version can start it on half a copy) and stopped; the data,
  archive and base backups copied and compared file by file (path, size,
  SHA-256); the copy's `archive_command` and the service's `-D` pointed at
  it; started, and it must answer, run from the copy (`postmaster.pid`
  there) and let Kazma sign in; the record names the new folders last; the
  old ones kept. The engine: its `KazmaEngine` task disabled (its 5-minute
  trigger would start the distro), Docker stopped cleanly in it, the distro
  ended, its disk hashed, moved by WSL (`wsl --manage kazma-engine --move`,
  WSL 2.5+), hashed again, the task run, Docker must answer. Refused while
  Kazma runs under a guard without `data_folder_move` in `guard_features`
  (`_MoveHold.guard_lacks`).
- **The engine's disk is free before it moves** (live, 2026-11-21: the
  owner's move found the distro stopped, moved at once, and WSL refused
  `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`; it was put back). WSL keeps a terminated
  distro's disk attached a while. `data_folder_move._release_disk` waits
  (`DISK_FREE_WAIT_S`) until the `ext4.vhdx` opens with no sharing
  (`Machine.disk_held`, `CreateFileW` share mode 0), then shuts WSL down
  when no other distro runs (a line of `wsl -l -q --running` counts only
  when it names a registered distro) -- never under one: the move is put
  back and names it. Checked before the hash, again right before `--move`,
  and before a put-back's move.
- **Every move holds a Kazma its guard runs, not only one that answers**
  (live, 2026-11-21: run seconds after `--resume`, the guard's child still
  booting, the port alone said "not running" and nothing was paused).
  `setup._kazma_to_hold`: the port answers, or a live guard (fresh
  heartbeat) supervises this install and is not paused for something else
  -- its pause holds a booting child and a backoff alike, as `kazma
  update`'s `_ServerHold` always did. One rule for the database's move from
  a container, the Postgres upgrade, the engine's move, the data-folder
  move and `kazma migrate import`. Every product call of
  `update._is_server_running` is declared with why it never decides "nothing
  to hold" under a guard. Gate: `tests/test_move_hold_counts_a_starting_kazma.py`
  (each move's hold with a booting child; the port-only rule as the
  negative control; a planted port-only caller).
- **The guard leaves a moving part alone** for `DATA_MOVE_HOLD_S` from the
  stage's start (`data_folder_move.GUARD_HOLD_S`, held equal): its database
  watch neither starts nor pages a moving database (state `moving`), its
  engine watch does not start a moving engine (`engine_moving`). The disk
  watch reads the engine's disk where WSL has it registered
  (`docker_cli.wsl_distro_location`, `HKCU\...\Lxss`; the root conftest
  answers None for it in tests).
- Gate: `tests/test_data_folder.py` (a fake Windows: its service, icacls,
  the service change, WSL's registration and the task; real folders. Each
  refusal; the choice not read, a run that knows no folder, no comparison,
  no journal, no hash check, a fresh import over a kept disk, no move
  journaled at the guard, a move straight after the running check, a disk
  checked once and a put-back that does not wait as negative controls),
  `tests/test_data_folder_drill.py` (the drill's judging).
- **Drilled** (`scripts/data_folder_drill.py`, 2026-11-21, `passed`;
  `docs/audits/evidence/data_folder_drill/`): on the drill VM with a second
  disk, Kazma installed with PostgreSQL on C:, `kazma setup data-folder
  E:\Kazma` moved it in 30 s with Kazma held (the service ran from the copy,
  a mark written before read back, a forced WAL switch archived into the
  new archive), then PostgreSQL's own uninstaller removed it and `kazma setup
  install` attached the kept database to the new service (the mark, a new
  segment archived there). Its `fresh` mode (also `passed`): a first `kazma
  setup install --data-folder E:\Kazma` on a clean VM, the installer's
  `--datadir` under the restricted `postgres-18` folder, Kazma's data kept
  and archived there. Not drilled: the engine's move (`wsl --manage --move`
  across drives; it needs WSL on the VM).

### 21b. Every system dependency is installed by Kazma (`kazma_core/system_deps.py`)

Resilience plan K2. `kazma setup system` (`kazma_cli.setup._setup_system`)
checks Tesseract with Arabic and English, LibreOffice, ClamAV and its daily
signature refresh, the Arabic fonts, Node.js (`npx`, version 18 or later:
the shipped MCP filesystem server) and Docker (`check_all`; the finders
`documents.binaries.find_soffice` and `docker_cli.find_docker_cli`), shows the
plan for the missing ones only (`install_plan`, one table per package
manager: `PACKAGES`), asks (`-y` for a script), runs it, and records the
result beside the Postgres record (`record_system`, `setup_record.json`
"system"). Windows' Tesseract brings English only: the Arabic and English
models come from a pinned tessdata_fast release, kept only when size and
SHA-256 match (`TESSDATA`, `fetch_tessdata`). The signatures get a daily
refresh of their own (a `KazmaFreshclam` scheduled task, a launchd job, the
distribution's freshclam service). `kazma setup install` (21c) runs the
system steps of the parts it installs; `kazma doctor` lists each and names
the command. A second run changes nothing. Gate:
`tests/test_setup_system.py` (every package manager faked; nothing installed
without a yes; a tampered model refused).

**A step that fails is tried again; one that would wait is given nothing**
(the drill VM, 2026-11-06: winget answered 0x80004004 "Cancelled" 59 MB into
LibreOffice, the setup stopped there with no ClamAV or Docker, its message
was winget's progress bar read in the ANSI code page, and the owner had to
press Enter for it to go on). Each step gets `_SYSTEM_ATTEMPTS` (3) tries,
15 s apart; a failed install whose package a check finds is done
(`system_deps.installs_package` / `package_is_in`); a dependency that still
fails stops only its own later steps (`Step.dep`: Tesseract's models,
ClamAV's schedule) and the end names what is not done. Output is read as
UTF-8 with the progress lines dropped, an HRESULT shown in hex. Every
program the setup modules start says its input (`stdin=DEVNULL` or the
step's own), winget gets `--disable-interactivity`, and a Postgres client
that connects to a host gets `-w`/`--no-password` (psql asks for a refused
password on the console whatever its input is). Gates: the drill tests in
`tests/test_setup_system.py` (one attempt, as before, as the negative
control; planted calls for the input and prompt gates). **The `dev` extra
holds `kazma[test]`**: pytest's addopts name `--timeout`, and without
pytest-timeout pytest refused to start on every fresh install, `fast_test.py`
too (`tests/test_setup_extras_run_the_suite.py`, the old `dev` list as the
control); setup says pytest's own last line when it cannot collect.

**A fresh Windows's winget is repaired, and a slow download is not cut off**
(the clean VM `KazmaVMs`, 2026-11-08, reached over SSH). winget answered
0x8A15000F ("Data required by the source is missing") to every install, so
Express left out OCR, LibreOffice, ClamAV and Node.js; `winget source update`
said "Done" and changed nothing. `setup.run_system_step` reads that answer
from a winget step (`_winget_source_missing`), registers the package list's
own signed MSIX (`WINGET_SOURCE_PACKAGE`, `Add-AppxPackage`) once and runs the
step again; a repair that fails says so in the step's answer. A step had 30
minutes: at about 1 MB/s Kazma's optional packages took longer, uv was killed
mid-download and the step said "could not run". A step now has
`STEP_TIMEOUT_S` (3 h: the programs keep their own network timeouts) and one
cut off says "still running after N min, stopped". **The Visual C++ runtime
is a system dependency** (`system_deps._vcruntime_version`, registry
`VC\Runtimes\x64`, at least `VCRUNTIME_MIN` 14.40; winget
`Microsoft.VCRedist.2015+.x64`; Windows only, `WINDOWS_ONLY`/`needed_here`,
checked and installed first): a fresh Windows has none, PyTorch failed to load
c10.dll and the meaning-search model and neural OCR could not install. Earlier
VMs had it only because a winget install before the model brought it along.
Meaning search and neural OCR name it (`system=("vcruntime",)`). **The service
task names its account in full** (`WindowsIdentity::GetCurrent().Name`): the
VM's account and computer were both KazmaDrill_1, and Register-ScheduledTask
refused the bare `$env:USERNAME` ("The parameter is incorrect", UserId); over
SSH `$env:USERDOMAIN` reads WORKGROUP. Gates: the 0x8A15000F tests in
`tests/test_setup_system.py` (the runner without the repair as the negative
control, failing all three attempts),
`test_a_long_step_has_time_and_a_cut_off_one_says_so`, the runtime's version
checks there,
`test_control_without_the_runtime_meaning_search_and_neural_ocr_fail`
(`tests/test_install_modes.py`, whose bare Windows now has no runtime), and
`test_the_task_names_its_account_in_full`
(`tests/test_windows_task_registration.py`). **Setup ends with the
install's exit code**: run 1 left seven parts out and `setup.ps1` still said
"Setup Complete" and exited 0; both scripts now say "Setup Stopped Short" and
exit with it (`test_setup_scripts_end_with_the_install_s_exit_code`). Run 2
on the fixed code: all 14 Express parts, Kazma up as a service ("needs
setup"), 0 errors in its log, 43 minutes.

**A re-run of setup removes nothing** (the same day, the owner: "uv sync
always removes what is there every time it is used again"). A plain `uv sync`
makes the environment exactly the extras it names; `setup.ps1`/`setup.sh`
ran one with rag, dev and tui, so a re-run removed whatever came after (the
Postgres driver among it). Both now run `uv sync --inexact` with every
extra the venv already holds (`update.extras_in_this_environment`: import
markers and the recorded file, never the settings store), and their fix-it
hints repeat that same command; the install's own extras come from 21c's
table, never from a list in a script. No shipped `.ps1`/`.sh` runs an exact
sync, every mode's extras hold the suite, and the Postgres part holds the
Postgres driver: `tests/test_setup_extras_run_the_suite.py` (planted old
lines as controls), and the 5.1 run in `tests/test_powershell_scripts_start.py`
reads the arguments the stand-in uv received (`--inexact`, each extra once,
those the venv held).

### 21c. Express, Full or Custom: one table of parts (`kazma_core/install_components.py`)

The owner's three installs (2026-11-07, after the drill VM needed a dozen
manual steps and met about ten fresh-install bugs one at a time). `COMPONENTS`
is the one table: each part's extras, system dependencies (21b), the parts it
`needs`, what it `gives` and what Kazma `lacks` without it, whether Express
holds it. **Express** (the default) is the parts marked `express`, on the
systems a part's `express_on` names (`express_ids(os_name)`,
`components_for(..., os_name=)`; with no system named, only
the parts in Express everywhere). **Full** is the whole table (`full_ids`), never a list
kept by hand, so a part added joins Full the day it is added. **Custom** is a
checklist from Express (`toggle`: on brings what a part needs, off takes what
needs it). Every extra in pyproject.toml belongs to a part or is declared in
`EXTRA_ALIASES` with why.

`kazma setup install` (`kazma_cli/install.py`) checks every part -- the ones
not chosen too (`_check_every_part`: one already here is "Here, not chosen",
never "Left out" with what Kazma lacks; only the chosen are recorded) -- then
lists every problem it can see before anything is done (`_preflight`: disk space,
the network, an administrator terminal, and `system_deps.docker_readiness`:
virtualization off in the firmware refuses Docker and what needs it; a
Windows virtual machine is told what its host must pass through; WSL 2
missing is installed first and a restart asked for), shows one plan, asks
once (`-y` asks nothing, the mode included), and runs it: a step is tried
again, a part that still fails stops only what needs it, and the end says
what Kazma lacks for each part not installed. The extras step is `uv sync
--inexact --project <checkout>` in a checkout (the lock's versions) and each
extra's own requirements with `uv pip` elsewhere -- never `kazma[...]` by
name (AUD-029). The choice and each part's outcome are recorded
(`setup_record.json` "install"): a second run takes the recorded mode, and
a recorded Custom choice, and continues where the first stopped. Every line
said and every program's output go to `<install>/.kazma/install.log`. With
the service part installed it waits for Kazma and opens the browser (the
chat page asks for a provider key). `setup.ps1` opens its own administrator
window in a terminal (`-NoElevate`), lets uv download a Python when the
machine has none, syncs the base and hands over (`-Mode`, `-Yes`;
`setup.sh`: `--mode`, `-y`); without a terminal it passes `--packages-only`.
Gates: `tests/test_install_modes.py` (a fake Windows machine: Express end to
end and a second run that does nothing, problems said first, Full where
Docker cannot run, WSL before Docker, a failing part and what needs it, an
administrator terminal, Custom kept on a re-run; every extra covered with a
planted one as the control; Express never fails for want of Docker; the
quickstart's table equal to `COMPONENTS`).

**A problem report is one report, seen before it is sent** (2026-11-14,
REMAINING 3.1; `kazma_core/support/problem_report.py`). **Send sends the
report shown** (2026-11-15): the web holds the previewed report by id for its
asker (`problem_report.hold`/`take`, ten minutes, 409 `report_expired`), and a
chat shows every part of it before `/report send`; both collected again on
Send before. `collect` gathers the
note, where it was asked from, version/commit, system, install parts,
readiness check results, open problems' titles and the last ERROR lines of
the log; everything passes `redacted` (credentials, the home folder, emails,
IPs); no memory, document, setting or key is read, and a chat only when the
person ticks "include this chat" (`chat_session`: its last `MAX_CHAT_MESSAGES`
user and assistant messages, each cut at `MAX_CHAT_CHARS`, `_chat_excerpt`).
Every surface shows
`preview` first: the `?` beside the bell and "Report this" (`Alpine.store
('report')`, `components/report_dialog.html`, `/api/support/*`, admin),
`kazma report`, `/report` then `/report send` in a chat app (an admin's:
`changes_global_config`). `send` posts to `support.report_url` (default
`https://status.kazma.ai/v1/report`, the Kazma Watch Worker's
`src/reports.js`: size-capped, rate-limited, D1, the owner told, listed behind
Access at `/reports`), at most `MAX_PER_HOUR` an hour; anything it cannot send
is saved in `<data dir>/problem_reports/` and the person told where. It is
offered where something went wrong: a turn that failed or ended without an
answer (`turn-header-report`), stuck or failed work (the Running work card),
an error toast (its action), `/report` in the web chat (opens the dialog), and
`kazma doctor`, an unfinished setup and the guard's `--status` (when Kazma is
not healthy, `REPORT_HINT`) name `kazma report`; the dialog's Save
to file keeps the report shown. Gates:
`tests/test_problem_report.py`, `tests/e2e/test_problem_report_browser.py`,
`deploy/observer/test/reports.test.mjs`.

**`kazma uninstall` takes off what setup put on, and keeps data unless
asked** (2026-11-14, REMAINING 2.5; `kazma_cli/uninstall.py`). One plan
(`build_plan`), shown and accepted before anything runs: Kazma stopped through
its guard; the service (`install_service.py --uninstall`, the `KazmaAgent`
task ended first); `KazmaFreshclam` / the macOS signature job; the containers
setup made (`container_services._image_state` says which: never another's,
volumes only with `--remove-data`); Kazma's engine
(`container_engine_setup.remove`, with its own refusal); `.venv` (Windows:
deleted by a detached `cmd` once Python has exited, started through
`Machine.spawn` so a test starts nothing). Data and Kazma's home are
kept; `--remove-data` MOVES them to `<home>/Kazma-uninstalled-<date>` -- first
backing up Kazma's database on the PostgreSQL setup installed (`pg_dump -Fc`
into the data folder) and then dropping it and its role (`_database`; a backup
that fails drops nothing) -- and only
`--purge` deletes (typed `delete`). PostgreSQL, system programs, fonts, uv and
the source folder are kept and named with their removal commands. **A service
that starts another folder is never taken** (`_service_folder`: the task XML's
`WorkingDirectory`, the systemd unit's or plist's guard path), nor the pieces
the computer shares while it exists: live 2026-11-14 a dry run from the dev
checkout planned to end and delete the live install's `KazmaAgent`. Gate:
`tests/test_uninstall.py` (that witness, admin refusals, nothing before the
plan is accepted, data moved not deleted).

**The setup scripts pass install options through, and CI installs from
scratch** (2026-11-14, REMAINING 2.2): `./setup.sh ... -- <options>` and
`setup.cmd ... -InstallOptions "<options>"` (split at spaces: `-File` hands
every argument over as one string; not `-InstallArgs`, which PowerShell would
read as the script's own `$installArgs`) reach `kazma setup install`. The CI
job `fresh-install` runs them on clean Ubuntu and Windows runners (Express
without `meaning_search` and `neural_ocr`; Windows also without the container
parts, no virtualization there), then `setup install --check` and Kazma's
`/health/live` and `/health/ready` on its port. **setup.ps1's administrator
window gets every parameter** (2026-11-19: it reopened itself with `-Mode`,
`-Yes`, `-Port` and `-Debug` and dropped `-InstallOptions`, so the owner's
Full install with three `--without` installed all three): the options go
single-quoted inside the window's one double-quoted `-Command`. Gate:
`tests/test_setup_passes_install_options.py` (each script's own parsing run;
every parameter in the elevation block, the old block as the control; the
built command run as Start-Process runs it).
**A clean Linux machine is drilled end to end** (REMAINING 2.3,
`scripts/linux_drill.py`, run from Windows): a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 WSL distro
of its own (`kazma-linux-drill`, Ubuntu's image checked against its
`SHA256SUMS`, systemd and lingering on), `./setup.sh --mode express -y` at a
given commit, a reboot (Kazma back by itself), `kazma update` to `main`,
`kazma uninstall` (service and `.venv` gone, port closed, data kept). It
leaves out the model downloads and the container parts: every WSL distro
shares one network with Kazma's engine. Passed 2026-11-14 (fc01c83a7 to
de5d671ce). Gate: `tests/test_linux_drill.py` (its parts and options exist).

**Private search and the memory graph install by default** (the owner,
2026-11-13, reversing "Express stays container-free" of 2026-11-12, decided
with Fable's review). `docker`, `private_search` and `graph_neo4j` are in
Express on Windows and Linux (`express_on`); macOS Express stays
container-free (Docker Desktop starts only at a sign-in there); the locked
document worker stays in Full. They are `best_effort`: a part the computer
cannot have (virtualization off, Docker already in another WSL distro, no
compose definition on a wheel install) is said with what Kazma lacks
(`_say_unavailable`) and the install still ends `EXIT_DONE`; a step that fails
is still `EXIT_NOT_DONE`. Before, any blocked part ended every run "stopped
short". Windows waiting for its WSL restart ends `EXIT_RESTART` (3), which
setup.ps1/setup.sh say as "restart, then run setup again". A part left out by
name is recorded (the install record's `without`) and a plain re-run keeps it out, so
Express gaining a part never installs one the owner declined.
- **Container services are one table** (`kazma_core/container_services.py`):
  each row names the part, its compose file and service, the container, the
  secrets setup generates into the install's `.env` before it starts (kept
  when set; compose reads the same file with `--env-file`), what Kazma is told
  to reach it (`kazma_env`, written into `.env`) and the address that answers
  once it is ready. `build_plan` makes the same four steps for every row
  (secret, `compose up`, point Kazma at it, wait for it) and `_check_parts`
  judges every row the same way; an install whose Kazma already reaches the
  service through its own settings (the SearXNG address setting, the memory
  graph's Neo4j provider) is judged by them, so setup never starts a second copy.
  With Kazma already running, the plan ends by asking the guard to reload it
  when idle (`.env` is read at start). A new service is a row and a compose
  definition. Neo4j runs from `deploy/docker-compose.neo4j.yml` (project
  `kazma-graph`, `KAZMA_NEO4J_PASSWORD` required, heap and page cache bounded,
  `KAZMA_NEO4J_HEAP` / `KAZMA_NEO4J_PAGECACHE`); Kazma uses it through
  `KAZMA_NEO4J_URL` and `KAZMA_NEO4J_DEFAULT=1` (`memory.backends`, SQLite
  stays the source of truth, Neo4j the dual-written copy).
- **The Neo4j setup made answers to setup's password**
  (`memory.backends._apply_neo4j_env_defaults`, 2026-11-20). For the
  container setup made -- `KAZMA_NEO4J_DEFAULT` on and the stored graph
  address the same Neo4j on this machine as `KAZMA_NEO4J_URL`
  (`_same_local_server`: loopback names, the same port) -- the password
  (and user) in `.env` win over the settings. A restore carried the old
  machine's password into the settings, the new container refused it, and
  every graph sync failed "the sign-in was refused". A Neo4j the owner
  chose elsewhere keeps the password stored for it. Gate:
  `tests/test_neo4j_setup_password_wins.py` (the old fill-empty-only rule as
  the control).
- **No service sends usage data home**: the Neo4j compose sets
  `NEO4J_dbms_usage__report_enabled=false` (Neo4j's default reports;
  `tests/test_container_services.py` holds every row to it, a Neo4j without
  the setting as the control).
- **Every image a shipped compose file runs is pinned by version and digest**
  (SearXNG, Neo4j, Postgres, nginx; a locally built image is the exception),
  and Dependabot's `docker-compose` ecosystem proposes updates.
- **Settings -> Packages names the parts Express gained** after an install
  ran (`install_overview(..., os_name)` `new_in_express`, without the parts
  left out by name) with `kazma setup install`; `kazma update` never installs
  them (administrator rights, about 1 GB, a possible Windows restart).
Gates: `tests/test_install_modes.py` (Express on Windows with the engine,
SearXNG and Neo4j; virtualization off ends done, the same table without
`best_effort` as the control; the WSL restart then a finishing run; `--without`
kept; an older Express record gaining the parts; a running Kazma reloaded),
`tests/test_container_services.py` (every row against its compose file, a
drifted row and an unpinned image as controls).

**Kazma's port is chosen at install and asked for in one place** (the owner,
2026-11-13; `kazma_core/server_port.py`, `kazma_cli/port_setup.py`). Before,
9090 was written out in some twenty places, most reading the shell's
`KAZMA_PORT` alone: a port kept in `.env` reached the server and not a
`kazma` command from another shell, and the guard probed its first port until
it was restarted.
- **One answer**: `server_port.server_port` -- the shell's `KAZMA_PORT`, else
  the install's `.env` files (`env_file_ladder(include_cwd=False)`, the most
  specific last; one key read), else `DEFAULT_PORT` (9090). The CLI's clients,
  `kazma serve`, `kazma-web`, the OAuth redirect addresses, the IDE note, the
  importer and the local API ask it; the guard keeps a standard-library copy
  (`install_port`, which now reads Kazma's home `.env` too), held equal on every
  layout.
- **`port_problem`** says why a port cannot be Kazma's: below 1024, one of
  Kazma's own services (`KAZMA_SERVICE_PORTS`), the guard's broker range
  (`BROKER_RANGE`; the broker also never takes Kazma's port), a range Windows
  keeps (`netsh ... show excludedportrange`, read only), or another listener
  (a bind and a connect). The port this install's Kazma holds is its own.
- **The install** (`--port N`; `setup.ps1 -Port`, `setup.sh --port`): a first
  install asks once after the mode (Enter keeps 9090), `-y` takes 9090 or the
  first usable port after it (said), a port already set -- or an install from
  before the record that answers on 9090 -- is kept and never asked; the choice
  is written as `KAZMA_PORT` after the go-ahead. `--port` on an installed Kazma
  moves it and reloads it through the guard when idle.
- **`kazma setup port [N] [--check]`** shows it, checks a port, or keeps a new
  one, reloads when idle, and names what still points at the old port
  (`KAZMA_PUBLIC_URL`, a cloudflared configuration, sign-in redirect addresses,
  bookmarks).
- **The guard reads the port again before every start** (`Guard._follow_port`,
  `guard.port_changed`), and a reload waits on the address the guard probes now
  (`_recorded_health`).
- `ui.port` and `ui.host` in kazma.yaml were read by nothing and are retired.
Gates: `tests/test_server_port.py` (the two copies on every layout, each refusal,
the install and the command, the guard following the port; no product code
writing 9090 outside the two definitions, a planted one as the control; the
install without its port step as the control).

**Windows setup starts from `setup.cmd`** (the clean drill VM, 2026-11-07):
a Windows client's PowerShell execution policy is Restricted until someone
changes it, so the README's `.\setup.ps1` was refused before its first line
("running scripts is disabled on this system"). `setup.cmd` is a batch file,
which the policy does not cover: it changes to its own folder and starts
Windows PowerShell with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` for that one process,
passing arguments and the exit code through; no setting is changed, and a
Group Policy still wins. Every published instruction (README in both
languages, the docs, setup.ps1's own messages) names `setup.cmd`, and
`*.cmd` is checked out CRLF whatever the clone's `core.autocrlf` says. Gate:
`tests/test_windows_setup_command.py` (run under a Restricted process policy;
`powershell -File setup.ps1` refused there, and a setup.cmd that does not
change folder, as the negative controls).

**Setup runs nothing it has not checked** (2026-11, supply chain). setup.ps1
piped `https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1` into `Invoke-Expression` (in the
administrator window it opens) and setup.sh piped `install.sh` into `sh`:
each ran whatever that address served. Both install ONE uv release
(`$UvVersion` / `UV_RELEASE`, equal) from uv's GitHub release, with the
SHA-256 of each platform's archive written in the script (uv's own `.sha256`
files, which GitHub's asset digests matched), checked before anything is
unpacked; a mismatch stops setup with both hashes. setup.ps1's download,
hash and unzip are .NET calls (`Save-UvArchive`, `Get-Sha256Hex`,
`Expand-UvArchive`): 5.1 started from a PowerShell 7 terminal cannot load
`Get-FileHash`. uv goes to `~/.local/bin` (Windows: also the user PATH, as
uv's installer did). The pip and snap fallbacks are gone. A new uv release
means new hashes in both scripts. Every Dockerfile starts `FROM` a digest
(`@sha256:`), and Dependabot's `docker` ecosystem watches each folder with
one. Gate: `tests/test_setup_downloads_verified.py` (no shipped script pipes
a download into a shell, every `FROM` pinned, one uv release with a hash per
platform; the real install functions cut out of each script and run on a
local archive: a match installed, a mismatch refused before unpacking; the
old installer lines and a bare tag as negative controls).

**What the install shows** (the owner, after the clean VM's first run,
2026-11-07: some 60 lines before one question, no version, and the mode
question answered by an Enter left in the console). The setup scripts open
with the version and commit and the first sentence of
`docs/docs/guide/what-is-kazma.md`; `kazma setup install` starts with
`_header` (`get_version()`) and, when installing, says only a summary by
part name (`_say_summary`): every part's state, what each part left out
lacks and every step's command go to the install log (`--dry-run` and
`--check` print them). `setup._ask` drops what was typed ahead before it
asks a person (`_drop_typeahead`). Colours are Kazma's royal blue and darker
green, amber and red (`_TONES`, setup.sh's 256-colour codes, setup.ps1's
24-bit originals), never a terminal's bright yellow, cyan or white, and none
off a terminal or with `NO_COLOR`; the log is plain. Gates in
`tests/test_install_modes.py` (the summary, the typed-ahead keys with a
question answered by code as the control, the colours, the scripts' fading
colours with the old ones as the control, the intro read from the page).

**The install downloads the meaning-search model** (the clean VM's first
start downloaded 4.3 GB before Kazma answered at all: 5.5 minutes, nothing
on screen). The `meaning_search` part is in place only with its model on
disk (`embedder.local_model_downloaded`, local cache only), and the plan
downloads it (`embedder.download_local_model`, the server's own loader).
The end's wait for Kazma counts the time each try takes (`_finish`: a
refused connection takes about 2 s on Windows, and 240 s became 325 s).
Gates: `tests/test_install_modes.py` (the model there as the control; the
old count of 48 tries).

**The shipped embedding model is pinned to one commit** (2026-11, supply
chain): `embedder.DEFAULT_MODEL_REVISION` (`refs/main` of every install's
cache, so nothing downloads again), passed by every load, download and cache
check through `embedder._model_revision`; without it the Hugging Face libraries
follow the repository's `main`. A model the owner configured that Kazma does
not ship loads unpinned unless they give one (`KAZMA_EMBED_REVISION`,
`memory.embedding.revision`); a remote config that falls back to the local
model takes the pin, never the remote model's revision. Never change the
pinned commit without re-embedding (the vectors are that commit's). Gate:
`tests/test_embedding_model_pinned.py` (every `SentenceTransformer(` /
`snapshot_download(` call in product code and scripts names `revision=`; the
old unpinned lines as the negative control).

### 21d. The setup guide (`/setup`, `kazma-ui/kazma_ui/setup_api.py`)

The owner, after a clean Windows install (2026-11-07): "why there is no Web
UI setup guide". The first visit had one card (a provider list, a key, a
model name to type), and on a fresh install it never showed:
`compute_setup_status` counted any LISTED local provider as set up, and every
install lists Ollama and LM Studio.
- **Ready means a model Kazma can use**: the active provider has a key or is
  a local server, or another provider has a key (Kazma falls back to it, and
  says so). A listed local server counts only as the provider in use.
- **The guide** (`templates/setup.html`, `static/js/setup_guide.js`, catalog
  slice `setup.*`, EN/AR): welcome (the first sentence of What Kazma is, the
  language), the model, optional extras, done. The installer's last step
  opens it (`kazma_cli.install._finish`); the chat page's card, Settings ->
  Providers & Connectors and the page search open it.
- **Choosing the model**: a cloud provider whose key is all it needs
  (`guided`; `custom`, Azure and Bedrock are Settings', `_NOT_GUIDED`), a
  local server (`/api/setup/local`: loopback `/models`, no proxy, 2 s, nothing
  saved), or a server on another computer of the network
