  (`/api/setup/local/address`: only an address on the owner's network,
  `ssrf.resolves_to_own_network`; saved as `server-<host>-<port>`, no key).
  Nothing is saved before the model answered (providers stage 1, §60):
  `/api/setup/models` lists the models with the key as typed and
  `/api/setup/check` sends the chosen model one message through the client
  chat would build (`kazma_core.provider_check`), then `/api/setup/bootstrap`
  saves the provider (an empty key keeps the stored one; an address set in
  Settings stays) and switches model AND provider (§1). Errors are codes the
  page words (`setup.err.*`), never the provider's reply text.
- **The models found are a list on screen** (2026-11-19): a `<select>`
  (`#setup-model`, values `m:<model>` so no model name is taken for "Another
  model") with "Another model" for a typed name (`#setup-model-name`,
  `pickModel`); Settings -> X's model the same (`xReplyPickModel`). They were
  a `<datalist>`, which shows nothing until the box is clicked and then only
  the names matching what it holds: the owner's fresh install said "3 models
  found. Pick one from the list" over no list. No page holds a datalist
  (`tests/test_no_hidden_lists.py`, a planted one as the control).
- Everything but `/api/setup/status` is admin (`platform_rbac._ADMIN_PREFIXES`).
- **A switch ends a stale fallback notice**
  (`model_fallback.report_provider_chosen`, from both switches in
  `runtime/model_switch`): saving a provider before switching let Kazma fall
  back from the shipped placeholder, and that notice closed only when the
  placeholder got a key.
- **Settings -> Packages reads the install's record**
  (`install_components.install_overview`, `annotate_extras`): the mode and
  date, an extra of a part left out "Not chosen" (never Missing or Partial),
  and `kazma setup install --with <part>` as each extra's command. **A part
  the last run could not put in place is said** (2026-11-19: the owner's
  fresh Full install had no Docker, SearXNG, Neo4j or document worker, and
  every row was green -- the page listed Python extras, and Neo4j's driver
  was installed): the route's install data names them (`not_in_place`) in a
  warning (`#pkg-not-in-place`), and an extra whose packages are here while
  its part is not (`part_missing`) is a warning badge, never "Installed"
  (`pkgExtraBadge`). Only a recorded `ok:
  false` counts; a record that says nothing of a part is no failure.
Gates: `tests/test_setup_guide.py` (each with the old behaviour as its
control), `tests/e2e/test_setup_guide_browser.py` (a fresh install's chat
card to a working model on a stand-in Ollama, three models listed, one
picked, then "Another model" typed; Settings to the guide in Arabic),
`tests/js/test_x_reply_model_picker.js`, `tests/js/test_packages_not_in_place.js`,
`tests/e2e/test_packages_not_in_place_browser.py` (EN/AR, by the sidebar).

### 21e. The Windows installer and release installs (REMAINING 2.7, 2026-11-16)

Kazma installs on Windows with no git and no terminal, as a third install
type beside a git checkout and a wheel install.
- **The installer** (`scripts/windows_installer/`: `kazma.iss`, Inno Setup
  6.7.4 pinned by SHA-256 in `build.py`) is built in the release workflow's
  `windows-installer` job from the source archive the `build` job made
  (`kazma-<version>.tar.gz`, the archive every release signs). `build.py`
  reads it with the updater's own rules (`release_tree.shipped_files`) and
  writes the release marker beside the files. Installed to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kazma` (admin, asked once), it runs the same
  `setup.cmd -Mode express|full -Yes -NoElevate` a clone runs; setup's
  `EXIT_RESTART` (3) leaves a RunOnce entry that runs setup again at the
  next sign-in. Shortcuts: Kazma (`kazma open`, the configured port), Update,
  Finish or repair setup. Uninstall runs `kazma uninstall --yes` (data kept).
- **A release install** is that folder: `.kazma-release.json` at its root
  names the release and the files it shipped (`kazma_cli/release_tree.py`).
  `update.detect_install_type` answers `"release"` for it first (it is
  installed editable, so it looked like a checkout); `update._install_root`
  is the one answer to "this install's folder" (a checkout's or a release
  install's), used wherever the updater located itself by `.git`.
  `kazma update` there (`do_release_update`) downloads the next release's
  source archive under the wheel's rules (`_source_archive`: named for the
  version, in SHA256SUMS and equal to GitHub's digest, Sigstore-signed from
  SIGNED_FROM on), lays it over the tree (`release_tree.apply_archive`:
  replaces and removes shipped files only, never `release_tree.KEPT` or the
  owner's own files, every moved file backed up first), installs the locked
  packages held (`_reinstall_via_subprocess`), and on a refused or failed
  install rolls the tree back and reinstalls its packages.
- **Signing** is one shared step, `.github/actions/sign-windows-installer`
  (2026-11-22), with the service the repository variable
  `KAZMA_WINDOWS_SIGNING` names: `signpath` (SignPath Foundation), `ssl-com`
  (SSL.com eSigner) or `artifact-signing` (Microsoft, OIDC). Changing service
  is that variable and the new service's secrets (`docs/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` "The
  Windows installer's signature"); any other value fails before anything is
  sent; a signed installer must read Valid and timestamped or the job fails;
  unset, the run says it is unsigned. The manual workflow
  `windows-signing-test.yml` signs a program it builds, never a release file,
  through the same step in its test environment (SSL.com's sandbox,
  SignPath's test-signing policy) and publishes nothing. No workflow names a
  signing action outside the shared step. The installer is also checksummed,
  attested and Sigstore-signed with the rest.
- Gates: `tests/test_release_install.py` (a failure half way and each refusal
  leave the tree as it was; without `KEPT` an archive replaces `.env`, the
  control), `tests/test_windows_installer.py`, the release gates reading the
  three jobs in order (`tests/test_release_supply_chain.py`). Drill:
  `scripts/windows_installer_drill.py` (a clean VM: install, restart, health,
  `update --check`, shortcuts, uninstall keeping the data).

### 22. Agent Skills Ecosystem (`kazma-core/kazma_core/agent_skills/`)

Kazma is a first-class citizen of the open **agentskills.io** `SKILL.md`
ecosystem — it can install, run, and publish skills that also work in Claude
Code, Cursor, Codex, etc. Four modules; understanding them is essential before
touching skill loading.

**A. Parser + spec (`parser.py`).** `SKILL.md` = YAML frontmatter + markdown
body. Required fields per the spec: **`name`** + **`description`** only.
`version` is OPTIONAL — do not re-introduce a "missing required field: version"
warning (it spam-listed every ecosystem skill). `validate_manifest` enforces
name+description and is the single gate.

**B. Discovery scopes (`discovery.py`).** `skill_base_dirs()` returns
`(scope, path)` pairs, lowest → highest precedence:
`bundled` (shipped with Kazma) → `user` (`~/.agents/skills` + Kazma/Claude/
Cursor compat dirs) → `project` (`<root>/.agents/skills`, `skills/`, …).
Project overrides user overrides bundled on name collision. The `bundled`
scope is `kazma_core/agent_skills/bundled/` — 3 Kazma-native starter skills.

**C. Integrity — two paths, do not flatten.**
- **User/project skills** (`integrity.py`): HMAC-SHA256 signed at install time
  (keyed by `KAZMA_SECRET`); activation verifies checksum+signature, **fail-closed** on tamper, warn-only on unsigned.
- **Bundled skills** (`catalog._verify_bundled_skill`): verified against the
  committed `bundled/checksums.json` (SHA-256 per skill); a bundled skill NOT
  listed in the manifest fails closed. Adding a bundled skill ⇒ regenerate
  `checksums.json` (see the generator at the bottom of the bundled dir's git
  history) or it won't activate.
- **Every surface shows activation's verdict** (`catalog.skill_integrity`,
  2026-10-02): `verified`, `unsigned` (loads with a warning) or `refused`
  (with the reason, which names `kazma agent-skills sign <folder>`). The
  model's catalog leaves a refused skill out and says so; the list tool, the
  CLI's `list` and the Skills page show the state. They used to call any
  recorded checksum "verified": live, nine skills another key had signed were
  offered to the model and refused at activation. The page shows a security
  score only where a manifest declares one (none does; it showed an invented
  "100/100"). `sign` takes several folders. Only activation logs a refusal
  (`verify_skill(warn=False)` logs nothing above DEBUG): the catalog is built
  every turn and logged each refused skill each time. `tests/test_skill_integrity_shown.py`.

**D. Activation always fences the body** (`catalog.format_skill_activation`):
the SKILL.md body is wrapped in `format_untrusted_block(source="agent_skill:…")`
— it is GitHub-sourced text, data-not-instructions. Never inject a skill body
raw into the system prompt.

**E. Install with no Node/npm** (`installer.py`). `install_from_any(source)`
handles `owner/repo`, full GitHub URLs, `tree/branch/path`, git URLs, local
paths, and `npx skills add …` strings — downloads the GitHub zipball via httpx.
`rglob("SKILL.md")` so multi-skill repos install all skills. One HITL approval
covers an install (the user is the gate for what enters the system).

**F. Marketplace search** (`tools.search_agent_skills` + `/api/skills/marketplace/search`):
GitHub `topic:agent-skills` repository search (GITHUB_TOKEN-aware for rate
limits). The `/skills` page has a Marketplace tab (debounced search + one-click
install). Do not build a parallel registry — the GitHub topic IS the index.

**G. The Skills page's switch is real** (`kazma_core/skills/switches.py`,
2026-09-28). `skills.enabled.<id>` was written and never read: a built-in
skill switched off kept its tools and was listed on again. A native skill's
tools carry `LocalTool.skill_id` (`native:<folder>`, set by the native
loader); a switched-off skill's tools are left out of
`get_tool_definitions` and refused by `_execute_inner`. The switches are
read once per settings store (weak reference, not `id()`) and updated by the
page's toggle, so no model call reads settings. Built-in skills cannot be
uninstalled (400; the page shows the switch only). Marketplace ("hub")
skill installs are not built: `kazma hub install` and the page refuse
("not implemented", 501) instead of reporting an empty install (audit
2026-10-26 AUD-074, `tests/test_hub_install_refuses.py`).
`tests/test_skill_switches.py`. **Settings → Skills uses the same routes**
(2026-10-01): it posted to `/api/settings/skills/*`, which wrote
`skills.<name>.enabled` (read by nothing) and "uninstalled" any skill,
built-in ones included, by writing it; those routes are gone, the tab posts
the skill's id to `/api/skills/toggle` and `/api/skills/uninstall` and shows
Uninstall only for a skill that is not built in
(`tests/js/test_settings_skill_controls.js`). The toggle is admin-only, like
install and uninstall, and a failure answers 500.

**H. The skill folders in the home come from one place**
(`discovery.skills_home()`, 2026-10-01): `.agents/skills`, Claude's and
Cursor's folders and the legacy `.kazma/agent-skills` are all under it, and
`KAZMA_SKILLS_HOME` moves it (a service account reading the operator's
skills). The root conftest pins it, as it pins the data dir: the live install
runs as the same user and reads those folders, an install writes there and an
uninstall removes from there. `uninstall_skill(target_dir=...)` removes from
that folder only -- it also removed the name from the real `~/.kazma`, so
the uninstall test could delete a developer's skill. Gates:
`tests/test_install_data_shield.py` (every skill folder under the test temp
folders; only `skills_home()` reads the home; negative control without the
pin), `tests/test_agent_skills.py`.

### 23. Windows asyncio.subprocess trap (`SelectorEventLoop`)

The Kazma server runs a **`SelectorEventLoop`** (`kazma_core/eventloop.py` —
forced because psycopg async refuses the Proactor loop, and Postgres-backed
checkpoints must persist on Windows). On Windows the selector loop **does not
implement subprocess transports**: `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` /
`create_subprocess_shell` raise `NotImplementedError`. This is a recurring
footgun — every tool that spawns a subprocess must avoid the bare asyncio API.

**The rule:** on the server loop, spawn subprocesses via
**`asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.run, …)`** (blocking, bounded) or
**`asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.Popen, …)`** (non-blocking start). The MCP
manager (`mcp/manager.py`) already has an explicit `NotImplementedError` →
Popen fallback — mirror that.

**Known-correct sites (keep them):**
- `system/installer.py`, `system/runtime_manager.py`, `telemetry.py`,
  `models/discovery.py`, `agent/tool_builtins/system.py:shell_exec` — all use
  `to_thread` + `subprocess`.
- **Playwright**: the browser tools (`kazma_skills/native/browser_automation`)
  run on the **sync API inside `to_thread`**; the heavier crawl/fetch paths
  (`knowledge_ingest.py`, `read_url.py`) route through
  `kazma_core/playwright_loop.py` (a dedicated ProactorEventLoop daemon thread).
  Do NOT revert these to the async Playwright API on the server loop.
- `security.process_budget.run_bounded_async` shields and joins its worker
  receipt on cancellation, including repeated cancellation. Setting a threading
  event alone cannot acknowledge that the native process tree/pipes have ended.
  Keep the join; `tests/test_process_budgets.py` holds real cleanup open and runs
  the old return-before-cleanup boundary as a negative control.

**Symptom of a regression:** a tool reports `error=False` in 0 ms while doing
nothing, and the log shows `Task exception was never retrieved …
NotImplementedError` from `playwright/_impl/_transport.py` or
`asyncio/base_events.py`. That means someone re-introduced
`create_subprocess_exec` on the server loop.

### 24. Import Integrity + Web Acquisition SoT + CSRF/Rate-Limit (2026-08-14 audit round)

**A. Import-integrity gates — `tests/test_imports.py` (deletion SOP).**
- Three tests: `test_every_product_module_imports` (imports every module
  of every `kazma-*/kazma_*` package), `test_no_dangling_kazma_import_references`
  (AST scan: every `kazma_*` import reference must resolve to a real file)
  and `test_every_imported_kazma_name_exists` (every `from kazma_x.mod
  import name` names something `mod` defines at its top level).
  **No try/except exemption for Kazma's own modules** (removed 2026-09-26):
  the module is in this repo, so the import resolves or it is dead code, and
  the `except` makes it a feature that is silently off. Six were: the
  Knowledge Library's meaning search (`memory.chroma_client`, deleted
  2026-07-31, reported as "chromadb not installed"), the gateway's §25
  Partial handling and its budget counter (one removed name,
  `record_budget_exhausted`, sank the three imported beside it), kazma.yaml's
  `agent.nonstop` (a `load_config` that never existed), the `/memory` count
  and a health helper nothing called. Only a third-party package may be
  optional.
- Born from the crawl.py incident: a module deletion left a dangling import
  in `web_acquire/__init__` — py_compile passed (syntax-only), no test
  imported the package, production research broke at first use
  (`ModuleNotFoundError`). **Rule: deleting a module requires green
  `tests/test_imports.py` in the SAME commit, and importers removed in the
  same change.** Optional pre-commit hook: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- **Every product module also imports ON ITS OWN**, in a fresh interpreter
  (`scripts/check_fresh_imports.py`, CI job "Every module imports on its
  own"). The one-process gate above cannot see an import cycle that works
  only when entered at the right module: each import finds the earlier ones
  loaded. `kazma_core.routing_engine` was one until 2026-09-26 -- the swarm
  package's `__init__` imports it, and it imported `kazma_core.swarm.task`
  back at module level. A module that a package's `__init__` imports must
  not import that package at module level; take annotation-only types under
  `TYPE_CHECKING` and the rest at call time. Both gates walk one list
  (the script's `iter_modules`).
- `tools/read_url.fetch_result` is the public typed ladder entry point used by
  `web_acquire.fetch_text`. `fetch_full_text` remains a public legacy text
  adapter (alias of `_fetch_full_text`); neither starts a second ladder.
  Product consumers use `FetchResult.ok`/`error_code`, never an `Error:`
  prefix in extracted text. `save_url_extract` returns a typed atomic-save
  result to research; it is not a registered agent tool. The chat/chunk tools
  fence remote text at the model boundary; internal typed bodies stay raw.

**B. Web acquisition — ONE egress stack.**

2026-10-12 additions (supersede older open-work descriptions below):
- Session process owners reconcile to interrupted; explicit session resume links
  the original durable job and restores verified terminal output without replay.
  History is bounded to 256 rows/128MiB; archive does not release storage.
  Chat `web_search` snapshots (`record_chat_research`, depth `chat`) have their
  own 1024 rows/32MiB: sharing the research allowance, 349 of the live 361
  rows were chat searches and Deep Research refused to start (2026-10-31).
- Origins/robots persist via shared ConfigStore CAS with finite tables and
  fail-closed clock/storage behavior. Fixed sync search and native HTTP share
  origin feedback. Opaque DDGS SDK fanout is skipped, not silently unmetered.
- Durable research snapshots explicit-key/local clients and failover routes;
  ambient AWS/Google ADC are refused. Configuration hashes include all provider
  coordinates and relevant environment; only digests are persisted.
- Native automation uses the contained owner/broker, joined cancellation and
  workspace/tenant identity. Supported form bodies are bounded; uploads refused.
  Strict OS network mode defaults required. Windows refuses strict launch;
  Linux requires a verified isolated network namespace plus cgroup controls.
  Explicit compatibility mode is labelled weaker and never attested as isolated.
- Retained pipeline reports have a separate 3GiB allowance: 512MiB reserved for
  each of the four research runs admission lets in, plus a 1GiB settled share
  (`artifact_storage._LIMIT`, FA-266: 2GiB held exactly four reservations, so
  the fourth admitted run failed after its session row existed). Storage is
  checked in the same admission that answers 503 (`artifact_storage.admit`,
  from `research_runtime._frozen`, before a row or a plan); readiness shows
  settled bytes and running reservations apart. Bounded legacy inventory and
  no automatic deletion; not a whole-install quota.
  Gate: `tests/test_research_storage_sized_with_admission.py`.
- Settings/CLI/TUI explicit credit actions use the same provider adapter; cached
  reads never refresh. Jina token budget is finite; unsupported monetary caps
  refuse dispatch. Never describe reservations/tokens as charges.
- Gates: test_acquisition_durable_controls.py, test_browser_acquisition_broker.py,
  test_research_pipeline_recovery.py and existing provider/origin/robots gates.
  Full suite authorized after implementation on 2026-10-12; run conservatively.

- SoT ladder: `tools/read_url.fetch_result` → `_bounded_fetch_result` →
  `_fetch_full_text_impl` (SSRF-validate → httpx →
  local Chromium → explicitly permitted hosted recovery), built on
  `proxy.client.get_scraping_client`. `web_acquire.policy` defaults to
  `local_only`; hosted Firecrawl/Jina and scraping proxies require both
  `local_first_with_remote_fallback` and their names in the remote allowlist.
  Keys and legacy flags never grant permission; they can narrow it. KB discovery
  uses local sitemaps/llms.txt/BFS; hosted mapping is refused because the
  provider cannot enforce navigation scope. Cache entries are partitioned by
  policy AND extraction profile (generic/knowledge/discovery). The complete text ladder has a 90s deadline (operator
  range 1–300s); HTTPX network errors reach local recovery. The raw GET layer
  `web_acquire.http.fetch_public` bounds the full redirect chain separately.
  `read_capped` checks the live peer BEFORE body reads, bounds raw gzip/deflate
  expansion with zlib max_length, and refuses unsupported content encodings.
  Hosted scrape responses use the same bounded decoder through
  `read_response_capped`, after their policy gate; this decoder alone is NOT
  a public-target egress gate. Bodies default to 5MB, hard-ceiling 20MB.
  The typed result records actual final URL/status/backend/attempts/bytes,
  clipping and quality. Unknown hosted origin provenance/usage/credits remain
  null. A cache hit makes no new attempts. Partial bodies are not cached or
  indexed into KB; automated research saves refuse them. Explicit chat saves
  may publish a visibly marked partial extract. A real password input plus an
  explicit login title fails `login_required`; authentication prose/widgets
  alone do not. Gate: `tests/test_web_acquisition_results.py`.
  `web_acquire.accounting` reserves finite remote job/day requests through the
  existing ConfigStore conditional batch BEFORE HTTP/proxy effects. Failures,
  cancellation and uncertain launch retain reservations; never refund or label
  them provider charges. Defaults: 256/job, 1024/UTC day; zero refuses, active
  limits may narrow only. Fixed HTTP search reserves six requests; DDGS proxy
  search is refused because SDK request counts are opaque. HTTP hooks precede
  transport dispatch, including redirects, hosted scrape, mapping and probes.
  `web_acquire.credits` explicitly refreshes Firecrawl's team balance through
  the same allowance, account scoped/fresh five minutes, 60-second cadence.
  Status reads are local only; unsupported balances/per-request charges stay null.
  Jina's single valid `X-Usage-Tokens` header is a provider-reported response
  observation, captured durably before body consumption. Keep zero distinct
  from missing/malformed metadata. Retain observations on body failure/cancellation;
  cache reads make no new observations. Tokens never imply money or account balance.
  Gate: `tests/test_acquisition_provider_usage.py`.
  Allowance/crawl journals and their CAS revisions are RUNTIME in
  `settings_restore.KEY_RULES`; backups must never rewind spent requests or
  completed effects. Gate: `tests/test_settings_restore.py`.
  Gates: `tests/test_acquisition_accounting.py`, `tests/test_acquisition_credits.py`,
  `tests/test_acquisition_postgres.py` (opt-in disposable real database).
  Unsupported monetary bounds refuse remote dispatch. Strict browser networking
  requires the qualified Linux namespace; Windows refuses strict launch. See
  `docs/audits/WEB_ACQUISITION_IMPLEMENTATION_2026-10-10.md` for remaining gates.
  `web_acquire.crawl_jobs` persists KB ownership before Web acceptance, bounded
  page/BFS frontiers and metadata effects before fetch/indexing. One settings
  row per job (`acquisition.crawl.<digest>`, its own CAS revision; Knowledge
  audit KB-E04, 2026-10-14): a page update writes its own job only. Four
  active, 24 retained, 16 MiB, 4 MiB a job (frontier admission checks it);
  finished jobs are evicted by count AND bytes, never a running one;
  `kazma acquisition purge-finished` is the operator's purge. Owners carry
  install, host, pid, start time and a lease renewed on every write (300 s,
  KB-E07): a dead owner on this host is recovered, another host's only after
  its lease lapsed, and the taken-over owner's next write is refused; rows of
  another install are never read. **A job's writers in one process take turns**
  (`_job_lock`, `_REGISTRY_LOCK`, 2026-10-31): the compare-and-set is for other
  processes, with a random pause between its 8 attempts (`_retry_pause`).
  Racing it, a research run's four parallel fetches starved each other
  ("journal is busy" on 16% of writes with 4 writers on Postgres) and every
  live deep research failed after its searches
  (`tests/test_crawl_journal_concurrency.py`). One crawl per KB library (`CrawlLibraryBusy`,
  KB-E14); the journal is the only crawl state (`kb.ingest_jobs` and
  `stores/kb_jobs.py` retired). An explicit KB resume fetches uncertain pages
  again and skips completed ones; resume requires identical policy. Gate:
  `tests/test_knowledge_crawl_journal.py`. Metadata keeps parsed links, never raw bodies.
  Faithful identity preserves `.md`, slash, matrix parameters and query bytes;
  do not infer aliases without an observed redirect. Web recovery uses the

  Gates: `tests/test_durable_crawls.py`, `tests/test_kb_api_routes.py`,
  `tests/test_kb_recovery_browser.py` (real EN/AR Alpine plus old-state controls),
  `tests/js/test_kb_recovery.js`. `research_pipeline_job` now extends this SAME
  CAS journal (kind `research_pipeline`), owning each stage BEFORE dispatch.
  Never turn its stages into fake URL pages or store raw bodies in settings.
  Completed values/files require SHA256/size verification; running stages settle
  uncertain on interruption. Explicit `run_research_pipeline(resume_job_id=...)`
  requires identical scope: skip uncertain sources with a partial report, refuse
  failed/uncertain required stages, never blindly repeat paid/search/publication
  effects. Evidence commits before source publication. Join all sibling tasks and
  file workers before journal settlement. Stages reserve retained bytes BEFORE
  action (512MiB/job, 128 effects, 512KiB values, 24MiB/file); no disk GC is implied.
  Configuration digests are checked between stages; explicit-key/local LLM and
  failover clients are snapshotted for each pipeline. Ambient AWS/Google ADC
  routes are refused. Sessions reconcile dead owners and require explicit resume;
  history and retained reports have independent finite allowances. Gate:
  `tests/test_research_pipeline_recovery.py`
  (real SQLite fresh-process crashes, original unowned planner negative control,
  concurrent resume, file tampering, scope changes and held-worker cancellation).
  Research crawl uses the same acquired HTTP document/Chromium snapshot for
  text and links (no separate raw GET). Scope reaches the content fetch and top-level Chromium
  navigation through a per-acquisition ContextVar. Scoped reads bypass the
  cache (policy/scope enforcement must precede reuse) and refuse hosted readers
  that cannot enforce navigation scope. Do not drop the `scope_check`
  propagation in acquisition. Gate: `tests/test_web_acquisition_scope.py`.
  Chromium HTTP uses `web_acquire.browser_network` CDP Request-stage pauses,
  NOT Playwright route continuation (routes skip HTTP redirect hops). Each
  request uses bounded HTTPX through the proxy factory, public DNS validation,
  direct pinning and a live-peer check. Fulfill the actual response, preserving
  redirects/relative URLs/repeated cookies. Never continue HTTP natively.
  Public acquisition target validation uses `web_acquire.dns_worker.validate_public_url`,
  including redirects and CDP assets. Do not replace it with
  `to_thread(validate_url)`: cancellation cannot terminate a native resolver
  in a Python thread. Four owned validators / 16 queued / 10s admission share
  a separate FIFO pool; each resolver is an isolated credential-free child
  capped at 5s, 256MiB and 16KiB output (128 unique addresses / 2048 raw records).
  Check every returned address with the existing SSRF validator; excess is a
  refusal, never a truncated permission. Direct HTTP connects validated pins.
  Windows Job kill-on-close and Linux verified parent-death/kernel wall timers
  protect the child; cancellation joins its process/pipes/per-call executor.
  Uncertain cleanup retains handles and quarantines capacity in readiness;
  the next validation starts one retained cleanup thread, with `_drain_cleanup`
  for joining it. `web_acquire.endpoint_transport` uses that same owned DNS
  for async/sync proxies and hosted async connections, preserving logical HTTP,
  CONNECT and verified TLS SNI. Only an operator-selected proxy endpoint may
  resolve private; content targets still require independent public validation.
  Reject alternate transports/mounts that would bypass this boundary. Sync
  proxy HTTP refuses execution on an event loop. Legacy synchronous validation
  outside acquisition remains separate work; native automation now uses the
  same owned DNS and broker. Gates: `tests/test_endpoint_transport.py`,
  `tests/test_acquisition_dns.py`; Linux evidence in
  `docs/audits/evidence/dns_linux_boundary_2026_10_11.py`.
  HTML and sitemap XML extraction use `web_acquire.parser` owned children (15s, 768MiB,
  24MiB encoded input, 8MiB output; XML refuses DTDs/entities and bounds
  leaf/index frontiers at 4000/64 -- a larger sitemap keeps its first URLs,
  answers `limited`, and discovery is marked partial; a sitemap past the
  parser's budget is skipped, never a failed crawl: rfc-editor.org's
  sitemap-1.xml holds 6,000 URLs, 2026-10-31); do not put hostile parsing back on shared
  Python threads. `search_runtime` owns the complete backend chain/deadline;
  `search_http` bounds HTTP and parsing in a fixed child. Both use the common
  owned-worker cleanup/quarantine contract. Research crawl seed/page
  prevalidation also uses `validate_public_url`, not native resolver threads.
  Gates: `tests/test_acquisition_parser.py`, `tests/test_search_http_worker.py`,
  `tests/test_search_sdk_worker.py`, `tests/test_acquisition_dns.py`.
  `BrowserJob` owns the context and a native deny proxy; sandbox enabled, service
  workers blocked, DNS/UDP suppression are defense in depth, NOT OS network
  isolation. Fixed per-page limits: 128 intercepted requests, 4 concurrent,
  5MB per response, 32MB aggregate retained decoded bytes, 5 redirects; DOM 5M
  characters, links 2000, supported lazy tabs 12. A page's text is
  `document.PAGE_TEXT_MAX` (1M characters) for every reader -- chat, research,
  crawls, Knowledge -- on the HTTP and browser paths alike (2026-10-31: at
  100K, RFC 9110's 464K was partial, so never indexed or saved). What a model
  gets stays bounded by its reader: `read_url` windows (16K default, 100K at

  reading is 50K+, an article extract under a tenth of it is a fragment and

  7,067 of RFC 9110's characters and called it complete). Gate: the long-page
  tests in `tests/test_web_acquisition_results.py`. Refusals/failed
  resources are typed or partial; KB never indexes partial content. KB text
  and BFS use the same typed ladder, with explicit seed scope and query-safe
  identity; metadata redirects stay on the seed host. Gate:
  `tests/test_browser_acquisition_broker.py`,
  `tests/test_knowledge_acquisition_profile.py`.
  `web_acquire.resources` provides process-wide FIFO admission across caller
  threads/event loops: 2 browser owners (8 queued), 6 ordinary acquisitions
  (24 queued), and 2 reserved acquisitions for existing browser owners (8
  queued); admission waits expire at 30s within the acquisition deadline.
  Reserve owner slots to avoid deadlock when ordinary calls wait for browsers
  held by a crawler that needs its next page. Cache hits need no admission;
  saturation is a typed `resource_limit` before dispatch. The Windows bridge
  tracks the actual task and joins asynchronous finalizers before acknowledging
  cancellation/timeout, including repeated caller cancellation. A failed
  browser teardown retains/quarantines its capacity and native deny endpoint;
  readiness exposes that unhealthy capacity. The native deny endpoint admits at
  most 16 handler tasks per owner and joins them before releasing its slot.
  Close the owned page BEFORE CDP detach: a paused navigation can otherwise
  leave detach waiting indefinitely, even after its HTTP stream has closed.
  `web_acquire.browser_driver` owns Playwright's Node driver and Chromium in
  one OS boundary before untrusted browser code starts: Windows Job Objects
  (2GiB aggregate, 32 processes, approximately two logical CPUs) or delegated
  Linux cgroup v2 (2GiB memory, no swap, 256 tasks, two CPUs). Linux needs
  writable memory/pids/CPU/group-kill controls, optionally selected through
  `KAZMA_BROWSER_CGROUP_ROOT`; missing controls refuse rendering. Never launch
  an unrestricted browser or substitute per-process RLIMIT_AS. The driver gets
  a minimal environment; credentials, proxy variables and NODE_OPTIONS stay out.
  Protocol frames/queued commands are capped at 32MiB, total traffic at 512MiB.
  An independent watchdog ends the process tree on cancellation, a 30-minute
  owner lifetime or five-second cleanup grace; parent-process death also ends
  descendants (Windows kill-on-close, Linux pidfd guardian). Capacity releases
  only after OS verification of no live descendants; uncertainty quarantines it.
  The private Playwright Connection/stdio compatibility seam is isolated here,
  qualified against 1.61.0 and, 2026-10-17, 1.64.0 (35 boundary tests, real Chromium). Upgrades must pass the real-browser/boundary gates.
  **1.65 rewrote Playwright's client** (2026-11-13): `_impl._connection` is gone, and 1.65.1 failed
  every page that needed the browser (37 browser tests). `BrowserDriver.start` now wires
  `_impl.connection.Connection(loop)` to `_Transport` as Playwright's own client does
  (`onmessage` -> `send`, `on_message` -> `dispatch`, `initialize_playwright()`, `close()`);
  qualified on 1.65.1 (141 browser tests, real Chromium). pyproject holds Playwright to one
  qualified minor (`>=1.65.1,<1.66`): `kazma update` installs the newest allowed and does not
  read uv.lock, so a new minor reaches installs only after these tests pass on it.
  **A job's browser is relaunched between pages, before a limit ends it under
  one** (2026-11-13, `BrowserJob._relaunch_reason` / `_retire_impl`): when its
  tree has ended (a limit, a crash: `BrowserDriver.failure`), Chromium
  disconnected, less than `_RELAUNCH_MARGIN_S` (180 s, at most a third) of
  the lifetime or `_RELAUNCH_TRAFFIC_HEADROOM` (128 MiB) of the protocol
  budget is left, or after `_RELAUNCH_AFTER_RENDERS` (150) renders. A job
  kept its dead context before: every render after the 30-minute lifetime
  failed `resource_limit` and a long Knowledge crawl lost every page that
  needed the browser. The retire ends the old tree first and keeps the job's
  capacity lease; a cleanup it cannot verify keeps every handle quarantined
  and launches nothing (the next page tries the cleanup again). A page under
  which the browser died (`RenderedDocument.lost`: the driver's failure, a
  disconnected Chromium, Playwright's "closed"/"crashed") is rendered once
  more in the relaunched browser (`_render_in_job` -> `_render_once`), never
  a third time. Gate: `tests/test_browser_relaunch.py` (real Chromium with the
  lifetime shrunk to seconds, and a Chromium killed mid-crawl: every page
  stored; the old rule as the negative control).
  Gates: `tests/test_browser_driver_budget.py`,
  `tests/test_acquisition_resources.py` and the broker suite. This boundary does
  not constrain arbitrary Python HTTP/XML threads or all install storage,
  and is distinct from the required Linux network namespace. Native automation
  shares this contained owner, with bounded mutating HTTP. Report/standalone
  publication and Knowledge SQLite have finite allowances; vector/WAL/temp and
  arbitrary user files are outside those disk bounds. Strict Windows launch is
  refused; compatibility mode is visibly weaker.
  `web_acquire.origins` shares HTTP origin limits across jobs and event loops:
  2 live origin reservations / 32 queued per origin, 512 retained origins and
  a 30s admission/spacing deadline. Crawl/KB extraction and KB metadata request
  starts have a 300ms floor; a crawler's larger requested delay also propagates
  through rendering. HTTPX streams retain their lease through body closure.
  Record Retry-After at headers (integer or HTTP-date), before body reads;
  propagate redirect delays to the destination authority. Never clamp server
  cooldowns downward, clear them on an older successful in-flight response or
  evict active/cooling origin state to reset a limit. Return `origin_throttled`
  before another request/recovery backend; do not turn it into bot recovery.
  Hosted readers reserve source and service origins in stable deduplicated order.
  Production origin leases, spacing and cooldowns use durable ConfigStore CAS
  across processes, including fixed sync search and native browser HTTP. Live
  capacity counters describe this Python process, not every concurrent process.
  **A lease is never held by a release that failed** (2026-11-05): this
  process's writers of a durable table take turns (`durable_state._table_lock`;
  the CAS is for other processes, with `_retry_pause`), a poll that only waits
  writes nothing (`durable_state.Unchanged`, `origin_state._waited`),
  `origin_state.release` never raises (a WARNING), and a lease naming this
  process that it no longer holds (`origin_state._HELD`) is taken back at the
  origin's next admission. Live, a deep research's parallel searches polled
  with a write every 50 ms until the table was "busy"; two releases gave up,
  the running server held SearXNG's two slots, and every later search waited
  its 30 s and failed until a restart. Gate:
  `tests/test_origin_leases_under_contention.py` (the old lock, poll and
  release as negative controls).
  Gates: `tests/test_origin_scheduler.py`, real browser/KB compatibility suites.
  Tests isolate the scheduler per case; production cooldowns persist across jobs.
  `web_acquire.robots` defaults automated crawl/KB/research-save jobs to KazmaBot
  robots enforcement. Check before cache reuse and every HTTP/browser hop,
  including assets. Raw public metadata is bounded to 500KiB/15s/five
  redirects, with dedicated bounded capacity to avoid nested content-slot
  deadlock. **robots.txt is read as RFC 9309 says** (2026-10-31, from the
  recorded corpus below): any 4xx but 429 -- 401 and 403 too -- means no rules
  apply (the page request decides); 429, 5xx, network, malformed or clipped
  checks refuse crawling; a redirect is followed across hosts, up to five,
  each hop checked public (http://python.org/robots.txt moves to
  https://www.python.org/), and the rules apply to the origin asked about.
  Refusing 401/403 and cross-host redirects left such sites uncrawlable.
  KazmaBot's name carries a contact link (`robots.USER_AGENT`): Wikimedia
  refuses a bot that names none (403, "please respect our robot policy").
  Explicit opt-out is visible; hosted
  recovery is refused while robots enforcement requires per-request control.
  Cache policy by origin, acquisition policy and route; separate manual/crawler
  page caches. Freeze policy per job; never retain a ContextVar across async
  generator progress yields. Robots metadata receipts are call-local; proxy
  request reservations use the durable ledger, with per-request charges unknown.
  Parsed robots policy and interrupted lookup refusals persist in a bounded CAS
  table. Full RFC conformance and broader compatibility qualification remain open.
  Gates: `tests/test_web_robots.py`, actual Chromium broker fixtures.
  **No acquisition state field is named like a credential** (2026-10-31): the
  settings store moves such a field into the vault and `get_category` reads
  the `vault://` pointer back, so the robots claim (then `token`, now
  `claim`) never matched and every robots-checked crawl failed "Robots lookup
  is owned or was interrupted". Every `batch_set` in `web_acquire` passes
  `durable_state.refuse_vaulted` (`config_store.vaulted_paths`, the store's
  own walk). Gate: `tests/test_acquisition_state_never_vaulted.py`.
  **A crawl's outcome says what happened to each page** (2026-10-31,
  `web_acquire/page_outcome.py`): ingested, unchanged, excluded (a rule:
  robots, scope, a sign-in, a page gone, a page past Kazma's size limit -- a

  page words with what to do (`knowledge.reason.*`, `knowledge.hint.*`). A
  crawl is partial only for a failed or uncertain page; limits and exclusions
  are notes (`crawl_verdict`); every page kept out with none failed is
  completed with `nothing_stored` (the monitor's yellow "empty", never red).
  A hiccup -- network, 408/425/429/5xx, a private DNS answer during an

  failed pages of one class (`REFUSAL_CLASSES`: bot wall, HTTP refusal,
  server error, network) with no page stored between end the crawl

  `crawl_jobs.stop_refused` / `refusal_text`); the pages not reached stay

  own. Other failures (no text, an unreadable format) neither count nor clear

  render behind a bot wall) to the page cap. A crawl a restart cut off in the
  last day resumes on its own (`interrupted_by: process_ended`,
  `kb_api.resume_interrupted_crawls`) up to `AUTO_RESUMES_PER_DAY` (3) times a
  day, each only if it settled more pages since its last automatic resume

  `KnowledgeStore.web_page_urls`); the site's own answer decides -- 410
  takes the page out at once, a 404 is recorded (`knowledge_pages_gone`,
  `gone_unconfirmed`) and takes it out when a later crawl finds it missing
  again at least `_GONE_CONFIRM_S` (an hour) after the first; a page that
  answers again clears its record (`publish_page`). Absence from discovery
  alone never takes a page out (KB-S14 stands). The page leaves the chunks,
  the keyword index (like a replaced page's words), its vectors and its
  fetched copy in one transaction (`KnowledgeStore.page_gone`,
  `KnowledgeIndex.page_gone`); never a Document's chunks. Outcome `removed`,
  counted apart (`row['removed']`, the note `removed`). Before, a 404/410 was
  "excluded: gone" and the text stayed searchable for good. **One text is
  stored once, and one page's query-string copies do not fill a crawl**
  (2026-11-13): a page whose text another page of the crawl stored (digest
  of the whitespace-folded text, `_text_digest`, kept on the journal's page
  so a resume knows it) is excluded `duplicate`; at most
  `_QUERY_VARIANTS_PER_PATH` (5) query-string addresses per page in the
  frontier (`_cap_query_variants`, note `query_variants_capped`) and in the
  link walk (`_QueryVariants`). The corpus held three duplicate pairs
  (`/` and `/index.html`, http and https, a `/stable/` alias). The
  Knowledge page previews a crawl (`knowledge_ingest.preview_site`: the
  crawl's own discovery, nothing stored) and takes a scope in the owner's
  words (this section / whole site / just this page), kept per library
  (`knowledge_libraries.crawl_scope`) for refreshes; a resume keeps its own.
  "Just this page" follows its seed's redirects within the site, and a
  version segment ("3" in /3/tutorial/) is not a section's topic. After
  discovery a Knowledge crawl's row keeps no parsed sitemap list and only the
  latest receipt. Every retained crawl's pages by outcome and reason, against
  the target of 99% stored or kept out by a rule (`crawl_jobs.PAGE_TARGET`),
  are the Dashboard's Knowledge crawls card (`/api/kb/outcomes`), `/metrics`
  (`kazma_kb_crawl_*`) and the weekly report ("Knowledge crawl", "Knowledge
  page not stored", "Knowledge page removed"); a removed page counts as
  handled. Gates: `tests/test_crawl_outcomes.py`,
  `tests/test_crawl_auto_resume.py`, `tests/test_crawl_preview.py`,
  `tests/test_crawl_report.py`, `tests/js/test_kb_crawl_report.js`,
  `tests/test_crawl_refusing_site.py` (a replayed site that turns to 403 after
  five pages: 15 fetched of 40; the streak out of reach as the control),
  `tests/test_crawl_removed_pages.py` (410 at once, 404 an hour later, the old
  refresh as the control), `tests/test_crawl_duplicates.py` (a replayed site
  of sixty months of one page; no cap and no text check as the controls).
  **Twenty real sites are recorded and replayed through the whole crawl**
  (`tests/_crawl_replay.py`, `tests/fixtures/crawl_corpus/`): every HTTP
  response a real crawl received, through the one HTTP seam
  (`proxy.client.get_scraping_client`), replayed with production's robots
  manager and the vault on; each site's outcome page by page is locked in
  `expected.json` (`scripts/crawl_corpus.py record|lock|show`; review the diff
  before committing a lock). The first recording found five bugs no synthetic
  test had. Also with a real Chroma store and on real Postgres
  (`tests/test_crawl_corpus.py`). **A daily canary crawls one known page
  for real** (`web_acquire/canary.py`, RFC 2606 by default, Settings ->
  System -> Web acquisition): the whole crawl into a private store
  (`<data dir>/canary`, `knowledge_ingest._PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE`), journal row
  kind `canary` removed after; a failure is the ops alert
  `acquisition.canary_failed` (error) the same day, a pass after one
  `acquisition.canary_recovered`; the weekly report expects seven runs
  (`tests/test_crawl_canary.py`). It also renders the page in Kazma's own
  browser (2026-11-13, `canary._render_leg`, the outcome's `render`): the
  crawl reaches Chromium only when plain HTTP fails, so a broken driver,
  contained process tree or request broker went unseen until a page needed
  JavaScript. A failed render fails the canary; no browser part, or a host
  that refuses to start it (`browser_isolation.browser_unavailable`, which
  holds the one "is Chromium installed" rule the install asks too), is
  `skipped` with why. A real Chromium renders the replayed page in the test
  where one is installed; the canary without the leg is the control.
  The factory provides
  (proxy provider + rotating UA pool); `web_acquire` is the façade
  (`fetch_text`/`search`/`rank_urls`/profiles) used by research pipeline, KB
  ingest, and readiness. Direct (no-proxy) hops pin the validated IP
  (`PinHostAsyncTransport`) and abort if the peer is private (§32). Do not
  pin through `proxy=` — CONNECT would break scraping.
- `crawl_site(profile=...)` accepts named cap presets (`research_brief` |
  `research_deep` | `kb_site` | `single_page`); explicit args win; hard env
  ceilings (`KAZMA_CRAWL_MAX_PAGES` etc.) still clamp.
  Its research frontier deduplicates pending URLs and retains at most four
  times the page cap (8192 characters per URL); exhausted coverage is visible.
  Partial extracts are not published automatically. Saves pin the starting
  workspace through the existing path scope. Validation errors preserve their
  typed class. `crawl_site(resume_job_id=...)` now uses the shared bounded
  crawl journal with `kind=research_crawl`; freeze workspace, output options,
  acquisition/robots policy and limits. Own each page before fetch/publication,
  persist its receipt before saving, and settle summary plus pending frontier
  atomically. Resume only interrupted jobs with identical scope, skipping
  completed/failed/ambiguous pages; uncertainty or capped coverage stays partial.
  Publication and terminal commits join cancellation; a committed terminal
  outcome must not be overwritten by interrupted cleanup. KB API filters
  research jobs; acquisition readiness can inspect them by job ID. Research
  pipeline/session durability remains separate required work.
  Gates: `tests/test_research_crawl_bounds.py`,
  `tests/test_research_crawl_recovery.py` (real SQLite child crashes before/after
  publication, cancellation/terminal race, concurrent resume and invalid state),
  `tests/test_acquisition_postgres.py` (real independent PostgreSQL connections).
- **A deep research covers what its plan asked** (2026-10-31). Each search's
  results are ranked against that search's own query and taken in turns
  (`web_acquire.rank_by_coverage`): every sub-question gets a source before
  any gets a second. Pooled and ranked against the topic, the address score
  decided alone (`.gov` +4): a Kuwait history report's first source was a
  COVID-19 cost study. The gap critic runs whatever the source count, with
  its own budget (`_gap_search_due`; half `max_sources`, at least 2); gated
  on a full quota it never ran in a deep run. Fan and meme wikis, copies of
  Wikipedia and pirate document sites are demoted (`rank._DEMOTE_HOST_SUBSTR`:
  the next run took polandball's "Kuwaitball" as its search's best address).
  **A link is judged by its search result too** (the fourth run): a query
  word in the result's own title and snippet (`SearchResult.snippets`, kept
  per URL in the search effect) counts like one in its address
  (`rank_by_coverage(texts=)`), and links with no sign of relevance come
  after every link that has one, from any search; a gap fill takes none
  (`require_signal=True`), so a follow-up search that found only games
  sites adds nothing. Result links are the `**URL:**` lines
  (`serp.extract_urls_from_search`): any URL in the text took the search
  engine's own address from the "_Source: ... searxng@http://..._" line as
  a source, and an empty search ("No web results for:") as one result.
  Gate: `tests/test_research_source_coverage.py` (pooled ranking, the old
  gate, the old demotions, the old URL extraction and the rule without the
  signal tier as negative controls). **A PDF answer is read, through the
  document worker** (`web_acquire/pdf_source.py`, the fifth step): the
  ladder refused every non-text answer, so the research read no thesis or
  journal article. A PDF type, or a nameless binary type whose bytes start
  `%PDF-`, goes to `DocumentService.parse_transient(allow_ocr=False)` from a
  private temporary copy (deleted after): the PDF policy and the sandbox or
  per-job container, never a PDF library in the server (§19 E3), no remote
  parse. Its body limit is decided from the headers
  (`read_capped(max_bytes=callable)`): 20 MB, read whole or refused. No OCR:
  no text on any page is refused as a scan, every page needing OCR is read
  and marked thin. Knowledge crawls keep PDFs out (`reads_pdfs`: profile
  generic only; the crawl corpus locks their outcomes). Gate:
  `tests/test_web_pdf_sources.py` (real PDFs, the real worker; the old gate
  as the negative control). **The planner, the gap
  critic and the report answer without hidden reasoning**
  (`reasoning="off"`): deepseek-flash spent all 8,000 tokens of a report on
  it, then 11,015 of the 16,000 retry, and the run failed at its last step.
  `resilient_chat` passes the switch only to a client whose
  `can_turn_off_reasoning()` is True (`_kwargs_for`): a failover can reach a
  provider whose `chat` takes no such argument
  (`tests/test_research_reasoning_off.py`, passing it through as the
  negative control).
- **Tavily is the search service after SearXNG** (resilience plan F1,
  `web_search._tavily_search`): a remote provider, asked only when the
  acquisition policy names `tavily` and `KAZMA_TAVILY_API_KEY` is set. Each
  query reserves one request of the remote allowance before it leaves and
  its HTTP status is recorded on the reservation (`accounting.record_response`);
  a spent allowance passes the query on. The search worker posts it with the
  key in a header (stdin to the child, never a URL), never through the
  scraping proxy (`search_http._proxy_for`), and never follows a redirect.
  SearXNG answering nothing for an hour pages once (alert "search.searxng_silent"),
  and an answer resets it. Research readiness says whether Tavily is on
  (`second_search`). Gate: `tests/test_search_tavily.py` (no policy, no key,
  the proxy and the chain without Tavily as negative controls).
- **A search answer about something else is no answer** (2026-10-31,
  `web_search._answers_the_query`): a backend's results of which fewer than
  half hold a content word of the query (`memory.query_terms`) in title,
  snippet or address count as empty (`<backend>:unrelated`, a WARNING) and the
  chain goes on. With the local SearXNG's engines rate-limited after a day of
  runs, Bing answered Kuwait history queries with Telegram, a perfume shop and
  a browser game, and the chain stopped there: nine of a run's ten sources.
  Bing result links are decoded as URL-safe base64 and must decode to a plain
  http(s) address, or the row is dropped (`search_http._bing`: the standard
  alphabet left control characters, or kept the Bing redirect itself). The
  Wikipedia fallback is a full-text search (`list=search`, `_wikipedia`), sent
  with `search_http.USER_AGENT`, which names a contact: `opensearch` matched
  title starts only, and Wikimedia answered "KazmaSearch/0.6" with 403, so it
  had never answered a research query. Gate: `tests/test_web_search_unrelated.py`
  (the chain without the check, and the old decoder, as negative controls).
- **The Research page lists research, then the chat's web searches apart**
  (2026-10-31). `list_sessions(kind=)` / `GET /api/research/sessions?kind=`:
  `research` (deep and brief runs) or `search` (`_CHAT_SEARCH_SQL`: depth
  `chat`, or an older row with no known depth and an `rs_chat_` id -- the
  page's `sessionTag` rule). The page reads each kind on its own (26 of the
  newest 30 rows were chat searches), lists papers and runs newest first, and
  the searches in a "Web searches from chat" group after them, each "web search
  from chat · N results" (`meta.results`, written by `record_chat_research(
  result_count=)` with the snapshot it counts). They were listed first, as
  "[Chat] <query> · session · done · 1 source", and read as Kazma's research.
  Gates: `tests/test_research_web_searches.py`,
  `tests/js/test_research_web_searches.js` (the old mixed list as control).
- **A research run's finished paper is kept with it** (2026-10-31,
  `tools/research_final_paper.py`): a run registered in a chat turn names it
  (`turn`, `proposals.current_turn()`), and a `generate_pdf`/`generate_docx`
  that succeeds in the SAME turn copies the document and the Markdown it was
  made from into the run's folder (`final/paper.{pdf,docx,md}`, replaced by a
  later call) and names them on the run's entry (`final`). The Research page
  lists the run by that paper (its title, a PDF button) and opens its text,
  the working report a link. Never matched by anything but the turn: a
  document of another turn, or of a chat that ran no research, is no research
  paper. A failure to keep it is a WARNING; the document is made either way.
  Gates: `tests/test_research_final_paper.py` (the run and the PDF through
  the real pipeline and tool; a later turn and an unstamped run as controls),
  `tests/js/test_research_final_paper.js`.
- Research pipeline execution uses `web_acquire.research_runtime`: four active
  pipelines and four background sessions in this Python process, with no waiting
  queue. Admit before planning/session creation, freeze workspace/operator and
  robots policy, and retain a background lease until its actual task finishes.
  Rejected Web starts return typed 503 capacity errors without creating a row or
  task. Pipeline execution has a cooperative 30-minute deadline; this is not a
  hard native filesystem deadline or durable pipeline recovery. Session/store/
  scoring workers, pipeline preflight/path/registration workers and extract
  publication join cancellation before releasing ownership. Unique per-run
  directories prevent same-topic/same-second collisions. Standalone extract
  saves pin their starting workspace before acquisition. Gate:
  `tests/test_research_runtime.py` (original admission controls, real API/SQLite,
  cross-thread dispatch, preflight/creation/publication cancellation and scope).
  Preflight requires an explicit boolean readiness receipt and stops before
  planning/output on failure. Source batches reserve remaining publication
  slots before dispatch; gap fills keep monotonic filenames. Persist bounded
  `sources.json` atomically before the first fetch and after each batch,
  including gaps; storage failure stops further acquisition. This manifest
  does not replace the unfinished durable pipeline effect/resume journal.
  Cached readiness honors `probe_search=False` even under legacy live-probe
  environment variables, opens a read-only diagnostic scope and omits search
  URL credentials. `web_acquire.operations` is the shared cached CLI/TUI status
  source; never add implicit balance refreshes to status reads. CLI supports
  `kazma acquisition status`; TUI Settings reads explicitly and keeps one
  worker until joined cleanup completes. Live capacities are process-local.
  Gate: `tests/test_acquisition_operations.py` (real API, SQLite, CLI and TUI).
- Deliberate direct-API exceptions (never route through the scraping proxy):
  Jina Reader, Firecrawl, loopback SearXNG. The gateway attachment URL fetch
  DOES route through `get_scraping_client_sync` (SSRF-per-redirect kept).

**C. CSRF + rate limiting (`kazma_ui`).**
- `csrf.py` middleware: a non-GET `/api/*` whose Origin (else Referer) is
  not the origin the request was served on or one of
  `browser_origins.configured_browser_origins()` (`KAZMA_PUBLIC_URL`,
  `KAZMA_CORS_ORIGINS`) → 403; whole origins are compared (scheme, host,
  port) and forwarded headers never add to the trusted set (§45).
  `Authorization`-header requests and origin-less clients
  (curl/CLI/webhooks) are exempt. **Starlette's URL has no `.host`** (the
  2026-08-14 every-browser-POST-500 crash). Tests must build REAL ASGI-scope
  Requests (`tests/test_csrf.py`) — MagicMock auto-attributes and hides
  exactly that bug class.
- `rate_limit.py`: per-principal sliding window (cookie > Authorization > IP),
  one bucket per `rate_limit("<bucket>", n)` dependency: chat, chat uploads,
  voice, research, swarm dispatch, approvals, scheduled jobs, runs,
  documents, IDE exec, skill installs, backups and admin operations (the
  system flush route it also covered was removed 2026-09-30, AUD-015).
  Active ONLY when auth is enabled (never demo mode); live ConfigStore
  `api.rate_limit.<bucket>_per_minute`; env `KAZMA_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=0`.

**D. Research sessions.**
- Cancellation is a request, not cleanup proof (2026-10-11). Active sessions enter
  `cancelling`; terminal `cancelled` follows joined pipeline workers. Delete must
  retain the row/subscribers/owner and return typed 409 while `_RUNNING` owns it.
  `update_session` reads and writes under one SQLite writer transaction, preserving
  cancelling/terminal states against late progress. Pre-first-step cancellation
  transfers its lease to a joined terminal writer; never cancel that writer from
  Delete. UI keeps/reconnects progress while cancelling. Gates:
  `tests/test_research_cancel_truth.py`, `tests/js/test_research_cancel.js`.
  Dead process owners reconcile to interrupted; explicit resume links the original
  durable pipeline. Verified terminal output is restored without effects. History
  is bounded to 256 rows/128MiB; archive does not release that allowance.
- `suppress_chat_recording()` (ContextVar, research_session.py): the deep
  pipeline wraps BOTH its search gathers in it — sub-queries must NOT mint
  standalone `record_chat_research` rows (the panel flood: one deep run
  showed 10+ "1 sources" rows). Chat-initiated searches still record.
- Sessions support delete + archive (idempotent `archived` column via ALTER
  TABLE; `list_sessions` EXCLUDES archived by default — pass
  `archived=True`/`None` explicitly for the Archived tab / everything).
  The panel routes `session:`-prefixed ids to `/api/research/sessions/*`
  mutation endpoints — sessions live in `research_sessions.db`, NOT the
  swarm TaskStore.
- Chat-tool snapshots persist up to `_CHAT_RESULT_MAX` (200K — the old
  [:500] cap discarded full output at write time); a longer re-query
  refreshes the stored summary, a shorter one never clobbers it.
- **asyncio objects are touched on their own loop only** (2026-10-01). The
  pipeline writes progress through `asyncio.to_thread(update_session, ...)`
  and the Research routes are plain `def`s, so `update_session`,
  `cancel_session` and `delete_session` run in worker threads; they used to
  `put_nowait` onto the SSE readers' `asyncio.Queue` and `cancel()` the run's
  task right there (asyncio's debug mode refuses both). A subscriber is
  registered with its loop (`_SUBS`, under `_SUBS_LOCK`); `_deliver` and
  `_cancel_on_its_loop` hand over with `call_soon_threadsafe`.
  `tests/test_research_session_threads.py` records the thread of every put
  and cancel (the old calls as negative controls). Any sync function that may
  run in a thread and holds an asyncio Queue, Event, Future or Task follows
  the same rule.

**E. Deep canary + CI gate.**
- `GET /health/deep` (kazma_ui/health.py): one REAL roundtrip per critical
  path — ConfigStore write→read→delete, a real `recall()`, workspace
  binding, research-stack readiness, brain entry-point imports, DB ping.
  503 when any check fails; TTL-cached 30s (aggressive polling is free).
  Poll it in ops dashboards — it exists to catch SILENT no-ops (the
  recall-NameError class), which structural checks cannot see.
- CI (`ci.yml`) GATES on the full suite: `python scripts/fast_test.py --chunks
  4` (crash-tolerant chunked serial pytest over ALL
  testpaths — the package suites were previously orphaned by `pytest tests/`),
  `-m "not slow"`, per-chunk `--timeout=120`. Compile-check (py_compile over
  every repo `.py`) and `node --check` over static JS are separate GATES.
  Never reintroduce `|| true` on the test step — that single flag let every
  regression class in this audit ship silently. Lint/bandit remain advisory
  (`--exit-zero`/`|| true`) until their backlogs are triaged. Known CI blind
  spots (deep-audit 2026-08-19, patched same day): the G1 commitment-latency
  file's `slow` marker was removed (it runs in ~6s and was the ONLY slow file,
  so `-m "not slow"` silently excluded it), and CI now installs the light
  pure-wheel deps (pillow/pymupdf/sqlite-vec/pypdfium2/numpy — without numpy
  the belief-graph PPR silently runs its degraded uniform-seed path) that the
  `.[test]`-only install left `importorskip`ing/degrading. Playwright is a
  separate CI job: smoke (`tests/e2e/test_smoke.py`, polls `/health/live`)
  plus a named GATE step for HITL view-model incidents 2 and 3
  (`tests/e2e/test_hitl_view_model.py`). Remaining `tests/e2e` files run in
  the same job. Incidents 1 and 4 are claimed by
  `tests/e2e/test_unified_turn_browser.py` in the `unified-turn-lifecycle`
  job (§31E). Torch-bearing `rag` extra is still too heavy for CI.

**F. Knowledge Library meaning search** (`memory/vector_store_global.py`,
`stores/knowledge_index.py`). Off from 2026-07-31 to 2026-09-26: the client
module was deleted and the import's `except` said "chromadb not installed".
- **One Chroma client per directory** for the process (`_shared_client`),
  telemetry off (Chroma's default posts usage events to PostHog). A failed
  start names its real cause and is retried after 5 minutes, not on every
  search.
- **Collections compare by angle** (`hnsw:space: cosine`) **and every vector
  is made unit length** before it is stored or searched. Chroma's default is
  squared L2, which every earlier collection has; with unit vectors it ranks
  the same, and `query` reports the true cosine for either (`_similarity`).
  It used to report `1 - L2` as a cosine. No embedding function: every write
  and search passes its own vectors, made from at most 1,500 characters
  (`_EMBED_MAX_CHARS`; keyword search reads the whole chunk). Measured on the
  live CPU: 64 chunks of median length embed in 3.4 s, the 32 longest took
  113 s at a 4,000-character cap.
- **The "knowledge vector repair" sweep** (15 min, up to 5 min a pass,
  LAST in the cycle so the memory sweeps never wait on it;
  `KnowledgeIndex.backfill_vectors`) makes each library's vectors match its
  active chunks both ways: embeds the missing, **shortest first across all
  libraries** (most of every library is searchable early, and a batch of
  like lengths wastes nothing on padding), and removes those of retired
  chunks (they took search slots and joined to nothing). Ingest still embeds
  on write; the sweep covers whatever the store missed.
- **`delete_library` opens the collection before dropping it** -- only a
  cached one was dropped, so a library deleted after a restart kept its
  vectors.
- **Vectors live at `KAZMA_VECTOR_PATH`, else beside the Knowledge
  database** (`data_dir()/vector_memory` for the install's), so a test's
  temporary store never writes into the install's. **They are not backed
  up** (`universal._rebuilt_dirs`; `chroma.sqlite3` is a `rebuilt` store):
  a file copy of a live Chroma database can be torn, and the sweep rebuilds
  them from the chunks, which are.
- **The Knowledge page shows each library's coverage** ("Meaning search:
  N of M", or "Keyword search only"), from `KnowledgeIndex.health` through
  `/api/kb/libraries`. Nothing showed it before, which is how the outage
  lasted two months. A library's `chunk_count` is COUNTED by every library
  SELECT (`_CHUNK_COUNT_SQL`): the column is a cache several writers keep,
  one missed, and the page listed 365 chunks for a library holding 366.
- **An embedding-model switch** (2026-09-27): a vector records the model
  that made it (`model` in its metadata; every write builds it in
  `_chunk_vector_metadata`) and the repair re-embeds another model's. Tags
  are read in Python (`VectorStore.models`): Chroma's `$ne` also matches a
  vector WITHOUT the key, and every vector written before the tag has none
  (it was made by the model of the day). A collection holding vectors of
  another size is rebuilt before the first write (`VectorStore._fit`, from
  the size it actually holds): Chroma keeps its first size and refuses any
  other. The memory Rebuild (`reembed.rebuild_embeddings`) used to finish
  with `shutil.rmtree(data_dir/vector_memory)` -- the V1 chat index once,
  the Knowledge Library's live store since 2026-09-26; it no longer touches
  it. Nor does `scripts/reembed.py` (2026-10-14): it kept its own copy of the
  rebuild, step 7 included, and now runs `rebuild_embeddings`. No function
  deletes a folder tree and names the store
  (`tests/test_reembed_keeps_knowledge_vectors.py`, the old step as the
  negative control).
- **A vector's tag names the embedder INSTANCE** (`embedder_identity`: class,
  model, size, endpoint digest; Knowledge audit KB-E03, 2026-10-14), never the
  configured name: a Settings change waiting for a restart, or a remote model
  that fell back to the local one, tagged vectors with a model that had not
  made them. Search filters on the active identity (`_raw_layers`), an
  untagged vector is re-made, and a query against a collection of another
  size waits for the sweep (one INFO). Health is the sweep's recorded
  coverage (`knowledge_vector_status`, states unknown/ok/rebuilding/
  unavailable/failed): listing libraries opens no collection and loads no
  model (KB-S15).
- **The sweep is isolated per library and observed** (`run_repair_sweep`,
  KB-E11): a failing library is recorded and the others repaired, then the
  pass raises for the runner's WARNING; the first unavailable pass and the
  recovery are WARNINGs; three bad passes raise the ops alert
  `knowledge.meaning_search` (6 h cooldown); `/metrics` carries
  `kazma_kb_vector_*`, readiness `knowledge_vectors` (never critical,
  `topology: single_install`), the daily digest a "Needs attention" line.
  The keyword index's coverage is checked each pass and rebuilt with a
  WARNING; an FTS storage error is a WARNING and `keyword_index_ok: false`,
  a query syntax error stays DEBUG. `KB_FOLD_VERSION` is stored in
  `knowledge_meta`; a new value rebuilds the index at open (a fingerprint
  test fails when `fold_for_search` changes without it).
- **One `KnowledgeIndex` per store** (`knowledge_index_for`, shared with
  Documents; KB-E12), and a collection another handle dropped is re-opened
  by name and the call retried once (`VectorStore._reopen_if_missing`). Only
  `knowledge_index_for` constructs an index in product code (gate in
  `tests/test_knowledge_vectors.py`).
- **Chroma's local store, kept honest** (`memory/chroma_local.py`, KB-Q01,
  2026-10-15; chromadb 1.5.9, the newest release that day, has every defect
  below):
  - *Dropped vectors leave the disk.* `delete_collection` removes the catalog
    rows and keeps the segment folder (~40 MB per 10k chunks): 17 folders in a
    4-minute soak. `remove_orphan_segment_folders` removes the UUID-named
    folders no row of `chroma.sqlite3`'s `segments` owns (folders listed
    BEFORE the catalog is read; an unreadable catalog removes nothing; a
    non-UUID folder is never touched) -- at client start, before any
    collection opens (`_shared_client`), after every drop
    (`VectorStore._drop_collection`, the ONE drop path: gate in
    `tests/test_knowledge_vector_lifecycle.py`), and at the end of each
    repair pass (`release_dropped_vectors`). On Windows a folder whose index
    this process loaded is held open until the client is closed: the pass
    then closes it -- a `_Gate` per client: every Chroma call of a
    `VectorStore` holds it shared (an embedding runs before it, so a model
    call never holds up a close), the close exclusive, so it waits for calls
    in flight and holds new ones -- removes the folders and bumps the
    client's generation; every store re-opens on its next call. `atexit`
    does the same.
  - *No index is evicted.* Chroma's HNSW pool is split over 64 shards
    (`POOL_SHARDS`), sized by default as `max_file_handles // 5` (102 on
    Windows: one or two a shard), and writes an index to disk only every
    `sync_threshold` (1,000) records; two collections in one full shard
    evict each other after the process replayed their logs. An evicted index
    under 1,000 records failed every read ("Nothing found on disk", 5 of 20
    short soaks); one of 1,000+ reloaded from its last disk write WITHOUT
    the records since -- no error, the search just missed them -- until the
    collection's next write (reproduced:
    `tests/test_knowledge_vector_text_and_pool.py`, a pool of 64 drops 150
    of 1,180 records). `chroma_local.start_system` starts Chroma's system
    for the directory with Kazma's pool before `PersistentClient` finds it
    (`hnsw_cache_size` is read only at `system.start()`): `index_pool_size`
    = 64 x (`library_ceiling()` + `SPARE_COLLECTIONS`), so a shard holds
    every collection a process can load, whichever shards they hash to.
    `LIBRARY_CEILING` is 500 libraries, lowered when the process cannot keep
    every index's 4 files open (`FILES_PER_INDEX`; Windows: ucrtbase streams
    raised to 8,192 -- lowered to 40, a process loads 9 indexes; msvcrt is
    only what Chroma's default pool reads; POSIX: soft NOFILE to 10,240
    under the hard limit). `KnowledgeStore.create_library` counts every
    library (archived too) in its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and raises
    `KnowledgeLibraryLimit` (a `KnowledgeStorageFull`, so every surface that
    refuses at the quota refuses it); `ensure_capacity(library_id)` asks
    before a crawl or page fetch; the Web API answers 409
    `kb_library_limit` (EN/AR). A read that still finds an index lost
    (`VectorStore._hnsw_read`) deletes the id `kazma:reload-index`: the push
    makes Chroma rebuild it from its write log before the read is asked
    again (WARNING, `kazma_kb_vector_index_reloads_total`).
    `hnsw:sync_threshold` does not fix it (minimum 2, and a persist rewrites
    the whole index).
  - *A log is replayed on one thread* (2026-10-21,
    `chroma_local.serial_index_inserts`, called by `_shared_client` before
    Chroma's pool first runs). The first read of a collection after a
    client starts (every boot, every client the repair pass reopens)
    applies its write log to the index Chroma loads from disk, on rayon
    worker threads, and that parallel insert races in hnswlib: an access
    violation in its graph search, always at one address, the Knowledge
    soak's crash (2026-10-17/19, three runs). Measured with
    `scripts/chroma_replay_race.py`: 6 crashes in about 28,200 client
    starts with Chroma's own pool, 0 in 28,000 with `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`;
    a crashed store replayed again never crashes (a race, not bad data).
    Price: 20,000 vectors at 1,024 dimensions insert in 60 s instead of
    8 s, a new client's replay of 999 records 6 s instead of 0.7 s. An
    operator's other value is kept and named once (WARNING). Every Chroma
    client in product code and scripts is built after the call; the drill
    alone measures Chroma's own pool. Gate:
    `tests/test_chroma_serial_inserts.py` (a real replay adds one thread,
    Chroma's own pool as the negative control; a planted client without
    the call fails the gate). Re-run the drill after a chromadb upgrade.
  - *No text beside a vector.* An older build stored each chunk's first
    2,000 characters as the Chroma document and its title, heading, address
    and hash as metadata -- read by nothing -- and SQLite keeps a deleted
    row's bytes in free pages and in pages' free space (`secure_delete` off,
    Chroma's own connection): a dropped 3,000-row collection's words had
    9,429 copies in the file. Chroma keeps a document in
    `embedding_metadata`, its trigram full-text index and its write log
    (until the next 1,000-record disk write). Every write keeps only
    `KEPT_METADATA` (`model`, `library_id`, `document_id`, `tenant_id`,
    `source`) and no document (gate: no `documents=` in a Chroma write in
    product code). A collection holding anything else (`holds_text`: a
    read-only catalog query on the metadata segment AND the write log,
    once per collection and process) is rebuilt by the repair pass
    (`VectorStore.rebuild_collection`, which replaced `rebuild_graph`: copy
    to `<name>.rebuild` with vectors and kept keys, counts compared, old
    dropped, copy renamed; nothing embedded again, 12 s for 10k at 1,024
    dimensions). Note: an upsert without documents KEEPS a record's old
    document and merges its metadata, so only the rebuild clears it.
  - *Deleted text leaves the catalog.* A deletion of rows that may hold
    text (`_note_deleting`: drops, `delete`, `delete_many`, unless the
    collection was found text-free) writes `vector_memory/
    kazma_compaction_due`; at the end of each repair pass `compact_vectors`
    takes the client's gate exclusive (calls in flight finish, new ones wait,
    the client stays open) and `compact_catalog` runs FTS5 `optimize` on
    Chroma's full-text index (rebuilt when the merge kept deleted words:
    `fts5_purge.purge_deleted_rows`, G below), then `VACUUM` (Chroma's own `chroma utils
    vacuum`), and clears the marker. 10k chunks: 41.0 -> 3.2 MB in 0.3 s; a
    text-free catalog 0.13 s. A failure keeps the marker (WARNING);
    `kazma_kb_vector_compaction_pending`.
  - *A search filters only when it must.* A collection holds one library,
    so `KnowledgeIndex._model_filter` asks Chroma no filter while
    `VectorStore.only_model(identity)` holds (one `$ne` read per collection
    and process; a write of another tag ends it; a mixed collection is
    re-asked after 60 s), else `{"model": identity}`. Chroma's metadata
    filter cost more than the search: 10k vectors, p50 40 ms with the
    library+model filter vs 4 ms without; 100k, 353 vs 6 ms (p95 442 vs 10),
    recall the same either way.
  - *The index is built for recall* (`_HNSW`: 48 neighbours, construction
    400, search 256 for a small library). Chroma's defaults (16/100/100)
    returned 31-39 of 40 planted answers at 10k chunks while exact search
    ranked all 40 first; these return 40/40 in EN, AR and mixed in 11 of 12
    harness measurements (39 in one: Chroma builds in parallel) for ~1 ms
    more a query. An older collection's graph is rebuilt by the repair pass
    from its own vectors (`VectorStore.rebuild_collection`).
  - *The search widens as the library grows* (`vector_store_global.search_breadth`,
    2026-10-15): one candidate for every 12 vectors, rounded up to the next
    of `_BREADTH_GRID` (256 below 3,072 vectors ... 12,288 from 98,304,
    24,576 from 196,608, 49,152 from 393,216: never under n/12, at most 1.5
    times it). `scripts/knowledge_soak.py breadth` (two corpora x EN/AR/mixed,
    240 planted questions a size, exact rank 1 each): at a fixed 256,
    239/218/210/203 of 240 found at 10k/50k/100k/200k; the least breadth that
    found all was at most n/12 at every size (512, 4,096, 6,144, 16,384, all
    Arabic); the rule's breadth found 240/240 at each, p50 ~3x 256's at 100k (the
    guide's "Meaning search at scale"). Chroma (1.5.9, measured) applies a
    breadth when it LOADS an index, every read loads it (a `count()` and a
    `get` too), and a loaded index keeps its breadth while the client lives
    (Kazma's pool never evicts): so the size comes from the catalog
    (`chroma_local.collection_size`, loads nothing) and `VectorStore._open`
    sets the breadth before anything reads the collection (`_fit_breadth`);
    the repair pass (`fit_search_breadth`) sets it for a collection that grew
    while loaded and then has every index loaded again
    (`reload_vector_indexes`: the client closed between calls, as
    `release_dropped_vectors` does); a breadth is kept until the size falls
    a fifth below its step (`_BREADTH_KEEP_SHARE`); a rebuilt collection is
    made with its size's breadth. Never set a breadth only by `modify` on a
    loaded collection and call it applied. Gate:
    `tests/test_knowledge_search_breadth.py` (the fixed breadth, a size read
    with `count()` and no reload as negative controls; recall on the real
    chromadb).

**G. The Knowledge store and its surfaces** (Knowledge audit 2026-10-13,
tracker `docs/plans/KNOWLEDGE_INDUSTRIAL_HARDENING_GOAL.md`).
- **Own file** `knowledge.db` (`paths.knowledge_db`, a `bundle` store; KB-E10):
  a quota on the store's own pages in use (1 GiB, refused before fetch with
  `KnowledgeStorageFull`, reads unaffected), `auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` and the
  maintenance pass's `compact()` (never `VACUUM`: it renumbers the rowids the
  FTS is keyed by). `settings.db`'s old tables move in on the first open
  (`copy_legacy_knowledge`, explicit columns, FTS rebuilt, a non-http seed
  blanked) and a bundle in the older layout is staged the same way
  (`importer._stage_legacy_knowledge`; no Knowledge DDL in `migration/`,
  KB-E01). Every connection sets the pragmas, `foreign_keys` included, and
  `close()` takes the store lock (KB-E13).
- **One publication path** (`KnowledgeStore.publish_page`, KB-E02): a page's
  retire and insert, FTS included, in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; a deleted
  library refuses (`KnowledgeLibraryGone`), a failed page fails and the crawl
  ends `partial`. Chunk ids carry the position (`make_chunk_id`, KB-E05). The
  FTS is keyed by rowid and deleted by `rowid AND chunk_id` (KB-E06); library
  deletes run in 500-row batches with the lock released between them.
- **A deleted library's words leave the index file** (KB-Q01, 2026-10-15):
  FTS5 keeps a deleted row's words in its older segments until a merge
  reaches them -- every planted word of a deleted 10k library was still in
  `knowledge_chunks_fts_data`. `delete_library` ends with
  `purge_search_index`: an FTS5 `merge` of every segment (memory's M01
  purge, bounded: `_PURGE_STEP_PAGES` = 1,000 pages a transaction, the lock
  released between steps). A replaced page or document version keeps its old
  words until FTS5's own merges (unsearchable; a full rewrite per page would
  cost the whole index each time). `tests/test_knowledge_store.py`.
  **A merge is not proof** (the multi-day soak, 2026-10-15: 8 words of the
  library deleted at cycle 76 left after the purge). FTS5 drops a delete
  marker -- which carries the word -- only when the merge writes the
  index's OLDEST segment, judged by place (the only segment on the
