  structure's last level); every full merge adds two levels and a larger
  new segment pulls older ones down, and with every segment on one level
  below the top `merge -N` and `optimize` merge it one level up and keep
  every marker. So the purge's last transaction reads the structure record
  (`db/fts5_purge.drop_deleted_rows`; an unreadable record counts as
  unchecked) and rebuilds the index (FTS5 `rebuild`) unless it is one
  segment on the last level. Every FTS5 `optimize`/`merge` in product code
  goes through `fts5_purge` or ends with that check -- memory's Forget
  purge and the vector catalog's compaction too (gate:
  `tests/test_fts5_purge.py`, the plain `optimize` as negative control).
  **The purge outlives the process:** each delete batch writes
  `knowledge_meta.keyword_purge_due` (a counter) in its own transaction;
  the purge clears it only if unchanged; every store open and the repair
  pass (`finish_pending_purge`) finish a purge a killed delete left, and a
  delete that finds no chunk still purges when it is set. Gate: a real
  child killed after a batch, after the library row, between two merge
  steps and inside the rebuild (`tests/test_knowledge_store.py`, the store
  without the mark as negative control). The soak's check reads whole words
  from the leaf pages and leaves out words a live row holds
  (`knowledge_soak._segment_residue`): its old test of a word's last 4-6
  letters anywhere in the blobs hit 6 of 20,000 random Arabic tokens.
- **A coverage record names the vector store it measured** (KB-Q01): the
  record is in knowledge.db (backed up), the vectors are not, and a restored
  database reported "ok, 10,000 of 10,000" before the first pass with no
  vector there. `knowledge_vector_status.store_id` is the id the sweep read
  from `vector_memory/kazma_vector_store_id` (`chroma_local.vector_store_id`,
  written at the directory's first client start); `KnowledgeIndex.health`
  shows an ok/rebuilding record of another store, or of none (a row from
  before the column), as `unknown` -- read from that file, no client, no
  model (KB-S15). `tests/test_knowledge_vectors.py`.
- **Delete goes through `knowledge_lifecycle.delete_library`** (KB-E08): 409
  while a crawl owns the library, the documents it holds unindexed through
  the Documents service first, then vectors, chunks and the fetched pages
  (`<data dir>/knowledge_provenance/<library>`, a `bundle` entry).
- **Model boundary**: the supervisor builds the turn's ONE Knowledge block
  (`_knowledge_inject_for_turn`, off the loop; KB-S08), stripping an earlier
  turn's note at iteration 0; the transports inject nothing. The "Memory
  used" record lists exactly the injected chunks (KB-S02), even with recall
  suppressed. `knowledge_search` keeps its scaffolding outside the fence and
  the page's text inside (KB-S01); so does the turn note since 2026-10-15
  (`KnowledgeInject.block` fenced, then `.footer` -- the library footer and
  the instruction to cite it -- after the fence: inside, the fence told the
  model to obey none of it; the note still opens with the fence, its
  `turn_notes` kind). Federated search ranks each store on its
  own budget. Stored URLs are http(s) only (`validate_web_url`, every
  writer), rendered through `safeHref` (KB-S09).
- **A search shows only what is about the question** (KQ01, 2026-10-15,
  `knowledge_index._judge`): the tool, `/kb search`, the page's test search
  and auto-inject all rank on memory's EVIDENCE rule -- meaning similarity
  above the question's background (meaning ranks 4-15) plus content-word
  coverage (`memory/query_terms`) -- with a floor (0.08), a gap (0.15) and
  memory's words-only rule when no vector judges; `score` is that evidence
  and `strength` "weak" is shown as possibly related. The fusion ranked by
  position and always showed something: five hits and three injected chunks
  for every question nothing answers. A keyword-only candidate is measured
  by its stored vector (`VectorStore.similarities`); the question is
  embedded once per search. A document-scoped search is not judged.
  **An identifier the question names wins** (`_sole_exact_match`,
  2026-10-16): the one candidate holding every content word of the
  question, when one of them is in no other candidate, leads with the best
  kept evidence. It reorders what is kept, never keeps more. The KB-Q01 72 h
  soak failed at cycle 1,757 on "Which port does zqfmbfjvdv listen on?": five
  look-alikes ("zqtkjhghfc listens on port 5997") were nearer by meaning, word
  coverage weighs 0.12, and the answer -- the keyword index's first hit --
  came 6th. Benchmark scores unchanged. Gate:
  `tests/test_knowledge_exact_identifier.py` (the soak's measured scores; the
  judge without the rule as control; the kept set identical with and without).
- **Retrieval quality is measured and ratcheted** (KQ01):
  `stores/knowledge_benchmark.py` publishes a versioned EN/AR/mixed corpus
  (`knowledge_benchmark_data/dataset.json`, built by
  `scripts/knowledge_bench.py build`) into a PRIVATE store through the
  product's publication path and asks every question through
  `search_all_sync` (the tool) and `build_knowledge_inject(store=)` (the turn
  note), with meaning (`hybrid`) and without (`keyword`), tuning and held-out
  questions apart. CI replays bge-m3's recorded vectors
  (`tests/fixtures/knowledge_bench/vectors.npz`) through an exact in-process
  client registered for the private vector folder only
  (`vector_store_global.directory_client`; `run --chroma` gave the same
  scores on chromadb 1.5.9, `run --real` on the live model). The scores are a
  ratchet stamped with the dataset version (`thresholds.json`; `lock` raises
  and refuses to lower, `lock --rebaseline` for a new version only). Gate:
  `tests/test_knowledge_benchmark.py` (the pre-KQ01 fusion order and a search
  that shows nothing as negative controls). Measured numbers: the guide's
  "Benchmark report".
- **A crawl seeded on a private network is refused at admission**
  (2026-10-15, `knowledge_ingest._admit_public_seed`, last check of
  `_prepare_ingest_site`, before the journal row; every caller creates the
  library only after it returns): the check acquisition makes
  (`dns_worker.validate_public_url`, never `to_thread(validate_url)`),
  `security_blocked` for a private, loopback or link-local address,
  `connect_error` (transient) for a name that resolves to nothing
  (`ssrf.UnresolvedHostError`). Until then the seed was admitted, the crawl
  refused it before discovery and the library stayed empty with no refusal
  shown. Gate: `tests/test_knowledge_crawl_admission.py` (every surface --
  Web crawl and refresh, `/kb crawl|refresh|add`, both agent tools, a page
  ingest -- and `STARTERS`, the class gate: a new crawl starter must be
  declared and admitted before its library exists; the old admission as the
  negative control), `tests/e2e/test_knowledge_outcomes_browser.py` (EN/AR).
- **Surfaces**: `/api/kb/*` refuses with stable codes (`KB_ERROR_CODES`,
  `knowledge.err.<code>` EN+AR; KB-S05) and reads bodies under 64 KiB with
  bounded models (KB-S13); every KB surface refuses an install with platform
  users (`kb_refusal`, the shared single-operator rule; KB-S04); `/kb
  add|crawl|refresh|delete` are handled in the gateway, admin-only through
  `changes_global_config`, and report the journal's outcome (KB-S07).
  `window.kazmaSave` rejects `{ok: false}` and every Settings save does too
  (KB-S10).
- Gates: `tests/test_knowledge_publication.py`, `test_knowledge_crawl_journal.py`,
  `test_knowledge_vectors.py`, `test_knowledge_model_boundary.py`,
  `test_kb_api_contract.py`, `test_kb_gateway_commands.py`,
  `test_knowledge_migration.py`, `test_knowledge_docs_claims.py`, each with
  its negative control.
- Gate: `tests/test_knowledge_meaning_search.py` (a fake chromadb in CI, the
  real one where the `rag` extra is installed).
- KB-Q01's harness is `scripts/knowledge_soak.py` (`scale`: ingest, search,
  idle-sweep, restore re-embed and delete measured per size and language on
  named hardware; `soak`: crawls, refreshes, documents, deletes, model
  switches, crashes, a restart every cycle, checked from the stores), held by
  `tests/test_knowledge_soak_harness.py` (its runs need the real chromadb;
  the negative controls run everywhere). It runs strict since the KB-Q01
  fixes: a dropped collection's folder, a deleted library's words in the
  keyword index, a restored coverage record claiming lost vectors and a
  collection a process cannot read are violations (`--tolerate-*` exists
  only to measure an older build); an index Chroma lost and the product
  rebuilt is a counted finding.

### 25. Long-Task Continue Protocol & Partial Pause (`agent/long_task.py`)

Born from the 2026-08-19 Telegram desync ("Saved. Ready…" acks instead of
executing commands after a mission ended Partial) — full diagnosis in
`docs/audits/AUDIT_DEEP_STRUCTURE_2026-08-19.md` §20.

**A. The continue-context injection is GATED by reply shape.**
- `consume_continue_context(thread_id, user_text=…)` returns the stored
  salvage ONLY when `is_continuation_reply(user_text)` is true: ≤8-word
  replies matching proceed/continue/yes/ok/go-on/keep-going/wrap-up
  (Arabic كمّل/اكمل/تابع/نعم/يلا/زين included).
- The stored `long_task.continue.{thread}` context is cleared on EVERY
  consume call — gated or not — so a stale "do not re-do / final report"
  directive can never leak into a later turn. The salvage itself is
  already in the conversation history (the user saw the Partial reply).
- The injection header carries an explicit escape clause ("if the user's
  latest message is a NEW task, ignore this directive") as defense in
  depth. Only injection site: gateway `agent_handler/store.py` — keep the
  `user_text=` argument if a second site is ever added. It reaches the model
  through `agent_handler/graph.py:_rebuild_turn_messages` (§43); until
  2026-09-29 the history rebuild replaced the state and dropped it whenever
  the chat had history.

**B. A Partial PAUSES the long task.**
- The gateway's recursion-Partial handler calls `pause_long_task()`:
  `long_task_status()` then reports `active: False` with baseline budgets
  (no mission framing/ceilings), `is_mission_mode()` defuses, and
  `consume_long_task_turn()` stops eating follow-up turns while paused.
- The paused record survives for `/long status` until TTL expiry; a fresh
  `/long` re-enable always works. The Partial reply tells the user the
  state machine ("reply **Proceed** to wrap up, or send a new task and it
  runs fresh").
- `/long off` (or `/abort`) remains the immediate manual clear on any
  build.
- An active `/long` (budget, mission or `/unrestricted`) lifts the turn's
  wall-clock limit for its chat on every surface; a paused one does not
  (§31, `agent/turn_budget.py`).
- **A budget preset never lowers the Settings baseline** (2026-11-15):
  `/long on` set the research preset's 40 tool rounds where the live chat had
  100 (`agent.max_iterations`); `enable_long_task` and the "long task by
  default" setting now take the higher of the two (an explicit number stays).
  Gate: `tests/test_long_task.py` (`test_long_on_never_lowers_the_installs_baseline`).
- **The gateway does both through `_settle_recursion_partial`**
  (`agent_handler/graph.py`), and a failure there is a WARNING. Inline, it
  imported a name removed 2026-09-04 inside `except Exception: pass`, so
  from then until 2026-09-26 no Partial was stored and no long task paused
  on Telegram/Discord/Slack. `tests/test_gateway_recursion_partial.py`.

### 26. Default-Deny Boundaries (2026-08-29 security audit)

Full report and reproductions: the audit artifact and
`tests/test_audit_2026_08_29_regressions.py`. Four boundaries were
default-OPEN; they are now default-CLOSED, and CI keeps them that way.

**A. Peer address is not a credential behind a proxy.**
- `_should_auto_issue_cookie()` mints an admin session for a loopback client
  with no credential — that is what makes localhost use work with no login.
  Behind a same-host nginx/Caddy, `request.client.host` is `127.0.0.1` for
  EVERY internet visitor, so all of them inherited it (finding F-01).
- `KAZMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES` declares the proxy. `X-Forwarded-For` and
  `X-Forwarded-Proto` are honoured from those addresses ONLY. With a proxy
  declared, a request that arrives THROUGH it never gets peer trust
  (`auth._peer_trust_allowed`); a peer that is not the proxy (a connection
  that bypassed it) keeps it, and `KAZMA_LOOPBACK_AUTOLOGIN=1` is the
  explicit opt-in that keeps it for all. Same rule in
  `websocket_is_authenticated()` — its Origin guard passes when the header
  is absent, so a curl client used to get the agent.
- Anything keying state per client (rate limit, login throttle, audit log)
  must call `auth.client_address(request)`, never `request.client.host`.
- The variable is the operator's CLAIM about the topology, and a wrong claim
  used to fail open (under Docker the proxy is the bridge IP, so `127.0.0.1`
  is the natural guess and it is wrong). `_note_forwarded_headers()` settles
  it from the traffic: an `X-Forwarded-*` header from an undeclared peer
  latches `undeclared_proxy_detected()` and revokes peer trust for the
  process. `proxy_health()` surfaces the state on `/api/auth/status`.
  The latch never clears at runtime — it may only close doors, never open
  them, which is also why spoofing the header gains an attacker nothing.
- **The app applies forwarded headers, not uvicorn**
  (`kazma_ui/proxy_headers.py`, the OUTERMOST middleware): it records the
  TCP peer (`auth.TCP_PEER_SCOPE_KEY`, read by `_peer_host`), then runs
  uvicorn's own `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` for the declared proxies, so routes
  see the same client and scheme as before. Every launcher passes
  `proxy_headers=False`. With uvicorn rewriting first, `_peer_host` read the
  forwarded client as the peer: behind Cloudflare Tunnel (declared
  `127.0.0.1`) the detector flagged the tunnel's own visitors on every boot
  (2026-09-23 to 2026-09-25) and advised trusting a visitor's IP, and
  `_peer_trust_allowed` saw the visitor instead of the proxy. Gate:
  `tests/test_forwarded_headers_peer.py` (real ASGI layers — fake requests
  whose `client` is the peer are why the unit tests never saw it).
  Entries may be CIDR ranges; `auth._is_trusted_proxy` is the ONE answer to
  "is this peer a declared proxy" (every check asks it, never set
  membership), and `*` is dropped so neither layer trusts every peer.
- **One body limit per request** (`kazma_ui/body_limits.py`, 2026-11-15, the
  defensive check before the independent review: the login route read a
  body of any size before sign-in). Outside every gate, a declared length
  past the route's limit is 413 unread and a chunked body stops at it; 64 KiB
  before sign-in, 2 MiB signed in, larger limits declared per route
  (`_route_body_limits`). `upload_limits.UploadSizeLimitMiddleware` is its
  old name. Gate: `tests/test_request_body_limits.py` (the built app's
  routes both ways).
- **Every credential but the shared secret carries a role** (API tokens: the
  role chosen at creation, operator by default), enforced in every mode, and
  `admin_decision` gives the same answer. A token handed to another agent
  for A2A could add an MCP server on a single-operator install
  (`tests/test_api_token_roles.py`).
- **Install-wide writes are admin** (`platform_rbac._ADMIN_WRITE_PREFIXES`:
  GitHub credentials, the active workspace and its folders, the chat apps,
  division requests, model profiles; `tests/test_install_wide_writes.py`
  finds every write route whose code reaches a credential, workspace or
  process sink). A stored key stays with its address: a masked key posted
  with a changed address is refused for profiles, providers and checks
  (`url_credentials.same_address`).
- **Gates judge `request_path.judged_path`**, the path the router serves,
  never `request.url.path` (a decoded `%3F`/`%23` cut it short); a decoded
  `?` or `#` in a path is refused (`tests/test_gates_judge_the_routed_path.py`).
  The login throttle groups IPv6 by /64 and keeps 4,096 keys at most; every
  refused local sign-in costs one full PBKDF2. `.local`, `.lan` and `.test`
  names are this machine only when `KAZMA_AUTOLOGIN_HOSTS` lists them.

**B. HITL default-denies.**
- `requires_approval()` ends on the `TOOL_TIERS` classification, not on a
  name list. An unclassified tool is GATED. **Every tool you register needs
  a tier** — `read` / `write` / `danger`; anything destructive, outbound, or
  credential-touching is `danger` and also belongs in
  `CANONICAL_DANGER_TOOLS` + `kazma.yaml`.
- A configured `require_approval_for` list ADDS to that floor. It can no
  longer un-gate `shell_exec` by omission.
- CI: `test_every_registered_tool_has_a_tier`, `test_danger_tools_are_gated`.

**C. Allowlisting a binary is not allowlisting what it runs.**
- `shell_exec` vets `argv[0]` and rejects shell metacharacters, but a bare
  program name is not path-shaped and `find`'s `+` terminator sidesteps the
  `;` rejection — `find . -exec whoami +` walked past the allowlist (F-03).
- `_EXEC_CAPABLE_ARGS` rejects per-binary flags that execute another
  program (`find -exec`, `git --upload-pack`/`-c`, `tar
  --use-compress-program`, …). Add an entry when you add a binary.
- **`shell_exec` git: the card is the gate, and it names what the repository
  runs** (2026-11-11, the owner's decision). Every git command it runs gets
  `-c core.fsmonitor=false` before its subcommand
  (`git_repo_programs.shell_git_argv`, added after the policy that refuses a
  `-c` the call names). The approval card (chat graph `card_notes`, chat
  apps, swarm bus) names the hooks present (not `.sample`) and every program
  the repository's own `local`/`worktree` configuration sets -- filter, diff
  and merge drivers, `core.sshCommand`, `core.pager`, a shell alias that is
  the command (`_repository_programs`, read with `git config --show-scope` and
  `git rev-parse`, which run none of them, with `tool_child_env`, off the
  loop). Nothing else is switched off: LFS and the owner's hooks keep
  working. One splitter for the command's words
  (`shell_arguments.split_command_line`). Gate:
  `tests/test_shell_git_programs.py` (real repositories, a global
  configuration of the test's own; the argv without the override as the
  control).

**D. Secret masking recurses.**
- `settings.mask_deep()` walks dicts, lists, and JSON-encoded strings.
  The old two-level version skipped lists, so `providers.list` shipped six
  live API keys in the clear (F-02). Key matching is on `.`/`_` token
  boundaries — a substring test made `pat` match `selected_path`.
- New API surfaces that echo config must go through `mask_deep`.
- **A provider row goes out through one masker**
  (`security/provider_mask.mask_provider_entry`, 2026-11-15): the key, extra
  keys, headers, AWS credentials and the address's password. The unified
  model options (`ModelRegistry.list_unified_options`: `GET
  /api/settings/models/options`, and `GET /api/swarm/models`, open to any
  signed-in user) returned the rows raw, and the Agents page showed the
  address with its password. Gate: `tests/test_no_get_route_answers_a_provider_key.py`
  walks every GET `/api` route with a provider whose every secret is a
  sentinel (the raw options as the control).
- **Masking is by key AND by value.** A password inside a URL is a secret
  whatever the key is called (`kazma_core/security/url_credentials.py`, the
  one home): `memory.backends.state.url` held the live Postgres DSN in
  plaintext and the Settings API returned it (2026-09-25), because every
  masker decided by key name. Every function named mask*/redact* that decides
  by key is found from the source and fed a URL password by
  `tests/test_url_credentials.py::test_every_key_name_masker_also_masks_url_passwords`;
  a new one needs a probe there. The mask is `****`, which
  `is_masked_secret_placeholder` refuses to write back, so a form can round-trip
  it. Provider, profile and connector saves go further
  (`url_credentials.restore_masked_url`, 2026-09-26): a URL posted back
  exactly as shown keeps its stored password; stars with any other change
  (host, user, path) are refused with a 400 — a stored password is never
  moved to a URL someone just typed (`tests/test_url_password_round_trip.py`).

**E. Nothing blocking on the event loop; nothing fire-and-forget.**
- A sync `sqlite3.connect` inside `async def` pins the loop that serves
  every SSE and WebSocket stream. Drop `async` (FastAPI threadpools sync
  handlers) or wrap in `asyncio.to_thread`.
- `asyncio` holds only a WEAK reference to a task, so a discarded
  `create_task(...)` can be garbage-collected mid-run, silently. Use
  `kazma_core.background.spawn_background(coro, name=…)`. Bare
  `loop.create_task` in product code (including `ops_alerts._dispatch`)
  is the same class of bug — prefer `spawn_background`.
- CI: `test_no_blocking_db_driver_in_async`, `test_no_bare_create_task`.
- **A cancelled task is waited for with a bound** (`kazma_core/bounded_cancel.py`,
  2026-10-23). A cancel that lands while anyio reads an httpx socket is
  sometimes absorbed (3.11 + selector loop, 3 in 4,000), and a loop that
  catches errors then runs on: the typing indicator's `stop()` awaited one
  under its lock, and every later message on every chat app waited on it
  before its turn began -- two hours of silence on Telegram, no error. Use
  `cancel_and_wait` / `wait_then_cancel` / `wait_for_bounded`; never
  `X.cancel()` then `await X`, nor `asyncio.wait_for(<task>)` (on timeout it
  cancels and waits unbounded), and never await a task's end while holding a
  lock others need. A loop that must stop also checks a stop flag. Gate:
  `tests/test_bounded_cancel.py` (the old shapes and the old indicator as
  negative controls).
- **The LLM ledger row is written off the loop** (2026-10-15). Async code
  awaits `observability.llm_ledger.arecord_llm_call`: the SQLite insert and
  the ledger's switch (a settings read) run in a thread, the caller waits
  for its row (a turn's totals, `turn_usage`, read after its calls returned,
  include them, in the order made), and the write is shielded, so a
  cancelled caller loses no row and waits for it, bounded. `resilient_chat`
  (every swarm worker and research model call) wrote it on the loop until
  then. `record_llm_call` and the ledger's readers are in
  `_LOOP_STALL_HELPERS`. Gate: `tests/test_llm_ledger_off_the_loop.py`
  (SQLite traced on the ledger's connection; the inline, unawaited and
  unshielded writes as negative controls). The non-stop settings the
  failover chains and the turn's envelope read (`get_nonstop_config`:
  kazma.yaml, then the settings store) are a loop-stall helper too; the
  supervisor, `resilient_chat`, `run_agent_turn` and the runner await it in
  a thread.
- **Every model call is in the ledger, with the cache's share** (2026-11-22,
  the memory plan's findings 6 and 9). Memory's own calls -- the deep pass,
  the weekly summaries and roll-ups, the lesson refiner, the V1 backfill --
  were in no ledger, so no spend report, product measure or person's daily
  limit counted them; they go through `llm_ledger.ledgered_chat` (one call
  and its row, thread `memory:<work>` when none is bound, whose call from
  the bound scope; a failed call an `error` row). And no row counted the
  prompt tokens a provider served from its cache: an answered call's row
  hands its usage over (`usage=`) and the ledger reads it with
  `kazma_core.token_usage.token_counts`, whatever the shape (DeepSeek's
  `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, OpenAI's and Qwen's
  `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, Anthropic's
  `cache_read_input_tokens` beside an `input_tokens` that leaves it out --
  read raw, an Anthropic row's prompt counted none) into `cached_tokens`;
  every sum gives `prompt_tokens` and `cached_tokens` beside each other.
  Entity resolution's tier 3 (a model deciding a merge) is removed: its
  `client.chat(` was a coroutine never awaited, so it never reached a
  provider; no product code calls a client's chat without awaiting it
  (`tests/test_coroutines_are_awaited.py`). Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_calls_ledgered.py` (the deep pass EN/AR, the summaries'
  chat and the refiner through the real code; today's calls, today's rows
  and planted sites as the controls).

**F. Errors do not carry internals.**
- API handlers return `kazma_core.errors.safe_error(exc)` — a stable code
  plus a correlation id, with the real exception logged under that id.
- 4xx **validation** paths use `validation_error(exc)` instead: the message
  is the caller's answer, and replacing it with a code makes the API
  unusable. Redaction applies either way.
- **No answer carries an exception's own text** (2026-11-14). A page that
  shows the error gets `described_error(sentence, exc)`: Kazma's sentence
  with the code and the reference ("Could not resolve the clone URL from
  GitHub (upstream_unavailable, ref: 1a2b3c4d)."), the text logged under it.
  The clone route, the email and X helpers (`str(exc)[:300]` whenever
  `KAZMA_PRODUCTION` was unset), the backup delete, the memory backend
  tests, the MCP add and the Knowledge page's "not stored" reasons answered
  library, OS and driver text: paths, hosts, SQL. A mail server's login
  answer, an FTP server's reply and the X API's answer stay (what the owner
  fixes). Gate: `tests/test_route_errors_carry_no_exception_text.py` -- every
  module under `kazma-ui/kazma_ui` and `kazma-gateway/kazma_gateway/routers`,
  every `except ... as e` (and parameter typed as an exception) whose text
  reaches a `return`, `raise`, `yield` or `*Response(...)`, also through a
  local value; Kazma's refusal classes and one site are declared with why,
  a declaration that excuses nothing fails, planted old shapes as the
  negative control.

**G. Fenced tool output.**
- Fetched pages, search results, saved research chunks and MCP resource
  bodies go through `prompt_fence.fence_untrusted()`. So do memory and
  Knowledge read back by a tool (Memory audit M11, Knowledge KB-S01,
  2026-10-13): `memory_search`, `memory_list_*`, `memory_admin`'s lists and
  `knowledge_search` (its citation directive stays outside the fence).
  `memory_search` shows a memory's display text and says "unavailable, NOT
  an empty result" when recall fails. The per-function gate
  (`FENCED_TOOL_FUNCTIONS`) reads tools registered inside `register_*` too.
  They are the largest source of attacker-controlled text in the system and
  used to reach the model raw. CI: `test_no_unfenced_web_tool_output`.

**H. One writer for the procedural recorder.**
- A thread-per-tool-call used to crash Windows (`AccessViolation` in FTS /
  schema / ConfigStore — three faces of one race). **One worker thread**
  now drains a bounded queue; schema is ensured once per process; the queue
  drops rather than blocks; `atexit` drains it. Do not reintroduce a thread
  per call. Repro: `tests/test_truncation_retry.py`.
- `reset_config_store()` must not close the sqlite handle out from under a
  background reader. Closing is **opt-in** (`close=False` is the default).
  The recorder reads `read_memory_cfg()` on the caller thread so the worker
  never touches ConfigStore. **A default every caller must override to be
  safe is the wrong default.**
- The *explicit* `ConfigStore.close()` was the remaining way to free that
  handle under a reader, and it did — see §8. Repro:
  `tests/test_config_store_close_race.py`.

**I. A process a tool starts gets no secrets (2026-09-26).**
- `shell_exec` / `python_exec` always used a minimal environment. pytest
  (`run_unit_tests`, the patch-set verify run), `pip`/`npm` installs, `ruff`,
  git and the IDE's read-only git passed the server's whole environment --
  `KAZMA_VAULT_KEY`, the database password, API keys -- to code nobody
  reviewed: a repository's conftest and tests, install scripts, hooks,
  `core.fsmonitor`.
- `security/child_env.tool_child_env()` is the builder: the server's
  environment minus every `KAZMA_*` name, credential-named variables and URLs
  carrying a password (git keeps HOME, its credential helper, SSH_AUTH_SOCK).
  `run_off_loop` (the skills' runner) fills `env=` with it when the caller
  does not; a caller that builds its own env starts from it
  (`get_commit_env`, `_git_sync`). `KAZMA_CHILD_ENV_ALLOW` lets named
  variables through, never `KAZMA_*` ones.
- Gate: `tests/test_child_env.py` finds every process started under the
  tool, IDE and skill folders and checks where its env came from (closures
  included); behavioural half runs real pytest and a real git hook.
- **The gateway routers, chat commands and web UI too** (2026-09-30):
  `/api/git/status` ran `git status` -- which starts a repository's own
  `core.fsmonitor` -- with the server's environment, and the web and `/ide`
  clones passed `{**os.environ}`, which the gate took for a minimal dict
  literal. Git in a workspace now runs with `tool_child_env()` and
  `-c core.fsmonitor=false`; a clone's token rides
  `github_client.clone_auth_env` (a git config header, never argv). The gate
  covers those folders, sees `asyncio.to_thread(subprocess.run, ...)`, and a
  dict that unpacks another is not minimal. Settings' server restart is the
  one exemption (it starts the server itself).
- **A minimal environment keeps Windows' `SystemDrive`** (2026-11-14). Every
  list of variables a child keeps held `SystemRoot` and dropped `SystemDrive`
  (the browser's, the page parser's, the search and DNS workers', the document
  workers' and broker's, the shell tool's, the local code runner's), and
  Windows expands `%SystemDrive%` in its own paths: the browser's font cache
  made a folder literally named `%SystemDrive%` in the live install. Gate:
  `tests/test_child_env_keeps_system_drive.py` (every literal list in the
  product that keeps SystemRoot keeps SystemDrive; a real `cmd` started with
  the old list prints `%SystemDrive%` as the control).
- **A shell command's home and temp folder are its own**
  (`post_hitl._tool_home_for`, 2026-10-02): one folder per workspace under
  the system temp folder (`kazma-tool-home/<hash>`, kept between commands so
  caches work), for HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA and the temp
  variables. They were the workspace itself, so every tool a command ran
  kept its user-level files in the repository the agent was working in: the
  live install folder (its workspace) held 143 MB of uv cache and temp files
  where `git add -A` would commit them. Still never the operator's own home.
  `tests/test_shell_child_home.py` (a real child; the old environment as the
  negative control).




### 27. Backups that report success (2026-08-29)

A backup that logs "complete" while the offsite copy cannot write is the
same as no backup. Reproductions: `tests/test_backup_silent_failures.py`.

**A. Prove the write.** `restic_repo.remote_writable()` PUTs a probe before
any restic call. `rclone:` and `s3:` are both probed (`s3:` = stdlib SigV4
PUT+DELETE under `locks/` — the prefix an append-only key must still be
allowed to delete). A read-only probe is worthless. `_run` refuses restic
when the probe fails (`backup.restic_remote_read_only`). Tests:
`tests/test_restic_s3_write_probe.py`.

**B. A missing passphrase is not a config note.** `alert_missing_password()`
is critical, and silent only when no repository exists yet.

**C. Mechanisms that only speak when they break cannot be told from
mechanisms that never run.** Successful restic snapshot + restore each log
one line. `observability/firing_ledger.py` (`run_weekly_sweep`, started
from `start_memory_worker`) counts them. `_log_paths()` must read
**guard.log and kazma.log, and their rotated siblings** (the app log rotates
at midnight; reading only the live file made a weekly report of one day and
called six days of backups "silent", 2026-09-23). Signatures are checked
against the code: `test_every_ledger_signature_matches_a_line_the_code_emits`
derives the emitted lines from logger format strings, ops-alert keys and the
result `summary()` methods -- a signature no code emits fails the build. A
mechanism logs on SUCCESS too (restic maintenance did not, and its signature
matched only the failure line). A health-gated restart is a
`guard.restarting` whose reason is `unhealthy (...)`, not a failed probe. The
sweep runs in a thread (it reads ~4M lines) and must stay scheduled (it
shipped unscheduled once).

**The report says everything, problems first (2026-09-30).** The week to
2026-09-29 read "15 of 29 mechanisms fired" and named eight: six health-gated
restarts and thirty loop stalls were among the seven it cut, "29" counted a
placeholder row, and 141 of its "149 alerts" were one alert held back 140
times by its cooldown. Now `firing_ledger.render` names every mechanism; each
signature has a kind (symptom / recovery / routine / alerting) and routine
ones a schedule (`per_week`: a job below 75 % of it "needs a look" -- the
daily digest ran 2 of 7); alerts count as SENT (a `(throttled)` line is a
repeat held back, counted apart); restart reasons and alert keys are tallied
(`group`); the stall dumps of the week are read for what blocked the loop
(the first Kazma frame above the storage layer, and its caller -- old dumps
by the thread in `_run_once`); manifest mechanisms with no signature are
"not watched", never a mechanism. Tests: `tests/test_firing_ledger_report.py`.

**The report is laid out in lines and sent whole (2026-11-11).** Telegram
showed the week to 2026-11-11 as one paragraph under a 111-character title,
cut at "Stops over budget 0": `firing_ledger.render` joined its sections with
spaces, `ops_alerts.alert` cut every detail at 600 characters, and the daily
digest printed the title as the alert's name. Now: a short title
(`firing_ledger._title`: what needs a look, the targets missed), sections
with a blank line between them and one item a line (a tally's reasons under
their mechanism; the targets marked ✅ ❌ ❔, `weekly_targets.render_targets`),
sent with `max_detail=firing_ledger.BODY_BUDGET`; past it the last sections
are left out whole and named. A missed target makes the report a warning; a
failure measuring the targets is the report's scan error, never the loss of
the report. Every detail `ops_alerts` cuts ends at a line or word with
`ops_alerts.CUT_MARK`, and the digest cuts an alert's label at
`daily_digest._LABEL_MAX`. **The finished-turn line has one reader**,
`turn_line.read_turn_line`: the targets matched `failed=True|False` while
`close_turn` writes `yes`/`no`, so "Turns that succeed" was unknown every
week (its fixture wrote the form no code writes). Gate:
`tests/test_weekly_report_reads_turns.py` (the real `close_turn` line; the old
pattern as the negative control; no second parser).

**D. One restic run per repository** (`restic_repo._run`, 2026-09-30). The
universal backup's snapshot and the maintenance task's `forget --prune` /
`check` are separate queue tasks and overlapped; `forget` and `check` lock a
repository exclusively, so the second failed "already locked" (a skipped
offsite snapshot 09-28 04:07, a skipped remote forget 09-29 22:21). A lock
per repository orders Kazma's own runs; `--retry-lock 10m` waits out a
restic started elsewhere (the restore listing too). A missed snapshot alerts
(`backup.restic_snapshot_failed`, warn, 12 h) -- it was a WARNING line only.
Tests: `tests/test_restic_one_run_per_repo.py` (negative control: a lock per
call overlaps).

**D2. Kazma's own stop is not a repository failure** (`restic_repo._run`,
2026-11-12). The guard stops the server with CTRL_BREAK / SIGTERM to its
whole process group, and restic, in it, quit mid-check: a deploy's reload
logged "restic check FAILED for remote", paged that the remote repository
failed verification, and `deploy_live.py` read the ERROR and reverted a good
commit. restic starts in its own process group (`_own_process_group`: a run
Kazma started finishes even when the server stops), and a run that still
fails while Kazma is stopping is `interrupted` -- said at INFO by every
caller, never alerted, run again at the next pass. `deploy_live.py`'s log
check reads from the new server's spawn (the guard's `child.spawned`,
`new_boot`), never from the reload request. And its revert is built on
`origin/main` in a worktree of its own (`revert_on_origin`), never on a
checkout's HEAD: run from the live install's copy, its revert was made on
the live HEAD and pushed the live install's own commits (its local
`kazma.yaml` since 2026-10-03) to the public repository, and `main` shipped
that file until it was restored. Run it from the dev checkout
(`.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/deploy_live.py --live
C:/Users/balfa/kazma`). Tests: `tests/test_restic_stop_is_not_a_failure.py`,
`tests/test_deploy_live.py` (each with the old behaviour as the control).

**D2b. A backup tool Kazma's stop ended is interrupted, never failed**
(`kazma_core/child_stop.py`, 2026-11-13). pg_dump and pg_basebackup stay in
the server's group -- killed at a stop, a dump starts again cleanly, where an
orphan would leave a half-written file -- and a reload during the 6-hour dump
paged "Postgres dump failed ... pg_dump: terminated by user" (2026-11-12,
twice). `child_stop.ended_by_kazmas_stop(returncode)` is the one answer: a
stop's exit code (`STOP_EXIT_CODES`: Windows' STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT, a POSIX
SIGINT or SIGTERM) and Kazma stopping within `STOP_WAIT_S` (the child sees the
signal 1-3 ms before the server marks its stop). The dump raises
`PgBridgeError(interrupted=True)`, `pg_backup.last_pg_backup_interrupted()`
says so, and the handler pages nobody; the base backup raises
`child_stop.StoppedByKazma`, which a new backup tool the server starts and
pages on raises too. Tests: `tests/test_child_stop.py` (real children).

**D2c. A missing local repository is made, and said once**
(`restic_repo._local_repo_made`, from `restic_repo.backup`, 2026-11-20).
Nothing in Kazma made the local repository (`<data dir>/backups/restic`): an
install restored from a migration bundle (the passphrase travels, the
backups never) had a passphrase and no repository, so every copy into it
failed "repository does not exist" and the Postgres dump's copy gave up as a
failed task. A copy into the install's own local repository makes it first
and raises `backup.restic_local_made` (earlier local snapshots are not in
it); a missing remote is never made (it may be a wrong address). Every restic
backup goes through `restic_repo.backup`. Gate:
`tests/test_restic_local_repo_made.py` (real restic; the copy without the
step fails as live did; the gate on the one backup function, a planted one
as the control).

**D3. A restore can be removed by the account that made it**
(`restic_repo.restore`, 2026-11-13). restic restores a snapshot under the
source's absolute path and gives each folder it rebuilt above the backup
the REAL folder's recorded rights. `C:\Users` lets an ordinary account read
but not delete, so pytest could not remove the restic tests' restores and
kept each run's whole temp folder (29 of them, 7.5 GB). After the restore,
`_release_rebuilt_parents` reads the snapshot's paths and gives each rebuilt
parent, top down, the rights it inherits from the target (`icacls /reset`,
never `/T`) and clears its read-only flag; the backed-up folder and its
contents keep what the snapshot recorded. Every `restic restore` goes
through `restic_repo.restore`. Tests: `tests/test_restic_restore_removable.py`
(parents that deny the account's own SID, so the case holds as administrator
too; restic's command alone as the negative control; a planted second
restore command fails the gate). Not in `tests/test_restic_repo.py`: the CI
recovery-drills job runs that file and fails on any skip, and these cases
need Windows.

**E. The daily digest reads every source of its window**
(`observability/daily_digest.py`, 2026-10-03). The live digest said "Turns
completed: 0" over a day with four turns (three web, one Telegram that paused
for an approval and finished), and "Needs attention: maintenance
pauses: 2" over two `kazma update` pauses of 41 s and 11 s that had ended. It
read only the live `kazma.log`, which rotates at local midnight (eight hours
of its 24 at the 05:17 UTC send), and counted turns by "SSE turn complete",
which only the web stream writes. Now:
- the live log and its rotated siblings written in the window
  (`_window_files`, as `firing_ledger._log_paths`);
- turns by the line `close_turn` writes once per finished turn, from every
  transport (`[turn] Turn finished: platform= key= failed=`;
  `turn_runtime._note_finished_turn`): the key hashes thread, turn number and
  question, and the digest counts distinct keys, so a close after a restart
  is not a second turn. A turn that failed (`turn_failed`) needs attention;
- approvals from the gate registry (`hitl_gates.gate_outcomes_since`, one row
  per question, a `superseded` twin not counted), never from log lines: the
  WebSocket logged one more each time a page connected while a question
  waited. A registry that is off or unreadable is said. A question the
  approval-timeout watchdog settled (`deny` by `hitl_gates.TIMEOUT_ACTOR`,
  `expired_unanswered`) is "expired unanswered", never a denial: the
  2026-11-01 digest said "denied 3" over two cards nobody saw in time;
- lines of either shape the log file is written in (`_app_line`: JSON, or
  the plain "standard" format in local time), and a turn or alert line it
  cannot read is "Needs attention: log lines this digest could not read".
  Kazma set up logging at a Windows boot before Postgres was up, the
  `logging.format` read failed, and the server wrote plain lines for 31
  hours (2026-10-30/31): the JSON-only digest said "Turns completed: 0 ...
  No failures, no restarts, no alerts" over that day. `logging_config`
  now falls back to the install's kazma.yaml when the store cannot answer
  (`tests/test_log_format_without_settings_store.py`);
- reloads (`guard.operator_reload`) and maintenance pauses (paired
  `maintenance.active` -> `maintenance.resumed`, with the longest) are
  "Planned work", never a problem;
- alerts from the line `alert()` writes for every occurrence
  (`[ops_alert] <key> | <title>`, ` (throttled)` on a repeat held back),
  never from `alert_state()`, which starts empty at every reload. Each
  reads by its title (its key when the title varies), every one is named
  (past 12 a section, the rest on one line: never "each is in the log"),
  and an alert of severity `success` or `info` -- logged at INFO by
  `alert()` -- is listed under "Notices", not "Alerts raised", and leaves
  the day quiet. The 2026-11-01 digest listed keys only, "Crawl completed"
  among the problems, and hid one behind "and 1 more";
- what ran without asking, chat by chat ("Ran without asking", times in
  the operator's zone, `cron.scheduler.resolve_cron_zone`): each YOLO
  window opened (`[SECURITY] YOLO ENABLED`, its length, who; the
  `YOLO DISABLED` that ended it) and each call a standing approval let skip
  its card, by YOLO, "Allow tool" or "Approve for task". Every gate that
  lets one through says it in ONE line, `safety/unasked.UNASKED_LINE`
  (`note_ran_without_asking`): the chat graph's split (`hitl.approval_need`,
  set only for a call its card would have asked about), its YOLO
  defense-in-depth branch, the swarm bus (`_allowed_without_asking`) and the
  MCP gate (`hitl.standing_approval`, the one reader of the three); before
  2026-11-01 a grant on the chat graph and anything on the MCP gate said
  nothing. The card that grants the approval is answered first and resumed
  after, so its own calls run under the grant: they were asked
  (`card_answered`, from the web route's `_apply_scope_grants`, the chat
  apps' "Approve for task" and `kazma ask`'s "always"; the 2026-10-31 log
  called that card's `file_write` a YOLO auto-approval). The older bus lines
  are read too. Gate: `tests/test_digest_ran_without_asking.py` (the
  writers' own lines through the reader; every function that reads a
  standing approval says it or is declared, every card grant names its
  calls, each with the old code as the negative control);
- the day is stamped only when a channel took the digest
  (`_deliver_digest` awaits `ops_alerts._deliver` on the server loop):
  `failed` is tried again in an hour, `no_channel` (nothing takes ops
  messages) waits for the next day. It was handed to the fire-and-forget
  `_dispatch` and stamped whatever happened. The weekly report counts
  "[digest] daily digest delivered" ("dispatched", the old line, kept for
  the week of the change).
Every marker and guard event it reads is checked against the lines the code
writes (`tests/_emitted_lines.py`, shared with the weekly report's gate;
"Detached turn completed" never counted anything: its line was removed the
day the digest shipped, 2026-08-28).
Tests: `tests/test_daily_digest.py` (each with the old code failing it).

**Chaos injection is only real where it lands.** `InjectionTarget.LLM_PROVIDER`
is injected INSIDE `resilient_chat`'s attempt loop. `ChaosInjectionError`
carries `.transient` (408/429/5xx) so retry/failover actually run.


### 28. A guard nobody has seen fail (2026-08-30)

Every guard test needs a **negative control**: assert it FAILS on a
synthetic violation in the same file, or "passing" means nothing. Enumerate
inputs from the **same SoT the system uses** (CSS gate parses `base.html`
stylesheet list — `kazma.v5.css` loads second and last-wins). Prefer
measuring behaviour to grepping source. A guard can be wrong in the
direction of blocking good work (`ast.walk` flagged a correct lazy
`import fitz`). Runtime corollary: `start_stall_watchdog` must be
stoppable — cancelling the heartbeat must not leave a thread reporting
stalls forever. HITL card CSS: do not duplicate selectors in `kazma.css`
and `kazma.v5.css` (Wave 8 L-2: standalone `.metric-card` lives in v5).


### 29. Context Integrity (2026-08-30 incident hardening)

Born from the @KazmaAI tweet-batch incident: 8 approved drafts vanished
between proposal and approval because deterministic trim deleted them, the
scratchpad built to prevent it was clobbered every turn, the summary net
never fired (24K→160K dead band), and a misread `what going on?` disarmed
recall. Plan + execution report:
`docs/plans/CONTEXT_INTEGRITY_HARDENING_PLAN.md`; the duplicated-stream
reproduction + fix: `docs/plans/S3_2_DUPLICATED_STREAM_INVESTIGATION.md`.
Tests: `tests/test_context_integrity.py` (56),
`tests/test_s32_stream_duplication.py` (3).

**A. The scratchpad channel is a merge reducer — never re-introduce a
replacing write path.** `SupervisorState.scratchpad` is
`Annotated[dict[str, str], merge_scratchpad]` (24 keys × 4000 chars,
oldest evicted, `SCRATCHPAD_CLEAR` sentinel for deliberate resets). The
transports must NEVER contribute a `scratchpad` key:
`build_turn_working_memory()` deliberately omits it, and the old
`scratchpad: {}` transport payload is precisely what wiped the
checkpointed value every user turn (LastValue replace). Adding any new
write path that puts a full replacement dict into the graph input
reopens the incident.

**B. Durable artifacts live in `agent/artifacts.py`, not in graph state.**
The SQLite store keyed `(tenant_id, thread_id, key)` is the source of
truth for scratchpad findings and proposals; graph state is a read-through
cache. House patterns are load-bearing: open through
`apply_sqlite_pragmas()`, DB under `kazma-data/` (universal backup for
free), GC rides the commitment-GC cadence (`worker_bootstrap.py` — no new
sweeper loop). Drafts are a row; the model reads the row. Context loss can
no longer destroy approvable content.

**C. The proposal chokepoint is the commitment resolver — the supervisor
nudge is NOT the guarantee.** `x_post` / `x_schedule_post` / `book_x_post`
refuse without a resolvable `proposal_id`
(`safety/commitment/authorize.py:_resolve_proposal_backed_post`, inside
`_resolve_send_outbound_act`); a broken artifact store denies fail-closed.
When the id resolves, the gate REWRITES `text` to the STORED text — the id
wins over whatever the model holds in context. The iteration-0 nudge in
`graph_supervisor.py` is advisory only and must never be the thing
standing between a draft and the wire. A scheduled post
(`x_schedule_post`) is the same incident with a delay — it is on the
required list for exactly that reason. The tool worker's proposal check
(`_commitment_resolve_gate`) passes ONLY the publish calls the resolver
verified in the same pass and refuses the rest (commitment layer off). It
must never refuse a verified call: from 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-24 it refused
every one, no chat post went out, and an eval test had locked that in as a
"property". `tests/test_x_post_proposal_gate.py` +
`test_a_verified_publish_stops_at_the_approval_card` pin both halves. The HITL card (Web `renderHitlCard`
+ gateway `_build_approval_prompt`) renders the stored proposal text, so
what the user approves is what publishes. That covers the time too
(Scheduled audit SCH-E08, 2026-10-14): a rebook of a cancelled, failed or
expired booking is a new key revision at the new time, a booking still live
at another time answers `booking_conflict`, and every booking reply gives
the stored time and state, `ok` only when the state is `scheduled`
(`tests/test_x_rebook_and_fire_cycle.py`).

**D. The summary net fires on EVERY trim that drops turns.** Never gate
`inject_summary_of_dropped` on a percentage-of-window again — trim fires at
`min(24K, window×0.6)` and the old 80% gate meant the net had effectively
never protected a trim. The injected note NAMES what was dropped ("4
assistant turns including 8 enumerated draft items"); under ~2K dropped
tokens the heuristic summarizer runs (zero extra LLM cost). Trims are
counted: `kazma_context_trims_total{summary=fired|missed}` +
`kazma_context_trim_dropped_messages_total` — a growing `missed` is a bug
report. **The budget is the context window** (95 %; the owner's decision
2026-10-18, `turn_input.resolve_trim_token_budget`): the 24K cap this plan
kept until real traffic was read trimmed a live day-long chat to its latest
message on every step. `agent.trim.token_budget` still sets an absolute
budget (clamped to [4000, window×0.95]). No other pruner caps the history
at a fixed size: `prune_messages_if_exceeding_cap` (30,000 tokens, every
tool output cut to 2,000 characters, saved to the checkpoint) ran first and
undid the window budget until 2026-10-22 (`tests/test_no_fixed_context_cap.py`).
**The window is configured, never
guessed** (`token_counter.resolve_context_window`): per model
`models.context_window.<model>`, else `context.max_context_tokens`, else
`memory.max_context_tokens`, else `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` -- 1,000,000,
shipped in kazma.yaml with installs on the old 128,000 following
(`config_defaults.RETIRED_DEFAULTS`). The prefix table that guessed windows by
model name (deepseek 64,000, gpt-4o 128,000...) is gone: stale, it capped
models below what the owner had set.

**E. `shift` is split — recall is disarmed only by an explicit pivot.**
`shift_explicit` (regex — the user verifiably said so; legacy `"shift"`
from old checkpoints counts) suppresses recall and supersedes the task.
`shift_inferred` (embedding drift) re-ranks only: recall stays ON and
`stub_prior_tool_chains(..., keep_assistant_prose=True)` collapses tool
payloads but keeps assistant prose IN FULL — a misread pivot must not
erase the thing being asked about. Interrogative check-ins
(`is_interrogative_checkin`, EN + Arabic شنو/وش/ليش/شفيه/وين/متى/شلون/شصار)
are gated BEFORE the embedder and can never classify as drift;
`_MIN_CHARS` is 25 plus a content-word requirement (length alone was never
the right signal). **An explicit pivot names the subject it leaves** ("new
topic", "let's switch topics", "خلنا نغير الموضوع") **or opens the message
with a word that drops it** ("never mind, ...", "مو مهم، ...")
(`turn_input._TOPIC_SHIFT_RE`, 2026-11-22, the memory plan's finding 11):
"switch to", "anyway", "unrelated", "forget it" and "مو مهم" anywhere were
pivots, and recall was suppressed for "did I switch to more water per
tablespoon?", a question about the user's own memory. Gate:
`tests/test_topic_shift_own_past.py` (EN/AR through `classify_turn_intent`,
the old rule as the negative control).

**F. A recovery attempt never re-streams content (the duplicated-prefix
invariant).** The SSE/WS bubble APPENDS token deltas; only `turn_complete`
has replace semantics. Once any delta of a user-visible LLM call has been
emitted, no recovery attempt of that same call may emit content deltas
again — the authoritative text arrives via the final response +
`turn_complete` backfill. Three sites enforce it: supervisor retries pass
`emit_deltas=(attempt == 1)` to `invoke_llm_chat`, the failover chain
passes `emit_deltas=False`, and `LLMProvider.chat_stream` tracks
`_emitted_any` so its blocking fallbacks yield only the final
`StreamDelta(response=…)`. Removing any one of these brings back the
`The proposal turn is The proposal turn is` incident string (locked by
`tests/test_s32_stream_duplication.py`).

**I. The trim keeps the conversation's skeleton** (2026-10-18,
`turn_input._with_conversation_skeleton`). Over budget, the deterministic
trim kept the latest message and its last tool rounds and dropped every
earlier turn: live, a day-long Telegram chat building a PDF archive of the X
posts was over its 24,000 tokens, and "send me the file here" reached the
model with nothing before it -- it listed the workspace, read all 67 posts
again (three times in one turn, each page trimmed away as the next came) and
asked which file was meant. The leftover budget now holds the earlier
requests and plain replies, newest first (16 messages, 1,500 characters
each, no tool chains), between the anchors and the latest message; it never
spends budget the trim did not leave; with the budget now the window (D
above) it is the net for a chat that outgrows even that. `x_status` gives each post's time in the operator's zone
(`created`, `time_zone`): the epoch alone sent the model to `python_exec`, an
approval card, to read it. Gate: `tests/test_trim_keeps_the_conversation.py`
(the old trim as the control), `tests/test_x_status_pages.py`.
`x_status(metrics=true)` reads the listed posts' `public_metrics` in ONE
budgeted request (`XClient.get_public_metrics`); a post X did not return is
`metrics_missing`, a failed read `metrics_error`, never a zero. And
`save_proposal` gives each X draft's length as X counts it
(`text_length.validate_text`). Live 2026-10-20 the agent answered "likes
unknown" from the posts' public pages, and asked to approve a `python_exec`
that printed `len(draft)`. Gate: `tests/test_x_post_metrics_and_draft_length.py`.
**A post's video is downloaded through the X API** (2026-10-24):
`x_download_media(post)` reads its media (`XClient.get_media`, one budgeted
read), fetches each file with `web_acquire.http.fetch_public` scoped to X's
media hosts (`_MEDIA_HOSTS`), a video's best MP4 under 50 MB (send_file's
limit), and saves into `<workspace>/downloads/x` (gitignored) for `send_file`.
Every failure is a `KnownEffectError`. Live, the agent searched the owner's
folders through six approval cards for a file nobody had downloaded. Gate:
`tests/test_x_download_media.py`.

**H. The running turn's tool outputs are not cut to fit** (2026-10-18,
`summarizer.prune_tool_outputs`). The supervisor prunes tool outputs when the
chat is over its budget and SAVES the pruned list to the checkpoint, so a cut
is permanent. The rule kept the newest 3 outputs of the whole chat and capped
every output past 1,500 characters, the running turn's included: live, an X
archive turn's `x_status` (1,571 characters) lost its fourth post as it
arrived and was cut to 250 two calls later; the archive held three posts, and
the model told the owner the tool could return no more. Now older turns' outputs
go first (to 250, then past 1,500), and only then the running turn's, past
8,000 characters, oldest first, stopping once the context fits. The running
turn starts at the last user message. Gate:
`kazma-core/tests/test_prune_tool_outputs.py` (the live shape; the old rule as
the control).

**G. Recovery spirals get an honest exit.** ≥3 turn-cumulative queries
against session/checkpoint/audit stores hunting the assistant's own prior
output force RESPOND with "what's missing + one concrete question"
(`tool_loop_breaker.count_recovery_probes`); digging only grew the history
that caused the trim.


### 30. HITL Gate Registry (`kazma_core/safety/hitl_gates.py`) — one gate, one row, one truth

Born from the 2026-09-01 chat-card incident chain (ghost cards, pre-approved
stamps, second question hidden on the dashboard). Plan SoT:
`docs/plans/HITL_GATE_REGISTRY_PLAN.md`. Every HITL approval across ALL FOUR
mechanisms (graph interrupt, swarm bus, pipeline checkpoints, semantic cards)
is one row in `kazma-data/hitl_gates.db` with a strict CAS state machine:
`pending → claimed → resuming → settled` (+ `timeout`/`superseded`/`error`).
Kill-switch `KAZMA_GATE_REGISTRY=0` degrades to a **thin execution
fallback**: a live checkpoint interrupt is pending (live card), never an
inferred Approved stamp. That is not a second decision author.

**A. Decision truth vs execution truth (the split is load-bearing).**
The registry owns the DECISION (was this gate answered, by whom); the
LangGraph checkpoint owns EXECUTION (is the graph actually paused). Readers
consult the registry (`hitl_thread_status`, `close_turn`,
`/api/pending-approvals`, chat.js `_serverGateViews` while
`_serverGatesAuth`). Paused + no covering
row is an **unregistered pending gate**: backfill from the snapshot and
keep the turn open — never treat absence as "no question". Auto-deny
uses the registry for *which* is pending and the checkpoint for *how*
(stale row must not resume nothing).

**B. Every transition is a single CAS UPDATE.** Zero rows affected ⇒
`TransitionConflict` carrying the row's actual state — that IS the 409 body.
Idempotent same-decision re-claim returns the row (200 semantics). `pending`
is the ONLY state a card renders live buttons for; the client never infers a
claim.

**B2. A decision names its gate, and the server checks.** `/api/approve`
verifies the body's `interrupt_id` against the registry BEFORE resuming
(`_gate_not_pending`, `routes_direct/misc.py`). Only a `pending` row may
be resumed; `claimed`/`resuming`/terminal answer 409 `not_pending` with
the server's actual view, and a row owned by another thread answers 409
`foreign`. The route resumes only a LIVE approval interrupt
(`_live_hitl_interrupt`: a checkpoint with a next step and no interrupt is
not paused, 409), keyed by that interrupt's id, and a gate the registry
knows that is not the live interrupt answers 409 (`gate_names_interrupt`);
the gate-less "security resume" fallback is gone on the web and the
gateway (2026-10-14, Time Travel audit TT-02: after a restore wrote a
mid-turn step, a still-live card resumed it and ran a call the human had
denied). A missing row or id can still reach the live interrupt
for legacy dashboard/TUI/platform clients, but execution now requires
`record_gate_decision(..., require_durable=True)` (2026-10-05). It backfills
the verified gate, strictly claims it once and records resuming before any
projection or drive. Registry off/unreadable answers 503 and stays paused;
a repeated identical claim answers 409. Legacy `claim_gate` idempotency is
retained only for projection callers (`allow_reclaim=True`). **Why (2026-09-20,
`tests/e2e/test_unified_turn_concurrency.py`):** the route's only test
was "is this THREAD paused". A resume pauses again at the next gate, so
a retried Approve — a double-click, a lost 200, a stale tab — decided
the question the human had never seen (approved `file_write`, authorized
`shell_exec`). The 409 translates registry words into client words:
`claimed`/`resuming` leave as `inflight`, because chat.js converges on
that and paints an ERROR on anything else.

**B3. A click on a pending card waits for the segment that showed it**
(2026-10-01). A segment journals its approval card and THEN finishes (the
turn's totals, the reply's save); until its task ends the thread counts as
running, and the route refused an Approve sent in that window as "no longer
pending" over a gate that was pending -- the button did nothing. When the
registry has the named gate on record as `pending` (`gate_is_pending`, the
positive question `gate_not_pending` does not answer), the route waits for
that task (`_await_segment_tail`, 10 s), checks the gate again and resumes;
no id, no row or a timeout keeps the old refusal. The lifecycle job caught
it once the route's own checks became faster than that tail.
`test_an_approve_sent_as_the_card_appears_is_taken` holds the tail open for
a second (negative control: the same turn without the wait is refused).

**C. Two-id rule.** `register_gate` is idempotent on both `gate_id`
(LangGraph `intr.id` preferred) and `alias_id` (the deterministic
`make_gate_id` hash) — one pause can never mint two cards. A terminal row
under a HASH id does not eat a NEW ask for the same tool+args (fresh row,
uniquified suffix); a native-id repeat returns the terminal row.

**C2. A row keeps no credential** (2026-11-11). `register_gate` is the one
writer of a row's call (`_record_view`): `args_json` as an approval card
shows it (`security.approval_args`), `payload_json` with every call's
arguments masked (`redacted_gate_payload`), `message` through `redact_text`,
and `args_digest` = `arguments_digest` of the REAL arguments -- the swarm
card's footer and the Swarm page's `describe` show it. A writer passes the
whole real JSON (a text cut before masking no longer parses, and its secrets
stay); the row is bounded after. Twins are matched by `args_digest`, never by
the stored text (two calls differing only in a hidden secret are two calls),
and only between graph rows (the one mechanism registered twice). Rows an
older build wrote are masked once at schema open (`_redact_stored_rows`,
digest from what they held). Execution never reads the row (A). Gate:
`tests/test_gate_records_keep_no_credentials.py` (every `GateRow(` writer
driven with a planted secret and the raw row read; the old storage and the
text twin rule as controls).

**D. Surfaces render; they never mint.** Gate transitions publish through
`GateEvents` into the EXISTING turn journal (`hitl` parts of the same
TurnDocument) — never a parallel event stream. Writer sites: SSE post-stream
scan (primary register, has `intr.id`), `/api/approve` (claim + resuming),
drive terminal (`settle_thread_gates` — settles claimed/resuming, NEVER
pending: a second live question keeps the turn open), gateway pause/resume
(`gate_claimed_for_thread` — platform cards are per-thread), swarm
`safety.check()` (register→bus→claim+settle), pipeline
`checkpoint_manager._gate_register_pipeline`/`_gate_settle_pipeline`.

**D2. A decision has ONE writer:** `kazma_ui/hitl_decision.record_gate_decision`
-- transcript part stamp, registry CAS, THEN the journal `hitl` frame (the
broker stamps the frame's view from the registry; emit-before-CAS painted "No
longer pending", 2026-09-20). The web approve route, the approval-timeout
watchdog (`decision="timeout"`) and platform buttons all call it (the WS
approve path did too, until the socket's graph client was removed, §31 D). Each used to write its own subset: the watchdog never stamped the
transcript, so an auto-denied card stayed `pending` in the chat forever and
the turn reloaded broken (2026-09-26); platform buttons never told the journal,
so a browser watching the thread never saw the decision. It stamps only a turn
the session already has (a minted id would add an empty bubble). Gate:
`tests/test_gate_decision_recorder.py` (every function that builds a resume
with `approved=` calls it; `kazma ask` and `hitl_supersede` are exempt with
reasons).

**E. Reconciler — every crash window has one behavior.**
Approve-on-missing-row backfills (`created_missing`); `close_turn` settles
pending rows whose checkpoint is NOT paused as `orphaned` (in seconds);
`boot_sweep()` holds interrupted claimed/resuming rows as `error`, preserving
the human's decision and actor. The exclusive runtime owner sweeps with zero
grace at startup, so a fresh claim cannot remain stuck forever. It NEVER
touches pending (the card must survive a restart). `display_gates` includes
error rows to override stale Approved transcript stamps; `live_gates` remains
the lifecycle reader. A terminal registry row for the exact checkpoint
interrupt cannot become pending through the thin fallback. TTL sweep rides
the 15-min commitment GC cadence in `worker_bootstrap.py` (no new scheduler
loop). Metrics: `kazma_hitl_gates_total{state,mechanism}`,
`kazma_hitl_gate_parity_mismatch_total{site}` (must trend to zero),
`kazma_hitl_gate_reconciled_total{action}`.

**E2. An approval that expires is said for what it is, in the chat it was
asked in** (2026-10-18). Live on Telegram: the watchdog auto-denied a
`file_apply_patch` card nobody had answered in 300 s; the model read "denied by
user", asked for `send_file`, and that card and the turn's answer went to the
web journal only (`_drive_graph_to_journal`): never seen, it expired too, and
the owner was told twice that they had refused. Twelve minutes later a tap on
the first card answered "Already handled -- this approval was applied
earlier". Now: (1) the tool worker gives a timed-out answer (`timed_out` in the
resume) its own result -- "expired unanswered ... the user did not decide",
the watchdog's instruction, outcome `terminal` (`_denied_result`); (2) a chat
app's turn (the checkpoint's `_gateway` routing: platform and
`delivery_target`, never the session store) is resumed by the gateway
(`hitl_timeout.register_chat_app_resumer`, registered by
`create_graph_handler`; `agent_handler.hitl.make_timeout_resumer`) under its
thread lock, and the chat gets a notice, the answer and any next card through
the same `_run_resume` / `_deliver_resume` a tap uses; a turn with no address
stays in the journal; (3) a late tap reads the card's own gate
(`_decided_card_message`): expired, denied, or the approve path. Gate:
`tests/test_approval_timeout_reaches_the_chat.py` (each with its control). **After an approval the chat gets what the resume
added** (`hitl._new_assistant_text`, 2026-10-20): the newest assistant text of
the running turn that the turn had not said before the resume. "The latest
assistant text" over the whole history re-sent the previous turn's failure
after every approval of a step that only called tools.
`tests/test_resume_sends_only_new_text.py` (the old search as the control).

**F. Honesty limits.** `hitl_gates.db` is single-process truth (like the
turn journal) — no multi-replica claims; a Postgres backend goes next to §21
when needed. The registry cannot stop the model narrating while paused —
that is handled by close_turn keeping the turn open on any pending row.

**G. Graph tool receipts (2026-10-06).** `agent/effect_journal.py` reserves a
mutating call before dispatch and commits its result before the graph's next
checkpoint, on `tool_effects.db` (WAL, synchronous FULL; carried in migration
bundles and on the complete state volume). Identity binds tenant, thread,
turn timestamp, iteration, provider call ID and tool; the request hash also
binds arguments and workspace. A completed replay returns the recorded result;
a started receipt, timeout or result-commit failure stops the turn with an
honest assistant warning and no synthesis. Never reset an unknown receipt
or enable whole-agent retries on this basis. Reads are not cached. Legacy
states without thread/turn scope have no graph receipt. Direct IDE tool calls
and in-process swarm tool loops now use the same receipt engine. The IDE HTTP
boundary binds an `Idempotency-Key` to principal, tenant, payload and captured
workspace; its saved response never dispatches or opens another gate. The browser
retains unresolved IDs in session storage across reload, without storing payloads.
Unkeyed clients receive a generated ID but cannot recover a lost response without
having retained their own key. `tests/test_execution_recovery_scope.py` covers
concurrent requests, changed payload/workspace, denied gates and failed writes.
`tests/test_effect_journal.py`
includes real child-process death, concurrent admission and visible warnings.

`LocalToolRegistry.execute` retries only classified reads. Mutating and unknown
tools have one invocation attempt; a failure after invocation carries
`effect_uncertain=True`, which the journal persists and holds on replay.
Argument validation before invocation is still correctable. Do not turn a
post-invocation error into a retryable ordinary result.
**A refusal before anything ran is not uncertain** (2026-10-18,
`agent/tool_refusal.RefusedBeforeEffect`): a tool raises it only before it
writes, sends or starts anything, and the registry answers it as an ordinary
`Error:` result (`exc.content()`; a JSON `{"ok": false}` answer stays as it
is). Live, two turns in a row on Telegram: an approved `shell_exec` refused by
the host-shell policy, then an approved `browser_navigate` this host cannot
launch, each recorded "effects unknown; must not be repeated" and the turn
failed. **Every tool that is not read-only refuses this way**:
`tests/test_tools_refuse_before_effect.py` reads each one's own body (and the
helper it hands the work to, `DELEGATES`) and fails on an error it RETURNS
outside an exception handler -- an `"Error..."`/`"Safety:"` text, a refusal a
helper built (`denied`, `refusal`...), `{"ok": false}`, or the answer of one of
its module's own helpers that returns one, followed to any depth (2026-10-31:
`generate_docx` returned `_output(...)`, whose "Error:" the name-only rule
missed) -- and on a
`raise RefusedBeforeEffect` that the tool's own `except Exception` would turn
back into a returned error (pass it through with `except RefusedBeforeEffect:
raise`). An error returned from a handler (the action raised) stays uncertain;
one known to come after the action (`send_file`'s "was not sent") is marked
`effect_unknown(...)`. A patch set whose failed hunk was rolled back checks
it: every file hashed as it was before the set is a `KnownEffectError` ("No
file was changed"); only a file the restore did not bring back stays unknown
(2026-10-31: one letter of 19 replace-all patches did not occur, the
checkpoint put the paper back, and the turn failed "effects unknown"). A typed refusal raised
from inside an action counts too: the browser's launch refusal is
`web_acquire.result.BrowserLaunchRefused` (an `AcquisitionError`, rebuilt
whole by Playwright's `type(error)(message)`). A test that calls a tool
directly reads its answer through `tests/_tool_answer.answer`. **A failure
whose effect the tool knows, where a repeat duplicates nothing anyone sees,**
raises `tool_refusal.KnownEffectError` (a `RefusedBeforeEffect`: the registry
answers it as an ordinary error). `generate_pdf`'s check that the requested
text reached the PDF names the incomplete file and asks for a new call;
returned as `effect_unknown` it failed the turn and forbade the retry it asked
for (live 2026-10-20). Every document tool's failed operation is one too
(`document_generator._output`, `document_processor._artifact_output`): the
operation deletes its export, so nothing was written, and the message says to
call again later when the service is down (retryable) or to change the request;
live 2026-10-31 a broker outage ended a `generate_docx` turn as "effects
unknown, must not be repeated". The check also compared table cells raw against
punctuation-free text, so every table with "°C" or "Jun – Sep" failed; cells
and text are normalized alike now (`tests/test_pdf_verification.py`). Never
for a send, a post or a payment. **And a call that cannot run gets no card**: `safety/call_preflight.call_refusal` (shell:
`shell_preflight.shell_refusal`, the policy then an empty command or a shell
metacharacter; the browser tools and `computer_use`:
`browser_isolation.launch_refusal`, the strict network mode's own decision,
off the loop) is asked by the chat tool worker before the commitment gate
(`_refuse_unrunnable_calls`, `outcome="policy"`, the turn goes on) and by the
registry before the swarm bus. The cards had said "BLOCKED: host shell is
disabled" and asked to approve a navigation Windows refuses. Gates:
`tests/test_shell_refused_before_card.py`, `tests/test_browser_refused_before_card.py`
(the live URL; the old browser tools give exactly the live `effect_uncertain`;
a launchable or runnable call still gets its card). So does a call whose
arguments the output limit cut off (`_refuse_unrunnable_calls(truncated=)`:
the response ended at max_tokens and the arguments are `{"raw": ...}` or
empty): live 2026-10-31 the owner was asked to approve half a JSON object
that the worker then skipped (`tests/test_truncated_tool_call.py`).
`dispatch_effects` tracks actual local/MCP mutator invocation across the worker
retry boundary, after validation and HITL. An unsuccessful dispatch after such
an invocation carries `retry_safe=False`; keep it on `WorkerResult` through
serialization and stop both retry and fallback chains.
Handoff failures retain earlier invocation evidence on every failed result,
including missing targets, so selecting the chain's final result cannot reopen
task-level fallback. IDE rate admission runs before receipt admission and once
per HTTP request; throttled requests retain HTTP 429 and can retry after expiry.
In-process workers stop
uncertain tool loops with an empty output and no synthesis. This does not qualify
whole-agent Temporal retries or custom workers' external effects outside the tool
registry. Completed effects and unknown effects both make whole-worker replay
unsafe; a successful tool receipt alone does not prove the next worker safe.
`UnifiedToolExecutor` carries the same uncertainty for a failed MCP mutator
dispatch, preserving the original failure through output hooks. Read errors
remain correctable. This does not make the external server transactional.

**A refusal counts on its own allowance, never as tool death** (2026-11-05,
plan D1). Every error the registry and `UnifiedToolExecutor` return before the
tool ran -- unknown or switched-off tool, a hook, commitment, permission or
division refusal, a preflight or approval refusal, missing arguments,
`RefusedBeforeEffect`, a read that answered with an error -- carries
`refused: True`, and `classify_tool_result` makes it `REFUSED` (a
policy-worded one keeps its class; `effect_uncertain` always wins). The
hard breaker neither counts nor resets on it; `update_breaker` counts refused
rounds apart (`REFUSAL_ALLOWANCE` = 6, reset by a success), and the same call
refused twice (`tool_signature`, kept in `SupervisorState.refused_signatures`)
ends the turn at once with the refusal and a stop note, so the model tells the
user what is missing. Live 2026-11-04 three wrong-path refusals ended a
research turn as tool death. The chat tool worker and the swarm worker use
the same breaker. Gate: `tests/test_refusals_stay_correctable.py` (every error
dict either executor builds carries `refused` or is declared post-invocation;
the unmarked results as the negative control).

Tests: `tests/test_hitl_gates.py`, `test_hitl_gate_bridge.py`,
`test_hitl_gate_read_cutover.py`, `test_hitl_gate_swarm_pipeline.py`,
`test_hitl_gate_reconciler.py`.

**Collision recipes** (also in `docs/audits/AUDIT_DEEP_2026-09-01_EXEC.md` —
keep both in sync):

1. **T-4 / `chat.js`:** scrub stays inside `renderTurn`. No second painter.
2. **H-8 / `tool_registry.execute`:** apply `rewritten_args`; `clarify`/`confirm`
   fail closed (“run from chat”). Never mint a second gate row on the web path.
3. **T-2 pipeline timeout:** finalize the task **and** `settle_gate`.
4. **H-9 bus:** `is_danger_tool()` → `approval_floor()` (the `requires_approval()` floor).
5. **H-12 (superseded 2026-10-14):** a bus request has one shared decision
   (`shared_approvals`): the first human Approve or Deny decides, every card
   shows it, timeout/cancel are their own outcomes. Must not retarget web `claim_gate`.

Protected files: `chat.js` (`_paintApprovalGroup`, `_paintHitlSlotCard`,
`renderTurn`, `_hitlAlreadyClaimed`, `_serverGateViews`, `_serverGatesAuth`),
`turn_document.js`,
`turn_runtime.py` (`close_turn`), `hitl_gates.py`, `hitl_status.py`.


### 31. Turn Delivery V2 — journal is SoT, client projects

Web/SSE/WS chat is **event-sourced delivery**, not a second brain.
Plan: `docs/plans/TURN_DELIVERY_V2_CURSOR_RESUME_PLAN.md` (P0–P4 shipped).
HITL sits on this as one projection (§30).

**A. `close_turn` is the only closer.** `kazma_ui/turn_runtime.py:close_turn`
decides whether a turn is open, waiting on HITL, or done. A pending
registry row keeps the turn **open**. Absence of a row is an unregistered
pending gate (backfill), never an inferred Approved stamp. Do not add a
client-side `forceEndTurn` wall-clock that marks CoT Done while the server
is still working. Its reply text is the RUNNING turn's
(`_helpers._this_turn_assistant_text`: after the last user message): a turn
cancelled before it said anything was saved with the previous turn's answer
(live 2026-10-20, `/abort` on a history request stored the swarm summary
before it). Gate: `test_an_aborted_turn_is_never_saved_with_the_previous_answer`
(`tests/test_turn_runtime.py`, the whole chat's last text as the control).
**An abort closes its turn** (`turn_runtime.close_aborted_turn`, both abort
paths): the cancelled run saved its row open and nothing closed it, so the
liveness watchdog paged `turn.stuck_open` ten minutes later (2026-10-20). A
partial answer is kept; an empty turn gets the cancellation note.
**An aborted request is answered "cancelled"** (`steer.abort_messages`, both
abort paths): the abort's system note alone is hoisted to the head by the
OpenAI-compatible path, the request was left unanswered, and the NEXT turn
wrote the aborted 2,000-word history (live 2026-10-20). Gate:
`tests/test_abort_leaves_no_pending_request.py` (the turn rebuild and the
hoist; the note alone as the negative control).

**B. The client projects; it does not author.** `chat.js` paints from the
TurnDocument / `_serverGateViews`. Token deltas APPEND; only `turn_complete`
has replace semantics (§29F duplicated-prefix invariant). Do not restore
`tokenAccum` dual-paint (T-4).

**C. Catch-up is resume, not replay of deltas.** Refresh / reconnect reads
the journal + gate status. Do not re-stream content the bubble already
appended.

**D. Transports are mouths.** SSE (`sse_chat/`) and the gateway graph
(`agent_handler/graph.py`) run turns and close through the same completion
contract. A new mouth that invents its own “Done” is a delivery bug.
**The WebSocket (`ws_chat.py`) runs no turn and takes no turn control**
(2026-09-30, AUD-026): send and approve are SSE, stop / steer / abort are
HTTP, and the socket answers those five actions with a refusal naming the
route (`_HTTP_ROUTE_FOR`). It carried a second copy of each -- a graph client
behind `KAZMA_WS_GRAPH` and stop/steer/abort twins -- that no shipped client
sent to, and the copies drifted (its approve lacked the gate-identity check
and dropped `approved_ids`, which fails open). What it still does: the
pending HITL card on connect, the cursor resume, `ping`, and clearing a
watched turn's orphan clock. The chat store sends nothing on it. Gate:
`tests/test_ws_chat_is_telemetry_only.py` (behaviour through the router with
a graph double; no graph-running call in the module; nothing reads the old
switch; the store sends no frame).
