- **An MCP server's secrets live in the vault** (`kazma_core/mcp/secrets.py`,
  AUD-030). An `env` entry named like a credential, `auth.value`/`auth.token`,
  a credential header, the value of a `--api-key=...`-style command flag and a
  URL password are stored at install scope (`cfg:mcp.servers.<server>.<field>`,
  in `INSTALL_SCOPED_SECRETS`: the manager connects at boot with no tenant);
  kazma.yaml, the settings database and config.raw hold `vault://` pointers.
  Every write in `mcp_servers_store` goes through `_write_everywhere`
  (externalize, keeping a masked or empty value's stored secret); a delete
  forgets the server's secrets; `KazmaAgent.connect_mcp_servers` first moves
  secrets stored as typed (`move_plaintext_secrets`, no write when none is
  left or there is no vault). Each transport's first statement resolves
  (`AsyncMCPManager._with_secrets`; `mcp_client._with_secrets`), and a pointer
  the vault cannot answer fails naming the field, never handed on. APIs and
  pages show `masked()`; the start log goes through `redacted_argv`.
  **Both MCP clients build a child's environment with
  `kazma_core/mcp/child_env.mcp_child_env`** (audit H-4's allowlist): the
  Test client used `{**os.environ, **cfg.env}` until 2026-09-30, and
  `tests/test_child_env.py` now scans `kazma_core/mcp` and `mcp_client.py`.
  Gate: `tests/test_mcp_secrets.py` (real vault, store, manager and routes;
  sink and transport gates with negative controls).
- **Every MCP preset is a published, maintained package** (AUD-031):
  `kazma_skills/certified_servers.yaml` names each preset's `package`
  (registry + name) and `source`; `scripts/verify_mcp_catalog.py --write`
  records what npm and PyPI say (`tests/fixtures/mcp_catalog_registry.json`)
  and `tests/test_mcp_catalog.py` holds the presets to it offline: exists,
  not deprecated, from the repository it names, no Kazma store path, keys in
  `env` (never the command). `kazma_ui/mcp_presets` reads the catalog from the
  installed `kazma_skills` package (the repo-layout path found nothing in a
  wheel install). Left out on purpose: a raw URL fetcher (bypasses the §32
  egress guard) and GitHub (Kazma's own tools).
- **Every JavaScript test file runs** (AUD-032): `tests/test_js_suites.py`
  runs each `tests/js/test_*.js` and `tests/test_*.js` (enumerated, so a new
  file needs no list) and CI's `js-check` job runs the same globs under node
  20. Until 2026-09-30 CI ran seven by name and 24 ran nowhere.

### 46. Chat-app slash commands say what they measured (2026-10-01)

- **A fact a command shows is read from where it lives**
  (`agent_handler/commands._build_slash_ctx`, per command). `/status`
  reports the `GatewayManager` (`stats`, `connection_report()`,
  `messages_in_progress()` -- the asking message excluded); `/cost` the
  per-call ledger (`llm_ledger.thread_usage`, off the loop); `/context` the
  chat's checkpoint through the `context_info` tool's report
  (`tools/context_cmd.context_report`, one report for both, off the loop);
  `/config` the active profile's model. A fact that cannot be read is left
  out and the command says so. Until then `/status` and `/cost` showed
  constants and `/context` measured the command itself.
  `tests/test_gateway_slash_facts.py` fails on a key a command reads that
  the builder fills from nothing, or from a literal.
- **`/config` writes one key, and a failed write is never a success.**
  `/config model` goes through `slash_commands.switch_model_from_chat`
  (`switch_active_model`: model AND provider, §1), which the `/model` menu
  uses too, in a thread; `/config memory` sets `memory.enabled`;
  `/config tools toggle` is Settings → MCP's `set_mcp_server_enabled`. They
  used to save the whole merged configuration back (`_save_config`, gone),
  and the tools toggle wrote `mcp.disabled_servers`, which nothing reads.
- **One rule for the admin gate:** `slash_commands.changes_global_config`
  (audit H-8, `allowlists.is_gateway_admin`), asked by `graph.py` before
  every slash command: code (`/skill install|uninstall`), the model, memory,
  MCP servers, the personality (the supervisor reads it on every step, for
  every user), the active workspace (`/ide repo switch|clone|<owner/repo>`)
  and the swarm's output routing (`/swarm config group|clear`). Showing and
  listing stay open. A new command that changes Kazma for everyone goes
  into it (`tests/test_slash_admin_gate.py`). The `/model` menu's pick runs
  before that gate and checks the same admin rule itself.
- **The "/" menu, `/help` and the reference agree**
  (`tests/test_slash_help_and_menu.py`): `BOT_MENU_COMMANDS` and
  `_cmd_help()` name the same commands, and
  `docs/docs/reference/slash-commands.md` shows `_cmd_help()`'s text and
  names every menu command. A new command needs all three. `/stop` is
  `/abort` on every surface (catalog, gateway, web chat): three "/stop"s
  answered "Unknown command" while a turn ran (live 2026-10-20).
- **A chat command that acts for everyone is an admin's** (2026-11-15, the
  defensive check before the independent review: `/x approve` posted to the
  owner's X account for any allowed sender). Every `/x` word but help,
  `list` and `subjects` (`slash_commands.X_OPEN_SUBCOMMANDS`, so a new word
  starts closed) and the `/skill owner/repo` shorthand are admin-only. Gate:
  `tests/test_chat_command_effects_need_admin.py` reads each `_try_*_command`
  branch's calls: a branch that acts needs `changes_global_config` or a
  `DECLARED_OPEN` reason (the old rule and a planted branch as controls).

### 47. Settings backup and restore keep the owner's keys (`kazma_core/settings_restore.py`, 2026-10-01)

The owner's rule: a restore never makes them enter a key again, and never
replaces one they have.

- **Every settings key is classed** in `KEY_RULES`: a setting, Kazma's own
  state (`system.`, grants, a chat's long-task record, cursors), a credential
  (`security.`, `account.`, `web_session.`, `platform.users`, push keys,
  `mcp.oauth.`) or learned data (the Soul). A backup holds settings and the
  learned Soul only, keys as `vault://` references, plaintext secrets and URL
  passwords as `****`. A restore writes settings only, so state and
  credentials in an older file are never written. Gate:
  `tests/test_settings_restore_classes.py`. It reads every write to the
  settings store in product code (literals, f-strings, constants, helpers). A
  key no rule names fails the build. A write it cannot read is declared in
  `DYNAMIC_WRITES` with the keys it writes. The stale-rule check catches
  typos.
- **Keys:** a held key is kept, even when the backup's differs. A missing key
  comes back only when its reference opens in this vault; otherwise it is
  listed to enter again. Named lists (providers, MCP servers, `email.accounts`
  by `alias`) and mappings merge: entries and fields added since stay. A mail
  account comes back only while the vault holds its sign-in. Nothing is
  deleted.
- **Preview, then exactly that plan.** `restore(dry_run=True)` runs inside
  `read_only_diagnostic`, so any write raises. An apply carries the preview's
  `digest`. A plan that changed since raises `PlanChanged` (409 + the new
  plan) and writes nothing. The undo record (`system.settings.restore_undo`)
  stores each written key's raw before and after. Undo reverts only keys still
  holding what the restore wrote, and keeps rows holding keys.
- **One check for every way a value is written**
  (`kazma_core/settings_validation.py`): the single and batch saves, a
  restore, `config_save` and the TUI (which falls back to a local write only
  when no server answers; `local_api.LocalApiRefused` means the server
  refused). A new validated key goes in `_rules()`. The agent cannot write a
  key that is not a setting: `safety.protected_config` asks `classify`, on
  the key without its tenant prefix.
- `/api/settings/import` and `/api/settings/reset` are gone (the import wrote
  raw rows and could not read its own export; the reset's buttons never sent
  its confirmation). `export_yaml()` copies the cached kazma.yaml before
  merging (`yaml_defaults()`). It used to write the rows into the defaults
  `get()` falls back to.

### 48. A saved chat-app setting reaches the running adapter (`kazma_gateway/chat_adapters.py`, 2026-10-01)

Live 2026-10-01: the owner revoked the old Slack app-level tokens and saved a
new one. The running adapter kept the revoked token and retried with
`invalid_auth`, and the Test, run right after the save, said "Kazma's Slack
connection is down right now" for a token that worked. Only a separate
Refresh applied it, and that Refresh rebuilt the adapters with its own copy
of the boot code. The copy had drifted: it started a platform switched off,
dropped Telegram's webhook secret and the allow-all posture, and sat out a 5 s
stop grace per adapter. Boot read the on/off switch from kazma.yaml, so the
Settings switch did nothing anywhere, and the swarm bus kept the bot token and
channel it booted with.

- **One builder.** `ChatAdapters` builds Telegram, Discord and Slack and the
  swarm bus's senders at boot (`build()`), on Refresh
  (`apply(force=True)`) and on a saved setting (`apply()`). Nothing else
  constructs an adapter or a sender: `tests/test_chat_adapters_follow_settings.py`
  scans the product code (git-listed) for one, with a negative control.
  Settings come from the store with the environment as the token fallback,
  and the switch `connectors.<platform>.enabled` is read from the store.
- **The settings store announces every write.** Each mutator of both stores
  carries a change-notice marker (`_announces`: the keys written, or None
  for "any": a raw transaction, an import, a reset), and the notice runs
  after the commit, outside the lock, where a listener's failure is logged
  and never fails the write. `add_change_listener` returns the call that stops
  it. The gate is in the same test file: every method that passes
  `refuse_write` or implements a protocol mutator must announce, unless it is
  declared with its reason. A new store write path therefore cannot skip the
  gateway.
- **What a change does.** `ChatAdapters` listens for `connectors.<chat
  platform>.<field>` keys and applies them half a second after the last write
  (a save sets five or six keys), on the loop, in the background:
  - an adapter field (`ADAPTER_FIELDS`: switch, token, app token, webhook
    secret) rebuilds that platform's adapter through
    `GatewayManager.replace_adapter`. The old adapter is halted first
    (`BaseAdapter.halt`: cancel now; `stop()` waits for a shutdown event a
    replacement never sets) and the others stay connected;
  - an allowlist field is applied to the running adapter in place;
  - a bus field (switch, bot token, destination) rebuilds that platform's
    sender, and an unchanged sender is kept with the approvals it is waiting
    for.
- **The Test applies before it tests.** It calls `apply([platform])`, then
  `first_outcome`, which waits up to 10 s while a fresh adapter has neither
  connected nor recorded a problem. A long-failing adapter is not waited
  for.
- **The Telegram webhook follows the running adapter**
  (`telegram_webhook_router(resolve)`, mounted always, 503 with no adapter).
  A router bound to the boot adapter kept its allowlist and secret after a
  rebuild.
- The page no longer calls `refresh-adapters` after a Save (it restarted every
  adapter a second time). Refresh Gateway remains for "reconnect
  everything". `/api/settings/connectors` (GET, PUT, /test) was a third,
  unused copy of the save and Test, and is gone.

### 49. The security report measures what it names (`kazma_core/security/hardening.py`, 2026-10-02)

Live 2026-10-02, `GET /api/security/hardening` reported 4 of 8 checks
failed, 3 of them critical, and none of the failures was true. The 48
"secrets" and 576 "escalation vectors" came from a package cache inside the
install. The 202 "vulnerable dependencies" came from asking OSV about each
requirement's minimum version. The skills check said "no manifests" because
it looked for the wrong file name. The four checks that passed did so on a
keyword found anywhere: "sandbox" in any YAML file, "permission" in any
Python file, "https" in `kazma.yaml`, and an audit class that nothing wrote
to.

- **Each check reads the answer the product uses.** Product files come from
  `project_files.iter_project_files` (§10 E2), with tests, docs and `.env`
  left out. Credentials are judged by `security/secret_scan.find_credentials`,
  the one detector, which never returns a value. MCP secrets come from
  `mcp_servers_store.servers_with_plaintext_secrets`, the list that
  `move_plaintext_secrets` empties. The scope guard is read through
  `mcp.manager.mcp_scope_guard_enabled`. Access and TLS come from
  `boot_guard.exposure` / `check_exposure_posture`, with
  `WEAK_SECRET_CHARS` in one place. Built-in skills are checked with
  `NativeSkillLoader.resolve_skill`/`problems()`, which `register_skill`
  also uses. Agent skills go through `catalog.activation_integrity`, the
  check activation applies, and `discovery.skill_files`. The audit check
  reads `hitl_gates.recorded_decision_count`. Shell and eval sites are
  checked against `_REVIEWED_SITES` (file, function, call, and the reason),
  and a test fails if an entry no longer matches the code.
- **A scan that did not run is never clean.** The dependency scan asks OSV
  about installed versions (`dependency_scanner.audit_installed`). It merges
  GHSA and PYSEC aliases, follows pages, and raises `DependencyQueryError`
  when OSV cannot be asked. A check that raises is reported as failed and
  does not hide the other seven. Each check's body runs in a worker thread,
  and the route is a read-only diagnostic.
- **Removed:** `SecurityAuditTrail` (written by nothing). The dead parts of
  the dependency scanner: multi-source queries without a version, a scan
  history database, `gh issue create`, and a cache kept forever. Also
  `fix_issues`, which wrote a `.env` into the install, and the
  `kazma_core.security` package's re-exports. `security_audit.db`,
  `security_scan.db` and `vuln_cache.json` are retired (`legacy`) in §37's
  registry.
- **A declared proxy is exposure** (`boot_guard.exposure`). Behind a tunnel
  the bind is loopback, so `KAZMA_AUTH_DISABLED` used to start cleanly with
  every `/api` route open to the internet. The boot guard now refuses it,
  and `KAZMA_DEV_WS_BYPASS`, when `KAZMA_TRUSTED_PROXIES` names a proxy. The
  middleware answers 503 to a proxied request while sign-in is off
  (`auth._arrived_through_a_proxy`), which also covers a proxy nobody
  declared.
- Gates: `tests/test_hardening.py` (each check's live failure shape and its
  keyword-era pass), `tests/test_secret_scan.py` (the old patterns as the
  negative control), `tests/test_dependency_scanner.py` (OSV faked with
  `httpx.MockTransport`; a silent-clean scanner as the control),
  `tests/test_security_report_sources.py`, and
  `tests/test_auth_disabled_behind_proxy.py` (the bind-only rule and an
  always-false proxy check as the controls).

### 50. Dependency floors reach every install, and the server says when one is behind (`kazma_core/install_requirements.py`, 2026-10-02)

The rewritten report (§49) found what OSV knows about the live install's
packages: 51 advisories in 14 packages (PyJWT, pypdf, urllib3, aiohttp,
cryptography...). `uv.lock` still pinned kazma 0.10.0 and the `aiogram` removed
on 2026-09-30, and CI's `uv export --frozen` exported it without asking
whether it matched `pyproject.toml`. Dependabot watched the `pip` ecosystem,
which never touches `uv.lock` and finds nothing to raise in `>=` minimums, so
no Python update ever arrived.

- **A minimum in `pyproject.toml` is a security floor.** It sits at the
  release that fixes the advisory, and also covers packages Kazma runs on
  without importing them by name. Base: urllib3, anyio, pyasn1. Per extra:
  aiohttp (push, rag), torch, transformers, oauthlib and setuptools (rag,
  docling), and virtualenv (dev). `kazma update` installs additively
  (`uv pip install -e`) and keeps any installed version that satisfies the
  range, so only a minimum makes an existing install upgrade. The lock changes
  only fresh installs.
- **The lock must match:** CI and the release SBOM run `uv export --locked`.
- **An update installs the locked versions** (2026-11-14). A checkout's
  install (`update._reinstall_local` -> `_install_editable`) passes `-c` with
  its `uv.lock` exported (`update._locked_versions`: `--locked`, every extra;
  a lock that no longer matches is not used, and the update says so). A wheel
  carries `LOCKED_VERSIONS_MEMBER` (`kazma_cli/locked_versions.txt`), written
  by the release workflow before `uv build` and kept in the wheel by hatch's
  `artifacts` although git ignores it, so the wheel's Sigstore signature
  covers it; `do_pip_update` reads it from the verified wheel
  (`_locked_versions_in_wheel`) and installs with it. A file that is not
  exact pins (`_LOCKED_LINE`: an option line could name another index) stops
  the update; a wheel with none (0.21.2 and older) installs unpinned, said.
  The release workflow fails a wheel that carries none. Gate:
  `tests/test_update_installs_tested_versions.py` (a stale lock and hostile
  files as negative controls).
- **Every release is tested as an upgrade from the one before**
  (`scripts/upgrade_drill.py`, 2026-11-14): the previous release's wheel,
  checked as the updater checks one and installed with its own locked
  versions (inside it, else its tag's `uv.lock`), runs on a private data
  folder; the new wheel is installed over it with its locked versions; it must
  report the new version, answer `/health/live` and `/health/ready` (or
  `needs_setup` only), keep a setting and every database the old one made, and
  log no ERROR line or traceback. Nothing of an install on the machine is read:
  `scrubbed_env` drops every `KAZMA_*` and credential variable and the servers
  start in an empty folder. The release workflow runs it before publishing; CI
  runs it on Linux and Windows on every push (`--any-version`: `main`'s version
  moves only at a release). Gate: `tests/test_upgrade_drill.py` (the whole
  drill opt-in with `KAZMA_TEST_UPGRADE_DRILL=1`).
  Dependabot uses the `uv` ecosystem.
- **The server says when it is behind.** A deploy is a `git pull` and installs
  nothing. At boot (background thread) `report_unmet_requirements` compares
  the installed packages with what this build declares and lists every
  requirement that is not met: a base requirement must be installed in range;
  an extra binds only a package that is installed. For a checkout "declares"
  means its `pyproject.toml`, because the installed metadata goes stale with
  every pull (the dev venv's still named `aiogram`). On a finding it logs a
  WARNING and raises the ops alert `install.requirements_unmet`. The fix is
  `kazma update --reinstall -y` (`install_requirements._update_instructions`).
  **The update stops Kazma itself, through the guard** (`update._ServerHold`,
  2026-10-02): the running server holds its packages' compiled files open on
  Windows, so a reinstall under it fails half way, and the guard restarts a
  server stopped any other way within seconds. The update waits until no chat
  turn runs, pauses supervision under its own reason, and waits for the
  guard's word that it holds (`stop_for_maintenance`; the gate before every
  spawn records `pause_held`, a guard too old to is judged by no child and
  nothing answering), then installs, lifts its pause
  (`resume_after_maintenance`, which never lifts another's) and waits for
  Kazma to answer. The hold covers the package step alone: the git update's
  pull runs under the server, and a refusal there puts the checkout back. A
  failed install keeps Kazma stopped (the guard would restart, again and
  again, a server that may not boot); the repair is the same command, which
  takes the pause over. **A failed install is repaired, never left partway**
  (2026-11-13): the additive `uv pip install -e` first, then every package
  rewritten (`--reinstall`, `_REPAIR_PAUSE_S` apart, twice at most), each
  judged by importing Kazma in a child (`update._environment_problem`:
  `kazma_core, kazma_cli, kazma_gateway, kazma_ui.app, dotenv`; a
  `find_spec` passed a package whose files were gone); the whole output of
  every step in `.kazma/update.log`. No `uv sync` fallback: it moved every
  package to uv.lock's version and, failing partway on live, removed about
  200 packages, Kazma among them (18 minutes down). After the packages,
  `update._bring_along` downloads the Chromium build the installed
  Playwright launches (`browser_isolation.chromium_installed` asks for that
  revision, in `chromium-<rev>` and `chromium_headless_shell-<rev>`, not any
  build) and puts each container setup made from this install's compose
  files on its pinned image (`container_services.refresh_images`: compose's
  project, service AND config-file labels must be this install's -- a
  checkout and an install in folders both called `kazma` share a project),
  never one whose secret `.env` lacks (`container_services._missing_secrets`:
  an update writes no secret, and recreated, SearXNG took the shipped
  placeholder key -- live 2026-11-14, on an install set up before setup
  generated it; the update names `kazma setup install --with <part>`).
  After a recreate it removes the image the container ran before
  (`container_services._remove_replaced_image`: exactly that image, by id,
  never forced, nothing when the container still runs it; a refusal is said
  as `updated; old image kept: <why>`): every update left the old version,
  about 4.8 GB on the live engine by 2026-11-14.
  Gates: `tests/test_update_repairs_a_broken_environment.py`,
  `tests/test_update_brings_chromium_and_images.py` (the old check, the old
  any-build rule and the project-only rule as controls). A pause also stops a server that is still booting, and wakes the
  backoff and crash-loop cooldown. Every installer (`_reinstall_local`,
  `do_pip_update`) refuses under a running server itself
  (`test_every_installer_checks_the_server_before_it_installs`), so a caller
  that skips the hold cannot replace packages under it; the wheel update and
  the extras repair had no server check at all. The same morning's fix
  refused and printed three guard commands to type around it.
  `tests/test_package_update_on_a_guarded_install.py`, and the real guard in
  `tests/test_guard_integration.py`. **The update runs as
  `python -m kazma_cli update`, never from a launcher it must replace**
  (Windows): a reinstall replaces `kazma.exe`, and Windows lets nothing
  replace -- or rename -- a running uv launcher (Python keeps the zip
  appended to it open). Live 2026-10-02 every reinstall from `kazma.exe`
  failed half way and left Kazma's own package half removed; renaming the
  launchers aside, tried that morning with a running `ping.exe` as its test,
  failed on the real launcher the same afternoon. So the update checks
  first (`update._launchers_in_use`: opening a launcher for writing fails
  while it runs, and writes nothing), refuses before it installs or pulls
  anything (pip does the same from `pip.exe`), and names the command;
  every instruction (the refusal, the boot alert, the guard's hints, the
  docs) names `<install python> -m kazma_cli update`.
  `tests/test_update_not_from_its_launcher.py` (a copy of a real uv launcher
  held by a running test; the rename it cannot do is the negative control
  of the old fix). The report's dependency check lists the same
  packages, without OSV. `packaging` is a declared dependency for this.
- **Advisories with no fix that Kazma cannot reach are reviewed, never
  hidden** (`dependency_scanner.REVIEWED_ADVISORIES`). Each entry has its
  reason and `reachable_if`, the code that would make the advisory reachable.
  Today: chromadb's Chroma-server advisories (Kazma embeds Chroma; no server,
  no `HttpClient`) and accelerate's `load_checkpoint_in_model`. The report
  names them as reviewed. A hub skill's scan does not apply the reviews.
- Gates: `tests/test_install_requirements.py` (pyproject over stale metadata
  as the negative control, extras, markers, self-references, the boot call),
  and `tests/test_dependency_scanner.py`. That file checks that no reviewed
  advisory's `reachable_if` matches product code, with planted uses as the
  controls, and that an unreviewed advisory fails the check.

### 51. A send says whether it was delivered (`kazma_core/tools/send_message.py`, 2026-10-02)

The gateway's send backend (`make_gateway_send_handler`) answered
`sent:<target>` whatever `GatewayManager.send` said, and the callers of the
send API mostly did not read the answer at all. A reminder a platform refused
was logged as delivered, a refused scheduled-post notice skipped the fan-out
that would have reached another chat app, `send_file` told the model "File
sent: ... -> Error: ...", and the document pipeline logged "✓ Delivered".
§33 makes the bus senders say the same thing.

- **The answer is `sent:<target>` or `Error: ...`**: the backend returns the
  error when the platform did not take the message (no adapter, a refusal, a
  timeout). `send_failed(result)` is the one reader. A caller either returns
  the answer (a tool) or reads it with `send_failed`: the cron outbox
  acknowledges a message only on `sent:` and otherwise retries it, then ends
  it `undeliverable` with an alert (§16E; the job was finalized DONE whatever
  the answer until 2026-10-14), the scheduled-post notice falls
  through to the fan-out and says when no chat app took it, the cron denial
  notice warns, `send_file` and the dispatcher tools return the `Error:` (a
  failed tool call, §37).
- **Files are read off the loop and carry their bytes.**
  `send_file_message` resolves the path and reads the file (up to 50 MB) in a
  thread (`_file_attachment`); the backend reads the Telegram auto-attach
  files in one (`_outbound_attachments`). An attachment without `data` is
  dropped with a warning: the backend read a `path` entry with no access
  check, and nothing passed one.
- Gate: `tests/test_send_results_read.py` (every call of the send API in the
  packages returns its answer or reads it with `send_failed`; the HEAD of
  2026-10-02 fails it at seven sites. Behaviour: the backend's answer, the
  reminder, the post notice, the dispatcher tools, `send_file` with no bound
  chat, reads off the loop).
- **A chat-app reply is kept until the platform takes it**
  (`kazma_gateway/chat_outbox.py`, resilience plan F3). Live, 57 Slack
  timeouts, about 65 Discord drops and 15 Telegram failures each lost a reply.
  `GatewayManager.send` records every durable reply (`OutboundMessage.durable`,
  the default) in `chat_outbox.db` as `sending`, tries it at once, and reads
  the adapter's report (`kazma_gateway/send_report.py`): the adapters' send
  loops call `part_delivered()` per accepted part and `part_failed(exc)` per
  failed one, which decides from the exception whether it may have arrived
  (a read timeout, a dropped connection: yes; a refused connection or a
  write that failed: no). Taken -> `sent`. Nothing arrived -> `pending`,
  tried again by the gateway's outbox loop after 30 s doubling to 15 minutes
  for two hours, then `undeliverable` with one alert
  (`chat.reply_undeliverable.<platform>`, never the text). Part arrived
  (`partial`) or may have (`unknown`) -> never sent again: the next reply in
  that chat opens with "an earlier message may not have reached you in full",
  in their language. A row a dead process left `sending` is `unknown` at the
  next start (`recover`). A reply sent more than a minute late says so. A
  settled row keeps no text and is purged after seven days (maintenance
  sweep "chat outbox retention"). **Not durable here:** an interaction's
  answer (`native_reply_id`: its token expires) and
  `make_gateway_send_handler`'s sends (`durable=False`): their callers read
  the answer and keep their own retries (the scheduled jobs' outbox, §16E),
  and two outboxes would deliver twice. Gate: `tests/test_chat_outbox.py` (a
  real process killed before, during and after a send: one delivery or one
  honest state; each adapter's report; the manager without an outbox as the
  negative control).

### 52. Run supervision: every running task watched, incidents you act on (`kazma_core/runs/`, 2026-10-25)

The owner asked for Kazma to be interactive about work that gets stuck or
fails, whatever it is. Before this each kind watched itself its own way (the
turn-liveness watchdog, the supervisor heartbeat with non-stop on, the
acquisition monitor) or not at all, and every notice was text with nothing to
press. Plan and evidence: `docs/plans/RUN_SUPERVISION_PLAN.md`; guide:
`docs/docs/guide/running-work.md`.

- **One read model, the stores stay the truth.** `kinds.KINDS` declares each
  kind (chat turns, swarm tasks, scheduled jobs, document jobs, research
  sessions, crawls and pipelines, X posts, memory tasks, maintenance sweeps):
  its adapter, its store, its budgets, what already announces which
  condition. An adapter reads its kind's store off the loop and NEVER writes
  it; `registry.list_runs` returns `contract.Run` records with the verdict. A
  kind whose store cannot be read is in `errors`, never "nothing running".
  Gate: `tests/test_run_kinds_declared.py` -- every product table with a
  status or state column is a kind's (`KindSpec.tables`) or in `NOT_RUNS`
  with why, and each adapter maps every native status, read from the kind's
  own enum or the status words its module writes. A new store holding a
  "running" status needs a kind or a reason.
- **Judged by progress** (`contract.judge`, pure): dead (owner gone past
  `dead_after_s`), stalled (alive, no meaningful progress past
  `stall_after_s`), slow, failed. Waiting on a human is never stalled. A
  verdict never cancels or fails a run. Progress: a chat turn's graph
  heartbeat, a swarm task's engine events (`SseBridge.emit` stamps
  `runs.progress`), a document job's `heartbeat_at`, the acquisition
  monitor's `since`.
- **Incidents** (`incidents.py`, `run_incidents.db`, a bundle store): one row
  per run and condition while live, every change a compare-and-set in
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a short-lived connection. A decided incident (closed,
  dismissed, expired) never opens again for the same run, condition and run
  version. Delivery is an outbox on the row: `pending` committed with the
  incident, `sending` just before the message leaves; a process killed at
  `pending` sends at the next start (once), at `sending` is `uncertain` and
  never resent; an `acting` row at start is closed `interrupted` and never
  replayed (`recover`). Incidents are NOT gate rows: a row in
  `hitl_gates.db` would hold a chat turn open (§30-31); a gate in
  `tests/test_run_decisions.py` keeps the runs code off the gate registry.
- **Telling** (`notify.py`): to the run's chat (its delivery target, captured
  at start: swarm dispatches record `source_delivery_target`, a chat turn's is
  its checkpoint's `_gateway` block) with `send_message(..., run_card=)`,
  which the gateway's send backend renders as buttons
  (`kazma_gateway/run_cards.py`); else `ops_alerts.alert` keyed per incident
  (never per condition: two stuck runs are two messages); always the bell
  (`/api/alerts/recent`). A condition another mechanism announces
  (`KindSpec.announced_by`: cron's alert outbox, the acquisition monitor, X
  notices, `memory.dead_letter`; a crawl an agent ran) is recorded with
  `notify = suppressed`. A failure that ended before this process started
  watching is quiet. One recovery note when a stalled run moves again. The
  turn-liveness watchdog no longer pages `turn.stuck_open`: the chat-turn
  adapter reports the abandoned turn and its card offers Close. A failed
  crawl's or research pipeline's reason is `crawl_jobs.failure_reason`: what
  the job recorded at its end (`_CrawlJob.finish(failure=)`, the pipeline's
  "found no URLs"), else the interruption, the stage, the page counts, else
  nothing; it gave "0 failed, 0 uncertain" for a search that found nothing
  (2026-11-05, `tests/test_failed_run_says_why.py`).
- **Deciding** (`decide.py`): claim (the first decision wins; a second is
  told who decided what, where), then `registry.perform` asks the run as it
  is NOW and refuses an action it no longer offers, then the kind's own
  control -- the same function its page uses (`swarm_panel/task_actions.py`,
  `turn_abort.abort_turn`, `task_queue.retry_failed_task`, the Scheduled,
  Documents, Research and X controls). A run whose effects are unknown offers
  only `retry_checked`. A button press is `/runs act <incident> <action>`
  from the presser (`platform_callbacks`, kind `run`), admin-only
  (`changes_global_config`, and each platform's press handler gates `run` with
  `hitl` and `swarm`). Web: `POST /api/runs/incidents/{id}/act` (admin, same
  origin). Gate: `tests/test_run_decisions.py` (every action of every kind
  reaches the page's control; an adapter wired elsewhere as the control).
- **Runbooks** (`runbooks.py`, setting `runs.runbooks`, all off): at most one
  automatic first step per lineage (`Run.lineage`: a retried task names its
  original) a day, never on unknown effects or through `retry_checked`.
  **Diagnose** (`diagnose.py`): a read-tier one-shot graph
  (`cron_fire_graph(agent, capabilities="read")`), the incident fenced, one at
  a time per incident; it decides nothing. Gate: `tests/test_run_runbooks.py`.
- **The supervisor** (`supervisor.py`, every 30 s from app startup, not under
  pytest) pages its own outage only after five minutes without a pass, and
  its recovery once. Surfaces: the Dashboard's Running work card
  (`static/js/runs_panel.js`, `/api/runs`), `/runs` in every chat (web:
  `sse_chat/_runs.py`, chat apps: `agent_handler/runs_command.py`), the
  agent's read tools `list_runs` / `run_status` (fenced). Gates: the files
  above plus `tests/test_run_adapters.py` (each kind's real store),
  `tests/test_run_supervisor.py` (fake clock), `tests/test_run_incident_crash.py`
  (a real child killed at each stage; sending before committing as the
  control), `tests/test_run_supervision_soak_harness.py`
  (`scripts/run_supervision_soak.py`, planted bugs as controls),
  `tests/e2e/test_runs_panel.py` (EN/AR, by the sidebar).

### 53. The full audit of 2026-10-26: side doors and failure paths (`docs/audits/AUDIT_FULL_2026-10-26.md`)

Each finding was a sibling of a hardened rule, not the rule. Each fix has a
test that fails on the old code.

- **A tool gets its arguments whole** (AUD-001). `UnifiedToolExecutor.execute`
  (every chat surface's executor) popped `user_id`, `division`, `resource`
  and `action` as RBAC context: `email_send(action="draft")` was approved as
  a draft and sent. The RBAC check those keys fed ran only when the model
  named a user, so it is gone; an engine passed in is asked nothing. Gate:
  `tests/test_tool_arguments_reach_the_tool.py`.
- **Text from outside never chooses a URL the server fetches** (AUD-002). A
  mention's pasted link is read from X's own `entities` (`expanded_url`, the
  mentions request asks for `entities`); `mentions_fire` followed the t.co
  redirect with a raw `httpx.get` before any check. In `x_api/` only the X
  client talks to the network. Gate: `tests/test_x_mentions_no_fetch.py`.
- **A migration import that stops leaves the target as it was** (AUD-003,
  AUD-004). Every pre-swap copy must succeed (`_back_up_live_dbs`) or nothing
  changes; a rollback deletes only a file that did not exist before; the
  vault key is written after the swap (`_sync_vault_after_swap`, which does
  not move the bundle's own vault.db aside) and put back by every later
  rollback. Gate: `tests/test_importer_failure_paths.py`.
- **One configuration masker** (AUD-005): `security/config_mask.py`, used by
  the Settings API and the agent's `config_read` (read tier), which returned
  nested provider keys and URL passwords. Gate:
  `tests/test_config_read_masks_secrets.py`.
- **`kazma mcp` and `kazma ask` never read the launch folder's `.env`**
  (AUD-084, `env_files.env_file_ladder(include_cwd=False)`): other programs
  start them in folders that are not the operator's, and a cloned repository's
  `.env` overrode the real environment. The installed checkout's `.env` is
  read instead. Other commands keep the launch folder (their data directory
  is found from there too). Gate: `tests/test_env_loading.py`.
- **The loop-stall gate sees a nested sync function called directly**
  (AUD-006/007/110). A nested `def` is threaded only when handed to
  `to_thread`; the SSE stream's `_persist_now` ran a whole-session write on
  the loop every 50 characters. Also off the loop now: instant-turn rows,
  `stamp_last_platform`, the tenant middleware's and rate limiter's settings
  reads, the capacity bar, and the document actions' preludes. Gates:
  `tests/test_static_gates.py` (`test_a_nested_sync_def_called_from_async_code_is_on_the_loop`).
- **More refusals before effect** (AUD-008, AUD-039): `file_apply_patch`'s
  refusals (a non-matching `old_string` above all) and a crawl refused at
  admission (`IngestResult.refused` for a page) raise `RefusedBeforeEffect`.
  Gates: `tests/test_refusals_keep_the_turn.py`, `DELEGATES` in
  `tests/test_tools_refuse_before_effect.py`.
- **A turn kept out of memory leaves no facts** (AUD-010): the heuristic
  pass asks `forget.refuses_write` first, and `enforce_ledger` takes back the
  facts of ledgered turns (`facts` in its result). Gate:
  `tests/test_memory_forgotten_turn_leaves_no_facts.py`.
- **Every guard reaper verifies the PID** (AUD-013): `_stop_recorded_child`
  too. Gate: `tests/test_guard_owns_reload.py`.
- **Smaller doors closed**: `shell_exec` refuses `uv run`/`uv tool`/`--with`
  and every `git config` that is not a read (AUD-085); the research readers
  refuse Kazma's stores (AUD-086, in the store-door gate); the IDE MCP
  server's `search_code` glob stays in the root (AUD-087); SSRF blocks the
  shared address space 100.64.0.0/10 (AUD-088); `git_status` runs with
  `core.fsmonitor` off (AUD-089); a card's YOLO is downgraded where
  `yolo_allowed()` is False (AUD-090); `docker exec` gets `-e PGPASSWORD` by
  name and a dump timeout carries no command (AUD-091); a scan converted to
  Word or Markdown keeps its artifact (AUD-009); Swarm's document listeners
  and Live voice are torn down on a soft navigation (AUD-011/012,
  `tests/js/test_soft_nav_listeners.js`).
- **The short-term batch (AUD-014..082)**, each with its regression test:
  - A provider 5xx is transient on the non-streaming path too (AUD-014).
    A pinned provider is never sent another vendor's active model (AUD-015).
  - A failed recall answers `degraded="recall_failed:<code>"`, never an empty
    result, through `memory_search`, federated search and `/health/deep`
    (AUD-026, 057). `mutate_belief` re-raises a refused write (AUD-027). The
    re-embed passes write each vector once, guarded against a forget landing
    meanwhile (AUD-028).
  - The MCP path gate reads every path-like argument (AUD-059).
  - A swarm retry names the chain's first task (AUD-016).
  - Cron recovery skips its own live sends (AUD-017). A fire's lease covers
    its task budget (AUD-019).
  - Claimed incident work always ends recorded (`runs/claims.py`, AUD-018).
  - A universal backup never deletes a running backup's folder (AUD-020).
    It counts the files it could not copy (`complete`, `backup.files_failed`),
    and retention keeps the newest complete one (AUD-021).
  - Document intake recovery leaves live uploads alone (AUD-022). GC skips a
    stage in use (`documents/live_scratch.py`, AUD-023). The heartbeat rides
    out a locked store (AUD-024). A block that fails to render fails the
    document (AUD-025).
  - The MCP Test client reads its own reply by id and drains stderr
    (AUD-038). `ollama pull` cannot block on its pipes (AUD-037).
  - Chat-app sends report each attachment and the swarm routes report a
    refusal (AUD-032). A rate limit of 0 means none, and one failing message
    never stops `gateway-consumer` (`dispatch_failed`, AUD-033).
  - Discord's fatal close codes stop the reconnect loop (AUD-034). The TUI
    writes locally only when nothing listens (`LocalApiUnreachable`,
    AUD-035). `send_approval_request` is a question with no HITL buttons
    (AUD-060).
  - Page scripts register leave hooks only through `window.kazmaAddLeaveHook`
    (`base.html`); no script assigns `window.kazmaOnSoftNavLeave` (AUD-030,
    `tests/js/test_soft_nav_lifecycle.js`). Dashboard chat links use `?s=`
    (AUD-031). The Dashboard's chat delete forgets the Time Travel steps
    (AUD-055).
- **The remaining Low items (2026-10-27)**, each with its regression test:
  - Core:
    - The commitment kill switches in the environment win over stored
      values (AUD-096).
    - MCP children never inherit a proxy URL carrying a password
      (AUD-097).
    - The MCP server gates a tool with no tier through `approval_floor`
      (AUD-098).
    - The shared HTTP client follows no redirects and uses the shared TLS
      context (AUD-099).
    - The vision tool has one byte cap (AUD-109).
    - The swarm worker's forced final answer is ledgered through
      `resilient_chat` (AUD-119).
    - `[KAZMA RECOVERY]` is a registered turn note (AUD-122).
    - An unreadable platform-user store fails closed
      (`PlatformUsersUnavailable`, AUD-123).
    - A module kept alive only by modules nothing reaches is an orphan
      (`tests/test_orphan_modules.py`, AUD-075).
  - Memory:
    - A failed macro sleep rolls back and commits nothing more (AUD-046).
    - The list-reopen repair never reopens a forgotten entry (AUD-047).
    - A failed ack counts attempts in SQL (AUD-048).
    - Neo4j relationship types are backtick-quoted and Forget removes
      orphaned value nodes (AUD-049, 063; unverified on a real Neo4j).
    - The swarm bridge and reconsolidation make no slow call under the
      write lock (AUD-112, in the D2 gate).
    - The dual-write mirror is set up once under its lock (AUD-117).
    - The bookmark store closes under its lock (AUD-118).
  - Documents and backup:
    - The parse floor counts the source (AUD-040).
    - Generated artifacts are left to GC (AUD-041).
    - Index, unindex and delete need write access (AUD-061).
    - Backups of the database read the snapshot `immutable` (AUD-116).
    - Intake inspects once when digest, name and policy match (AUD-114).
    - Listings are two queries on both backends (AUD-115).
    - Offsite uploads stream: OneDrive upload session, WebDAV streamed,
      S3 multipart (AUD-113).
    - `backups.offsite.` and `backups.extra_paths` are protected config
      (AUD-094).
    - The bounded-cancel gate also catches `wait_for` over a `gather`
      (AUD-071).
  - Gateway and CLI:
    - Telegram webhook updates take the polling path (`_dispatch_update`,
      AUD-065).
    - Kazma announces only its own join to a group (AUD-050).
    - Discord buttons follow the guild allowlist (AUD-066).
    - `kazma gateway` reports the server's real answer (AUD-073).
    - `kazma ask`'s "a" grants that one tool, never YOLO (AUD-107).
    - Package installs refuse option arguments (AUD-108).
  - Web UI:
    - Every session write in the stream package goes through
      `_mutate_session` (`SessionManager.transact`, AUD-052).
    - Approve records the session's actor, not the body's (AUD-100).
    - The login throttle reserves the slot before the await (AUD-101).
    - Route errors carry no exception text (AUD-102).
    - Push endpoints must be public https (AUD-103).
    - Soul confirm is admin-only with real statuses (AUD-104).
    - Every saved model profile keeps or refuses masked secrets
      (`ModelRegistry.save_model_profile`, AUD-105).
    - The OAuth message is origin-checked (AUD-106). Superseded 2026-11-11:
      the GitHub sign-in runs in the same tab and posts no message (§62).
- **A result that says whether it worked is read where it is returned**
  (2026-10-27, the audit's recurring pattern 2,
  `tests/test_failure_results_are_used.py`). A backup, migration, send or
  delivery function returning `bool` or an `ok` field may not have its
  answer dropped by a product caller (a bare call, or `_ = ...`). Calls are
  resolved through imports, aliases, `self`/`cls` and bases. A receiver the
  gate cannot type must be classified (`RECEIVERS` / `NOT_OURS`), or it is a
  finding. A site that may drop the answer is declared in `DECLARED` or
  `REPORTS_ITS_OWN_FAILURE` with its reason, and a declaration that matches
  nothing fails. Fixed when it was built: the importer's document restore
  (a failed safety copy went on to overwrite, and a failed install deleted
  the live `documents.db`; it now copies beside the file and swaps it in),
  and the gateway logging "HITL interrupt surfaced" over an approval card
  the platform refused (a WARNING now names the Web panel and `/hitl`).
- **No helper call stalls the loop in any area** (AUD-111, 2026-10-27): see
  §35. `TurnBroker.emit` stamps the gate view in a thread inside the
  thread's emit lock, so frames keep their call order. `ops_alerts._dispatch`
  asks its sinks from a thread when a loop runs. The LLM provider reads its
  egress target in a thread and changes the client on the loop.

### 54. The functional audit of 2026-11, Stage 1 (`docs/audits/AUDIT_FUNCTIONAL_LIVE_2026-11.md`)

The live install used like an owner, end to end (128 findings; plan
`docs/plans/FUNCTIONAL_AUDIT_2026-11_REMEDIATION.md`). Stage 1 is the High
findings. Each fix has a gate that fails on the old code.

- **A database outage is ridden out** (FA-259, §44 extended). On Postgres a
  settings statement runs OUTSIDE `ConfigStore._lock` (`_statement_lock`:
  reads take no lock, writes `_pg_write_lock`; the cache is touched under
  `_lock`, a write bumps `_write_epoch` so a read that raced it does not cache
  the old value). A refused connection marks the store down for
  `_PG_OUTAGE_HOLD_S` (5 s): calls fail at once (`ConfigStoreUnavailableError`)
  and a read answers from the cache, one caller probes (`_pg_access`). The
  probes (`/health`, `/health/live`, `/health/ready`, `/health/deep`) skip the
  auth and tenant middleware (`auth.HEALTH_PROBE_PATHS`), readiness runs one
  thread per check (`health._offloaded_check`: a check still running is
  awaited, never started twice), and boot waits for the settings store up to
  `config_availability.BOOT_WAIT_S` (13 min, `wait_for_settings_store`).
  Documents and the swarm count the outage as an outage
  (`documents/errors.infrastructure_errors`, `engine._store_error_passes`).
  Gate: `tests/test_pg_outage_ridden_out.py` (the old lock scope as the
  control; a real Postgres stop with `KAZMA_TEST_PG_OUTAGE_CONTAINER`).
- **A crawl a reload cut off resumes** (FA-263): a crawl that ends
  `interrupted` while Kazma shuts down says `interrupted_by: process_ended`
  (`crawl_jobs._CrawlJob.finish`, `_process_is_ending`), the mark
  `resume_interrupted_crawls` acts on. Gate: `tests/test_crawl_auto_resume.py`.
- **The documented restore restores** (FA-267/268/269/270). A restic restore
  is assembled into a data folder Kazma reads (`backup/restore.py`
  `_flatten_into_data_dir`: `assets/` first, `dbs/` over it, sidecars
  removed), checked by a child that resolves every store through
  `kazma_core.paths` (`_check_layout`), its databases opened `immutable=1`;
  the Postgres dump lands in `pg/`. The universal backup no longer copies a
  live database a second time into `assets/` (`_copy_assets`' `held` set).
  The CLI names the passphrase file. Gate: `tests/test_restore_layout.py`
  (the old assembly and copier as controls).
- **A migration export is of an install, and an import revives no revoked
  state** (FA-252, FA-255). `export_bundle` refuses a folder that holds no
  store of an install (`ExportRefused`, before the settings store is opened;
  `paths.data_dir(create=False)`) and `verify` refuses a bundle with none;
  settings travel as whole rows (`settings_rows.json`) and the import writes
  only what `settings_restore` classes as carried (never RUNTIME: grants,
  long tasks, cursors; never a web session). Gates:
  `tests/test_migrate_export_needs_an_install.py`,
  `tests/test_migration_carries_no_revoked_state.py`.
- **`kazma update` reads its stash restore** (FA-101): a pop that conflicts
  resets the tree to the updated code, names the stash and exits 3
  (`EDITS_NOT_RESTORED`); the postflight refuses unmerged paths. Gate:
  `tests/test_update_reads_its_stash_restore.py` (real git).
- **A fork keeps what its chat keeps out of memory** (FA-246):
  `forget.inherit_ledger` copies the source's ledger rows (whole-chat
  keep-out, each kept-out turn) under the fork's keys, journaled, before the
  fork is written; a ledger that cannot be copied refuses the fork (503
  `memory_ledger_unavailable`). Gate: `tests/test_fork_keeps_the_ledger.py`.
- **A lesson comes only from a turn memory would keep** (FA-212, §11): the
  one hand-off is `close_turn` (`learn_from_finished_turn`); no lesson from a
  failed turn, a turn or chat kept out of memory, a refiner that could not
  answer (no template line), or a lesson that does not fit whole. Gate:
  `tests/test_lessons_only_from_kept_turns.py`.
- **A streaming 429 waits and retries** (FA-214): the stream path honours
  `Retry-After` with the blocking path's bounded schedule
  (`_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES`, `_rate_limit_wait`); `LLMError` carries `attempts`
  and `waited_s`, and `friendly_llm_error` words a rate limit from them, not
  as a lost connection. Gate: `tests/test_stream_rate_limit.py`.
- **A Settings control changes something** (FA-250). Settings > Tools'
  switch is real (`skills/switches`: `switched_off_reason` for a skill or a
  tool, `offered` applied by the supervisor to every model call -- the graph
  holds the list it was built with -- and the registry refuses the call).
  Class gate `tests/test_settings_keys_have_readers.py`: every key the
  Settings writers write has a reader outside the Settings page (the rules
  and `DECLARED` readers are in its docstring); a section written field by
  field is checked field by field (`EXPANSIONS`). It found: Change password
  wrote a hash sign-in never reads (the route now changes the platform user
  sign-in checks, `platform_rbac.set_local_password`, and ends the user's
  other sessions; a `KAZMA_SECRET` session is told the secret is in `.env`);
  the session list read a key nothing wrote (now `web_sessions.list_sessions`);
  the context strategy and threshold, the sidebar position and custom CSS
  were read by nothing (removed); the accent colour applied on the Settings
  page only (now every page). The logging, safety and proxy writers take
  only their fields. Gates: `tests/test_tool_switch_is_real.py`,
  `tests/test_settings_account_is_real.py`.
- **Kazma reads its own Arabic-page PDF** (FA-004, §19H): a block takes the
  glyphs whose baseline is inside it (`pdf_rtl._BASELINE_SLACK`, 0.05 of a
  size; half a size took the line above), and a left-to-right line keeps its
  word gaps. Gate: `tests/test_document_pdf_ltr_blocks_on_arabic_pages.py`.
- **The free-slot search is the operator's day** (FA-112, §34): one finder,
  `calendar/backends/base.free_slots`, in the scheduler's zone, around every
  event that overlaps the working day (multi-day, all-day, overnight); the
  backends only list events. Gate: `tests/test_calendar_free_slots.py`.
- **Every advisory has a floor at its fix** (FA-258, §50):
  `tests/test_dependency_floors.py` holds pyproject to a recorded OSV answer
  (`tests/fixtures/osv_advisories.json`, refreshed with
  `scripts/record_osv_advisories.py --python <live python> --python
  <this checkout's .venv python> --write`: what live runs AND what a fresh
  install gets from the lock; rows only accumulate, so a floor an advisory
  once needed stays held). Recorded from live alone, the drill VM's fresh
  install (2026-11-06) got certifi, oauthlib and pypdf below their fixes
  past a green gate. A `uv lock` upgrade that crosses a major version
  (pypdf 7) is kept to the series the fix is in until it is tested, in
  pyproject too (`pypdf>=6.21.4,<7`): `kazma update` installs the newest
  version within the floors and does not read uv.lock, so the drill VM's
  update installed pypdf 7.0.0 while the lock said 6.21.4. A
  default provider's imports are base dependencies with floors (FA-248:
  `edge-tts>=7.3.1`), and a failed voice reply on Telegram is a WARNING.
  Gate: `tests/test_default_voice_providers_declared.py`.
- **Kazma notices its services reachable beyond the machine** (FA-218):
  `security/service_exposure.py` reads `docker ps` (Kazma's containers by
  name: the image of a recreated container is an id) and `pg_roles`; the
  security report's `check_service_exposure` and a boot WARNING plus the ops
  alert `security.service_exposed`. The compose files publish on loopback.
  The way off a superuser login is `deploy/postgres/kazma_app_role.sql`
  (role `kazma_app`: no superuser, no CREATEROLE, CREATEDB for the restore
  rehearsal; it owns the database, its schema and every object, each named:
  Postgres refuses `REASSIGN OWNED BY` the bootstrap superuser), the steps in
  `docs/docs/ops/postgres-and-saas.md`; the memory mirror keeps its own copy
  of the address (`memory.backends.state.url`, no fallback to
  `KAZMA_DATABASE_URL`). Gates: `tests/test_service_exposure_check.py`,
  `tests/test_compose_ports_loopback.py`, `tests/test_pg_app_role.py` (every
  store's setup, a dump and the rehearsal as the role, on a database seeded
  as the superuser; the bare role as the negative control). **A refused
  sign-in says why** (2026-11-03: the live switch to `kazma_app` waited 18
  minutes on a role with no password while the log said "unreachable"):
  once the pool gives up, `postgres_pool.refusal_reason` signs in once and
  words Postgres's answer (a refused password, a missing role or database,
  nothing listening), logged at ERROR and carried in `PostgresUnreachable`
  and `ConfigStoreUnavailableError.reason` (`config_store._refusal_in`).
  `scripts/check_database_login.py` signs in as Kazma will before a reload
  (psql inside the container proves nothing: it trusts loopback). Gate:
  `tests/test_postgres_refusal_reason.py` (the probe answering nothing as
  the negative control; a role with no password on real Postgres).

### 55. The functional audit of 2026-11, Stage 2 (the Medium findings)

Plan `docs/plans/FUNCTIONAL_AUDIT_2026-11_REMEDIATION.md`, Stage 2. Each fix
has a gate that fails on the old code.

- **Secrets and error text.** Every `GET /api/settings*` route is walked with
  every sensitive key seeded with a sentinel: none echoes one (the S3
  `access_key` and the decrypted proxy password did, FA-206/129); the app's
  catch-all answers `safe_error` (FA-222); a plaintext secret row becomes a
  vault pointer even when the vault already holds the value (FA-271; the
  GitHub App key rotation stays the owner's). Gates:
  `tests/test_settings_never_echo_secrets.py`,
  `tests/test_plaintext_secrets_move_to_the_vault.py`.
- **Provider honesty.** A 200 that is not a model answer (not JSON, no
  choices) is `LLMError(kind="unusable_answer", transient=True)` naming the
  body, never an empty answer (FA-211); a stream that ends with neither
  `[DONE]` nor a `finish_reason` is `stream_truncated` (FA-213); a turn that
  ends without an answer says why -- the step limit, an output cut, an
  unusable answer -- and lists only this turn's tools that ran
  (`graph_respond._stop_cause`, `plan_fence.running_turn`); a tool call cut
  off twice ends the turn. The `done` frame names the model that answered
  (FA-210), and so does every save of the reply (`model`): the page's stream
  saved it once more with the model it asked for, and a reload named another
  model (2026-11-07). The row keeps the model the turn ran with apart
  (`run_model`): a client that names no model continues with it, never with
  the answering one (after a failover that is the backup). Failover chains follow a provider change
  (`ModelRegistry.generation`, `reset_failover_cache`, FA-106). Discovery
  returns a typed `DiscoveryResult`, the route answers 502 with the reason,
  the page says it (FA-107). Recall waits for an embedding slot inside its own
  deadline (FA-276). Gates: `tests/test_partial_result_says_what_happened.py`,
  `tests/test_stream_cut_off.py`, `tests/test_done_frame_names_the_answering_model.py`,
  `tests/test_reply_keeps_the_answering_model.py`,
  `tests/test_failover_follows_provider_changes.py`,
  `tests/test_model_discovery_failure_is_said.py`,
  `tests/js/test_discovery_failure.js`,
  `tests/test_recall_waits_for_an_embedding_slot.py`.
- **Failure results read where returned.** `vault_store` raises
  `VaultWriteFailed` and a sign-in whose tokens were not kept fails (FA-104);
  a Discord chunk counts only on a 2xx (FA-105); a rewind journals before it
  opens the database (`forget_journal` kind `rewind`, FA-102); the vault's
  first use is one locked construction (FA-103); an MCP Test says why it failed
  and pages nothing (`connect_from_config(quiet=True)`, FA-245/256). Gates:
  `tests/test_vault_write_failure_fails_the_sign_in.py`,
  `tests/test_chat_send_rate_limited_is_not_sent.py`,
  `tests/test_rewind_journaled_first.py`, `tests/test_vault_first_use.py`,
  `tests/test_mcp_test_says_why.py`.
- **Settings that reach what they name.** The per-tool timeout is
  `agent.tool_timeout_seconds` (the old Non-Stop key moved once,
  `config_store._MOVED_KEYS`, FA-125); Skills' Validate checks the real skill
  (`agent_skills/checkup.check_skill`, FA-249); a log level applies at once
  (`logging_config.apply_level`, FA-114); the proxy card names the
  acquisition policy (FA-115); `config_save` cannot redirect secrets or memory
  (`protected_config` prefixes and `PROTECTED_CONFIG_PATTERNS`, FA-126); a

  `tests/test_tool_timeout_setting_is_real.py`,
  `tests/test_skill_validate_checks_real_skills.py`,
  `tests/test_log_level_applies_now.py`, `tests/test_proxy_names_the_policy.py`,

- **Language parity.** "Remember" provenance judges the stored value in

- **Kazma refreshes stale malware signatures itself** (resilience plan H).
  The maintenance sweep "malware signatures"
  (`documents/malware.signature_alert_sweep`) runs freshclam

- **What Kazma says about itself, and what it sends.** The backup text says

### 56. The functional audit of 2026-11, Stage 3 (the Low findings)

Plan `docs/plans/FUNCTIONAL_AUDIT_2026-11_REMEDIATION.md`, Stage 3. Each fix
has a gate that fails on the old code.

- **A result is said as it is** (FA-108/109/110/202/236). `persist_reply`
  logs what the transcript store answered; orphan recovery counts a task the
  store refused to write as not recorded; an agent that cannot take a new
  provider key reports it as a model substitution (§38), not at DEBUG; a
  document worker logs its store's outage once and its recovery once, not
  every poll; a swarm dispatch whose workers are all unknown is 404
  `workers_not_registered` with nothing recorded, and the CLI prints the
  server's answer. Two metric families say what their names say:
  `kazma_commitment_decisions_total` is counted when the gate decides (it
  was a COUNT of a table the GC trims), `kazma_hitl_gates_total` is recorded
  by the registry once per real transition, every mechanism (FA-257). Every
  model call names its work: the ledger takes the thread from the caller's
  context, research names `research:<job id>` (FA-260). A call refused before
  it ran (a commitment deny, a refusal before its card) is a step of the turn:
  a start and an end activity carrying the refusal, a `failed` row on the
  page; the expected deny logs at INFO (FA-253). Gates:
  `tests/test_results_said_as_they_are.py`,
  `tests/test_metrics_say_what_they_name.py`,
  `tests/test_model_calls_name_their_work.py`,
  `tests/test_refused_call_is_a_step.py`, `tests/js/test_refused_tool_row.js`.
- **What answers before sign-in says no more than it must.** The GitHub
  OAuth result page escapes its message (FA-130); a failed readiness or deep
  health check shows the exception's type, a code and a reference
  (`health._check_failure`), the text in the log (FA-131); the Telegram
  webhook warns about refused POSTs once per ten minutes, not per POST
  (FA-132); `/api/auth/status` before sign-in answers `auth_enabled`,
  `authenticated: false`, `mode` and `oidc`, never the proxy list (FA-219).
  OIDC sign-in state is per attempt (`auth.oidc.pending`, ten minutes, 32 at
  most, written by `atomic_update`), bound to a cookie on `/api/auth/oidc`,
  compared with `hmac.compare_digest` and taken once; a RUNTIME key in
  `settings_restore` (FA-133). Gates: `tests/test_open_answers_say_no_more.py`,
  `tests/test_oidc_sign_in_state.py`.
- **Request bodies and refusals.** `upload_limits.UploadSizeLimitMiddleware`
  refuses a chat upload or a voice clip past its limit by its declared length
  before reading, and a streamed one as it passes the limit (FA-134). The
  Documents and Scheduled routes answer every refusal in one envelope,
  `{"ok": false, "error", "code"}` (`kazma_ui/error_envelope.py`), FastAPI's
  validation answer included, which no longer echoes the input (FA-234,
  FA-241); a library that does not exist is 404 `library_not_found`. A JSON
  body that does not parse is 400 `invalid_json` (`kazma_ui/json_body.py`;
  the chat's session bind answered 503, FA-274). A memory GET that finds
  nothing is 404 (`memory_actions` reads GET answers too, FA-275). The chat
  session list refreshes from the database at most every 10 s, one refresh at
  a time, the others reading the cache: 10 readers at once took 155 ms each,
  now 0.9 ms; the sidebar groups and searches on the page, so no paging was
  added (FA-278). Gates: `tests/test_upload_limits.py`,
  `tests/test_document_error_envelope.py`, `tests/test_scheduled_api.py`,
  `tests/test_json_body_reader.py`, `tests/test_memory_actions.py`,
  `tests/test_session_list_concurrency.py`.
- **Every store says how long it keeps what it holds** (FA-141).
  `store_registry.RETENTION` has an entry for every store and family (a rule
  and the sweep that runs it, or "kept:" and why); decided gates, completed
  tool receipts and finished task ledgers go after 90 days, model calls after
  365, the pipeline log by the swarm task retention -- each a maintenance
  sweep (§15B) that removes decided rows only. `hitl_gates.db` is on the
  erasure horizon. Gate: `tests/test_store_retention_declared.py`.
- **Files and maps that only grew have a bound** (FA-142/143/144/145/203/
  204/224). Stall dumps are pruned (200, 30 days); old-format document
  backups older than the oldest verified one kept are pruned; a read-only
  diagnostic writes nothing to the crawl journal; the guard rotates its own
  log; manifests are written whole (`kazma_core/atomic_files.py`); the alert
  throttle and the approval-card counter keep a bounded number of keys;
  SQLite WAL files are capped (`SQLITE_JOURNAL_SIZE_LIMIT`) and `settings.db`
  is compacted once after the Knowledge tables left it. A chat attachment is
  stored once, named by its content hash (FA-146). The `file_read` cache is
  per reader (a turn's thread, a swarm worker's scope), so one reader's read
  never answers another's (FA-111). File I/O in async tools runs in a thread
  (FA-139). A bare `*.db` a shell command names is the workspace's file
  unless only the data dir holds it (FA-217). Gates:
  `tests/test_files_and_maps_stay_bounded.py`,
  `tests/test_attachments_stored_once.py`,
  `tests/test_file_read_cache_per_reader.py`,
  `tests/test_async_tools_file_io_off_the_loop.py`,
  `tests/test_workspace_db_is_the_users.py`.
- **Document GC runs where the catalog is** (FA-205). The Postgres mark read
  its rows by position and failed, so GC on a Postgres catalog never removed
  anything (`repository_pg._cell` reads by name). An install whose catalog is
  SQLite also sweeps the orphan blob rows a Postgres catalog left
  (`retention._sweep_idle_catalog`, same mark and grace). Gate:
  `tests/test_document_idle_catalog_orphans.py`.
- **Schedulers keep their time, and stop.** Chat-app rate limits follow the
  setting live (`rate_feedback.follow_rate_limit_settings`, FA-127); macro
  sleep and reconsolidation stamp their last run, so a reload does not run
  them again (FA-149); `_distinct_tenants` runs in a thread (FA-150); the
  daily digest is sent at `observability.daily_digest.time` (08:00, the
  operator's zone), not 24 hours after the last boot (FA-208); every loop
  sleep is `shutdown.sleep_or_shutdown`, so a stop ends it at once (FA-265).
  A delay before background work is `spawn_background(..., start_after=)`,
  which a stop ends with the work never started; a background coroutine
  that is not `never_completes` never sleeps with `asyncio.sleep` (the crawl
  auto-resume's 20 s wait held a reload for the drain's 10 s, 2026-11-13;
  `tests/test_background_tasks_end_at_a_stop.py`).
  `/abort` pauses an active `/long` task (`pause_long_task_for_abort`,
  FA-148). Gates: `tests/test_rate_limits_follow_settings.py`,
  `tests/test_scheduler_cadence.py`, `tests/test_abort_pauses_the_long_task.py`.
- **Smaller truths.** The CLI prints UTF-8 and answers `--version` (FA-225);
  a malware name with no dot is read (`malware._signature_from`, FA-231); an
  IDE diff keeps its lines (FA-244); research reports the sources it acquired
  (FA-240) and its rubric reads the report's content -- cited paragraphs,
  sources used, citations that resolve, repetition, the topic (FA-235); a
  Gmail listing uses one connection, 8 reads at once (FA-242; the Microsoft
  and calendar readers were not N+1); each swarm template declares its tools,
  so a worker's prompt holds its own (FA-239); every shipped setting has a
  validation rule, a type rule from its shipped value at least, and a restore
  refuses a key this build does not read (FA-251); every workflow action is
  pinned by SHA (FA-209). Gates: `tests/test_cli_prints_utf8_and_version.py`,
  `tests/test_malware_signature_name.py`, `kazma-core/tests/test_ide_service.py`,
  `tests/test_research_counts_sources_acquired.py`,
  `tests/test_research_rubric_reads_content.py`,
  `tests/test_gmail_listing_one_connection.py`,
  `tests/test_swarm_worker_prompt_bounded.py`,
  `tests/test_every_shipped_setting_has_a_rule.py`,
  `tests/test_actions_pinned_by_sha.py`.
- **Secrets at rest.** The security report checks that every secret file of
  the install is readable by its owner only (`check_secret_file_access`,
  `security/file_access.readable_by_others`, FA-272): the restic password
  file, the install's `.env` family, the vault and the broker token
  (`store_registry.install_secret_files`), each other reader named
  (`file_access._account_name`). It checked `restic.pass` alone until
  2026-11-03, when the live install folder was found granting read to a
  group another program had added (`CodexSandboxUsers`), inherited by `.env`
  and `vault.db` too; removing that grant is the owner's. The offsite copy
  leaves every secret-named file out at any depth, zip and rclone alike
  (FA-215, the owner's decision; by the registry's name rule since
  2026-11-10, §62). Gates: `tests/test_secret_file_access_check.py`,
  `tests/test_offsite_copy_leaves_env_out.py`.
- **What Kazma's words say is what the code does** (FA-119/120/121/122/123/
  229). The cron zone hint names its order (`cron.timezone`, `KAZMA_TZ`,
  UTC); the memory mirror, vault and Knowledge auto-inject hints say what
  they do; `python_exec`'s description is built from its constants and its
  timeout is clamped to 120 s; the system prompt's rules are in the shipped
  `kazma.yaml` (installs on the old prompt follow, `RetiredDefault`), and the
  rule to stop all tool calls on any tool error is gone; the Knowledge footer
  is in the turn's language (`knowledge_index.knowledge_footer`) and a failed
  search hands the model `safe_error`'s code. Gates:
  `tests/test_hints_say_what_the_code_does.py`,
  `tests/test_python_exec_description_is_true.py`,
  `tests/test_prompt_rules_reach_the_model.py`,
  `tests/test_knowledge_footer_language.py`.
- **A workflow's token is its own, and a release is published last**
  (2026-11-09). Every workflow declares its permissions (CI and the skill
  review read only; each write is listed with its reason in the gate), so the
  repository's default token can be read-only: three of six declared nothing
  and took a default that could write. The release workflow creates a draft
  with every file attached, publishes last, and refuses a release that is
  already published; a re-run used to replace a published release's files,
  which the updater checks against that release's SHA256SUMS, and GitHub's
  immutable releases refuse. Gates: `tests/test_workflow_permissions.py`,
  `tests/test_release_supply_chain.py` (the old publish step as the control).
- **A tool a workflow or build script runs names one release** (2026-11,
  supply chain). `uvx`/`npx` with no version run whatever PyPI or npm serves
  that day: the release workflow's SBOM tool (`cyclonedx-bom==8.0.1`), the
  PyPI reservation workflow's `twine==7.0.0` and the CodeMirror minifier
  (`vendor_codemirror.TERSER_VERSION`, terser 5.51.2) are exact. Raise a
  version by hand, after trying it. Gate: `tests/test_actions_pinned_by_sha.py`
  (every `uvx`/`npx` package in `.github/workflows/` and `scripts/` --
  `--from`, `--with`, `--package` or the command itself, Python argv lists
  with their module constants resolved -- is `name==1.2.3` or
  `name@1.2.3`; the three old forms as negative controls).
- **AGENTS.md names what exists** (FA-151/152/154). §2 states the `_gateway`
  exception; the stale names, counts and paths of §1-§45 are corrected.
  Every backticked code name here -- a dotted path, a name after its file
  (`graph_tool_worker.py:tool_worker_node`), a page script's camelCase name,
  a bare private name, a test -- must exist; what
  only looks like code is declared with why. Gates:
  `tests/test_agents_md_names.py` (planted stale names as the control),
  `tests/test_gateway_routing_block.py`.
- **A test never writes into the checkout** (found during this stage). A
  fresh workspace store seeded its first active row from the working folder
  even with `KAZMA_WORKSPACE` set, and that row outranks the variable (§10A):
  under pytest the working folder is this repository, and a test's relative
  `file_write` landed in it. The seed takes `KAZMA_WORKSPACE` first, and the
  root conftest pins it to a temp folder. Gate:
  `tests/test_install_data_shield.py` (no variable as the control). **And
  what a test leaves in the store is put back** (2026-11-08): a research
  recovery test's child process, handed the session's `KAZMA_DATA_DIR` but
  not `KAZMA_WORKSPACE`, was first to open the session's store file and
  seeded the checkout, and a later test wrote `d2-<hex>/report.md` into the
  repository. The root conftest makes the store before the first test and,
  after every test, restores the singleton (`peek_workspace_store` /
  `set_workspace_store`) and the file's workspace rows, whoever wrote them
  (`KAZMA_TEST_WORKSPACE_GUARD=0` turns it off); a child given the session
  data folder is given the session workspace too. Gates:
  `tests/test_order_independence.py` (three planted shapes, each with the
  guard off as its control), `tests/test_install_data_shield.py`.

### 57. The weak-spot roadmap of 2026-11 (`docs/plans/FUNCTIONAL_AUDIT_2026-11_REMEDIATION.md`)

The audit's findings clustered into twelve themes; each theme is a standard
held by a class gate, beyond the single findings. Themes 3, 8 and 9 were met
by Stages 1-3; theme 10 (GitHub Actions billing) is the owner's, and theme 7
is the reasoning setting below plus the tool count per turn (open).

- **How much the model reasons before a chat answer is a setting** (theme 7,
  2026-11-03, the owner's choice: `low`). `agent.chat_reasoning`
  (`agent/chat_reasoning.py`; Settings -> System; `default` / `off` / `low` /
  `high` / `max`) reaches every model call of a chat turn -- the supervisor's,
  its failover, the empty-answer nudge, the respond synthesis -- as
  `chat_reasoning_kwargs(client)`: only where the client takes it
  (`LLMProvider.can_turn_off_reasoning`: DeepSeek's own API, `thinking`
  for off, `reasoning_effort` for the rest, `llm_provider.REASONING_EFFORTS`;
  Qwen's on Model Studio, `enable_thinking: false` for off alone -- no
  effort level is documented for Qwen, so one is sent as nothing; the
  memory plan's finding 12, 2026-11-22), so a failover to a provider with a
  `chat` of its own receives nothing. A model that refuses the field is
  asked again without it (the blocking path's reasoning-switch fallback,
  every field of `llm_provider._REASONING_FIELDS`; the stream's 4xx falls
  back to it). X drafting, research and the intent classifier's refinement
  (`intent/classify._refine_acts_llm`: a thinking model spent its whole 4 s
  reasoning) keep `reasoning="off"`. Settings' card says what the active
  provider takes (`chat_reasoning.levels_taken`: every level, Off only, or
  nothing; the API's `takes`). Gates: `tests/test_chat_reasoning.py`
  (each level on the wire, the refusal, the stream, a real turn through the
  supervisor graph with the call before the setting as the negative
  control, every `invoke_llm_chat` call in the chat turn's modules carrying
  the level), `tests/test_qwen_reasoning_off.py` (Qwen's switch on the wire,
  the classifier in English and Arabic, today's classifier as the control).
- **Qwen caches Kazma's leading system prompt explicitly** (2026-11-23, the
  memory plan's W4 pilot). Model Studio caches a prefix on its own when it
  chooses (20 % of the input price); `llm_provider._with_qwen_cache_marker`,
  applied in `_chat_payload` (the blocking and the streaming body) for a
  Model Studio address (`_is_qwen_api`), sends a leading system message of
  at least `_QWEN_CACHE_MIN_CHARS` characters as one text part with
  `cache_control` (cached five minutes, renewed on each hit; Model Studio's
  page gives a hit at typically 10 % of the input price and a first write
  at 125 %, qwen3.8-flash's own ratios by region). Measured through Kazma's
  own provider on qwen3.8-flash and qwen3.7-plus with the deep pass's
  prompt: 1,614 of about 1,850 prompt tokens served from the cache from the
  second call on. Any other message and provider are sent as before. Gate:
  `tests/test_qwen_context_cache.py` (a host that only looks like Model
  Studio's as the control).

- **A result that says whether it worked is read where it is returned**
  (theme 1). `tests/test_failure_results_are_used.py` covers the vault, the
  chat store, the swarm task store and the updater too; a call that returns
  nothing worth reading is in `NOT_AN_ANSWER`. Fixed when it widened: a
  pipeline checkpoint's approve, reject and timeout wrote their task with
  the answer dropped, as did the step journal (`SwarmEngine._journal_step`)
  and a Research session's archive (now 409 `not_recorded`). Gate:
  `tests/test_refused_task_writes_are_said.py`.
- **Recovery is drilled with the real thing, in CI** (theme 2). The job
  `Recovery drills` runs, with a skip failing it: a universal backup sent to
  a real restic repository, restored by `restore.restore_files` into a
  scratch folder, and recalled (`tests/test_drill_restic_restore_recall.py`;
  the generation before the memory as the control); a throwaway Postgres
  stopped under a real settings store; the memory restore drill on
  Postgres; and the REAL guard reloading the REAL `serve.py` in a private
  install with a web turn streaming and an OCR job running
  (`tests/test_drill_graceful_reload.py`, `KAZMA_TEST_RELOAD_DRILL=1`; a hard
  kill as the control: the job's next attempt). The drills found four
  defects, each with its own gate:
  - a SQLite install's restore ended FAILED for want of a Postgres dump its
    manifest says it never had (`restore._postgres_not_used`);
  - the tab that sent a turn reads it through the journal-attached tail,
    which returned the moment the stop began, before the producer's
    `done(stopped_for_shutdown)`: FA-262's frame never reached the page.
    The tail passes on what is queued and sends the same frame itself
    (`_streaming._end_attach_for_shutdown`, one payload
    `_shutdown_done_payload`); a paused turn still ends quietly. Gate:
    `tests/test_attached_stream_told_of_restart.py` (the early return as the
    control);
  - a stopping document worker set its stage's event, but the sandbox polls
    the `documents.cancellation` signal, which only `run_cancellable` bound:
    the OCR process ran on to its last page after the job was given back.
    Every stage now runs under `cancellation.call_with_cancel`. Gate:
    `tests/test_document_stage_stop_ends_its_worker.py` (a real sandboxed
    process; the unbound call as the control);
  - the server did not end after its own shutdown: uvicorn re-raised the
    stop signal through the C runtime's default action, and interpreter exit
    joins executor threads. `serve.py` calls
    `process_exit.prepare_server_exit` (SIGBREAK/SIGTERM come back as
    KeyboardInterrupt; a stop listener, `shutdown.add_stop_listener`, arms a
    deadline at the stop's budget plus `EXIT_MARGIN_S`) and leaves through
    `process_exit.exit_after_shutdown`, which runs the `atexit` handlers
    first, bounded (the procedural recorder's drain, the vector store's
    release: a bare `os._exit` skips them). Gate:
    `tests/test_server_exit_after_stop.py` (real processes; each piece
    removed as its control, a bare `os._exit` among them). `serve.py` reads `KAZMA_PORT` now (documented,
    never read: the drill could not run beside a live server). The console
    log handler escapes what stdout cannot encode
    (`logging_config._console_never_raises`;
    `tests/test_console_log_never_raises.py`).
  A Knowledge crawl in flight is not drilled: its seed must be public, so a
  drill would need the internet; its reload is held by
  `tests/test_crawl_auto_resume.py`.
- **Every setting has a reader, the TUI's too** (theme 4).
  `tests/test_settings_keys_have_readers.py` reads the TUI's writers
  (`TUI_WRITERS`); its dead toggles are gone and its chat reads the system
  prompt the web reads (`agent.system_prompt` first).
- **Forgetting a turn takes back the lessons it taught** (theme 5).
  `self_improvement.forget_lessons_from(chat_keys, turn)`, called by
  `forget._forget_turn` (after its commit, before the journal entry is
  marked applied) and by `forget_chat`; a lesson another turn also taught
  stays. Gate: `tests/test_forget_takes_back_lessons.py` (the forget without
  the call as the control).
- **Arabic and English as equals** (theme 6). `tests/test_paired_languages.py`
  runs each path that decides by language once per language, through the
  real function, and compares the answers; every product module with Arabic
  in its code is paired there or declared with why (`DECLARED`). Its first
  run found: Arabic calendar words unparsed ("بكرة الساعة 9 الصبح" asked
  when; `relative_time._RE_CALENDAR_AR`, and "the day after tomorrow" in
  English); Gulf document requests unrecognised and a bare "مستند" never
  matching (`intent.heuristics`: the verbs, the formats' Arabic names, a
  named format beating the generic word); plan approval words that did not
  mirror (`plan_mode._APPROVE_RE`); and fixed replies in Arabic whatever the
  user wrote -- the supervisor's budget message and four chat-app replies
