  -- now `language_lock.in_their_language`.
- **A dependency advisory reaches the owner the day it is published**
  (theme 11). The maintenance sweep "dependency advisories"
  (`security/advisory_watch.advisory_sweep`) asks OSV about the installed
  versions once a day (`audit_installed`; an hour's retry after a failure,
  which raises nothing) and raises `security.advisories_new` once per new
  advisory, naming the package, the fixed version and the update command;
  reviewed advisories stay quiet. What is still open is kept in the RUNTIME
  key `system.security.advisories` (`open_advisories`), and each stored one
  is held against the version installed NOW (`advisory_watch._still_open`):
  read as stored, the drill VM's five advisories stayed on the Dashboard after
  `kazma update` had installed the fixes, under "It closes when the installed
  version is past the fix" (2026-11-07; `tests/test_advisories_close_when_fixed.py`).
- **An unmet requirement stays in front of the owner** (theme 12). The boot
  check records its result (`install_requirements.REQUIREMENTS_KEY`,
  `last_requirements_check`; a check that finds none clears it), and the
  daily digest lists each unmet requirement and open advisory under "Needs
  attention" until it is gone. Gate for 11 and 12:
  `tests/test_dependency_notices_reach_the_owner.py`.

### 58. Signals people can use (resilience plan Part G)

- **Quiet logs** (G1, `observability/log_noise.py`). A live day (2026-11-05)
  wrote 32,090 lines: 12,459 "Batch set" lines and 11,200 access lines of
  polls. The settings store's batch line, the X mentions poll and a reply's
  save while it streams are DEBUG; `QuietPolls` on `uvicorn.access` keeps the
  answered requests of the polled routes (`POLLED_ROUTES`: the bell, pending
  approvals, a chat's status, `/health/*`) out, never an error status. Gate:
  `tests/test_quiet_logs.py` replays that day (`tests/fixtures/log_noise/live_day.json`,
  shapes and counts only) against the code: no routine line more than 30
  times an hour (the recorded day without the change as the negative control).
- **One list of open problems** (G2, `observability/open_problems.py`): the
  bell's open alerts, run incidents, research and crawl alerts, unmet install
  requirements, open advisories and the observer's open incident, built each
  time from where each lives, so a resolved problem leaves by itself. The
  Dashboard's card (`GET /api/problems`, `static/js/problems_panel.js`) words
  each in the page's language (`problems.source.*`, `problems.resolved.*`;
  titles and details are the problems' own data); Acknowledge (until it
  changes: a changed problem has another id) and Snooze (a day) are kept in
  `system.problems.seen`, admin-only. A source that cannot be read is named.
  The daily digest reads the same list (`_open_problems_line`). Gates:
  `tests/test_open_problems.py`, `tests/e2e/test_problems_panel.py` (EN/AR,
  reached by the sidebar). **Every problem says what to do** (2026-11-20):
  a problem with no command of its own shows its kind's "what to do" line
  (`problems.todo.<source>`, EN/AR) beside when it closes; a failed run's
  bell text carries its reason; the observer's problem opens Settings →
  Alerts. Gate: `tests/test_problems_say_how_to_fix.py` (every kind the card
  knows has its line in both languages).
- **The weekly report against targets** (G3, `observability/weekly_targets.py`):
  uptime (the observer's), turns that succeed, restarts not asked for, the
  median time to recover, backups fresh every day, stops over budget and
  alerts sent, each met or missed with the week before, measured from the
  app's and the guard's logs (only the lines a target reads are kept). A
  target with nothing to measure is "unknown", never met. It follows "Needs
  a look" in the weekly message. Gate: `tests/test_weekly_targets.py` (a
  recorded fortnight with a missed target).

### 59. What the UI says must be true (resilience plan Part I)

Each with its test (the old rule as the negative control):
- **A row shows done only when its record says it ended** (`chat.js`
  `_endedRows`): on a finished turn a row still "running" is drawn plain
  (`info`), never with a check ("Kazma is thinking…" read as a step that
  finished). `tests/js/test_rows_done_only_when_ended.js`.
- **Two model calls' narrations stay two paragraphs** (`sse_chat/_streaming._paragraph_break`):
  a blank line between them on the live path whatever the text ends with
  (one newline joins in Markdown), and on the resume leg after an approval,
  which added nothing. `tests/test_narration_paragraphs.py`.
- **A finished turn with no answer says so** (`turn_presentation` phase
  `no_answer`, "Ended without an answer", terminal, offers Retry), never
  "Completed". `tests/js/test_turn_without_answer.js`.
- **A new, empty chat offers "Don't remember this chat"** (`#chat-memory-choice`,
  `chat.js` `_watchMemoryChoice`), applied to the chat's id at once, so the
  first turn is kept out too. `tests/e2e/test_new_chat_memory_choice.py` (EN/AR,
  by the sidebar).
- **Every answer-quality row links to its chat or says it was deleted**
  (`chat_deleted`). `tests/js/test_quality_rows_name_their_chat.js`.
- **The Scheduled page's counts come from one place** (`HISTORY_CLASSES`):
  Failed plus Ended is the History tab's count, and each tab's count is the
  rows it lists. `tests/js/test_scheduled_counts.js`.
- **A switched-off provider shows "Off" and nothing else** (`cardState`,
  `checksFor`, `storedDetail`). `tests/js/test_provider_off_state.js`.
- **A file_search query that reads like a file name is matched as a name
  first** (`_named_like`, any extension, whatever the glob).
  `tests/test_file_search_names_first.py`.

**The weekly chaos drill** (plan J, `scripts/chaos_week.py`): the database
stopped, the server killed, Docker stopped, the network cut, the disk filled
to its floor, an operator reload -- each with its expected outcome read from
the target's own answers and the guard's own record (its state file and
`guard.log`), on a private install only (it refuses the live port, a folder
without `.kazma/chaos-ok`, the live `.env`, a target that is not ready, and,
on Windows, a shell that is not elevated). The database step stops what the
install runs: the service `kazma setup postgres` recorded (and the guard must
start it itself), else the container `--db-container` names. Docker is
skipped when Kazma uses no container there. A command the drill could not
run fails its step with the reason. It judged restarts by a `restarts` field
the guard never writes and stopped a `kazma-db` container a service install
lacks (2026-11-06): the drill reads only the state fields and log events the
guard's source writes (`STATE_FIELDS`, `GUARD_EVENTS`; the gate in
`tests/test_chaos_week.py`, the old drill as the negative control). Where it
runs (a VM or a separate PC) is the owner's choice.

### 60. Providers, stage 1: correct what exists (2026-11-08)

The owner's goal: any provider in the world, with ease. A review of the live
install that day found the backup model unusable, every DeepSeek call priced
as gpt-4o-mini, stale model settings and duplicate provider rows; the code
review found more. Stage 1 makes what exists correct. Stages 2-4 are the
provider list as data with per-type forms, per-model details with
`provider:model` references, and several keys per provider.

- **A price is the model's own, or unknown** (`kazma_core/model_prices.py`).
  In order:
  1. the owner's price (`models.prices`, Settings → Providers & Connectors →
     Model prices, under `provider:model` or the model name);
  2. free for a server on this network (`url_is_local`);
  3. the Anthropic and Bedrock tables, matched by `table_price`: a dated id
     or variant only, never a newer version (`claude-opus-4-5` is not
     `claude-opus-4`);
  4. otherwise unknown.

  OpenRouter's own `usage.cost` wins over all of them. `LLMConfig`'s prices
  default to None. `LLMResponse.cost_known` says whether a price was found.
  - The ledger's `priced` column counts the calls with no known price apart
    in every sum (`unpriced`).
  - Rows written before the column were priced at gpt-4o-mini's $0.15/$0.60
    (8,839 live rows, $50.05). They are marked unknown, with their cost
    cleared, once, by `_migrate`.
  - A row names its provider, not the client class
    (`llm_ledger.provider_of`).

  The chat stats line, the cost badge, `/cost`, the Dashboard, the daily
  limit, and the research and replay pages say "unknown" (or "at least") and
  never `$0.0000`. A reply row keeps `cost_known`; a row saved before has
  none, and its made-up cost is not shown (`chat.js` `_savedCost`). A write
  to `models.prices`, by any path, rebuilds the cached clients
  (`ModelRegistry._on_settings_written`). Gate: `tests/test_model_prices.py`.
  The Dashboard's Total cost card reads the in-memory trace store, which now
  counts the calls of unknown price (`TraceEntry.priced`,
  `unpriced_llm_calls`): it said `$0.0000` beside "Spent today"'s "—" (live
  2026-11-15). `dashboard._cost_text` and `dashboard.js` `costText` are one rule
  (`tests/test_dashboard_total_cost.py`).
- **Requests newer models take**: OpenAI's own API gets
  `max_completion_tokens`. A 400 that refuses `max_tokens`, or any
  temperature but the default, is asked once more without it, and the fix is
  remembered per endpoint and model (`llm_provider._PARAM_FIXES`,
  `_retry_refused_parameters`).
- **A call to OpenRouter names Kazma** (2026-11-14, REMAINING 4.6,
  `llm_provider._attribution_headers`): `HTTP-Referer: https://kazma.ai` and
  `X-Title: Kazma`, OpenRouter's app attribution, to openrouter.ai's own API
  only, the same from every install (never the person); a provider row's own
  headers win; `KAZMA_OPENROUTER_ATTRIBUTION=0` turns them off. Gate:
  `tests/test_openrouter_attribution.py`.
- **Vision is one order** (`vision_capability.classify`):
  1. a name that says it sees (`*vision*`, `*-vl*`, `KAZMA_VISION_MODELS`);
  2. the text-only families;
  3. the allow-list (GPT-5, o1/o3/o4-mini, Grok 4, GLM-V, `claude-*`);
  4. the `*-instruct` guess.

  Matched on the id after a vendor prefix. Gate:
  `tests/test_provider_request_fixes.py`.
- **Addresses**: `/v1` is added only to an address with no version anywhere
  in its path (DeepInfra's `/v1/openai` was doubled). A preset that moved
  takes its stored rows along at boot (`providers.RETIRED_PRESET_URLS`;
  Cohere → `/compatibility/v1`). Gate: `tests/test_provider_addresses.py`.
- **A server on the owner's network needs no key**
  (`runtime/live_llm.url_is_local`, one IP rule with discovery:
  `security/ssrf.own_network_ip`). That means loopback, private ranges,
  Tailscale's shared space, a host with no dot or a network suffix. Never
  link-local or a metadata address (`169.254.169.254`, `100.100.100.200`).
  - Discovery asks a host only when every address it resolves to is on that
    network (`resolves_to_own_network`). `allow_private` skips every check,
    metadata included: never pass it for this.
  - The providers list carries `local`; the chat and sidebar pickers share
    one rule.
  - The guide finds such a server by address (§21d).

  Gate: `tests/test_network_model_servers.py`.
- **One check, through the client chat uses, before saving**
  (`kazma_core/provider_check.py`):
  - `candidate_entry` is the stored row with the typed values over it; an
    empty or masked key means the stored one.
  - `list_models` calls `ModelRegistry.discover(candidate=)`, which neither
    caches nor prunes.
  - `check_model` builds the client with `build_client` and sends one message
    with `CHECK_MAX_TOKENS` (160, the old probe's lesson). An empty answer
    fails. A failure is a code plus the HTTP status, never the provider's
    reply text.

  Who uses it:
  - `POST /api/providers/check`: the dialog's Test, which saves nothing.
  - `POST /api/providers/{name}/test`: a saved provider. It records
    `healthy` / `chat_failing` / `down`, and keeps a typed key only when the
    check answered.
  - The setup guide.

  The Bearer probe (`provider_probe.py`) is gone: Anthropic, Azure and
  Bedrock failed its Test while chat worked. The dialog's Save opens on an
  answer; a failure offers Save anyway behind a confirm, and an edit of the
  key or address needs a new test. Gates: `tests/test_provider_check.py`,
  `tests/test_provider_conformance.py`, and in a browser (by the sidebar,
  EN/AR, Model prices too) `tests/e2e/test_provider_settings_browser.py`.
- **The backup model can answer** (`kazma_core/failover_backup.py`):
  - `backup_status` gives each chain entry, the provider the runtime would
    send it to, and whether that provider can be called.
  - `suggest_backups` offers a model of each usable provider of another
    vendor, only one the runtime would route there, never a provider
    whose last check failed (`down`, `chat_failing`).
  - Saving a backup nothing serves is a 400. Settings shows the status and
    one-click suggestions (`/api/settings/failover-backup`).
  - The drill says `failover_off` and `backup_unusable` for what they are; it
    said "No backup model is configured" for both.

  Gates: `tests/test_failover_backup.py`, `tests/test_model_failover_drill.py`.
- **No switched-on cloud provider without a key**: a save leaves one off
  (`switched_off: no_key`), and the toggle refuses (409 `no_key`). A second
  row at one address is named, not refused (`same_address_as`). Gate:
  `tests/test_provider_list_hygiene.py`.
- **Dead model settings retired**. These were read by nothing, or only to
  add gpt-4o-mini to the model lists:
  - `llm.input_cost_per_1m` and `llm.output_cost_per_1m`;
  - `models.default`, `models.fallback` and `models.router`.

  They are removed from kazma.yaml with `RetiredDefault(removed=True)`.
  `llm.model` is the legacy `custom` profile's model only: as every
  provider's last resort it sent gpt-4o-mini to DeepSeek. A saved profile's
  **Use** switches to it (Load filled fields nothing showed). Gate:
  `tests/test_dead_model_settings.py`.

### 61. Providers, stages 2-4: one list, model choice, several keys (2026-11-08)

The rest of the plan in §60, done the same day.

**Stage 2: one provider list, kept as data** (`kazma_core/providers.py`).
- **The catalog is the one list.** `PROVIDER_PRESETS` is it: 35 providers,
  each with `api_style`, `auth`, `form`, `kind`, `local`, `default_model`,
  `models_endpoint` and `url_hint`. `capabilities()`, `DEFAULT_MODEL_FOR`,
  the setup guide (`_guided`, `_LOCAL`) and `provider_check.LOCAL_NAMES` read
  it. The Settings dialog reads `GET /api/providers/catalog`; the page's own
  ten presets (`providers.js` `PRESETS`) are gone.
- **Seeding.** Only the presets an install had before are seeded as rows
  (`model_registry_store.SEEDED_PRESETS`). The new ones are offered by the
  dialog and the guide.
- **A row says which preset it was made from** (`preset`). `build_client`,
  discovery and the credentials rule read the preset, so a row named
  "Work Azure" speaks Azure.
- **A row keeps the dialog's other fields**
  (`model_registry_store.OPTIONAL_FIELDS`):
  - `kind` (`chat` or `speech`);
  - `url_as_typed`;
  - `secret_headers`, sent on every request (`LLMConfig.extra_headers`);
  - Azure's `api_version`;
  - Bedrock's `region` and `aws_*` keys (`provider_adapters._bedrock_kwargs`);
  - extra keys (`api_keys`, stage 4).

  Every secret among them is vaulted by its name: a field called `headers`
  would not have been, so it is `secret_headers`. The API masks them all
  (`_mask_provider_entry`), and a masked value posted back keeps the stored
  one (`provider_check.merge_typed_secrets`).
- **An address kept as typed** is one set every normalizer asks
  (`url_utils.is_as_typed`). The registry fills it from the rows, and a
  check adds the address it is checking.
- **One rule for whether a provider has what its sign-in needs**
  (`provider_check.credentials_problem`): a key, Bedrock's AWS keys or the
  AWS chain, a Vertex project, or nothing for this network. The check, the
  save, the toggle (`_can_be_called`), the backup (`failover_backup._usable`),
  the pickers and the background check all use it.
- **Speech is not chat** (`models/modality.row_is_speech`). A row whose
  address is a speech endpoint (`_is_speech_address`: a path with an `audio`
  part or ending at a speech endpoint, `SPEECH_PATH_ENDS`, or a speech-only
  host, `SPEECH_HOSTS`; it wins over `kind: chat`), whose `kind` is speech,
  or whose every model is a speech model, is kept out of model lookup, the
  fallback choice, the pickers and backups, and is listed under Speech
  services. `is_speech_model` also matches a vendor-prefixed id
  (`nvidia/parakeet-...`). Test sends a speech row no chat message (code
  `speech_provider`, health untouched) and the dialog's Save opens without
  it. Live's "Cohere Transcriptions" (`/v2/audio/transcriptions`, no models,
  no kind) passed the model rule as chat (2026-11-08). Gate:
  `tests/test_speech_address_and_deleted_presets.py` (the model-only rule as
  the control).
- **A deleted catalog provider stays deleted**
  (`model_registry_store.REMOVED_PRESETS_KEY`, a list of the deleted names).
  `list_providers` merges every missing seeded preset in and every start
  seeds them, so Delete did nothing for `zai`, `cohere` and the rest. Deleting
  a `SEEDED_PRESETS` row records it in the same `batch_set` as the list; the
  list and `seed_missing_presets` skip it; adding it again takes it off.
  Same gate (no record as the control).
- **The providers page stays short** (2026-11-08, the owner: "why the
  providers page is too long"; live's ran to ~2,000 lines). The default
  model, Model details, Model prices and saved profiles are the Models
  sub-tab (`hubSubtab` `models`, deep link `?tab=models`), styled as the
  provider control plane (`.mc-*` in kazma.css, 21c): four counts, the
  default model's panel, and Model details as one table that scrolls under
  its own header and becomes labelled cards on a narrow panel. The table
  lists `shownModelDetails()`: In use is the default, models with calls in
  the last 30 days (`llm_ledger.used_models`, the route's `used`), the ones
  you changed and the one being edited; All models, a provider or words
  for the rest; a header sorts (`sortModelDetails`); unsaved edits are
  said and Save opens only then (`modelDetailsDirty`).
  A provider that is off and cannot be called (`callable`, from
  `provider_check.credentials_problem`) folds away (`providerFoldedAway`)
  unless it is the one open. Model prices offers a model only when a working
  provider serves it with no price known (the route's `_still_to_price`:
  live listed the 1 November audit's `fault-*` drill models). Gates:
  `tests/test_providers_page_short.py` (the ledger's raw list as the
  control), the browser case in `tests/e2e/test_provider_settings_browser.py`.
- **Voice is one setting, `voice.*`.** `gateway.voice.*` is moved by
  `config_store._MOVED_KEYS`. `reconcile_from_yaml` now moves keys BEFORE it
  seeds: kazma.yaml's `voice.enabled: false` would otherwise win over an
  owner's stored `gateway.voice.enabled: true`.

Gates: `tests/test_provider_catalog.py`, with the old behaviours as
controls.

**Stage 3: per-model details and model choice.**
- **References** (`kazma_core/model_refs.py`): `provider:model`. The part
  before the first `:` is a provider only when a row has that name, so
  Ollama's `llama3:8b` stays bare. The registry's `find_provider_for_model`,
  `get_client`, `get_model` and `set_active_model` take one. A bare name
  that two providers list goes to the provider in use.
- **Details** (`kazma_core/model_details.py`), the first that says wins:
  1. the owner's (`models.details`, validated whole);
  2. what the provider's model list stated: OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, vLLM
     and Gemini fields, `from_listing`, kept by discovery in
     `registry.model_details.<name>` (runtime);
  3. `CATALOG`: vision, tools and the vendor's own list price, on its own
     API only, dated `CATALOG_AS_OF`.

  The catalog holds no window or output limit: the owner's 2026-10-18 rule
  (§29D). The details are used for:
  - the context window, capped at a known size (`token_counter`);
  - the request's output limit;
  - vision, which a known value decides before the name rules;
  - the price, after the owner's price and before unknown.
- **One list for every picker** (`kazma_core/models/options.py`,
  `GET /api/models/options`): every model a provider that can answer a chat
  offers, by reference, with its details and the default.
  - The web chat's picker sets that chat's model: localStorage
    `kazma.chatModel.<session>`, else the chat's `run_model`, which is now a
    client row field, else the default. It never changes the install's model.
  - The sidebar and Settings → Model details set the default
    (`PUT /api/settings/active_model`).
  - The terminal app's picker lists references (it merged duplicates).
- **The chat apps' `/model` is the chat's**
  (`kazma_core/chat_model_choice.py`: `chat.models`, runtime, at most 2,000
  chats).
  - `/model <n|ref|name>` sets the chat's model, and `/model reset` clears
    it. Any allowed user may do either.
  - `/model default ...` changes the install's default. It is admin-only:
    `slash_commands.changes_global_config` lists it, and `/_models_select`
    is no longer listed.
  - The gateway pins the chat's model around `run_agent_turn`.
  - Telegram's buttons carry references; elsewhere the list shows every
    model, numbered (it showed five per provider).

Gates: `tests/test_model_refs_and_details.py`.

**Stage 4: several keys, checked in the background.**
- **Extra keys** (`kazma_core/provider_keys.py`): a row's `api_keys` are
  tried after its own key. `current_key` gives the first key not resting;
  `key_failure` reads why a call failed (refused 401/403, no credit 402 or a
  "no balance" answer, or out of requests after the client's waits).
  `next_key` rests the failed key (`REST_SECONDS`) and returns the next. The
  state is `registry.key_state.<name>` (runtime) and names keys by
  fingerprint only.
- **The switch happens inside the call.** `LLMProvider._with_key_switches`
  wraps `chat`, and `chat_stream` switches before any text has streamed;
  Anthropic's `chat` does the same. The registry's `switch_provider_key`
  drops the cached client and raises `llm.key_switched.<name>`.
- **The background check** (`kazma_core/provider_health.py`, maintenance
  entry "provider health") runs hourly. It lists each callable chat
  provider's models: no tokens, results in `registry.provider_check.<name>`.
  - Unreachable twice in a row: `health: down`, and when it is the provider
    in use, one `llm.provider_unreachable.<name>`.
  - An answer again: Not tested (`unknown`), and for the provider in use one
    recovery note.
  - A refused key rests when the provider has another.

Gates: `tests/test_provider_keys.py`, and in a browser (by the sidebar)
`tests/e2e/test_provider_settings_browser.py`. The browser test found that
the setup wall stayed up over a network server in use: readiness now
counts the active provider's address (`setup_api.compute_setup_status`).

### 62. The security audit of 2026-11-10: the High findings

Five findings, each fixed with a test that fails on the old code. The
audit's remaining findings are not listed here until each is fixed (the
repository is public).

- **A saved web extract is a note, never a file a program loads** (SEC-01,
  `tools/read_url._extract_path_refusal`). `read_url_to_file` (write tier, no
  card) and `crawl_site`'s save name their file through
  `_safe_workspace_path`, whose only rules were "inside the workspace" and
  "not there yet"; a JSON answer is saved byte for byte under `# ` header
  lines. A fetched page that steered the model could plant
  `.venv/Lib/site-packages/x.pth` (Python runs its `import` lines at the next
  start) or `kazma.local.yaml`. Now: a `.md` or `.txt` file with a plain
  name, in no dot folder and no folder of `GENERATED_DIRS` (compared without
  case), no `:` in the path, never one of Kazma's own files. Any other
  destination is `file_write`'s, which asks. Gate:
  `tests/test_extract_saves_are_notes.py` (the old rule as the control).
  Since 2026-11-15 every save lands under `research/` (or
  `KAZMA_RESEARCH_DIR`; `notes/x.md` becomes `research/notes/x.md`), never
  under a name in `read_url.LOADED_FILE_NAMES` (`requirements*.txt`,
  `constraints*.txt`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`,
  `SKILL.md`...): a page's text saved at the workspace root as
  `requirements.txt` was code at the next `pip install -r`.
- **shell_exec resolves what it is given** (`safety/shell_paths.py`,
  2026-11-15, the defensive check before the independent review: with the
  workspace the install folder, `grep -r` over `.` and the Windows short name
  `ENV~1` read the vault key). Every value is resolved to the file it opens
  (8.3 names, trailing dots, `::$DATA`, links, junctions, `~`, wildcards by
  long and short name) and asked `is_kazma_store`; a folder the program walks
  (`WALKS`: recursive grep, find, ls -R, du, tar -c, cp -r, git add...; the
  working folder when none is named) may not hold Kazma's files
  (`store_registry.kazma_file_under`). Asked before the card
  (`call_preflight.call_refusal` -> `shell_target_refusal`) and by the tool.
  git runs `shell_arguments.GIT_SUBCOMMANDS` only (an allowlist: aliases,
  `web--browse`, `send-email`, `instaweb` are out); tar refuses volume scripts
  and `host:path` archives. `git_commit` refuses to stage a Kazma file
  (`git add --dry-run` first). Gate: `tests/test_shell_exec_kazma_files.py`
  (every allowlisted binary is in `WALKS` or `NO_WALK`).
- **Kazma's configuration is readable, never writable**:
  `is_kazma_store(path, write=True)` covers `CONFIG_FILE_NAMES` (`kazma.yaml`,
  `kazma.local.yaml`, `kazma-permissions.yaml`) wherever Kazma reads them and
  the data-dir entries declared `config`; every write door asks with
  `write=True`. An approved `file_write` of `kazma.local.yaml` turned the
  approval gate off and added a hook command. Gate:
  `tests/test_kazma_config_files_protected.py`. Containment is by real path,
  and walks prune links (`workspace/real_paths.py`; gate
  `test_no_product_code_asks_isjunction`). **A git command is a write door
  too** (2026-11-16): `git checkout <branch>` and `git merge` write every
  file the other commit holds differently, an ignored `kazma.local.yaml`
  included (git takes an ignored file as expendable), so on an
  install-folder workspace a branch tracking it replaced the owner's
  configuration. `safety/git_tree_writes.git_command_refusal` lists the
  files a tree-changing subcommand writes (checkout, switch, merge,
  cherry-pick, revert, stash, restore, rm, mv; reads that start nothing the
  repository chose, `safety/git_read`) and refuses one of Kazma's; asked by
  `shell_paths.path_refusal` (before the card and where it runs) and by
  `git_checkout` and `git_merge`. `git_pull` fetches, checks the upstream
  commit (`switch_refusal`) and merges it by its hash; the push's rebase
  onto the remote is checked the same way. A list that cannot be read
  refuses. Gate: `tests/test_git_tree_writes.py` (git overwriting the
  ignored file, and a plain merge of the upstream, as witnesses; every
  tree-changing git argv in product code checked or declared).
- **A workspace's `kazma.yaml` is content, never configuration** (SEC-02).
  The settings store's YAML fallback is the install's own file for the life
  of the store. `ConfigStore.reload_from_root` (boot, every workspace switch
  and clone) pointed it at the active workspace, so a cloned repository's
  file answered every key with no stored row: chat-app allowlists (gateway
  admin), the commitment layer's switches, the offsite backup's destination.
  The method and its four callers are gone; nothing assigns `_yaml_path`
  outside `__init__`. Gate: `tests/test_workspace_yaml_is_not_config.py`
  (the repoint put back by hand as the control; a planted repoint).
- **The markdown renderer stashes every tag it writes** (SEC-03,
  `static/js/streaming.js` `inline`: `stash`, `oneToken`). Each generated
  `<a>`, `<img>` and `<span>` is held behind a token, like code spans, until
  the last pass has run, and restored newest first; a link or image address
  is one token (no space, quote, angle bracket or backtick, escaped or not).
  The auto-link pass ran over anchors already written: a second URL after a
  space inside a link's address closed the outer `href` and the rest became
  attributes (`onmouseover`). Never add a pass that reads emitted markup.
  Gate: `tests/js/test_markdown_no_attribute_injection.js` (the old passes as
  the control).
- **A chat-app sender sees and takes over only their own seasons** (SEC-04,
  `sessions/directory.py`: `list_directory(only_for=)`,
  `resolve_session(only_for=)`, `sender_may_take_over(admin=)`;
  `agent_handler/session_commands.py`). `/sessions` listed every chat and
  `/switch` bound the sender to any chat with no owner on record, which is
  every chat started on the Web; with an empty allowlist that was anyone who
  could message the bot (private since 2026-11-11, §42). A sender who is not a gateway admin
  (`allowlists.is_gateway_admin`) now lists and resolves their own seasons,
  and an unowned season is an admin's. `KAZMA_SESSION_OPEN_TAKEOVER=1` still
  opens both. Gate: `tests/test_session_takeover_needs_admin.py`.
- **A session's role is enforced in every mode** (SEC-05, `auth.py`
  `create_auth_middleware`: `_multi_user or _session_cred`). `role_allows`
  ran only under multi-user; an OIDC sign-in mints viewer/operator sessions
  with no local user, and such a session reached the MCP, settings and token
  routes. A request carrying a session credential is now always judged by
  its role; an unreadable user list is a WARNING and never "single
  operator". API tokens and the shared secret are unchanged. The install's
  mail and calendar connections (`/api/email`, `/api/calendar`) are admin
  prefixes. Gate: `tests/test_session_role_always_enforced.py`.
- With them: the API token hash is compared with `hmac.compare_digest`, and
  a file shared into a web chat that is not an inline image is served
  `Cache-Control: no-store` (`routes_chat_upload.shared_file`).

**The second batch (same audit, 2026-11-10)**, each with a test that fails on
the old code:

- **Agent tools.**
  - `shell_exec` finds git's and uv's real subcommand after their global
    options (`safety/shell_arguments.split_subcommand`; an unknown global
    option is refused): `git -C . config ...` and `uv --directory . run ...`
    passed the old first-word rule. More flags that start a program are
    refused (`git grep -O`, `git difftool --extcmd`, `git bisect run`,
    `sort --compress-program`/`-o`), abbreviated long options included
    (`matches_blocked`), and a value attached to a short option reaches the
    path policy for every binary (`attached_values`). Gate:
    `tests/test_shell_exec_subcommand_and_attached_values.py`.
  - The git read tools start no program the repository chose (`_git_read`:
    no external diff, textconv, pager, hooks, signature program or filter
    driver). Only `core.fsmonitor` was off. Gate:
    `tests/test_git_read_tools_start_no_repo_program.py` (a real repository).
  - Every branch and remote a git tool passes is a plain ref name
    (`_checked_ref`, `_checked_revision`), a remote must be one the
    repository has, and `--` precedes positionals. Gate:
    `tests/test_git_tool_refs_validated.py`.
  - A network or device path is refused on its text, before anything
    resolves it (`workspace/remote_paths.remote_path_reason`, called by
    `resolve_tool_path`, `check_path_access`, the shell argument check and
    the workspace routes): resolving `\\host\share` connects to that host.
    `/api/research/download` takes a name, never an absolute path. Gate:
    `tests/test_remote_paths_refused_before_touching.py`.
- **Secrets.**
  - `vault_retrieve`, `vault_store` and `vault_delete` are in
    `ALWAYS_HITL_TOOLS`, and the vault tools refuse Kazma's own rows
    (`vault.is_kazma_owned_secret`: `cfg:` names and install-scoped ones) and
    leave them out of `vault_list`. Gate: `tests/test_vault_tools_kazma_secrets.py`.
  - The universal backup keeps registry entries out by pattern
    (`store_registry.kept_out_of_backups`; `.migrate-*` is not backed up),
    and the offsite copy drops every secret-named file at any depth. The
    importer never extracts `meta.env`; the exporter removes it whatever
    happens. A leftover staging folder loses its `meta.env` and is otherwise
    kept. Gates: `tests/test_offsite_copy_leaves_env_out.py`,
    `tests/test_migration_leaves_no_vault_key.py`.
  - One redactor for every approval card (`security/approval_args.py`): the
    chat card, the swarm bus card and the Swarm page hide a secret-named
    argument, a tool's declared secret argument and URL passwords; every
    name stays and the digest is of the real arguments. Gate:
    `tests/test_approval_cards_hide_credentials.py`.
  - Every key the Settings masker masks is vault-routed
    (`is_sensitive_config_key`; the Web Push key was plaintext, and its
    vault row is install-scoped). Gate:
    `tests/test_masked_settings_go_to_the_vault.py`.
  - `read_system_logs` uses the shared `redact_secrets` (which gained JSON
    members, Authorization credentials and Telegram bot tokens). Gate:
    `tests/test_system_logs_redact_secrets.py`.
  - A first boot keeps its generated keys in the install's env file,
    restricted to the owner before the key is written
    (`env_files.persist_generated_secret`,
    `security/file_access.restrict_to_owner`). Gate:
    `tests/test_generated_keys_kept_in_the_install.py`.
- **Sign-in and sessions.**
  - The security switches (`boot_guard.SECURITY_SWITCHES`, the chat apps'
    two since 2026-11-11, §42) are read only
    through `boot_guard.env_flag` (1/true/yes/on). The app factory refuses a
    sign-in-off switch on a bind no launcher checked
    (`factory_exposure_refusal`). While sign-in is off, a loopback request
    whose Host could be a rebound public name is refused
    (`auth._open_mode_host_refused`). A name without a dot passes only when
    it is `localhost`, this machine's own name (`socket.gethostname()`, with
    and without its domain, `auth._machine_names`) or one
    `KAZMA_AUTOLOGIN_HOSTS` names: any single-label name passed until
    2026-11-11, and a DNS search suffix or a LAN name answer (LLMNR,
    NetBIOS) can hand a browser one. Gates:
    `tests/test_security_switch_spelling.py`,
    `tests/test_open_mode_rebinding_and_launchers.py` (the old single-label
    rule as the negative control).
  - A demo visitor is an operator: admin routes need an admin credential.
    Gate: `tests/test_demo_mode_admin_routes.py`.
  - Deleting, disabling, re-roling or resetting a platform user ends their
    sessions. Gate: `tests/test_user_changes_end_sessions.py`.
  - `/ws/voice` and `/ws/dashboard` ask their HTTP twins' role
    (`auth.websocket_principal`, `auth.principal_allows`). Gate:
    `tests/test_websocket_roles.py`.
  - OIDC: optional allowlists (`KAZMA_OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`, `_DOMAINS`,
    `_GROUPS`), an unverified email refused, every role value read, a nonce,
    a rate-limited start route. Gate: `tests/test_oidc_who_may_sign_in.py`.
  - Telegram checks the sender before it downloads or transcribes. Gate:
    `tests/test_telegram_sender_checked_before_download.py`.
  - Every local sign-in costs one PBKDF2, and the username throttle is per
    address. Gate: `tests/test_login_timing_same_for_every_name.py`.
  - `analyze_image` fetches through `web_acquire.http.fetch_public` (pinned).
    Gate: `tests/test_vision_fetch_is_pinned.py`.
  - **An OAuth sign-in is one attempt, started by POST**
    (`kazma_core/security/oauth_attempts.py`, `kazma_ui/oauth_sign_in.py`;
    GitHub, Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft mail, Outlook Calendar).
    GitHub kept ONE install-wide state compared with `!=` (a second start
    replaced the first, and any browser could finish it), the mail and
    calendar sign-ins an unbounded dict in memory, and every start was a GET
    that wrote it. A start is a POST from Kazma's page (the CSRF rule; the
    mail and calendar routes also `_verify_same_origin`) that answers the
    provider's URL and sets a cookie named for the attempt
    (`oauth_attempts.binding_cookie_name`: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, the
    callback's path, ten minutes). The attempt is kept as its state's hash
    in the settings store (`oauth_attempts.PENDING_KEY`, RUNTIME, at most
    `oauth_attempts.MAX_PENDING`); the callback takes it once
    (`oauth_attempts.take`: the cookie compared with `hmac.compare_digest`
    before anything is read, then one `atomic_update`) and refuses a state
    used twice, from another browser, past ten minutes or of another
    provider, with a code the pages word (`window.kazmaSignInFailed`). A
    start from another origin than the callback is refused with the origin
    to open (409), before anything is kept. The page follows the answer with
    `window.kazmaStartSignIn` (http(s) only); the GitHub callback sends the
    browser back to the page it started from
    (`oauth_attempts.safe_return_path`). Gates:
    `tests/test_oauth_attempts.py` (the real app, stand-in providers; the
    old single state as the negative control),
    `tests/js/test_kazma_start_sign_in.js`.
- **Infrastructure.**
  - The root `.dockerignore` excludes every secret file name and `.kazma/`
    at any depth. Gate: `tests/test_dockerignore_secrets.py`.
  - Headers: `style-src`, `font-src`, `frame-src`, `worker-src`,
    `manifest-src`, HSTS over HTTPS only, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`,
    `Permissions-Policy`, no `Server` header. No `default-src`: every kind
    a page uses is named.
  - **No script from another host; connections to this server and the
    configured LiveKit server only** (2026-11-11,
    `kazma_ui/security_headers.py`). The LiveKit browser client was loaded
    from cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpinned, when Live voice started, and kept the
    pages from sending `script-src`. It ships with Kazma now
    (`static/vendor/livekit`: `livekit-client` 2.23.0, Apache-2.0, its
    version, npm integrity and SHA-256 in `vendored.json`, rebuilt by
    `scripts/vendor_livekit.py`; the two files are `-text` so a Windows
    checkout keeps their bytes). The policy: `script-src 'self'
    'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'` (the pages' inline scripts and handlers,
    and Alpine's expressions, compiled with `new Function`), and
    `connect-src 'self'`, this server's own `ws`/`wss` origin, and the
    LiveKit server (`LIVEKIT_URL` or `voice.livekit.url`, while duplex is
    on; `_livekit_connect_sources`: its `wss` and `https` origin, a plain
    origin only, and `*.livekit.cloud` for LiveKit Cloud). The LiveKit
    address is read off the loop and kept `_LiveKitSources.TTL_S` seconds
    (`_livekit_sources`: the first response waits for one read in a thread,
    later ones refresh in the background). A page keeps the policy it was
    opened with: a LiveKit address saved in Settings reaches pages opened
    after the save (Settings says so). Gates: `tests/test_security_headers.py`
    (the directives, a hostile address or Host, the read off the loop and
    kept; the old policy as the control), `tests/test_vendor_livekit.py`
    (the files as recorded, served as a script, no page loading a script,
    stylesheet or module from another host; the old `voice.js` line
    planted), `tests/e2e/test_pages_load_clean.py` (every page and Settings
    tab under the policy; a CDN script and an outside socket refused, the
    old policy as the control), `tests/e2e/test_livekit_client_and_policy.py`
    (the vendored client defines `LivekitClient.Room`; the configured LiveKit
    host reachable, an outside one and an unconfigured one refused, live
    voice's own socket never).
  - **No sign-in runs in a popup; every page sends
    `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`** (2026-11-11). The GitHub
    sign-in opened a window whose callback page answered
    `window.opener.postMessage`, so the opener policy had to stay off. Every
    sign-in now runs in the same tab (`window.kazmaStartSignIn`, the callback
    sends the browser back), and the header is on. The one window a page
    still opens for a sign-in is an MCP server's authorization page
    (`mcp.js`, `noopener`, its callback a loopback listener of its own,
    declared). Gates: `tests/test_no_popup_sign_in.py` (no `window.open` of
    a sign-in, no opener read, no window `message` listener in any product
    script, template or server page; planted shapes and the old Workspace
    line as negative controls), `tests/test_security_headers.py`,
    `tests/e2e/test_github_sign_in_same_tab.py` (reached by the sidebar,
    English and Arabic: GitHub and Gmail sign-ins with stand-in providers,
    no window opened).
  - MCP presets name an exact version, held to the recorded registry answer
    (`tests/test_mcp_catalog.py`). The release workflow checksums the built
    files before any other tool runs and checks them again before signing;
    the metrics workflow's token job installs nothing.
  - **SearXNG's secret key is generated by setup** (2026-11-11, the owner's
    decision; `security/searxng_secret.py`). `kazma setup install`'s private
    search part keeps a generated `SEARXNG_SECRET` in its `.env` before it
    starts SearXNG (`container_services.ensure_secret`, through
    `env_files.persist_generated_secret(path=)`: restricted before the value
    is written; an owner's value, in the file or the shell, is never
    replaced; the placeholder is not a value) and runs compose with
    `--env-file` on that file. The part is not in place while the key is
    missing, so a re-run fixes an older install. `docker-compose.yml` keeps
    the placeholder as its fallback, so a start without setup still works;
    Kazma's SearXNG container on it (`uses_placeholder`: its
    `SEARXNG_SECRET`, else the `secret_key` of the settings file it mounts)
    is a boot WARNING (`service_exposure.searxng_secret_problems`, no ops
    alert) and the security report's `check_searxng_secret`. Gate:
    `tests/test_searxng_secret_generated.py` (the old setup as the negative
    control).

### 63. Kazma's own container engine (`kazma_core/container_engine.py`, `docker_cli.py`)

2026-11-12: a Windows update restarted the PC and nobody signed in; Docker
Desktop starts only at a sign-in, so every container stayed down for six
hours. Plan, measurements and an independent review:
`docs/plans/CONTAINERS_WITHOUT_A_SIGN_IN_PLAN.md`. On Windows the only
"Docker as a service" for Linux containers is Docker Engine in a WSL distro
started by a boot task: `kazma-engine`, kept up by the `KazmaEngine` task
(S4U, normal rights; its `keep-engine.ps1` holds a `wsl.exe` attached to the
distro, since WSL stops a distro about 15 s after the last `wsl.exe` leaves;
the holder is the channel of its clean stop at a shutdown, below), reached
as the Docker context `kazma-engine` (mutual TLS on 127.0.0.1:2376). Drilled
on a clean VM: it starts with nobody signed in, services as SYSTEM and LOCAL
SERVICE (a tunnel) reach its published ports, and it is back 19 s after a
`wsl --shutdown`.

- **The choice is explicit.** `containers.engine` is `kazma` (Kazma's
  engine), `desktop` (Docker Desktop, the owner's choice), or unset: then the
  engine setup recorded it installed (`setup_record.json`
  `container_engine`), else nothing is pinned and the docker CLI's current
  context serves, as before (`container_engine.engine_setting`). Never "the
  engine exists, so use it": on the owner's PC, engine made and nothing moved,
  that would have sent Kazma to an empty engine at the next reload.
- **Pinned in `DOCKER_CONTEXT`** for the process and every docker call it
  starts (`docker_cli.apply_engine_choice`); the operator's own
  `DOCKER_CONTEXT` or `DOCKER_HOST` wins. The server applies it at boot
  before the background loops and follows the setting
  (`watch_engine_setting`); any other Kazma process applies it at its first
  `find_docker_cli` (the CLI, setup, scripts). The guard's copy of
  `docker_cli.py` (loaded by path) never reads settings: it takes the choice
  from the server's record (`guard_dependencies`, field `engine`) and hands
  the context to the document broker (`_BROKER_ENV_KEEP`), which restarts
  when the choice changes.
- **Mount paths follow the context** (`docker_cli.engine_host_path`): Kazma's
  engine mounts fixed drive `G:` at `/g` (its distro's `[automount] root=/`);
  a share, mapped, `subst` or removable drive is refused with the reason;
  Docker Desktop takes the Windows path. Never decided from a cached
  `docker info`.
- **The guard brings Kazma's engine back, never Docker Desktop**
  (`Dependencies._start_kazma_engine`): it runs the `KazmaEngine` task,
  restarts Docker inside the distro (a running keep-alive does not mean a
  running dockerd), and holds a keep-alive of its own when the task is
  missing or refused (`engine_task_missing`, `engine_task_denied`).
- **Express holds the engine on Windows and Linux since 2026-11-13** (the
  owner's request: private search and the Neo4j memory graph install by
  default, §21c); it was container-free from 2026-11-12. Setup installs
  Kazma's engine when a container part is chosen; Docker Desktop only when
  the user picks it (`kazma setup install --docker desktop`).
- **Setup installs it** (`kazma_core/container_engine_setup.py`, assets in
  `container_engine_assets/`): `check` names what is missing (wsl, distro,
  docker, cli, context, task, shutdown), `install_steps` puts in only that, in order,
  the record last (it waits for `docker version` and writes
  `setup_record.json` `container_engine`, the setting's fallback). WSL first
  (pinned MSI, the two features); a step that needs Windows restarted
  answers `RESTART` and the container steps after it wait (Docker
  Desktop's own path keeps its order). The distro is the dated Ubuntu 24.04
  image, Docker Engine set up by `setup-engine.sh` piped over stdin (LF,
  idempotent, docker packages held, Docker's apt key kept only when its
  fingerprint is the published one, `kazma_trust_docker_key`,
  `tests/test_engine_docker_key.py`, Ubuntu's archive read over HTTPS
  before the first `apt-get update`, `kazma_https_sources`,
  `tests/test_engine_apt_over_https.py` -- over plain HTTP the network on the
  way handed back a corrupted package list on every try and the first fresh
  install after the 2026-11-19 reset could not set the engine up -- TLS keys
  made once, listening on 127.0.0.1 only with client certificates); Docker's
  Windows CLI and the
  compose plugin from Docker's own downloads. **Kazma's own CLI, not any
  CLI** (2026-11-14): the check's "cli" is
  `container_engine_setup._own_cli_installed_check` (`docker.exe` in
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Kazma\engine\bin` and the compose plugin), and
  `find_docker_cli` takes that copy first on Windows. The check took Docker
  Desktop's CLI for Kazma's, so the owner's PC never got its own, and
  uninstalling Docker Desktop would have cut Kazma off from its engine; the
  engine is still asked through whatever CLI there is, so a Docker that
  answers is never set up again (gate: `tests/test_container_engine_setup.py`,
  the old rule as the control). Every download is pinned by
  URL, size and SHA-256 and kept only when it matches (`_fetch`). What would
  stop it is said before anything is installed (`preflight`: WSL's
  localhost forwarding off, Docker already in another distro), and stops
  only the container parts. `kazma setup engine` installs, repairs, checks
  or removes it; removing is refused while another project's containers
  live in it or it cannot be asked (`--force`). On Linux Kazma's engine is
  the system's Docker service: setup starts it at boot and adds the account
  to the `docker` group (`system_deps._docker_access_steps`; a socket this
  account may not use is `DOCKER_GROUP`, fixed with the group alone).
- **Drilled on a clean Windows VM** (2026-11-12): WSL, a restart, then the
  rest in 321 s; after a reboot with nobody signed in Docker answered 29 s
  after boot, and a container read a mounted `C:` folder. The drill found
  three bugs, each now held by a test: WSL is told by `wsl --version`
  (`_wsl_installed`; Windows' stub fails it, and a WSL with no distro fails
  `wsl -l` too, which read as "no WSL" and asked for a restart on every
  run); a download setup makes opens with `http_tls.open_download` (certifi's
  roots: a fresh Windows' store lacked GitHub's, and Python reads the store
  alone; the Tesseract models too); and a program's stdin is bytes (`_out`:
  text mode on Windows wrote `\r\n`, and bash refused the script's first
  line). Docker's CLI folder joins the user's PATH (`_on_user_path`, never
  `setx`), and Kazma's own CLI off PATH is no warning.
- **Readiness and the disk watch name the engine** (2026-11-12). Kazma's
  engine comes back by itself and Docker Desktop waits for a sign-in, so
  "Docker does not answer" asked for two different steps.
  `docker_cli.engine_in_force` is the one answer (`kazma`, `desktop`,
  `system`, `other`), read from the context in force with no process
  started, so a down engine is named too; `docker_cli.engine_label` names it.
  Readiness's code sandbox check carries `engine` and says it in its error
  ("Kazma's container engine is not running"), which the guard quotes in its
  page and `--status`. The document isolation report carries `engine`, and
  its step is `start_kazma_engine` (with `kazma setup engine` to repair it)
  or `start_docker_desktop` (sign in), in both languages. The guard's
  `DiskWatch` watches the disk of the engine in force: the `kazma-engine`
  distro's folder (`docker_cli.kazma_engine_disk_dir`, where setup imports
  it) when Kazma's engine is in use, else Docker Desktop's disk image; never
  a disk no Kazma container lives on. Gate:
  `tests/test_engine_named_where_kazma_waits.py` (22 of its 24 fail on the
  old code; the general step and the catalog are the controls).
- **Its disk can live in the data folder** (2026-11-21, section 21 G3): with
  a data folder chosen, setup imports the distro into `<folder>\engine`, a
  disk kept there from before a reset is registered in place (`wsl
  --import-in-place`), and `kazma setup data-folder` moves an installed one
  (`wsl --manage kazma-engine --move`, hashed before and after, its task
  disabled meanwhile). Where the disk is, is WSL's own registration
  (`docker_cli.wsl_distro_location`), which `kazma_engine_disk_dir` and the
  guard's disk watch read.
- **The boot drill is a script** (`scripts/engine_boot_drill.py`, Stage 2's
  gate, run from the host). It reverts the drill VM to its clean checkpoint,
  copies one commit (`git archive`) and `uv`, runs `kazma setup install
  --mode full -y` detached (an SSH drop must not end it), restarts Windows
  when setup asks (WSL) and runs it again, sets the strict code profile from
  the install folder (it refuses unless the install's `.env` is the one
  loaded: from the home folder the first drill wrote it to a store of its
  own), restarts Windows with nobody signed in, and reads Kazma's readiness,
  `kazma_guard.py --status` and SearXNG every 15 s. Every container part must
  be ready within 5 minutes of boot; a reading with a session in `query
  user` makes the verdict `invalid`. Passed on 2026-11-13: every part ready
  within 90 s (`docs/audits/ENGINE_BOOT_DRILL_2026-11-12.md`). `--docker
  desktop` is the negative control (verdict `not_up`). Changing the
  `KazmaEngine` task's trigger is no control: the guard runs that task on
  demand and holds its own keep-alive. Its reading of `--status` is held to
  the guard's own line builders: `tests/test_engine_boot_drill.py`.
- **Setup's programs get no input, and it waits for what it started** (the
  drill, 2026-11-12). `container_engine_setup._out` passed `input=None`:
  `wsl.exe` inherited setup's console, and Windows' WSL stub waited on "press
  any key to install" until the 60 s timeout at every WSL call (a key
  pressed then would have installed WSL from the Store); it passes
  `stdin=DEVNULL`, and the terminal gate (`tests/test_setup_system.py`)
  covers this module and `install.py` and counts an `input` that can be None
  as the terminal. A Full install asked SearXNG 2 s after `docker compose
  up` and ended "not installed", exit 1; the step "wait for SearXNG to
  answer" (`SEARXNG_READY_WAIT_S`, 120 s) waits for it
  (`tests/test_install_modes.py`, a SearXNG that never answers as the
  control). `--docker desktop` installed WSL with `wsl --install`, which
  Windows refuses outside a signed-in console, so an unattended Desktop
  install never got Docker Desktop; both paths get WSL from one step,
  `engine:wsl` (the pinned MSI), and the container steps wait for the
  restart on either path.
- Gates: `tests/test_container_engine_choice.py` (the first rule, "the
  context exists", as the negative control), the engine cases in
  `tests/test_guard_dependencies.py` (the same outage on Docker Desktop as
  the control), `tests/test_container_engine_setup.py` (a fake machine and
  download: a mismatched download keeps nothing, a script without its ready
  line fails its step), `tests/test_install_modes.py` (Full installs the
  engine and never Docker Desktop; `--docker desktop` as the control),
  `tests/test_setup_system.py` (the docker group; Windows as the control).
- **An install on Docker Desktop moves with one command** (Stage 3,
  `kazma setup engine --move-from-desktop`, `kazma_core/engine_move.py`, on
  the pattern of the database's move, section 21 G). It sets Kazma's engine
  up if it is not, then moves only the containers Kazma's record names: the
  rule the server tells the guard with
  (`guard_dependencies._match_containers`), read against Docker Desktop's
  containers; another project's container is never named, and a volume one
  shares refuses the move. Kazma's database in a container refuses it too,
  naming `kazma setup postgres --move-from-container`. Every refusal
  (Docker Desktop down, a name or a port already on the engine, a mount the
  engine cannot take, `containers.engine` already `kazma`) comes before
  anything changes. Images (`docker save` into `docker load`, else pulled by
  digest, held to the same layers), the sandbox image and the document
  worker image (copied when Docker Desktop holds this code's build, else
  built on the engine, only in the container profile) are put on the engine
  while Kazma runs; then Kazma is held through its guard (`_MoveHold`, its
  own pause reason), and each container is stopped on Docker Desktop with
  restart `no` and kept, seen stopped (`_seen_stopped`: never a volume read
  while its container runs), its volumes copied by tar between the engines
  and compared entry by entry (path, kind, owner, mode, size, SHA-256; a
  hard link counts as the file it names: `_manifest_of`), made again from
  its own settings (`_create_args`; Docker Desktop's Windows or
  `/run/desktop/mnt/host` bind sources as the engine mounts them,
  `_engine_bind_source`), files added or changed inside it carried, started,
  and seen healthy and answering on its ports from Windows. Then
  `containers.engine` = `kazma`, the guard's record told
  (`guard_dependencies.set_record_engine`), Kazma started and seen ready.
  A failure puts everything back: before the switch this run's objects are
  removed from the engine (they hold only the copy); after it they are
  stopped and kept (Kazma may have written to them); Docker Desktop's
  originals get their restart policy back and run; `containers.engine`
  says `desktop`. Every change is journaled before it is made
  (`setup_record.json`, `engine_move`): a run that died half way is rolled
  back by the next one, which takes the dead run's pause over
  (`_MoveHold.adopt_leftover`); Ctrl+C rolls back before it stops.
  `kazma setup engine` alone on a Docker Desktop install writes
  `containers.engine` = `desktop` before it records the engine
  (`engine_move.keep_desktop`): recorded, the engine would be Kazma's choice
  at its next start, with none of its containers. Gate:
  `tests/test_engine_move.py`, against `tests/_fake_docker_engines.py` (a
  fake docker CLI with two engines run as a real program: real argv, pipes
  and tar streams), each rule with its negative control (a mover that trusts
  the stop, a copy without the check, no journal, no Docker Desktop choice
  written). **Drilled on a clean VM** (2026-11-13, Docker Desktop 4.99,
  SearXNG and Neo4j from the shipped compose files, another project's
  container beside them). The move ran in the signed-in session in 766 s,
  the engine's install included; Neo4j's 528 MB came across entry for entry,
  and the other project's container was untouched. After a restart with
  nobody signed in, both containers were healthy 39 s after boot. The drill
  found three things:
  - The hold found its guard only through `.git`, so on an install
    unpacked from a source zip it said "no guard supervises it" and refused.
    `_MoveHold` now finds the guard from the install's own folder
    (`setup._checkout_root`).
  - `_MoveHold.ready` now counts a Kazma waiting for its provider key as
    up, as the guard's resume does.
  - The carried files are said in one line per container (Neo4j's start
    changes the owner of its whole folder: 248 lines).

  At a Windows restart its containers got only seconds (Neo4j:
  "Stopping..." and never "Stopped."), and a line Neo4j's start script had
  just appended came back as NUL bytes: the next bullet.
- **A Windows shutdown stops the engine cleanly** (2026-11-13,
  `KazmaEngineShutdown`, `container_engine_assets/engine-shutdown.cs`,
  `engine-stop.sh`, `keep-engine.ps1`). Measured on the drill VM, nobody
  signed in: WSL's VM was ended about 2 s into a restart with no signal to
  anything in it (WslService and vmcompute are `IGNORES_SHUTDOWN`; WSL shuts
  a distro down gracefully only at a sign-out of the session that started
  it, and the boot task's is session 0), and a writer container lost 760
  bytes to NULs. Task Scheduler ends every running task and what it started
  60 ms into a shutdown (event 111), before any service hears of it, and
  starts none (`0x8007045B`, ERROR_SHUTDOWN_IN_PROGRESS); WSL refuses
  LocalSystem. So the channel is opened before:
  - the `KazmaEngineShutdown` service (LocalSystem, built at setup from
    `engine-shutdown.cs` by the .NET Framework's own `csc.exe` into
    `Program Files\Kazma\engine-shutdown`, never a folder the account can
    write) takes the preshutdown notice, sets its own preshutdown timeout
    (`SHUTDOWN_BUDGET_S`, 120, plus 30) and serves two named pipes
    (`KazmaEngineHold-in`/`-out`; network denied);
  - `keep-engine.ps1` starts the distro's holder through WMI
    (`Win32_Process.Create`: outside Task Scheduler's job) as `cmd /c wsl.exe
    ... kazma-engine-hold piped <in-pipe >out-pipe`, holds the distro itself
    as before when no service listens, and starts nothing once
    `SM_SHUTTINGDOWN` is set;
  - at preshutdown the service writes `stop`: `kazma-engine-stop` stops
    Docker, then containerd (a daemon shutdown: every container gets its
    stop signal and its own stop timeout, and its restart policy brings it
    back at the next boot; a `docker stop` would keep an `unless-stopped`
    one down), then masks them at runtime (masking first reloaded them as
    empty units with no order: containerd went at once under a Docker still
    stopping, "Force shutdown daemon"), writes the distro's own disks
    (`sync -f` per ext4/xfs/btrfs mount, bounded; a plain `sync` also
    flushes the Windows drives at `/c` and never returned during a
    shutdown), answers `ENGINE_STOPPED`; then `poweroff`. Windows waits for
    it. Stop and poweroff are two lines so the answer crosses before the
    distro ends; the holder strips a CR (.NET's `WriteLine` sent `stop\r`).
  Control 128 (`sc.exe control KazmaEngineShutdown 128`) makes the same
  stop without a restart, and keep-engine starts the engine again. Setup's
  step is `engine:shutdown` (admin): check() counts the service not
  running, an older `keep-engine.ps1` or older helpers in the distro
  (`engine-stop.sha256`, read with no call into WSL) as missing, so
  `kazma setup engine` brings an existing engine (the owner's PC) up to it;
  the helpers also go in with Docker (`engine:docker`). Measured after: the
  service heard the restart 1.1 s in, the writer got TERM, finished its 8 s
  stop and wrote DONE, no NUL byte, and Windows went on at +10.2 s. The
  drill is `scripts/engine_shutdown_drill.py` (a fresh VM, the engine
  through setup, a writer, Windows restarted; `--control` on a commit
  before it must be `unclean`): on 2026-11-13 the fix was `clean` in both
  rounds (Windows took 9.4 s and 9.0 s) and the control `unclean` (the
  writer cut off mid-run, no TERM; 0.3 s), report
  `docs/audits/ENGINE_SHUTDOWN_DRILL_2026-11-13.md`. Not covered: a power cut or a crash (no
  notice at all), and Docker Desktop (it runs only in a signed-in session;
  not measured). Gates: `tests/test_engine_clean_shutdown.py` (the distro's
  scripts run under bash with stand-ins, their first versions as negative
  controls; the service built with `csc` on Windows),
  `tests/test_engine_shutdown_drill.py`.
- **A Windows shutdown stops Kazma first** (2026-11-20, `kazma_core/shutdown_notice.py`).
  The owner's restart and Windows Update's after it cut Kazma off: the start
  card said "the last run did not shut down cleanly". Task Scheduler ends the
  guard at the start of a shutdown; the server lived on, heard of the
  shutdown only at the very end (Windows' console shutdown event, 37 s in),
  after the database service had stopped, logged "Shutdown signal sent" and
  was ended in the same second, with no stop stamp written.
  - The `KazmaEngineShutdown` service serves a third pipe,
    `KazmaShutdownNotice` (16 instances: one per Kazma server on the
    machine). Each server connects from `serve.py`
    (`shutdown_notice.start`, a daemon thread; never another process: a
    test's app never connects to the machine's real service) and says
    nothing.
  - At the preshutdown notice the service writes `stop` to every connected
    server. A server stops the way the guard's CTRL_BREAK stops it
    (`signal.raise_signal(SIGBREAK)`: uvicorn's handler, then the app's own
    shutdown and `exit_after_shutdown`). It keeps its end of the pipe open
    until its process ends, and the service waits for every end within
    `SHUTDOWN_KAZMA_BUDGET_S` (75), before it stops the engine.
  - Windows stops the database service after every preshutdown service is
    done. The service's preshutdown timeout is Kazma's budget plus the
    engine's plus 30 s. Control 129 makes Kazma's stop alone (a drill; the
    guard then starts the server again). `--notice-drill N --notice-pipe
    NAME` runs the same stop with no service, for tests.
  - The guard starts no server while Windows shuts down
    (`kazma_guard.windows_shutting_down`, `SM_SHUTTINGDOWN`).
  - The service is installed with Kazma's own service, on any engine:
    `kazma setup install`'s service part counts as done only when it runs
    this build (`container_engine_setup.shutdown_service_current`: running,
    the source the build left beside the program equal to this build's, the
    registered command line equal). The part's step
    `engine:shutdown_service` (`shutdown_service_step`, administrators only)
    puts it in alone; the task is registered again only when missing. The
    engine's own shutdown step uses the same build, and either finds the
    other's work current. `kazma uninstall` takes the service off
    (`remove_shutdown_service`) unless the engine's removal does.
  - A server with no service listening says so once: a WARNING under the
    guard, naming `kazma setup install` in an administrator terminal. Lines
    said before the app sets up logging are held and said after
    (`shutdown_notice._log`).
  - Gates: `tests/test_windows_shutdown_notice.py` (the real service
    program built with `csc` and the real listener: two servers told and
    waited for, the real SIGBREAK ending a process; a server that never
    ends, and no server, as controls), the install, uninstall and engine
    tests (the task alone as the service part's control).
  - The real restart is `scripts/restart_drill.py` on the drill VM: a
    Custom install (PostgreSQL and the service only), then `shutdown /r /t 0
    /f`, judged from the stop stamp, the server's own stop line, the
    service's Application log and event 6006. Passed 2026-11-20
    (`docs/audits/evidence/restart_drill/`): the fix `clean` (the service
    told the server 1.7 s in, the stop recorded 1.9 s in, Windows stopped
    2.1 s in); the control at 9b96c2b8c `unclean` ("Shutdown signal sent"
    0.9 s in, as Windows stopped, no stamp: the live symptom). The VM has no
    TPM since the PC reset (its virtual TPM was locked to the old Windows'
    guardian certificates); its clean checkpoint is
    `engine_boot_drill.CHECKPOINT`.

### 65. A2A: other agents call Kazma (`kazma_ui/a2a_api.py`, 2026-11-14)

REMAINING 4.5. `kazma_core/a2a_protocol.py` holds the protocol (A2A 0.3,
JSON-RPC 2.0): the agent card, reading `message/send`, task and error
objects. `kazma_ui/a2a_api.py` serves `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and
`POST /api/a2a` only while `ENABLED_KEY` (`a2a.enabled`, off; Settings ->
System; `_strict_bool`, a SETTING) is on; off, both answer 404.

- **Sign-in is the API's**: `/api/a2a` is under `/api`, so the auth
  middleware requires a credential; an agent uses an operator API token.
- **Read only, no memory, no approvals**: a request is one turn on
  `cron_fire_graph(capabilities="read")` (the scheduled task's set: read and
  safe tiers, never write, danger, always-ask or MCP), run by
  `run_agent_turn(persist=False)`, labelled as another agent's (`_NOTE`).
  Widening what A2A may do is a decision for the owner, never a default.
- **Bounded**: `MAX_RUNNING` turns at once (`busy` past it), `TURN_BUDGET_S`
  each (`asyncio.timeout`), rate bucket `a2a`; tasks and a conversation's
  last turns are kept in this process (`_Store`), a day.
- Gate: `tests/test_a2a.py` (every call, the read-only graph by name, no
  memory, cancel, busy, a failed turn, refusals as JSON-RPC errors).
- **A read set never writes** (2026-11-15): `crawl_site` is read tier but
  saved files by default. `side_effects.READ_ONLY_ARGUMENTS` (`crawl_site`'s
  `save`) is dropped from the tools a read set offers and forced off by
  `DeclaredToolExecutor(read_only=True)`, for A2A and a scheduled task's
  `read` capability alike; an A2A body is at most `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (256 KiB,
  also declared in `body_limits`). Gate: `tests/test_read_tools_never_write.py`
  (every read- and safe-tier tool's code read for file writes).

### 64. WhatsApp (`kazma_gateway/adapters/whatsapp.py`, 2026-11-14)

The fourth chat app, through Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API. It is built by the one
builder (`chat_adapters`, §48) like the others, from Settings only (no
environment fallback): `connectors.whatsapp.token`, `.phone_number_id`,
`.app_secret`, `.verify_token`, `.api_version`, `.allowed_users`, `.enabled`.
The three credentials are install-scoped in the vault
(`vault.INSTALL_SCOPED_SECRETS`, `cfg:connectors.whatsapp.`).

- **Meta calls Kazma; nothing polls.** The webhook
  (`whatsapp_webhook_router`, mounted at `WEBHOOK_PATH` =
  `/api/webhooks/whatsapp`, open in `auth.ALWAYS_OPEN_PREFIXES`) answers GET
  with the challenge only for the saved verify token (compared in constant
  time), and POST only with Meta's signature: `whatsapp_parse.signature_ok`
  checks `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body under the app
  secret) before the body is parsed. No app secret saved: 503 to every call
  (fail-closed); a body past 1 MiB: 413. It answers 200 at once and the
  adapter reads each sender's messages in order behind it (`_chains`), so a
  slow download or transcription never makes Meta resend; a resend is counted
  (`duplicate`) and never handed on twice, and the first copy's fate stays
  under its id. `settled()` waits for what was taken (tests).
- **Every message a person sent is counted, then judged** (§42): a message to
  another number of the account (`not_this_number`), the sender rule
  (`SenderGate`; a stranger is told once a day, `sender_rule.private_notice`
  names the number and "Allowed numbers"), a kind Kazma does not read
  (`unsupported_type`), a file it could not download (`media_failed`).
  WhatsApp's reasons word the shared refusals by its own field
  (`whatsapp_receive.WHATSAPP_REASONS`).
- **A number is a user id in any spelling**: `wa_digits` (the adapter) and
  `allowlists._platform_user_id` (owner ids, `KAZMA_GATEWAY_ADMINS`
  `whatsapp:+965...`, the admin check) turn "+965 9999 1234" into the
  `wa_id` WhatsApp sends. The exact-text rule the other platforms keep would
  not match it (the negative control in `tests/test_whatsapp.py`).
- **Calls to Meta** (`whatsapp_api.WhatsAppClient`): one httpx client, no
  redirects, the token in the Authorization header only; a send is retried
  only after a 429 (a 5xx may have delivered it), a read after a 5xx too;
  downloads capped (`MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES`); `explain` words the codes the
  owner can act on (131047 the 24-hour window, 131030 the test number's
  recipients, 190 the token). What a call can fail with is
  `_META_FAILURES`; no handler catches more.
- **Sending**: `md_to_whatsapp` (WhatsApp's marks, code untouched) and
  `split_for_whatsapp` (4,096 characters, a fenced block kept whole when it
  fits); files are uploaded and sent as media; each part reports to the chat
  outbox (`send_report`). Links never get a preview.
- **Buttons are one table for every chat app** (`adapters/markup.py`):
  `MARKUP_KEYS` names each platform's send-context field (WhatsApp's is
  `whatsapp_buttons`), `attach_markup` puts a markup there, and
  `approval_markup` / `semantic_markup` build the approval card's and a
  clarify question's buttons. The approval card (`agent_handler/hitl.py`,
  both card shapes and the resume path) and the gateway's in-turn card
  (`agent_handler/graph.py`) and the run supervisor's cards (`run_cards.py`)
  ask it; they named three fields at each site before. A new chat app is a
  row there. A press is the shared callback scheme
  (`platform_callbacks.parse_callback_data`); approvals, swarm and run
  buttons need a gateway admin (`is_gateway_admin`), as on every platform.
  `agent_handler/store.py` keeps `whatsapp_buttons` and `blocks` out of the
  stored session context.
- **No swarm sender**: WhatsApp lets a business message a person only within
  24 hours of their last message (templates after that), so a swarm card or
  reminder could not reliably reach the owner there (`BUS_FIELDS["whatsapp"]`
  is empty and `_build_swarm_sender` returns None for it).
- **The Test** (`whatsapp_diagnose.diagnose`, `POST
  /api/connectors/whatsapp/test`): Meta's answer for the number, the app
  secret, the webhook address (`KAZMA_PUBLIC_URL` + `WEBHOOK_PATH`, also the
  connector list's `endpoint`, which the card shows) and whether Meta called
  it, the last message's fate, the 24-hour window, allowed numbers, the
  connection. `connector_test.allowlist_check` takes the field's name
  (`field`, `id_word`). The card-title gate finds every `*_diagnose.py`
  (`tests/test_telegram_slack_receive_and_test.py`), so a new chat app's
  checks need titles the day it is added.
- Gate: `tests/test_whatsapp.py` (a stand-in Meta behind
  `httpx.MockTransport` and the real router, adapter, builder, routes and
  Test; an unsigned call, another secret's signature, a resend, a stranger,
  a non-admin's button and the old admin rule as negative controls). Not
  verified against Meta's real servers until the owner's first live test.

### 66. Code scanning (GitHub CodeQL, 2026-11-14)

GitHub's CodeQL default setup (Python, JavaScript, C#, Actions; on since
2026-11-13, every push and weekly) reported 388 alerts. Each was judged
against the code: the real ones are fixed, each class with a gate; the rest
are dismissed on GitHub with the reason (most: Kazma's own checks, which
CodeQL does not know -- `safe_error`, `remote_path_reason`, the session hash).
A new alert is judged the same way; never dismiss one without reading the
code it names.

- **Every JavaScript file parses** (`scripts/check_js_syntax.py`, CI's
  js-check): every tracked `.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`, a `.js` checked as a script
  and as a module, each from a copy (`node --check` on a `.js` leaves it to
  node's module detection, which accepted a file valid as neither).
  `loadtests/k6_swarm.js` began with Python imports: k6 could not run it, and
  CodeQL's "could not process" warning was on every analysis. Gate:
  `tests/test_every_js_file_parses.py`.
- **A web session is named by `web_sessions.session_label`** (the start of
  its hash: the `id` Settings lists), never by its cookie, which is the
  sign-in credential. `web_actor.actor_for_session` is the one builder (the
  Memory page's trail, the approve route, Time Travel's audit, `web_actor`);
  four kept the cookie's first eight characters in kazma.log and the audit
  tables. Gate: `tests/test_session_label_never_the_cookie.py`.
- **No log line carries a password inside an address.** The log writer
  masks every message and traceback before it is queued
  (`logging_config._LogQueueHandler.prepare`, `url_credentials.mask_urls_in_text`):
  model discovery and the model registry logged provider addresses as they
  were. `kazma doctor`'s rows (`doctor._line`) and the update log
  (`update._without_url_passwords`, a local copy: the updater runs while
  Kazma's package may not import) mask too, and the settings store's change
  log masks a list's or mapping's nested secrets by name (`_redact_for_log`,
  `config_mask.mask_deep`). Gates: `tests/test_logs_never_carry_url_passwords.py`,
  `tests/test_update_log_masks_url_passwords.py`.
- **A network path is refused before anything resolves it** (the 2026-11-10
  rule, §62) in the places it had missed: `IdeService.resolve`, the
  Workspace file list (`/api/workspace/files`: only "/" was stripped, so a
  backslash path became the join), the extra folders
  (`path_grants.set_durable_roots`, `_extra_root_problem`; one kept from
  before is skipped by `list_durable_roots`), the store check before an
  approval card (`control_plane_store_targeted`), a skill installed from a
  folder (`install_from_any`) and the workspace-roots policy
  (`normalize_workspace_roots`). Gate:
  `tests/test_remote_paths_refused_before_touching.py`.
- **No answer carries an exception's own text** (§26 F, the rule and its
  gate): 17 routes and 5 near misses CodeQL named (py/stack-trace-exposure),
  and the helpers they answer through, now answer `described_error` or
  `safe_error`; Kazma's own refusals go through `validation_error`, except
  where its redaction would hide the folder the owner typed
  (`put_extra_roots`, declared).
- **Patterns that read untrusted text stay linear** (possessive quantifiers,
  bounded classes; Python 3.11.5 is the floor): the memory graph's version
  test (`ego_anchor._VERSION_RE`, exponential: a subject of "0.0", thirty
  letters and "!" took minutes), the forged-fence filter
  (`prompt_fence._FENCE_TAG_RE`, quadratic over every fetched page; an
  opener with no ">" is redacted too), the provider address's version test
  and its "/v1/v1" trim (`normalize_provider_url`), the attachment-name
  scan (`extract_active_attachments`) and the problem report's e-mail
  scrubber (`problem_report._EMAIL`). Gate: `tests/test_regexes_stay_linear.py`
  (the old patterns' answers on random inputs, their growth as the control).
  Measure before changing a flagged pattern: the schedule parser, the bare
  host and file-path patterns were linear on their real input.
- **Smaller ones:** maps keyed by server frames in the turn view are
  prototype-free (`Object.create(null)`; a turn id of "__proto__" answered
  `Object.prototype`, `tests/js/test_turn_view.js`); ids the web pages make
  come from the browser's cryptographic source on plain-http pages too
  (`window.kazmaRandomId`, `tests/js/test_random_ids.js`); the Kuwaiti
  tokenizer's emoji class is the emoji blocks (a copied range took Arabic
  presentation forms, CJK and Hangul, `tests/test_tokenizers.py`); a new
  restic passphrase file is restricted before it is written
  (`tests/test_restic_password_file_restricted.py`); Kazma Watch's report ids
  draw every letter evenly (`newId`, rejection sampling); two address checks
  compare host names exactly (`tests/test_url_host_checks.py`); the test
  servers find a free port on loopback, and the document broker's port probe
  skips an address with no host. Second pass (2026-11-16): a backup's name
  from a request is rebuilt from its number before a path is made
  (`universal._backup_dir_name`: the old match let a trailing newline
  through), and the `*_KEY` env-name rule is two plain checks instead of an
  overlapping pattern (`tests/test_codeql_followups_2026_11_16.py`, the old
  check and pattern as controls).

### 67. Secrets in files, copies and masks (2026-11-15)

Found by the defensive check before the independent security review: a
rewritten `.env` lost its owner-only restriction, backups and bundles copied
secret files readable by `Users`, URL passwords under most keys stayed in
plaintext, and maskers missed token shapes Kazma itself holds.

- **One owner-only writer.** `security/owner_only.py` (standard library; the
  guard loads it by path, so there is no second copy) replaces a file's whole
  access list with this account and reads it back;
  `file_access.restrict_to_owner` is True only when `readable_by_others` then
  finds no one (`icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r` kept other accounts'
  explicit entries). `file_access.write_private` is the one raw writer of a
  secret file (made empty, restricted, filled, renamed, checked again); env
  files go through `env_files.set_env_values` / `write_env_text`, copies
  through `copy_private`. Gate: `tests/test_env_files_written_one_way.py`
  (the old writers and a planted one as controls); behaviour:
  `tests/test_secret_files_owner_only.py`.
- **Copies stay private.** Backups and restores restrict every file
  `store_registry.holds_a_secret` names (`restrict_secret_files`); backup
  archives and migration bundles are made by `create_private` or not at all
  (`ExportRefused`). `kazma migrate export` writes to `~/kazma-bundles` by
  default, never inside a git checkout, and says the bundle holds the vault
  key; `kazma-bundle-*.zip` is ignored by git.
- **A URL password goes to the vault under any key**
  (`config_store._secret_vault_name`: `cfg:<key>` when install-scoped, else
  the install-scoped `cfg-url:<key>`, so background readers find it, §38;
  nested values such as `providers.list[].base_url` too; `acquisition.`
  journals are read back raw and excepted). Upper-case `*_KEY` names are
  secrets for vaulting, masking and MCP. Gate:
  `tests/test_url_passwords_vaulted.py`.
- **One table of token shapes** (`security/token_shapes.py`: Slack, Discord,
  Google, Meta, JWTs, Kazma API tokens, Hugging Face, GitLab, AWS...), read by
  every redactor and masker (`errors.redact_secrets`,
  `url_credentials.mask_urls_in_text`, `mask_deep`, settings backups, the
