  pg argv, `/config export`); linear patterns. `mask_deep` masks URL
  passwords inside text; `approval_args.SECRET_WHEN_NAMED` hides
  `config_save`'s value when its key is secret, and Bearer tokens are masked
  on every card. Census gate: `tests/test_token_shapes_masked.py` (the
  form maskers that post their value back are declared: a masked token would
  be saved as stars).

### 68. What OpenSSF Scorecard reads, held (2026-11-16)

Kazma's first Scorecard run scored 5.7 (published at scorecard.dev, badge in
both READMEs). Each check Kazma can meet is now met and held by a gate:

- **Token-Permissions**: a workflow is read-only and a job names the writes
  it needs (`release.yml` granted four to the whole workflow);
  `tests/test_workflow_permissions.py` refuses a write at the workflow level.
- **Pinned-Dependencies**: every pip install in CI and the images comes from
  uv.lock with `--require-hashes`, Kazma itself editable with `--no-deps`
  and the locked build backend (`--no-build-isolation`):
  `.github/actions/install-locked` (inputs `extras`, `groups`,
  `only-groups`) in every job, `uv export` in the Dockerfiles (uv from its
  image, pinned by digest). What a job adds beyond an extra is a
  `[dependency-groups]` group (`ci-light`, `build`, `lint`, `scan`,
  `fuzz`): locked, never installed by `uv sync`, never published. CI thus
  tests the versions users get (an update installs the locked ones, §50); a
  new version reaches CI as a uv.lock update. The shipped-wheel job installs
  the locked set, then the wheel with `--no-deps`. Gate:
  `tests/test_installs_pinned_by_hash.py` (Scorecard's own pip rule, every
  workflow, composite action and Dockerfile; the old lines as controls);
  `tests/test_major_versions_held.py` holds the lock below each held major.
- **SAST**: CodeQL runs from `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` (default setup is
  switched off: GitHub refuses both), with default setup's categories
  (`/language:<name>`) so alerts and dismissals carry over.
- **Fuzzing**: `fuzz/fuzz_*.py` are Atheris targets (Linux, Python 3.12+,
  group `fuzz`) over the code that reads outside text: the data fence, the
  secret maskers, the Telegram converter, shell_exec's command reading, the
  Arabic search fold, the MCP sign-in challenge. Each states its invariant in
  `check(data)`; `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` runs each 45 s on every push
  (300 s weekly) and keeps a breaking input; `tests/test_fuzz_targets.py`
  runs every `check` on seeds and generated inputs on every platform (a
  fence without its sanitiser, a maskerless redactor and a raw converter as
  controls). A new parser of outside text gets a target. Their first run
  found two bugs, both fixed: `documents.arabic.fold_for_search` was not a
  fixed point (a mark after a removed tatweel composed only on a second
  fold; it now folds to a fixed point, `KB_FOLD_VERSION` 2 refolds the
  Knowledge index), and `telegram_format.md_to_tg_html` misnested
  overlapping bold and italic (`***x***` -> `<b><i>x</b></i>`, refused by
  Telegram; `_balance_style_tags` re-nests them).
- **Vulnerabilities**: `osv-scanner.toml` lists exactly the advisories
  `dependency_scanner.REVIEWED_ADVISORIES` reviews as unreachable (GitHub
  id with the package first, PyPI id naming it), and `docs/osv-scanner.toml`
  the docs site's build-only ones, each with the version the lock holds.
  Gate: `tests/test_osv_scanner_ignores.py` (a planted ignore and a stale
  version as controls). Remove an entry when its package moves past it.
- **Coverage** (Codecov, 2026-11-16): `.github/workflows/coverage.yml` runs CI's suites
  again under coverage.py -- the unit suite, the Postgres-marked tests on a real Postgres, the
  browser suites, the recovery drills, the document worker's container profile and the
  Temporal path -- each job uploading under its own Codecov flag, merged into one report.
  `.github/actions/coverage-setup` measures every Python child a job starts (`patch =
  subprocess`, absolute sources: the reload drill's server runs in another folder);
  `.github/actions/coverage-upload` combines and uploads with GitHub's OIDC token
  (`use_oidc`; no Codecov token is stored). They measure and never gate: CI's jobs are the
  gates, and tests that check a child's exact environment see coverage's variable there.
- **Not met, on purpose or not yet**: Code-Review, CI-Tests and
  Branch-Protection count pull requests and their reviews (the owner pushes
  to `main`); Signed-Releases rises as `release.yml` signs new releases;
  Contributors needs other organisations; CII-Best-Practices is 5 at
  "passing" (silver 7.5).

### 69. The SonarCloud review of 2026-11-16

SonarCloud reported 1,623 open issues. Every one was read against the code:
448 were real, 908 false positives (most: `sqlite3.Row` read by column name,
Alpine bindings Sonar cannot evaluate, taint "sources" that are the
operator's own command line) and 267 by design. The real ones, each fixed
with a test that fails on the old code and a gate for its class:

- **shell_exec never runs Kazma's own command line, nor `ps`.** The
  development allowlist (KAZMA_PRODUCTION unset: the default after setup)
  added `kazma`, whose `migrate export` writes the vault and its key into a
  bundle and whose `restore`/`import` replace stores, and `ps`, whose `eww`
  prints the server's environment. `shell_paths.NEVER_ALLOWED` names the
  programs no mode may allow (shells, interpreters, `env`), read against the
  allowlist's source. Gate: `tests/test_shell_exec_kazma_files.py`.
- **A model server's address has one rule**,
  `security.ssrf.check_model_server_url`: this computer or the owner's
  network (`resolves_to_own_network`), else a public address; never cloud
  metadata or link-local. `GET /api/models?base_url=` and `/v1/models` passed
  `allow_private=True`, which returns before every check, so a link the
  signed-in owner opened (a GET carries the cookie) fetched
  `169.254.169.254`; both routes are admin-only now
  (`platform_rbac._ADMIN_EXACT`, exact paths: `/api/models/options` stays
  open). The `KAZMA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_LLM` opt-in is gone. Settings sent the
  provider's key in the address; it is a header. Gate:
  `tests/test_model_server_address_rule.py` (no product code passes
  `allow_private` other than False; no page script puts a key in an
  address).
- **The release job runs only locked tools.** sigstore and cyclonedx-bom ran
  through `uvx`/`uv run --with`, pinning the tool and resolving its
  dependencies fresh in the job that holds the signing identity; they run
  from uv.lock's `sign` and `sbom` groups (`uv run --frozen --only-group`).
  Every `uv build` (release and CI) takes uv.lock's `build` group as
  hash-checked build constraints. Checkout keeps no token
  (`persist-credentials: false`); only the tag push gets it. Gates:
  `tests/test_installs_pinned_by_hash.py` (`uv_problems`: uvx, `uv tool`,
  `uv run` without `--frozen`/`--locked` or with `--with`, `uv build`
  without hashed constraints), `tests/test_release_supply_chain.py`.
- **Kazma Watch's toolchain comes from its lock.** `kazma observer setup`
  ran `npx --yes wrangler@X` (wrangler pinned, its dependencies not) with
  the owner's Cloudflare login and the Worker's secrets. It installs
  `deploy/observer/package-lock.json` (shipped in the wheel) with `npm ci
  --ignore-scripts` in its work folder, once per lock, and runs that copy
  (`npx --no-install wrangler`); Dependabot watches the lock.
  `watch_setup.WRANGLER_VERSION`, package.json and the lock name one
  wrangler (`tests/test_watch_setup.py`).
- **The image leaves out what git leaves out**: `.keys/`, `*.pem`, `*.p12`,
  `*.pfx`, migration bundles, `*.local.yaml`, a `kazma-data/` at any depth and
  the memory repair copies (`tests/test_dockerignore_secrets.py`).
- **OIDC**: the discovery document must name the configured issuer (OpenID
  Connect Discovery 4.3), the id_token is held to that issuer, and PyJWT's
  key fetch runs in a thread (`get_signing_key_from_jwt` is a loop-stall
  helper; `tests/test_oidc.py`).
- **A cancel reaches the code that asked for it** (python:S7497). The
  telemetry and swarm task streams turned a request's cancel into a normal
  end, and `kazma ask --acp` answered "cancelled" to Ctrl+C and kept serving
  while `asyncio.wait` left the turn running; the ACP prompt now cancels its
  tasks and both re-raise. Gate: `tests/test_cancel_not_swallowed.py`: every
  handler of `asyncio.CancelledError` re-raises, sits in one that does, or is
  declared (file, function) with why ending normally is what its canceller
  wants (an owned loop task, a swarm run that records its ending).
- **Correctness found with it** (`tests/test_sonar_correctness_2026_11_16.py`,
  each through the real code, every one failing on the old code): the memory
  backfill made its registry with no settings store, a TypeError at DEBUG, so
  every CLI backfill skipped belief extraction (`backfill_v2._backfill_client`;
  gate: every `initialize_model_registry` call names its store); two packages
  listed names in `__all__` they never defined, so `import *` raised (gate:
  every `__all__` names what its module defines, or a submodule); the SQLite
  graph backend called itself available whatever happened and left a
  connection open per read; the dialect detector gave text with no dialect
  marker MSA at confidence 1.0, English included (now 0.5, formal MSA phrases
  raising it to 0.8); the raw settings `transaction()` rolled back only on
  `Exception`, leaving a cancelled one open on the shared connection; the
  gateway's lifespan stopped nothing when the app ended with an error.
- **Hardening** (`tests/test_sonar_hardening_2026_11_16.py`): no product
  `cmd /c` takes a value Kazma did not write and quote (the restore cleanup's
  `rmdir` and the WAL archive's `mkdir` read an `&` in a path as a second
  command; Python removes and makes them now, taking ownership only for what
  a plain removal left); no source file holds a raw direction-control
  character (Trojan Source; vendored files declared); GitHub's naming rules
  hold every owner and repository a `/repos/` path is built from
  (`routers.github.github_names_ok`: a repository's remote URL could name
  `..`); `recall(conn=...)` gives a plain connection the row factory for the
  call and back after. Also: `--` and `--end-of-options` before the values
  two scripts pass to pg_restore and git, the images install wheels only
  (`--only-binary :all:`), the Settings restart closes its log file, and the
  lifespan's cancelled teardown is no longer logged as "completed".
- **A slow pattern on outside text is fixed, not run in a thread.** Python's
  `re` holds the GIL for the whole match, so a slow match in `to_thread`
  stalls the event loop as much as one on it; only a child process contains
  it. Measured and fixed: the fork-bomb deny pattern every `shell_exec`
  command met before its card (9 s on a 1,204-character command), the code
  span reader of a `generate_pdf` body line (`image_refs`: two single-pass
  functions now), every WhatsApp and Telegram reply's heading, link and image
  patterns, the render-resource check (`documents/resources.py`, each
  reference type scanned on its own; it also let a Markdown image through
  after an HTML `src=`), the skill-manifest and secret scans, reminder
  timings, memory notes, the web chat's Markdown, and the rest of the
  reviewer's list. Gates: `tests/test_sonar_regexes_linear.py` (each new
  pattern's answers equal to the old one's on random input, any intended
  difference tested; hostile input fast; the old pattern's growth as the
  control) and `tests/test_regex_sweep.py`: every `re.*("literal")` in the
  product packages runs in a child process against inputs built from its own
  characters, and one that grows faster than its input fails unless declared
  with why its input is bounded or contained (a planted quadratic and
  exponential pattern as controls; a declared pattern no longer in the code
  fails).
- **Log lines cannot be forged** (113 issues, one class). Every record passes
  `_LogQueueHandler.prepare`, which now makes it one line: CR, LF, the other
  control characters, DEL, U+0085 and U+2028/2029 are written as visible
  escapes and traceback lines after the first are indented, in every format
  (`logging_config.FORMATTERS`, the file following `logging.format`, the
  console always plain). The readers -- the daily digest, the weekly targets,
  the weekly report, the finished-turn line -- read through one module,
  `observability/log_lines.py` (`read_app_line`, `read_guard_line`,
  `opens_with`), and match a marker only at the start of the parsed message;
  a guard signature reads only the guard record's `event`. A logged value
  could fake a failed turn, a "ran without asking" entry, a day of fresh
  backups or the firings of the backup and restore-drill jobs, in the default
  JSON format too; `/ws/chat/{id}` logged its decoded id before refusing an
  unsigned handshake (it logs `%r`, cut). Gates:
  `tests/test_log_lines_cannot_be_forged.py` (hostile values through the real
  handler in every format, the unsigned handshake as witness, a plain
  formatter as control), `tests/test_log_readers_read_markers_at_the_start.py`
  (every marker after a prefix counts nothing; the readers of the commit
  before as control; no `.search`/`in` on a message in the reader modules).
- **Every control on every page has a name** (479 issues: labels written
  beside their control with nothing tying them). 172 labels gained `for` and
  their control an `id` from its `x-model` path; unnamed controls an
  `aria-label` from the catalog (EN/AR); group captions are
  `fieldset`/`legend`; toggles nested in a second label take the page's
  `toggle-row` shape; switches carry their platform's or provider's name;
  the import chips work from the keyboard; the Swarm dialogs are dialogs and
  close on Escape. Nothing looks different (full-page screenshots compared).
  Gates: `tests/test_controls_have_accessible_names.py` (every page rendered
  through the app; a control named only by its placeholder, or not at all, an
  orphan or nested label, a missing or duplicated `for` fail; planted shapes
  as controls) and the accessibility-tree check of the page tour
  (`tests/e2e/test_pages_load_clean.py`, every page and Settings tab, its own
  negative control).
- **A system program linked out of the tool path still runs** (found the same day: GitHub's
  `ubuntu-latest` became Ubuntu 26.04, where every coreutils program in `/usr/bin` links
  into `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/`). `post_hitl.resolve_shell_binary` refused any
  program resolving outside a tool-path folder, so shell_exec ran no `ls`, `cat` or `sleep`
  there; it now also takes a target root owns and no one else may write, all the way up
  (`_root_owned`; a link to a file another user could change is still refused). Gate:
  `tests/test_shell_binary_resolution.py` (POSIX). CI's Postgres is 18 (26.04's `pg_dump`
  writes `SET transaction_timeout`, which 16 refuses; live runs 18).
- **The report says what is product code**: `.sonarcloud.properties` marks
  the suites, the fuzz targets and the Worker's tests as test code and leaves
  out vendored libraries, examples and the audits' evidence scripts. Marking
  the false positives that remain is done in SonarCloud with the owner's
  account.
- **The second pass, BLOCKER and HIGH (2026-11-21)**: 20 open issues, each
  read against the code.
  - **A ContextVar's default is never an object a caller can change**
    (python:S8508): `ContextVar(..., default={})` makes ONE dict that every
    context which never set the variable shares, so a write into what
    `.get()` answered outside a recall would reach every later recall.
    Recall's member names (`recall._ENTRY_NAMES`) default to None and are
    read through `recall._entry_names()` (an empty mapping nothing can
    write). Gate: `tests/test_context_var_defaults_immutable.py` (every
    `ContextVar(` in the product packages and `scripts/`; the old declaration
    and the old default's leak as negative controls).
  - **The backup folder's Test** (pythonsecurity:S2083 x4): the folder the
    admin types is written to by design; reading its rules found device
    paths taken for folders, a second name of the data folder taken for
    another place and a save that kept a path with an unnamed refusal code,
    all fixed (section 21 F, `tests/test_backup_folder_path_rules.py`).
  - **A return value no caller reads is dropped**: `self_improvement._update_soul`
    answers nothing (python:S3516; its three callers count in their own
    *change*). `setup-engine.sh` uses `[[ ]]` throughout: setup runs it only
    as `bash -s` (shell:S7688).
  - Judged safe, for the owner to mark: WinZip AES's fixed algorithms in
    `security/sealed_zip.py` (S4790, S5344, S5542), the operator's own
    command-line arguments in `kazma migrate` and `scripts/` (S8705, S8707),
    and two S3516 whose one returned object is built or edited before it is
    returned (`research_pipeline._candidate_report_roots`, an
    `atomic_update` updater in `space_data._erase_settings`).

### 70. Spaces: the foundation (`kazma_core/spaces/`, 2026-11-17)

Several people on one Kazma (`docs/plans/SPACES_PLAN.md`; its "State of the
items" table says what is done). A space's id is the stores' `tenant_id`.
Stage 1's foundation is in; Spaces is NOT enforced, and the one switch
that turns it on (S1-33, below) is refused until its preconditions hold, so
an install with one account behaves as before.

- **The scope is space and asker, bound together** (`spaces/scope.py`):
  `bind_scope(space_id, asker)` binds both and the tenant ContextVar;
  `install_work(reason)` declares work of the install, which reads no
  space. `require_scope` / `require_space_id` answer the bound scope; with
  nothing bound they answer the owner's scope only while the install does
  not enforce Spaces, and raise `NoSpaceBound` once it does.
  `tenant_isolation.require_tenant_id` asks them. Never catch `NoSpaceBound`
  to fall back to `default`, and never write a new `or "default"` for a
  tenant: the ratchet in `tests/test_no_space_no_data.py` counts the ones
  left and only goes down (the four left are in `memory/recall.py`, which
  the memory session holds, since 2026-11-22). A stored record that names
  no space is read with `scope.space_of_record` (written before Spaces: the
  owner's, N19). A parameter some caller leaves out resolves with
  `scope.space_named_or_bound`: the owner's while Spaces is off -- what
  such code wrote before, so nothing moves -- and the bound space once it
  is on. Not `require_space_id` there: while Spaces is off it answers the
  ambient tenant and refuses inside `install_work`, which would move rows
  today. Work of the install or the machine that needs the owner's space
  names `OWNER_SPACE_ID` and says why. Enforcement is one stored switch
  (`identity.ENFORCED_KEY`) kept in memory (`scope.spaces_enforced`): asking
  for a space reads no settings.
- **The identity store** (`spaces/identity.py`): accounts, spaces and
  memberships in one document (`identity.REGISTRY_KEY`) changed only by
  `update_registry`, one `atomic_update` per change. The owner
  (`scope.OWNER_ACCOUNT_ID`, the one admin) and the owner's space
  (`scope.OWNER_SPACE_ID`, `default`) are always in it; an install with one
  account stores nothing. The older multi-user mode's users are accounts:
  `platform_rbac._load_users_from_store` reads them and every change goes
  through `platform_rbac._update_users` (one atomic step). Nothing outside
  `platform_rbac` calls `_save_users_to_store`. A personal space has one
  member forever; an unreadable store raises `IdentityUnavailable`, never
  "no accounts". Its functions are loop-stall helpers.
- **Every store declares its space rule** (`store_registry.SPACE_RULES`:
  `row`, `folder`, `install`, `derived`, `host`, what it does today, its
  content columns), and **every route its scope** (`kazma_ui/route_scopes.py`:
  `install`, `space`, `account`, `open`). A new store or route with neither
  fails `tests/test_store_space_rules.py` / `tests/test_route_scopes.py`.
- **A sign-in is an account, or none** (`kazma_ui/space_binding.account_of`):
  the shared secret, an API token and the loopback auto-login are the
  owner's account; a local user's session is that user's; an OIDC session
  is none (refused once enforced).
- **The page names its space on every call** (`static/js/space_scope.js`:
  header `X-Kazma-Space`, or a `space` query value), and the tenant
  middleware checks membership every time, before the handler
  (`space_binding.space_for_request`; 403 `not_a_member`, one answer for a
  space that does not exist and one the caller is not in). The space is the
  tab's, never the session's. **Only on an install that enforces Spaces**:
  elsewhere the page names nothing, reloads nothing and remembers nothing
  (it reads `<meta name="kazma-spaces-enforced">`), and the server runs a
  request that names exactly the tenant it would run in anyway as before
  Spaces; any other named space still needs membership. The older
  multi-user mode's users and OIDC sign-ins are members of no space: as
  first written, a page named the space it was rendered for and every call
  after its load was refused (found in review, before any merge). A test of
  a request rule drives the page's own flow: page load, then a call naming
  the rendered space. **A page that names no space is drawn, an API call
  is not** (`space_binding.must_name_its_space`, 2026-11-18, the first run
  of the two-tab browser test): a GET outside `/api/` and the sockets is
  drawn for the person's own first space, and `space_scope.js` loads it
  again for the space the tab remembers. The sidebar's soft navigation
  drops `?space=` from the address, so a reload refused with 400 left the
  tab unable to get back to its space. **With no sign-in at all** (sign-in
  off) there is no account to check: once enforced, a space route that
  names another space is refused, never answered from the owner's space
  (S4-03 refuses sign-in off at boot once a second account exists). Gates:
  `tests/test_web_request_space.py` (the middleware, and `create_app()`'s
  `/chat`; the old rules as controls).
- **A turn runs in its thread's space** (`spaces/threads.py`,
  `thread_scopes.db`): a thread is recorded once with its space and opener,
  and `turn_segment_budget` binds the turn's scope from the record. Every
  graph run sits in that block (`tests/test_turn_scope_bound.py`). A turn
  whose entry point bound no tenant keeps none bound (the vault tells "no
  tenant" from `default`).
- **The matrix** (`tests/_space_matrix.py`, `tests/test_space_matrix.py`):
  every `space` route and every agent tool has a case, or names the plan
  item that adds it. A new one with neither fails. An item registers its
  cases in a module named in `CASE_MODULES` (Documents:
  `tests/_document_space_cases.py`, run with Spaces enforced, the real router
  behind the real tenant middleware, engines stubbed) and lowers
  `PENDING_BASELINE` in the same change.
- Gates: `tests/test_identity_store.py`, `tests/test_no_space_no_data.py`,
  `tests/test_sign_in_is_an_account.py`, `tests/test_web_request_space.py`,
  `tests/test_turn_scope_bound.py`, `tests/js/test_space_scope.js`, each
  with the old behaviour as its negative control.
- **Chat state follows the space (S1-08, 2026-11-18).** A guard refuses
  only where Spaces is enforced; a stamp (a row's space, a message's author)
  is always written. Never refuse, or move a stored value, on an install
  that does not enforce Spaces.
  - **The thread's record decides for everything kept by thread**
    (`spaces/threads.py`): `thread_home` is the record's space, and the
    owner's for a thread from before Spaces (N19); `thread_refusal` and
    `require_thread` refuse work bound to another space. Work that bound
    nothing (a sweep, the start pass) acts for the thread and is not
    refused. A new store or reader keyed by thread asks them.
  - **Checkpoints** (`kazma_gateway/stores/checkpoint.py`, `_open`): once
    enforced the saver is the THREAD's, whoever asks: a read of another
    space's thread is "no checkpoints", a write raises
    `ThreadInAnotherSpace`. On Postgres every space then uses the one
    table, and a listing or a clear goes thread by thread
    (`_filters_by_thread`). Not enforced: the bound tenant's saver, as
    before.
    On one shared table a listing is held to the space's threads by its own
    statement, before its limit, and a listing or a clear asks the record
    store once (`threads.space_threads`: the owner's space is every thread
    no other space recorded, N19).
  - **Time Travel** steps are kept by id alone. Restore and fork ask
    `thread_rewind._in_this_space`, and a fork's thread is recorded
    (`threads.record_new_thread`) before anything is written under it. A
    record store that fails is the refusal `thread_record_unavailable`
    (503, a WARNING), and a fork bound to no space once enforced is
    `no_space`; each refusal code is worded on the chat apps and the Time
    Travel page. A chat delete of an id the space's store does not hold
    deletes nothing more (`_not_this_spaces_chat` in `sse_chat`). A deleted
    chat's record is removed last, and only when nothing of the chat is
    left: not when its checkpoints, its steps or (the Dashboard's delete)
    its chat could not be deleted, or no checkpoint store was there to ask
    (`threads.forget_thread`).
  - **A step's space** is `scope.space_of_state(state)`: the state's own
    tenant while Spaces is not enforced (a receipt's identity is hashed
    from it, so it must not move), the bound scope's once it is. Drafts,
    the scratchpad and receipts use it; a plan (`task_ledger.py`) is read
    and made only through a thread of its own space. Every read of a
    thread's record remembers its space (`threads.record_of`), so a guard
    a turn's own code asks on the loop reads no store.
  - **Sockets** name their space like any request:
    `space_binding.space_for_socket` checks membership at the handshake of
    `/ws/chat/{session_id}` and `/ws/voice` (close 4003 with the refusal's
    code) and `space_binding.bound_to` binds it. A live-voice room is its
    space's (`routes_voice._livekit_room`: the owner's keeps its name), and
    so is an A2A task or conversation (`a2a_api.py`).
  - **Messages name their author.** `reply_sink.authored` stamps `author`
    (the bound account) on a user's row; history and the `user_message`
    frame add `author_name` for another member only where Spaces is
    enforced (`space_binding.other_authors`, off the loop), and the page
    shows it (`_otherAuthorName` in chat.js; the page's own account is
    `<meta name="kazma-account">`).
  - Gates: `tests/_chat_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases: the product's
    routers behind the real tenant middleware), `tests/test_chat_state_spaces.py`
    (each guard taken out must fail its case on its own assertion, never a
    stand-in's error; the checkpoint store on one shared table, "the shared
    table reads across" as the control, and on real Postgres; Time Travel
    through the product's own `CheckpointManager`; drafts, notes and
    receipts against the tenant an older checkpoint left), `tests/js/test_message_author.js`,
    `tests/e2e/test_two_tabs_two_spaces.py` (two tabs in two spaces, by the
    sidebar, EN and AR).
- **Memory: the space is the tenant, always (S1-09, 2026-11-18).** As
  S1-08: a guard acts only where Spaces is enforced, a stamp is always
  written.
  - **One rule for who sees every tenant** (`memory/tenant_view.py`:
    `sees_every_tenant`, `narrowed_to`, `ledger_reach`): Kazma's own work
    (no tenant named) always; the owner's tenant `default` only while Spaces
    is not enforced; any other tenant never. Once enforced, `default` is the
    owner's personal space: its own rows, its own forget ledger, its own
    About me. Memory code never compares a tenant with the literal `default`
    (the class gate in `tests/test_memory_default_is_a_space.py`; a
    comparison that means something else is declared there).
  - **The mode setting is retired.** Only `shared` can be saved. A stored
    `per_platform` or `per_user` is honoured while Spaces is not enforced
    (`config.legacy_tenant_mode`) and ended from Settings ("Use one
    memory"); enforced, `resolve_tenant_id` answers the bound space.
  - **A turn's memory tenant is `scope.space_of_state(state)`** in the graph
    nodes, Time Travel and the rewinds; never `state.get("tenant_id") or
    "default"`.
  - **An episode's id carries its space** (the owner's decision 17: `id`
    stays the key, no table is rebuilt). `dual_write.episode_ids` and
    `swarm_bridge.bridge_episode_ids` give today's id and the other form:
    plain for the owner's tenant, salted with the tenant for every other.
    The writer picks the id inside its transaction (`_id_in_tenant`): the
    one the turn is already stored under, else one no other tenant holds.
    Code that finds a turn by id asks for both forms together with the
    row's tenant (recovery, the history import).
  - **A writer names its tenant or asks the scope**: the tool-outcome
    recorder reads `require_space_id()` on the caller's thread, the swarm
    bridge and `import_history` when none is passed; with Spaces enforced
    and nothing bound, nothing is written for the owner.
  - **The worker**: `worker_bootstrap.memory_tenants()` is every tenant that
    holds memory plus every space, the owner's first, and raises when it
    cannot be read; the cadences that visit every tenant list them through
    `worker_bootstrap._queue_per_tenant` alone (a failed listing is a
    WARNING, queues nothing and writes no stamp). A queued task's binding is
    `task_queue._task_binding`: not enforced, the payload's tenant when it is
    not the owner's, as before; enforced, the task runs whole -- its space
    (the payload's tenant, or its row's for `ROW_NAMED_TASKS`) and the
    account it acts for -- or as the install's work (`INSTALL_TASKS`). A new
    task type goes in exactly one of `TENANT_TASKS`, `ROW_NAMED_TASKS`,
    `INSTALL_TASKS`. A memory sweep names the tenant of each row it touches
    and asks for no scope. The deep pass is queued for the id the writer
    returned, never a recomputed one. **A turn's tasks run as the person the
    turn was for** (the S2-05/S2-07 second review: they ran as the space's
    maker): `post_turn_memory` and `micro_consolidation` (`_PERSON_TASKS`)
    bind `identity.work_scope(space, person)` -- the payload's `asker` (the
    deep pass carries it), else `said_by`, else the episode row's
    `metadata.said_by` (`task_queue._person_of`) -- so the person's models
    and limit apply. The deep pass (`_PERSON_MODEL_TASKS`) waits, put back
    with no attempt spent (`_MemoryWorker._put_back`), while they are
    disabled or past their daily limit, and is not run for a person who
    left the space (their message is still written, as Kazma's own work).
    Gate: `tests/test_memory_tasks_bind_their_person.py` (the maker's
    binding as the control).
  - **No row under the "no tenant" sentinel** (`schema_v2.NO_TENANT`,
    triggers on every table with a tenant column, both files). The operator
    trail records the space the request acted in (`request.scope["kazma_space"]`,
    left by the tenant middleware).
  - **Recall** holds its episode candidates to the asker's tenant
    (`recall._own_episodes`) before anything reads one by id; a database
    error there rises, and recall says it failed.
  - **A statement that picks a memory row by id alone** names its tenant in
    the same WHERE, `(? IS NULL OR tenant_id = ?)` with
    `tenant_view.narrowed_to` (nothing filtered on an install that does not
    enforce Spaces), or is declared (S1-35): `tests/test_memory_id_only_statements.py`
    is a gate, its `DECLARED` table naming each function, how many such
    statements it holds and why another tenant's row cannot be reached -- a
    row the same work chose by tenant, recall's candidates held by
    `recall._own_episodes`, a queued task that names its own row, Kazma's own
    sweeps, the mirror. A new statement fails, in a declared function too.
    The ones that take an id from a request or the model -- the Memory page's
    edit, undo, invalidate, detail and recall trail, Forget of a memory, a
    fact's source and a weekly summary -- name it themselves: the route's
    check before them was the only thing keeping another space's row out
    (`tests/test_memory_id_scoped_statements.py`, each with the check taken
    away and the statement without its tenant as the control).
  - **Memory outside every space** (a tenant of the retired modes) is
    counted in memory health (`tenant_view.tenants_outside_spaces`), never
    merged. Memory's copies outside the data folder declare a space rule
    (`memory_stores.EXTERNAL_SPACE_RULES`).
  - Gates: `tests/_memory_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases),
    `tests/test_memory_default_is_a_space.py`, `tests/test_memory_spaces.py`
    (each rule with the old behaviour as its control).
- **Lessons (the Soul) are per space (S1-10, 2026-11-18).**
  - `self_improvement.soul_space(space)` is the one answer to "whose Soul":
    the owner's, always, on an install that does not enforce Spaces (one
    Soul, whatever tenant a turn runs for); enforced, the space named or
    bound, and `NoSpaceBound` when there is none (nothing is read or learned
    for no one). The owner's space keeps `self_improvement.agent_evolution`;
    every other space's Soul is inside `self_improvement.space_evolution`
    (`{"spaces": {id: {"agents": ...}}}`). Every change of a Soul is one
    `atomic_update` with the read inside the updater
    (`self_improvement._update_soul`), under `_agent_evo_lock` for this
    process: read before it, another process's lesson written meanwhile was
    lost. Every reader and writer of a Soul takes `space`.
  - **Learning**: `learn_from_finished_turn` passes the turn's tenant
    (`_post_turn_memory.tenant_id`, which `respond_node` sets from
    `space_of_state`) down to `apply_agent_mutation(space=)`. Once Spaces is
    enforced the background task binds a whole scope: the turn's space and
    the person the turn ran for, else `spaces.identity.acting_account` --
    the one answer to "who does Kazma's own work for a space act for" (the
    queued memory tasks use it too), so the refiner's own memory search
    reads that space. Not enforced: the context `close_turn` handed it, as
    before.
  - **Reading**: on every install the supervisor adds a turn's lessons at
    its first step, one current fenced copy (§11): the one Soul, or once
    enforced the lessons of `space_of_state(state)`.
  - **Forgetting**: `forget_text` and `forget_lessons_from` take the
    tenant; with none (Kazma's own replay) they read every Soul.
  - **A held lesson** (`mint_soul_commitment(space=)`) is a commitment of
    its space; the confirm queue's routes act only on a `soul_delta`
    commitment of the request's space (`commitment_api._lesson_here`) that
    is still held: confirm and reject move it only from `needs_confirm`, in
    the same UPDATE (`update_status(..., expected=)`); a decided one answers
    409 `not_held` (an applied lesson was "rejected" while it stayed in the
    Soul, and a second confirm applied it twice).
  - Gates: `tests/test_lessons_per_space.py` (the real hand-off and the
    real supervisor graph; the single Soul as each control),
    `tests/_lesson_space_cases.py`.
- **Documents follow the space (S1-12, 2026-11-18; §19 B4b and B4c).** The
  asker in its space on every surface, the refusal of chat and the agent
  lifted where Spaces is enforced, each space's files in its own folder once
  it is (the root keeps every tenant's copy in this release, for a revert).
- **The Knowledge Library follows the space (S1-13, 2026-11-18).** Guards
  act only where Spaces is enforced; the older multi-user mode keeps its
  refusal (`knowledge_lifecycle.kb_refusal`), and work bound to no space is
  refused once enforced (`NO_SPACE_REFUSAL`).
  - **A library's id is its space's**: `knowledge._library_id_in_space` -- the
    owner's ids never change, every other space's are `slug.<8 hex>` (a slug
    never holds "."), and the Chroma collection name keeps the "." apart.
    `KnowledgeStore.own_library_id` resolves an id for a lookup and
    `library_id_for` for a new library; **every route, tool and `/kb`
    resolves once and uses the answer** (a check of `get_library(x)` then a
    read of `x` reads another space's library). A new entry point that takes
    a library id does the same. **Every name built from an id** (the Chroma
    collection, the fetched-pages folder, the soak's copy) comes from
    `knowledge.library_name_part`, which keeps the mark: as "_" it made a
    space's library and an owner's of the same text one folder.
  - Reads keep to the space (the store's tenant filter is on whenever Spaces
    is enforced); `publish_page` writes only into a library of the bound
    space (`_writing_space`). Maintenance lists every library through
    `all_library_ids` / `library_space`, never the filtered reads.
  - The crawl journal is the install's: once Spaces is enforced the routes
    show a space the crawls of its own libraries (`kb_api._own_libraries`,
    keyed on `spaces_enforced()`, never the store's tenant filter, which
    production mode turns on too); a crawl a restart cut off resumes in its
    library's space (`kb_api._in_the_crawls_space`; one whose space cannot
    be read waits for Resume, the others go on); the canary runs as the
    owner's space on its private store.
  - A quota per space (`_SPACE_QUOTA_BYTES`, `KnowledgeSpaceFull`) beside the
    install's file quota, an admission check like it. `space_used_bytes`
    reads on a connection of its own, never under the store lock, and a
    measure answers for `_SPACE_BYTES_TTL_S`.
  - Gates: `tests/_knowledge_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases),
    `tests/test_knowledge_spaces.py` (each guard taken out as a control).
- **Scheduled follows the space (S1-14, 2026-11-18).** Guards act only where
  Spaces is enforced; the older multi-user mode keeps its refusal
  (`cron.single_operator.scheduled_refusal`), and work bound to no space is
  refused once enforced (`NO_SPACE_REFUSAL`).
  - A job carries its space (`tenant_id`) and the account that booked it
    (`ScheduledJob.creator`, always stamped). Every Scheduled read and change
    keeps to the caller's space (`scheduler._tenant_scope`); another space's
    job id answers as an unknown one.
  - A fire runs as a whole scope (`scheduler._fire_binding`): the job's space
    and its creator, else `identity.acting_account`. A job whose tenant is no
    space of the install does not fire (`no_space`).
  - **Only the owner's own jobs use the owner's address.** Until people link
    their own chat apps (S3-05) every address a job can deliver to is the
    owner's, so a booking by anyone else is refused
    (`scheduler.NO_OWN_ADDRESS`, code `no_own_address`) and a job that would
    act for anyone else does not fire. S3-05 lifts it; never lift it by
    sending a member's job to the owner's chat.
  - A job takes a sibling's address only within its tenant
    (`sibling_delivery_target(thread_id, tenant_id)`).
  - **What a job says and when it runs again are its person's** (S1-14
    review): only the account the job fires as may give it a new prompt,
    Run it again, make it recurring, or change its time while it fires
    (`CronScheduler._not_theirs_to_change`: `not_yours`, 403). Anyone else in
    the space may only move a pending one-off to another one-off time. In a
    shared space a member's words, or a daily recurrence, would otherwise
    reach the owner's chat as the owner. Such a change is made only to the
    job it was allowed for (S1-16 follow-up, `CronScheduler._change_rule`):
    the write pins the version read and `update_job(pending_only=True)`
    answers `conflict` when a fire began meanwhile -- a claim keeps the
    version.
  - **The fire's binding is inside its `try`**: an identity store that
    cannot answer because the database is away gives the claim back at the
    same occurrence (`_hold_for_identity`, reported to the database watch),
    and while the database is away the poll holds reminders too once Spaces
    is enforced (who a reminder fires as is in the database). Any other
    failure to read it (a registry that is not a mapping) fails the fire
    once (`identity_unavailable`), never a claim and release every pass; a
    locked SQLite settings file is held the same way, without being an
    outage (`_sqlite_lock_passes`, S1-16 follow-up). The
    missed path asks the same fire rule: a job that would not fire is
    recorded missed and queues no notice (`mark_missed(refused=)`).
  - Gates: `tests/_scheduled_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases, a member of
    a shared space among them), `tests/test_cron_spaces.py` (each guard
    taken out as a control).
- **The swarm follows the space (S1-15, 2026-11-18).** Guards act only where
  Spaces is enforced; the older multi-user mode keeps its refusal
  (`swarm.single_operator.swarm_refusal`), and work bound to no space is
  refused once enforced (`NO_SPACE_REFUSAL`).
  - A task carries its space and the person who asked (`metadata`
    `tenant_id` and `asker`, stamped at admission: once enforced the
    admitting scope overwrites what the task arrived with,
    `SwarmEngine._stamp_whose`). **Whose task it is is Kazma's to record**:
    every key the swarm reads from a task's metadata is declared a request's
    or Kazma's own (`swarm.task_metadata`: `REQUEST_KEYS`, `KAZMA_KEYS` --
    whose task it is, where it came from and where its result goes, what its
    worker may do, how a run ended), and the dispatch route refuses a request
    naming a Kazma key (400 `metadata_set_by_kazma`, nothing recorded or
    run). A new key the swarm reads is declared in one of the two or the
    gate fails (`tests/test_swarm_task_metadata.py`). Every list, task,
    stream, action and the export keep to the caller's space
    (`single_operator.task_of_this_space`; the task store's list filter
    names the bound space, `"*"` is Kazma's own work); another space's task
    answers as an unknown one.
  - **A worker runs as its task's person**: `worker_dispatch._worker_scope`
    binds `identity.work_scope(space, asker)` (the asker while still a
    member; a task whose asker left is refused, `identity.AskerLeft`, never
    run as the space's acting account, the S2-12 review; a task of no space
    runs nothing). A worker usually inherits the dispatching request's scope;
    the binding is what holds for a task run with nothing bound (a pipeline
    resumed after a restart, the durable path), a hand-off target and its
    approval's resume. A sub-agent runs in its spawner's scope. The scope is
    resolved once, before the worker's breaker is asked
    (`worker_dispatch._scope_or_refusal`): a task of no space, or an identity
    store that cannot answer (reported to the database watch), is refused
    there and never counts against the breaker every space shares.
  - **A worker serves every space**: its log lines and last task carry
    their space (`mark_dispatched(space=)`, `logs_for`) and are shown in it
    only (`services._kept_to_space`). A worker's lessons are the task's
    space's (`self_improvement.worker_lessons`, kept under
    `worker:<name>` in that space's Soul, never in the registry prompt every
    space shares); the registry prompt's own lessons were learned before
    Spaces and are shown in the owner's space only
    (`worker._prompt_in_this_space`).
  - A bus approval records the space and the person that asked
    (`shared_approvals` `space` and `asker`, the gate row's tenant); the Web
    page shows it only in that space. **Only the person who asked answers**
    (decision N4, `single_operator.answered_by_caller`): a task's approve,
    reject, cancel and retry and its worker's approval are refused to anyone
    else (403 `not_yours`); another member of a shared space sees them. The
    check is the shared action's, `task_actions.task_refusal` (S1-16
    follow-up): the page's routes and the run supervisor's buttons ask the
    same one, so a retry never takes a member's task into the caller's space
    through the admission stamp, and work bound to no space acts on no
    task's (`no_space`). **Who may act on a task is decided by its kind, in
    one place** (`task_actions.caller_may_act_on`, S1-17 follow-up): a
    research task (`metadata.kind` `research`) follows N32 on every route
    -- its author or the space's owner -- and any other task N4, on the
    Research page's routes too. The Swarm page held every task to N4 and the
    Research page every task to N32.
    **Someone else's card and result stay off the owner's chat apps** (O1,
    `single_operator.for_the_owner`): until people link their own chat apps
    every one is the owner's, so a request that does not act for the owner
    is never posted to the bus (`safety._kept_in_its_space`: it waits on its
    row, answered in its space) and a chat app's button never decides it;
    its result goes to neither the output target nor a chat
    (`chat_delivery`). Delivering a request to its asker (the bell, Web
    Push) is S2-05's. An identity store that cannot say whose a result is
    holds it (`single_operator.wait_for_owner_answer`, through an outage, up
    to `OWNER_ANSWER_WAIT_S`): the owner's is never dropped; an approval
    whose person cannot be read answers 503 and stays pending. That wait is
    never the request's: once Spaces is enforced a foreground dispatch
    answers once its task is done and hands the result over in the
    background (`routes_tasks._hand_over_result`, S1-17 follow-up: the
    page's request hung through an outage); not enforced, the hand-over
    stays in the request, as before. A failure of the dispatch or of the
    result's routing sends its safe message either way
    (`routes_tasks._reported`, one handler for both).
  - **The swarm's writes stay the admin's in every mode** (dispatch, a
    task's actions, an approval's decision) until feature grants give the
    swarm to others (S2-11); the install's swarm, read -- workers' totals and
    breakers, the output target -- is the admin's once enforced
    (`route_roles.INSTALL_READ`). The agent's `dispatch_swarm` follows the
    routes' rule once enforced (`single_operator.swarm_write_refusal`: open
    with sign-in off, the owner only with it on).
  - Gates: `tests/_swarm_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases),
    `tests/test_swarm_spaces.py` (each guard taken out as a control; the
    unscoped dispatch as the control for a task run with nothing bound; the
    review's forged dispatch with both layers out; a shared space of two;
    a real worker's real tool call), `tests/test_swarm_task_metadata.py`.
- **Research follows the space (S1-16, 2026-11-18).** Guards act only where
  Spaces is enforced.
  - A research session carries its space (`ResearchSession.tenant_id`,
    always stamped from the bound scope). A space's list holds its own
    sessions, the owner's space also those from before Spaces (no tenant).
    Every route and tool that names a session asks
    `research_session.session_here` (another space's answers as an unknown
    one); never `get_session` where a request names the id. Once enforced,
    work bound to no space makes no session (`NoSpaceBound`: it became the
    owner's), and a session records its author (`asker`, always stamped).
  - **Shared research is read by every member and changed by two**
    (decision N32, the S1-16 follow-up): its author and the space's owner
    archive, restore, delete, cancel or resume it; another member reads it
    (403 `not_yours`). One rule, `spaces.shared_work.may_change`, for a
    session (`research_session.session_to_change`, every route and tool
    that changes one) and a research task (`_task_to_change`, archive and
    delete alike). A task's rule is its kind's on every page
    (`task_actions.caller_may_act_on`): a swarm task reached through the
    Research routes follows N4.
  - **A chat's web search is one row per question, per space, per person**
    (`_chat_search_key`): the owner's keeps the ids it had (12 hex digits of
    the question); every other key starts with `s` and hashes the space, the
    person and the question together, so no question of the owner's shares
    an id with another space's. A row of another space under an id is a
    miss, never written (`_row_is_this_spaces`).
  - A research task is a swarm task of kind research: it keeps to its space
    as every swarm task does (S1-15; the research routes' `_find_task`).
  - The research files (reports, papers, extracts, digests, a saved page, a
    crawl's pages, the pipeline's files, the acquisition journal) are the
    workspace folder's and wait for S1-19, the space folder.
  - Gates: `tests/_research_space_cases.py` (the matrix cases),
    `tests/test_research_spaces.py` (the unfiltered list as the control,
    and each other guard taken out; a shared space of two, any member
    changing shared research as the control; the review's crafted
    collision; a session for no one as the owner's as the control).

- **A mailbox and a calendar belong to a space (S1-17, part a,
  2026-11-18).** Guards act only where Spaces is enforced; one account
  behaves as before. Parts b (X) and c (GitHub) follow.
  - **One rule for a connected account's names**
    (`kazma_core/spaces/connected_accounts.py`): the owner's space keeps
    today's vault names and the process environment, so the owner's existing
    connections stay where they are (N26); every other space keeps its own
    under `space:<id>:<name>` (install-scoped in the vault, so a refresh with
    nothing bound reads the space it was told), and its environment values in
    the vault too (`space:<id>:env.<VARIABLE>`). `connected_space()` is the
    bound space once enforced, `NoSpaceBound` with none: a connection is never
    looked up for no one, nor the owner's lent to it.
  - **Every mail and calendar secret and environment value goes through
    `email_manager.credentials`** (`vault_retrieve`, `vault_store`,
    `vault_delete`, `cred`, `account_env`, `set_account_env`). The install's
    app registration -- the Google and Microsoft client ids and secrets, the
    Microsoft tenant, Kazma's own address -- is the install's in every space
    (`_INSTALL_NAMES`, `_INSTALL_VARIABLES`). The extra-accounts list is
    `email.accounts` for the owner's space and `email.accounts_by_space`
    (CREDENTIAL in `settings_restore`: S1-28 carries it) for the others. The
    mail presets and the two app-registration routes are `install` routes.
  - **A member connects their space's own accounts** (the review of
    S1-17c, N26): once Spaces is enforced, the mail and calendar routes,
    GitHub's token, sign-in and disconnect, and X's credentials (the OAuth
    1.0a keys, the app's Bearer token and OAuth 2.0 client), Sign in with X
    and Disconnect (the owner, 2026-11-18: "Yes, per space") need membership,
    not admin (`platform_rbac._connects_a_spaces_own_account`, checked before
    the X rule and the admin prefixes; a member is an operator); the
    install's pieces stay the admin's -- the mail presets and app
    registrations (held equal to `route_scopes`' `install` routes), the
    GitHub App and a clone -- and so do X's reply bot policy and resuming X
    after a stop (continuing authority). What publishes on X is unchanged:
    the always-ask card, N4, O1, a draft seen before it is published. Not
    enforced, every one is the admin's, as before. The matrix's mail, GitHub
    and X cases put the auth middleware's role check (`auth._role_refusal`,
    the one rule the middleware applies; `Matrix.role_checked`) in front of
    the routers: they mounted the tenant middleware only, and no case met an
    admin-only route a member could not reach. The page a member connects
    mail, calendar and X from is S1-23's (Settings is the admin's today).
  - **A sign-in finishes in the space it started in**: `oauth_attempts.begin`
    records the bound space and person, and a callback binds them back
    (`kazma_ui.oauth_sign_in.attempt_scope`); an attempt of no space, or of a
    person no longer a member, is refused (`no_space`, worded in both
    languages); one whose membership cannot be read (the database away) is
    the refusal `identity_unavailable`, never a 500 (S1-17 follow-up). X's
    and GitHub's callbacks bind theirs (parts b and c).
  - **The practice mailbox and calendar are each space's** (S1-17
    follow-up): `sandbox_emails.db` keys a message by space and id
    (`backends/sandbox.py`; a file from before is rebuilt once, every
    message the owner's), and the in-memory practice calendar is one per
    space (`calendar.router._sandbox_instances`). One mailbox for every
    space put member A's sent mail in member B's Sent folder.
  - **The background connector check goes space by space**
    (`connector_health.check_connectors`): each space's grants are refreshed
    in that space; only the owner's space raises the owner's alerts.
  - Gates: `tests/test_connected_accounts_spaces.py` (two spaces, two
    mailboxes; a refresh writes only its own; the source gate -- no mail or
    calendar module reaches the process environment or the vault itself, and
    no other module names their secrets but the declared offsite backup and
    settings restore; each with its control), `tests/_mail_space_cases.py`
    (19 routes and 12 tools; with the space names taken out, the cases fail).

- **An X account belongs to a space (S1-17, part b, 2026-11-18).** Every
  X key and row was already kept per tenant (`x_api.ownership.x_config_key`,
  `tenant.<t>.connectors.x.*`; the stores "apart"), and a space is a tenant.
  Guards act only where Spaces is enforced; one account as before.
  - **The tenant X work is under is the bound space**
    (`ownership.x_tenant_id`, a tenant bound by older code naming its space
    as `require_space_id` reads it): work bound to no space reads no X
    account (`NoSpaceBound`) -- it read the owner's.
  - **The owner's environment and legacy names are the owner's space's**:
    the OAuth 1.0a keys from the environment, the legacy vault names
    (`x_api_key` ...: the same names in every space, and the vault's read
    still falls back from a space to a global row, for any name -- so a
    global copy of one answered every space; read now for the owner's space
    only. A space's own names, `tenant.<space>.connectors.x.*`, are its
    alone: a global row under one could only come from its own write) and
    `X_BEARER_TOKEN` (`auth_tokens.bearer_from_env`: another space spent the
    owner's X API budget). Source gate: no other X code reads the
    environment but Kazma's own switches.
  - **Background X work runs in its row's whole scope**
    (`ownership.x_work_scope`, resolved off the loop: the space and the
    account its own work acts for, as every queued work): a booked post, its
    receipt, a projection repair, the legacy schedule's migration and fire,
    the mention poller (the owner's space: it answers the owner's account).
    A row of no space does not run -- with the tenant alone bound it was
    sent: a booked post is held for review, a legacy post marked failed.
    Whose row it is that cannot be read for now (the database away, a
    locked file: `ownership.identity_failure_passes`) waits for a later

  - **Another space's X notice stays off the owner's channels** (O1,

    the address its booking captured nor to the chat apps

  - Gates: `tests/_x_space_cases.py` (every X route, the X page, the

    call to X carrying the asker's keys), `tests/test_x_account_spaces.py`
    (each rule with its control; the source gate with a planted read).
- **A GitHub sign-in belongs to a space (S1-17, part c, 2026-11-18;
  decision N26).** Guards act only where Spaces is enforced; one account as
  before.
  - **The owner's space keeps today's sign-in**: its stored tokens, the
    install's GitHub App (its installation token acts on the owner's
    repositories) and `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_PAT` in the process

    read the owner's environment, App, or a global vault row an older
    install keeps.

    space). One function hands out the App's token in the git tools,
    `_owners_app_token`, and every caller of `get_app_installation_token` /
    `mint_app_installation_token` asks the space first, or is declared (a
    gate, the old retry as its control). The GitHub tools refuse before any
    request in a space with no account (`_no_account_here`; the owner's
    space as before). A token saved in another space never reaches the
    process environment (`bind_github_token_to_process`, owner's only), the

    search read the environment's token for the owner's space only.
  - **Sign in with GitHub finishes in the space it started in**: the
    callback is open before sign-in, so with no binding it ran in the owner's

  - **Disconnect deletes** (`clear_oauth_token`, `oauth_revoke`): it wrote
    the keys empty, the settings store refuses to blank a stored secret, and
    Disconnect cleared nothing (the bug X's Disconnect had; found on the
    way). It deletes every copy the vault keeps (`forget_github_keys`,

    install-scoped, and the settings store's delete reached the request's

    that fails answers 503 `disconnect_failed`, never "disconnected" (the

  - **The GitHub client reads its token off the loop**: `GitHubClient()`
    with no token is a loop-stall helper; async code makes it with
    `await GitHubClient.of_this_space()` and the tools in a thread.
  - Left: the repository the routes and tools act on is still the install's
    active workspace (`resolve_repo`, S1-19 and S1-20); the commit author
    (the bot's name and email) is the install's.
  - Gates: `tests/_github_space_cases.py` (every GitHub route and the five
    tools: A with nothing connected sends no token, the tools refuse; then A
    connects its own and every request carries it alone; B and the owner
    keep theirs -- 18 of 23 fail with the space rule taken out),
    `tests/test_github_account_spaces.py` (each rule with its control; a
    source gate on the environment -- any shape naming the variable but the
    one reader's and the owner's binding -- and on the sign-in's keys --
    each key constant handed to `github_key` -- each with planted shapes).
- **The vault has a space scope (S1-18, 2026-11-19).** Guards act only
  where Spaces is enforced; not enforced, the vault is exactly as before.
  - `security.vault.secret_scope(name)` is the one answer to whose a name
    is: the install's (`INSTALL_SCOPED_SECRETS`, which stays; the offsite
    backup's passwords; every `cfg:` settings secret that is not a space's
    connected account, until S1-23 classes settings) or a space's (a name
