    owner's space's, though the install list still stores them as one row;
    only the app registration is the install's
    (`connected_accounts.INSTALL_ACCOUNT_SECRETS`, the one list). Work with
    no space that uses the owner's grant binds the owner's space
    (`cloud_sync._as_the_owners_space`).
  - A space's secret is returned only to work in that space
    (`SecretVault._scopes_to_read`): another space, and work with no space
    bound, get None. No `default` rung (`retrieve_scoped` asks the same
    rule). A row with no tenant is the owner's space's (N19). The caller's
    space is the bound scope's first (`_callers_space`: the mail code pins
    the tenant to none while its scope stays bound).
  - A secret is never written for no one (`NoSpaceBound`) nor for a space
    its name does not carry (`VaultScopeError`), and the settings store
    refuses such a save: it never keeps the secret as plaintext instead
    (`config_store._vault_scope_refusals`).
  - A list, a delete (`every_scope` too) and the divergent-duplicate scan
    keep to the caller's space; a drill that must judge every row uses
    `sample_opens`. No product code passes a tenant to a vault call
    (`SecretVault.for_space(id)` is the declared way).
  - A new vault name read by the install's own work with no space bound goes
    on the install list, or it reads None once enforced.
  - Gates: `tests/test_vault_space_scope.py` (the old read as each control),
    `tests/_vault_space_cases.py`.
- **A space's files live in its own folder (S1-19, 2026-11-19).** Guards
  act only where Spaces is enforced; not enforced, every folder and the
  machine's workspace are as before.
  - `kazma_core/spaces/files.py` is the one home: `space_dir(id)` is
    `<data dir>/spaces/<id>/`, with `files/` (the working folder),
    `attachments/`, `images/`, `documents/`, `exports/`
    (`space_folder(kind, install=)`). The owner's space keeps the install's
    folders and the machine's workspace (a mapping, not a move). A new
    writer of a file asks `space_folder`, never `data_dir() / "<folder>"`.
  - **A sandboxed space cannot leave its folder.** `resolve_active_root`'s
    first rung is `sandboxed_files_root()`, and `check_path_access` allows
    only paths inside the space folder (`path_policy._space_home`): no
    durable root, session grant, absolute-path switch or skill folder.
    Enforced with no space bound, the policy opens no file; a space whose
    kind cannot be read raises `SpaceKindUnknown` (never "host").
  - **Nobody opens another space's folder, the owner included** (O1):
    `store_registry.in_another_spaces_folder` is part of `is_kazma_store`,
    so every door refuses a path inside `spaces/<other>/` (the machine's
    workspace can hold the data folder: on live it does). A database or
    `.env` in a person's `files/` is theirs (`_a_persons_files`).
  - An upload or shared-file id resolves only in the space that holds the
    file. `python_exec` never uses the machine's own Python in a sandboxed
    space (`local_exec_forbidden`). The install's one browser page belongs
    to the space that opened it: another space's call closes it first
    (`browser_automation.tools._page_space`).
  - Research files follow the working folder; the acquisition status shows a
    space its own journal jobs only (`research_panel.routes._jobs_of_this_space`).
  - Gates: `tests/_files_space_cases.py` (every tool that takes a path or
    writes a file, with B's file, the owner's file and climbing paths),
    `tests/test_space_files.py` (each rule taken out as a control).
- **Host tools exist only in a host space (S1-20, 2026-11-20).** Guards act
  only where Spaces is enforced; not enforced, every tool is offered and runs
  as before.
  - `kazma_core/spaces/tools.py` holds every tool's group: `DEVELOPMENT`,
    `ADMIN`, `SPACE`, `OUTSIDE`. A new tool goes in one of them or
    `tests/test_host_tools_absent.py` fails; a tool in no group (an MCP
    server's) is `development`.
  - `host_allowance()` is the one rule: a sandboxed space has no host tool;
    the owner's space has the admin tools, and Development's while
    `identity.holds_development` (N28, on at first); a shared space with a
    project folder has Development for each person who holds it and never
    the admin tools (S2-12, piece 3); no space bound, none.
  - Applied at the offer (`skills.switches.offered`, a swarm worker's list,
    both through `offered_here`) and at the call
    (`LocalToolRegistry._execute_inner`, `UnifiedToolExecutor`'s MCP
    branch). A new place that offers or runs tools asks it too: hiding alone
    is never enough.
  - The Development routes (`route_scopes.DEVELOPMENT_ROUTE_RULES`) are
    refused by the tenant middleware where Development is not (403
    `host_only`); the sidebar's Workspace and IDE entries sit inside
    `{% if development_here() %}` (no read while drawing). A new Development
    page or route goes in the rules. A page that is not Workspace or the IDE
    asks a Development route only after reading the flag its page was drawn
    with (the chat page's `#chat-root` `data-development`): the chat page
    asked `/api/workspaces` on every load, two or three 403s in a sandboxed
    space, and main's browser job failed on Linux from 2026-11-20
    (`tests/test_development_routes_asked_where_offered.py`, the old chat
    page as the control; `tests/e2e/test_two_tabs_two_spaces.py`).
  - A clone builds its environment with `security.git_auth.clone_env`:
    outside the owner's space, none of the machine's credentials.
  - **Work on the machine acts as the admin** (`kazma_core/spaces/machine.py`,
    2026-11-20): once enforced `kazma ask`/`acp` and `kazma mcp` bind the
    owner's account in the owner's personal space, or in a space they name
    (`--space`) that the owner is a member of (`machine_space`, read off the
    loop in async code); any other space is refused before anything runs.
    The terminal app's and the CLI's calls name the owner's personal space
    (`local_api.auth_headers`). A new entry point that runs work on the
    machine binds the same way.
  - Gates: `tests/test_host_tools_absent.py` (controls: a policy that only
    hides the tool, the route rule taken out, the clone environment as it
    was), `tests/_host_tools_space_cases.py`,
    `tests/test_machine_work_acts_as_the_admin.py` (nothing bound and a call
    naming no space as controls).
- **Running work and approvals carry their space (S1-21, 2026-11-20).**
  Guards act only where Spaces is enforced; not enforced, every surface lists
  and acts as before (the older multi-user mode keeps its refusal).
  - `kazma_core/runs/spaces.py` holds the rules: `visible_here` (a run or
    incident of the space bound now; none with no space bound),
    `kept_in_its_space` (O1: news of a space other than the owner's stays
    off the install's channels), `may_act` (its asker or an owner of its
    space, `spaces.shared_work.may_change`), `runs_refusal`.
  - **Every run carries `space` and `asker`** (`contract.Run`), stamped by
    its adapter from the kind's own record: a thread record, a swarm task's
    metadata, a job's tenant and creator, a document job's tenant and actor,
    a research session's columns, a crawl's working folder
    (`spaces.files.space_of_folder`) or library, an X operation's tenant, a
    memory task's payload. Empty is the install's own work and work from
    before Spaces: the owner's space's (N19). A new adapter names `space=`
    on every `Run(` (gate; `maintenance.py` is declared install work).
    Adapters read every space's runs (the swarm with the task store's `"*"`
    once enforced; a chat turn's title inside its thread's own space).
  - **The registry keeps a surface to the bound space**
    (`list_runs(everyone=False)`); the supervisor alone reads `everyone`.
    `perform` refuses another space's run ("gone") and anyone but its asker
    or an owner of its space (`not_yours`, 403); a kind's own control may be
    stricter (a swarm task answers only its asker, N4).
  - **Incidents carry `space` and `asker`** (columns added to an older
    file); `recent(space=)` and `live(space=)` keep a surface to its space,
    a row with none being the owner's. The supervisor opens another space's
    incident with `notify = suppressed` (`KEPT_IN_ITS_SPACE`), `deliver` and
    the recovery and diagnosis notes refuse it as a second line, the bell
    shows the bound space's, and the runbooks step only on the owner's
    work, as the owner. Delivering a member's incident to them is S2-05's.
  - `/api/runs` answers in the bound space; a member decides on their own
    space's incidents (the admin rule stays while not enforced). Chat apps'
    `/runs` and a card's button refuse until their chats are bound to a
    space (stage 3).
  - **An approval gate names whose work asked**: `GateRow.asker` (column
    added to an older file), stamped by `register_gate` from the bound
    scope, and its tenant from the bound space when the writer named none.
    The pending list was already per space (the chat store, a bridge gate's
    tenant); an MCP server's sampling request is shown only where
    Development is. Only the asker answering is S2-05's.
  - Gates: `tests/test_gates_and_runs_spaces.py` (the unfiltered listing,
    today's supervisor paging a member's stuck X post with its words, and
    the decision path without its space checks as controls),
    `tests/_runs_space_cases.py`.
- **Model calls name their space and asker (S1-22, 2026-11-20).**
  - The per-call ledger stamps each row with the scope bound where the
    call was made (`llm_ledger._whose`, read in the caller's own context by
    `arecord_llm_call`): a turn's, a scheduled fire's, a swarm worker's.
    Kazma's own work and a call with nothing bound name nobody. Columns
    `space` and `asker` are added to an older file; rows from before name
    nobody. A new model call site needs no argument: it is made inside the
    work's scope, or it is Kazma's own.
  - `llm_ledger.spend_by_person(since)` is the admin's view (N11: spend and
    counts, never a text): `GET /api/dashboard/spend-by-person` (admin), the
    Dashboard's "Spent today, per person" card, shown once two people have
    spent or Spaces is enforced (an install with one account sees the page as
    before).
  - **The trace feed keeps to its space**: a `TraceEntry` carries `space`
    and `asker` (stamped by `TraceStore.add` from the bound scope; a trace's
    details are the start of a turn's prompt); `TraceStore.recent` and
    `stats` take the space shown (`tracing.shown_space`, `tracing.view`:
    every one, asked the old way, while Spaces is not enforced), per-space
    totals are kept, and a socket registered for a space is sent that
    space's entries and totals only. The Agents page and API, the Dashboard's
    trace list and totals, and `/ws/dashboard` (membership checked at the
    handshake, `space_binding.space_for_socket`) show the bound space's; the
    Agents page counts the running turns of its space.
  - Gates: `tests/test_ledger_names_the_asker.py` (every call of a real
    turn, a scheduled fire and a swarm task; the ledger without the stamp
    and a call site with nothing bound as controls; a socket registered as
    before as the feed's control), `tests/_traces_space_cases.py`.
- **Settings in three areas (S1-23, 2026-11-20).** Guards act only where
  Spaces is enforced; not enforced, Settings and its saves are as before.
  - `kazma_core/settings_scope.py` holds every settings key's scope:
    `install` (the admin's), `space` (a space's own: its connected
    accounts, its chats' state, its Soul) or `account` (a person's sign-in
    and sessions). `_scope_of_key` is the one answer (the longest pattern
    decides; a key under `tenant.<id>.` is that space's). A new key goes
    under a rule there, or `tests/test_settings_scope.py` fails.
  - The install's own writers write install keys only
    (`install_writer_refusal`): Settings' generic and batch saves answer
    400 and `config_save` raises `RefusedBeforeEffect` for a space's or a
    person's key. Such a key is changed through its own route, in its space.
  - Settings is three areas, My account, This space and Install
    (`#settings-root`'s `data-areas`, `settings._settings_areas`). A member
    reaches `/settings`, their password and their sessions
    (`platform_rbac._reaches_own_settings`) and is shown My account and This
    space; Install, the API tokens and the platform users are the admin's
    and are not on a member's page at all. A new Settings tab is placed in
    an area (`settings_core.js` `_tabArea`).
  - Gates: `tests/test_settings_scope.py` (a planted key, the
    not-enforced save and a page built for everyone as controls),
    `tests/e2e/test_settings_areas_browser.py` (EN and AR, by the sidebar).
- **What reaches the admin carries no member content (S1-24, 2026-11-20).**
  Guards act only where Spaces is enforced, except the finished-turn line's
  `asker=`, which is always written.
  - Every log line at INFO or above that quotes someone's words goes through
    `kazma_core/observability/log_words.py` (`words_for_log`,
    `args_for_log`): once enforced it says how long they are, never the
    words. A new such line uses it.
  - The finished-turn line names the person by account id (`asker=`, read
    by `turn_line.read_turn_asker`). Once enforced the daily digest shows
    the turns by person, counts what ran without asking in a chat another
    person opened under that person (`daily_digest._others_chats`: never
    the chat's id or its tools), and counts other people's open problems by
    person; its own list is the owner's space's.
  - Langfuse gets only the owner's space's work once enforced
    (`KazmaTracer._to_langfuse`); the rest gets the console line.
  - Gate: `tests/test_admin_signals_hold_no_content.py` (a member's real
    turn, every INFO line, alert, the digest and the weekly report read for
    a planted word; the log's words as before, today's digest and every
    call sent to Langfuse as controls).
- **The admin boundary (S1-25, 2026-11-20).** Guards act only where Spaces
  is enforced; not enforced, the older user routes answer and there is no
  People tab.
  - The admin opens no space they are not a member of: the membership check
    (`space_binding.space_for_request`), never a role check, on every route
    and socket. A new way into a space's data asks membership too.
  - Settings' own writers write settings only
    (`settings_scope.install_writer_refusal` asks `settings_restore.classify`):
    the identity store and every other record of Kazma's are written by
    their own code, or the admin could add themselves to any space.
  - People (`kazma_core/spaces/people.py`, `kazma_ui/people_api.py`, Settings
    -> Install -> People): add (an account and its sandboxed personal space),
    reset (sessions end), delete (sessions end, every membership goes, the
    personal space stays closed, `account_deleted_at`, for S1-27). Every
    change is an event of the identity store's record, in the same step; the
    record is append-only (`identity.update_registry`) and hash-chained
    (`people.broken_at`). A reset is told to the person at their next page
    load, once (`/api/account/notices`, `account_notices.js`). The older
    mode's user routes refuse once enforced (`use_people_page`).
  - Gates: `tests/test_admin_cannot_open_a_space.py` (a role check alone
    and an untouched record as controls), `tests/e2e/test_people_page_browser.py`
    (EN and AR, by the sidebar; no tab without Spaces as the control).
- **A key per space; a space's secrets sealed with it (S1-26, 2026-11-21).**
  Sealing happens only where Spaces is enforced; an install with one account
  writes the rows it always wrote (no key, no sealed row, the same
  encryption).
  - **The keys live in the vault's file**, table `space_keys` (not the
    identity store, whose registry no longer holds the empty field): the
    salt, the wrapped keys and the rows they seal are one file, so a backup,
    a migration bundle and a restore carry them from one moment, and a
    Postgres restore of another date cannot part a space's key from its
    rows. A key is 32 random bytes named by a random id, wrapped with
    AES-256-GCM under a key derived (HKDF) from the vault's for wrapping
    alone, bound to its space and id; the `wrap` column says how, for the
    version where members hold it.
  - **Made when the space is made**: `identity.update_registry` keys every
    space a change added (`identity._key_new_spaces` ->
    `space_keys.ensure_keys`), best effort; a space without one gets it in
    the same transaction as its first sealed secret. **The owner's space has
    none** (decision N22: its secrets are not sealed again until stage 4).
  - **Which rows**: `security.vault.sealing_space` -- another space's
    secrets (a name that carries the space, or the row's tenant); the
    install's and the owner's keep the vault key. A sealed row names its
    key (the `key_id` column; NULL is the vault key) and **a read follows
    the id the row names**, enforced or not; a row whose key is gone, does
    not unwrap or is another space's raises `SpaceKeyMissing`, never opens
    with another key. In `vault.py` only `_open` opens a row and only
    `_seal` / `_reseal` seal one; a new statement that inserts a secret
    names `key_id`, one that selects a sealed value selects it too.
  - **Moves are explicit, checked and reversible**: `SecretVault.seal_space`
    (rows written before the space had a key), `unseal_space` (its inverse),
    `rotate_space_key` -- one transaction each, every value read back before
    it is written. Never on a read. `space_keys.report` is what the
    switch-on check (S1-33) reads.
  - **Erase** takes the space's keys with its rows
    (`SecretVault.erase_space`); the vault's connection zeroes deleted data
    (`secure_delete`) and the erase empties the write-ahead log. The restore
    drill's `vault:space_keys` check fails a backup whose sealed rows name a
    key it does not hold. The export is unchanged (N10's password seal;
    secret names only, never a key).
  - **Key care (S4-07, 2026-11-23).** A space's key can be changed
    (`space_keys.change_key`; `kazma spaces keys change SPACE` / `--all`,
    and `kazma spaces keys` lists key ids, never a key): its sealed secrets
    are sealed again with the new key, read back first, in one transaction
    (`SecretVault.rotate_space_key`), and its old keys are destroyed --
    deleted there, zeroed, and the write-ahead log emptied
    (`SecretVault._empty_the_log`, the erase's too; a reader that holds the
    log is said at WARNING). **A change never loses a secret** (the review
    of S4-07): it is refused, naming the rows (`SpaceKeyStillNamed`,
    `rows_elsewhere`), while a row that is not the space's own -- a name a
    later build classes elsewhere -- is sealed with one of its keys, and a
    key some row still names is never deleted; a row of the space that does
    not open refuses it too (`rows_damaged`), and `--all` reports that space
    and goes on. Recorded (`space_key_changed`). Refused for the owner's
    space, a space not held or erasing, the vault off. A deleted
    space's key is destroyed: the erase takes it, and the maintenance sweep
    "erased space keys" (`space_keys.destroy_erased_keys`) destroys again
    what an older vault file restored over the identity store brings back,
    for a space the record says was erased (`space_erased`) only. A running
    Kazma keeps an old key it unwrapped in memory until it reloads. Gate:
    `tests/test_space_key_rotation.py` (a change under the old key, a change
    that leaves the log, the change of before losing a real secret under a
    drifted name, and no sweep as controls).
  - What it does not do: the vault key wraps every space's key, so this
    keeps one space's secret from another's key, not from the person who
    runs the machine. Rotating the install's vault key is stage 4.
  - Gates: `tests/test_space_keys.py` (the single vault key opening both, a
    space made with no key, a read by the newest key, an unbound wrap, a
    build that seals without enforcement, a row-by-row move, the erase and
    the drill of before as controls; two source gates with planted shapes),
    `tests/test_backup_restore_spaces.py` (a real backup and a real
    migration: each space reads its secret back, sealed; a restored vault
    without its keys as the control).
- **Before a second person is let in (S1-33, 2026-11-21).** Spaces is still
  not on anywhere; this is the check and the refusal.
  - `kazma_core/spaces/preconditions.py` is the one table (`PRECONDITIONS`):
    work with no space is refused (`PROBES`, each called with nothing bound
    under `scope.as_if_enforced`, plus `TENANT_FALLBACKS_LEFT`, held equal
    to the S1-02 ratchet's baseline), one value per secret
    (`SecretVault.copies_that_disagree`), a daily limit per person and
    features per person (missing until the modules `_BUILT_BY` names exist
    and their own `precondition()` holds -- a module alone is not the rule in
    force, `preconditions._module_answer`: S2-02, S2-11), no plain copy of the
    backup leaving the machine (`universal.plain_copy_configured`, N10), the
    owner's API token for the deploy check (N15), a key per space
    (`space_keys.report`), and for the switch alone no account left by the
    older multi-user mode. A check that cannot be made is missing. A new
    precondition is a row there and a break in the gate's `BREAKS`.
  - **Who asks**: `people.create_person` for every new account (409
    `preconditions_missing`, each one named) and `preconditions.switch_on`,
    the only product code that writes `identity.ENFORCED_KEY`. A new writer
    of an account or of the switch fails the source gates.
  - **A function that answers "which space"** refuses with nothing bound
    once enforced and is added to `PROBES`. `safety.hitl.get_current_tenant_id`
    asks `require_space_id` (it answered `default`).
  - **The command** is `kazma spaces migrate`: `--check` and `--dry-run`
    run inside `read_only_diagnostic`; the move (`preconditions.apply`)
    copies the vault first, records each step in `system.spaces.migrate`,
    settles copies (`SecretVault.settle_copies`: the newest copy's value, no
    row deleted, each row kept under its key), keys and seals spaces, and
    makes the owner's token (`<install>/.kazma/owner_api.token`, one of
    Kazma's secret files; `scripts/deploy_live.py` signs in with it and
    falls back to the shared secret). `--switch-on` is refused while
    anything is missing. **Never run the move or the switch on the live
    install without the owner's word.**
  - **Tests take the preconditions as met** (the root conftest's
    `_second_account_preconditions_hold`); a test of them is marked
    `real_preconditions`.
  - Gate: `tests/test_second_account_preconditions.py` (each precondition
    missing alone; the switch stored by hand, an account made with no check
    and the old fallback as controls; planted writers for the source gates).
- **Count, export and erase one space (S1-27, 2026-11-20).** Only once
  Spaces is enforced (409 `spaces_off`); never the owner's personal space
  (`owners_space`); not yet on Postgres or with memory's Postgres copy
  (`postgres_not_yet`).
  - `kazma_core/spaces/space_data.py` walks every table of every `row` store
    (`store_registry.SPACE_RULES`) and finds the space's rows by its rule:
    `TABLE_RULES`, else a space column (`tenant_id`, `tenant`, `space`,
    `space_id`), else an FTS index its triggers keep, else its thread. A
    table with none refuses the count, the export and the erase (500
    `unknown_table`): a new table, or one the app makes at start, gets a
    rule in the same change (`keep` says why it holds no space's words),
    and so does a table a feature makes only when it first runs: the
    approval bus's `hitl_watchers` had none, and every count, export and
    erase refused on live's `hitl_gates.db`; the test world makes each such
    table by its own code (`tests/_space_world.py`).
    Settings, secrets (`SecretVault.erase_space`, whatever scope is bound)
    and libraries (`knowledge_lifecycle.delete_library`) go through their
    own stores; the space's folders after; then it leaves the identity
    store, recorded (`space_erased`).
  - An erase first closes the space (`people.close_space`: `erasing_at`, and
    `identity.is_member` is False for everyone); one that stopped half way is
    run again. Each store file's rows go in one transaction. A table whose
    trigger refuses every delete (the SQLite document job queue's
    `document_job_events`, in `documents.db`) has that guard lifted inside
    the erase's transaction and put back before it commits
    (`space_data._lift_delete_guards`): the erase failed "document job events
    are immutable" on such an install (CI, 2026-11-20). The test world makes
    the queue's tables by their own code
    (`test_an_append_only_table_is_erased_and_keeps_its_guard`, the erase
    without the lift as the control).
  - Who may (`kazma_ui/spaces_api.py`, from the memberships): the admin or a
    member counts (numbers only); the space's owner exports; an owner deletes
    a shared space; the admin erases the closed personal space of a deleted
    person and never exports a member's. An API token below admin does none
    of it (403 `own_sign_in_only`, in `_refusal`, 2026-11-24): every token is
    the owner's account, and an operator token moved the owner's shared
    space out, secrets included. The export is sealed with a
    password the person chooses (decision N10, `security/sealed_zip.py`:
    WinZip AES-256, at least 12 characters).
  - Pages: Settings -> This space -> This space's data; People lists the
    closed spaces with Erase.
  - Gates: `tests/test_space_export_erase.py` (a word planted in every table
    of A and of B; A's export holds A's only; erasing A leaves no column or
    file holding A's word, B whole; yesterday's erase that misses a store, a
    table with no rule and a Postgres copy of memory as controls),
    `tests/test_sealed_zip.py` (7-Zip and bsdtar open it with the password
    only, ZIP64 too; a big-endian counter as the control),
    `tests/e2e/test_people_page_browser.py` (EN and AR, by the sidebar).
- **Backups carry the identity store; a restore keeps spaces apart (S1-28,
  2026-11-20).** The universal backup, the Postgres dump and a migration
  bundle carry the identity store (a settings row) and the thread records
  (`thread_scopes.db`) with the stores: a restore keeps every chat in its
  space. Guards act only where Spaces is enforced.
  - The Settings file is the admin's (`settings_restore._held_by_another_space`):
    it holds no other space's `tenant.<id>.` keys and no other space's Soul,
    and a restore of an older file writes none (`kept.other_spaces`).
  - With a second account, no plain copy of the backup leaves the machine
    (decision N10, `universal._plain_copy_refused`): restic's encrypted copy
    only.
  - Gate: `tests/test_backup_restore_spaces.py` (a real universal backup and
    a real migration of two planted spaces, judged by a child pinned to the
    restored folder; a restore without the identity store, the Settings
    file of before and the plain-copy check of before as controls).
- **The docs say what Spaces promises and what it does not (S1-30,
  2026-11-20):** the threat model's first section and section 6, the safety
  design's section 10, and `docs/docs/guide/spaces.md`. Each says Spaces is
  not switched on in any release yet, keeps nothing from the person who runs
  the machine, and has not been reviewed independently;
  `tests/test_threat_model_accuracy.py` holds them to the code. **The
  identity store and the Spaces switch are written only by their own code,
  in every mode** (`settings_scope.install_writer_refusal`): before Spaces is
  enforced Settings' generic save wrote the switch (`identity.ENFORCED_KEY`), turning Spaces
  on before S1-33's checks. Gate: `tests/test_settings_scope.py` (the rule
  of before as the control).
- **The environment note is the space's own (S1-31, 2026-11-20).** In a
  sandboxed space `ide/env_context._sandboxed_space_note` names the space's
  folder by relative paths only, the Python policy and the tools the space
  has; never the install's workspace, data folder, repository, branch, MCP
  root, host shell or GitHub sign-in (a task naming a workspace, or a space
  whose kind cannot be read, is told nothing of the machine). The admin's
  space and an install without Spaces keep the note they always had. Gate:
  `tests/test_environment_note_per_space.py` (a real turn through the
  supervisor graph; a sandboxed space read as a host one as the control).
- **The bell, open problems and Running work are per person (S1-32,
  2026-11-20).** The acquisition monitor records each research and crawl
  notice's space (`web_acquire/monitor._crawl_space`; unreadable: shown to
  nobody, sent nowhere) and lists it only in its space
  (`monitor._shown_here`); another space's notice stays off the install's
  channels (O1). The install's own notices -- service alerts, requirements,
  advisories, the outside watcher -- are the admin's
  (`runs.spaces.install_notices_here`). Gate:
  `tests/test_bell_and_problems_per_person.py` (words planted in one
  person's topic and chat title, read through the real routes as everyone
  else; the lists of before as the control).
- **Each host space has its own root (S1-34, 2026-11-20).** Workspace rows
  carry their space (`space_id`; existing rows the owner's) and each space
  has its own active one; a switch or clone moves only its own space's, and
  only the owner's space moves the process pin and the MCP servers
  (`notify_root_changed`). `resolve_active_root` answers the bound space's
  active workspace; a host space other than the owner's with none works in
  its own folder (`spaces.files.host_space_root`), its file tools stay in
  its workspace (`path_policy._space_home`). The IDE service, code index,
  IDE undo and the MCP guard follow the root. Gate:
  `tests/test_host_space_roots.py` (one active row for the install as the
  control).
- **Who is "I" in a shared space (S1-11, 2026-11-20; the R3 study,
  N30 to N36).** `kazma_core/memory/speakers.py` is the one module that
  knows about members; everything else asks it.
  - **Which spaces file by member** (`speakers.room`): a shared space (no
    `personal_of`) once Spaces is enforced, from its first turn. A personal
    space, and every space while Spaces is not enforced, keeps the one
    `user` entry, and its rows are stored exactly as before (no `said_by`,
    subject `user`). An unreadable identity store raises: nothing is filed
    under a guessed member.
  - **Where a fact goes** (`Room.filed`): ``user`` (what the passes write
    for "I", as a subject or an object) is the speaker's entry
    `member_<account>`; a member's name, or one they are called by
    (`identity.set_called_names`), is theirs. A model never writes an entry
    (`belief_extractor._sanitize_belief`, the memory tools). With no speaker
    a first-person fact is not filed; the turn is still remembered.
  - **The speaker travels with the turn**: `respond_node`'s record
    (`said_by`), the post-turn thread and queue, the episode
    (`metadata.said_by`), the quick and deep passes, turn reconcile (the
    chat store's `author`), history imports, the memory tools. A new writer
    from a turn passes `said_by` (or the episode's `metadata`):
    `test_every_writer_from_a_turn_passes_its_speaker`.
  - **Whose words** (`Room.label`): another member's words about a member
    are `member_stated`, which never replaces that member's own (N34).
  - **One vector text** (`speakers.fact_vector_text`): a member's facts
    embed as `user <predicate> <object>` (the study's 4.3). No fact vector is
    built by hand (`test_one_text_for_a_facts_vector`).
  - **Recall reads a shared space for its asker** (`recall(asker=)`): their
    own facts and turns as `user` / `User:`, another member's under their
    name, a note outside the fence. Whose facts a question is about is
    chosen before ranking (`recall._whose_facts`: named first, then self
    first; `speakers.refers_to_asker` reads the first person, from the
    grammar: a three-letter imperfect, an object "me" on another person's
    verb and MSA "لديّ" are named apart); chosen after, another member's
    best match pushed the asker's own out by the gap.
  - **The speakers benchmark** (`benchmark_data/speakers.json`,
    `run_speaker_benchmark`) has its own ratchet (`thresholds.json`
    `speakers`, `scripts/memory_bench.py lock`); the study's vectors are
    replayed (`speakers_vectors.npz`).
  - **About me** is each member's own in a shared space
    (`memory_member_profile`, N31), with "Copy from my personal space".
  - **Forget** (N32, N33, N36): a shared turn is its author's and the space
    owner's to forget (`speakers.may_forget_turn`), a shared chat its
    opener's and the owner's to keep out; a fact about oneself another
    member stated goes, never filed from that message again
    (`metadata.not_again`), and Forget says the message stays
    (`forget.notes_for_forgotten_facts`); `forget.forget_entry` forgets every
    fact under an entry, journaled (kind `entry`).
  - **The notice** "Memory here is shared with ..." near the composer and
    on the Memory page (`static/js/shared_memory_notice.js`, N35).
  - Gates: `tests/test_memory_speakers.py` (each rule with its control),
    `tests/e2e/test_shared_memory_notice.py` (by the sidebar, EN/AR).
- **Each person's answers, settings and copies stay theirs (2026-11-21).**
  Guards act only where Spaces is enforced, except where a line says always.
  - **Web Push** (`kazma_ui/push.py`): every subscription records the
    account that subscribed it (`_account`, always stamped, from the
    request's sign-in). Once enforced a finished turn goes only to its
    thread's opener's devices (`_recipient`: the thread's record, the
    owner's for a thread from before Spaces), while they are still a member
    of the thread's space; a turn with no thread, or a device with no
    account, reaches nobody. `TurnBroker._push_terminal` hands its thread
    over. Gate: `tests/test_push_per_person.py` (every device, whatever the
    thread, as the control; nothing else reads the stored devices).
  - **An echo of every setting** (`settings_scope.echo_view`,
    `shown_in_echo`): Settings' `GET /api/settings`, `/config show` and
    `/config export` (`slash_commands._load_config`) and `config_read` show
    settings only -- never Kazma's own records (`settings_restore.classify`)
    -- and a space's key only in that space (`tenant.<id>.` is `<id>`'s, an
    unprefixed space key the owner's), a person's only to them; with no
    space bound, the install's alone. `config_read` answers `not_here`.
    Gate: `tests/test_settings_echo_per_space.py` (every product
    `.get_all()` is an echo through `echo_view` or declared; the echo of
    before as the control).
  - **One answer to "is a plain copy configured"**
    (`universal.plain_copy_configured`): the universal backup's copy while
    it is on, or a native provider set at all -- the Postgres WAL archive's
    segments and weekly base backups go to it whatever
    `backups.offsite.enabled` says. Every path that sends a plain copy asks
    `universal._plain_copy_refused` before anything leaves
    (`wal_archive._push_offsite` too). Gate: `tests/test_plain_copies_refused.py`
    (every upload to a provider and every rclone copy in product code asks;
    the push without the refusal and the rule of before as controls).
  - **A chat app works in the owner's space** (`spaces/chat_apps.py`):
    until each person links their own chat app (stage 3), the gateway's
    handler binds the owner's scope before it reads or builds anything of
    the chat (`chat_app_scope`, `_handler_body_in_its_space`), and a chat
    recorded in another space is refused with a reply. A chat-app command
    reading the owner's accounts (`/x`) runs in the bound scope
    (`chat_app_work`; before Spaces the owner's tenant, as it was). Gate:
    `tests/test_chat_apps_once_enforced.py` (the real handler on four
    platforms; no scope bound as the control; every tenant or scope the
    gateway binds comes from this rule or is declared).
  - **Research is each space's** (`tools/research_pipeline.py`): the papers
    index is per space (`papers_index_key`: the owner's keeps
    `research_pipeline.PAPERS_INDEX_KEY`, every other space's is under `tenant.<id>.`,
    so its count, export and erase reach it); the machine's other report
    roots (`KAZMA_WORKSPACE`, the default sandbox, the process folder) are
    the owner's space's only (`_owners_space_here`), every other space reads
    under its own root; a research job freezes its space in its policy
    (its `space`, read first by `runs.adapters.research._CrawlSpaces`,
    which the acquisition monitor uses too; a resume in another space is
    refused). Gate: `tests/test_research_papers_per_space.py` (one index for
    the install, the roots of before, the folder guess as controls).
  - **Only the owner's space runs code on the machine itself**
    (`code_exec.local_exec_forbidden`): every other space, and work bound
    to no space, a container or nothing, whatever the lab switch says.
  - **A URL password in a space's setting is that space's**
    (`config_store._secret_vault_name`: a `tenant.<id>.` key's goes under
    `cfg:tenant.<id>.`); `cfg-url:tenant.<id>.` is read as the same space's
    (`vault.secret_scope`, `_install_scope_rule`), and
    `vault.space_name_prefixes` is the one list of names that carry a space
    (erase, and the count and export's `space_data._vault_rows`). Gate:
    `tests/test_space_url_secrets.py`.
  - **Who may decide on a run incident is asked before anything is claimed**
    (`runs/decide._not_theirs`, every action, a dismissal and a diagnosis
    too); the run's own control is asked again by `registry.perform`.
    Gate: `tests/test_gates_and_runs_spaces.py`.
  - **A space's swarm approval rows go with it**: `space_data._settings_keys`
    reads a settings row that records its space
    (`_SPACE_RECORDING_PREFIXES`: `swarm.approval.`) beside `tenant.<id>.`
    keys and its chats' state. Gate:
    `tests/test_space_erase_takes_its_approvals.py`.
  - **A new web chat's thread id is one rule** (`threads.new_web_thread_id`,
    the chat's stream and live voice): the session id in the owner's space,
    a fresh id in any other. Gate: `tests/test_web_thread_ids.py` (no web
    code gives a thread its session id itself, but two declared places).
- **A daily spending limit per person (S2-02, 2026-11-22; decision N8).**
  Only where Spaces is enforced: an install that does not enforce it reads
  nothing more (`daily_limits.may_apply`, a check in memory).
  - `kazma_core/spaces/daily_limits.py` is the one rule. A limit is tokens
    always (every call, a model of unknown price too) and dollars where the
    price is known (0: none). Whose: a person's own
    (`identity` `policies[account]["daily_limit"]`), else the limit for
    people (`identity` `defaults["daily_limit"]`), else `SHIPPED_DEFAULT`
    (3,000,000 tokens and $1.00: about 40 ordinary turns, from a median turn
    of 71,830 tokens on the live install's ledger in November 2026); the
    admin has none unless one is set for them (the install's own
    `agent.daily_cost_limit_usd` covers the admin and is unchanged).
  - Counted from the ledger by the person the calls were for
    (`llm_ledger.usage_of`, `asker` and `ts`, index `idx_llm_calls_asker_ts`)
    since the local midnight (`cron.timezone`). A spend that cannot be
    counted (the ledger off or unreadable) refuses: a person's limit is
    never taken as unspent.
  - Asked where a model is called for a person: the supervisor refuses a
    turn at iteration 0 before any model call (`verdict`, off the loop,
    after the install's own check), and `resilient_chat` refuses a call
    outside a turn (`call_refusal`: `LLMError(kind="daily_limit")`, a swarm
    worker's, research's), and so does X Studio's `x_chat`
    (`XDailyLimitReached`, the work held), which also writes each answered
    call to the ledger the limit counts. A turn that started under the limit
    runs to its end; its own token budget bounds how far past.
  - **Past the limit, a turn still runs on the person's own key** (S2-04's
    follow-up, 2026-11-23): the supervisor resolves the client the turn's
    call will go to (`graph_supervisor._turn_client`, the one answer for the
    call and the admission) and lets the turn in when they hold a key of
    their own for its provider (`daily_limits.on_own_key`; a store that
    cannot say is no). In that turn every model call goes on their own
    keys: the state's `own_keys_only`, read by every graph node first
    (`hold_to_own_keys`: LangGraph runs a node in a copy of its caller's
    context, and only turns the rule on, so a sub-agent keeps it), and
    `LLMProvider._person_call` refuses a call that would go on the install's
    key (`LLMError` kind `daily_limit`, worded by `friendly_llm_error`) -- a
    respond synthesis on another provider, a failover. A call outside a turn
    stays refused by `call_refusal`. Gate: `tests/test_member_own_keys.py`
    (a real turn on her own key past her limit, one on the install's
    refused, today's refusal and the failover under the limit as the
    controls; every graph node holds the rule, a planted node as the
    control).
  - **A tool that pays another API with the install's key keeps off it in
    such a turn** (the review of de6874f3f, `kazma_core/spaces/install_paid.py`):
    `generate_image`'s paid backends (`INSTALL_PAID_TOOLS`; asked by name,
    refused before the card by `call_preflight` in the person's language and
    at the call; `auto` and the install's default, `KAZMA_IMAGE_PROVIDER`,
    draw with the keyless pollinations: only a paid backend the call names
    is refused), the acquisition policy's remote providers (Tavily, Jina,
    Firecrawl, the proxy: `AcquisitionPolicy.permits` answers no) and E2B
    (`e2b_enabled`). A Knowledge crawl started in such a turn records the
    rule on its journal row (`own_keys_only`), and every resume binds it
    (`kb_api.resume_job`, `daily_limits.own_keys_scope`): auto-resumed after
    a restart it lost it. A document job's remote parse (LlamaParse,
    Reducto: outside any turn) is refused for a job whose asker is past their
    daily limit (`daily_limits.call_refusal(asker)`, read in the stage's
    thread; `extract_salvage.salvage_audit_scope(remote_refusal=)`), and the
    local reading is kept. `PAID_KEY_READERS` declares every tool-reachable
    module that reads an API key from the environment -- by its literal name,
    or from a table (a read whose name is not a literal, in a module whose
    tuple, list or mapping holds a key's name) -- with how such a turn keeps
    off what it pays; a new one fails `tests/test_install_paid_tools.py` (a
    planted tool and a planted table read as controls; outside such a turn
    every path is as before). **The one
    accepted exception**: the remote embedder (`memory/embedder.py`, when the
    owner chose a remote embedding model) embeds the turn's question for
    recall on the install's key -- it costs very little. Speech in and out
    of a turn (`voice/stt.py`, `voice/tts.py`) is outside the turn and was
    never counted by a daily limit.
  - **Every model call is checked or declared**
    (`tests/test_model_calls_checked.py`): each product `.chat(`,
    `.chat_stream(`, `invoke_llm_chat(`, `ledgered_chat(` and each `.chat`
    handed on is in a function that asks `daily_limits.call_refusal` or
    `verdict`, or is declared with why (in a checked turn; Kazma's own work
    after a turn, not refused until S2-07 but in the ledger since the memory
    plan's finding 6, so counted; the admin's own; a client's own retries). A new model call asks `call_refusal` or is
    declared; a planted direct call and `x_chat` without its check are the
    controls.
  - The admin sets limits on People (`people.set_daily_limit`,
    `set_default_daily_limit`, `PUT /api/people/{account_id}/daily-limit`,
    `PUT /api/people/default-limit`), each change an event of the identity
    store's record; `GET /api/people` gives each person's limit and today's
    spend (counts and money, N11). Deleting a person takes their limit.
  - The precondition of a second account (`daily_limits.precondition`,
    S1-33) holds while the ledger counts and every person but the admin
    resolves to a limit.
  - Gates: `tests/test_person_daily_limit.py` (the real supervisor graph and
    `resilient_chat`; the install-wide sum as the control, the checks taken
    out fail seven), `tests/e2e/test_person_daily_limit_browser.py` (by the
    sidebar, EN/AR).
- **Features per person (S2-11, 2026-11-22; plan 4.8, decision N18).** Only
  where Spaces is enforced: an install that does not enforce it refuses
  nothing and reads nothing.
  - `kazma_core/spaces/features.py` is the one table: each feature's pages,
    routes (`kazma_ui.route_scopes` patterns), tools, chat commands,
    background loops and connected accounts; `ALWAYS_ON` (chat, memory, My
    account, with why) and `INSTALL` (the admin's commands, Kazma's own
    loops) declare the rest. A new page, route, tool, command or loop with
    neither fails `tests/test_feature_grants.py` (planted ones as controls),
    and so does a declaration that names nothing.
  - Who has what (`grants_of`): the admin every feature, Development theirs
    to switch off (N28, the switch `identity.holds_development` reads);
    anyone else N18's (`Feature.new_member`: documents, knowledge, research,
    web, images and voice) plus what the admin turned on
    (`identity` `policies[account]["features"]`). People sets them
    (`people.set_features`, `PUT /api/people/{account_id}/features`), an
    event of the identity record each time. A grant never passes S1-20's
    group rule.
  - Refused at every part: the tenant middleware answers a feature's route
    403 `feature_off` (`route_scopes.features_of_route`: a route's own
    feature and `features.ALSO_NEEDS`'s, one thread with the host check,
    `auth._rules_here`; a page is a page in its language,
    `auth._feature_off_response`) and remembers the page's grants for the
    sidebar (`feature_here`); a socket at its handshake
    (`space_binding.space_for_socket`, close 4403 `feature_off`); the
    command palette and shortcuts offer only what the sidebar shows
    (`search_pages.pageOffered`); tools at the offer and the call through
    `spaces.tools.tool_refusal` (host groups and features together:
    `offered_here`, the registry, the MCP branch, the environment note);
    chat commands (`features.command_refusal`, which reads a command as the
    handlers do: a bot's name and a prefix, and every chat-app handler's
    `_command_claimed`); the intent engine (`features.INTENT_HANDLERS`: a
    decision whose work needs a feature the person lacks is dropped).
    Refusals name the feature as People does (`features.NAMES`, held equal
    to the catalog) in the message's language.
  - **Checked where the work is admitted** (the S2-11 review):
    `features.ADMISSIONS` names, per feature, the functions every door to
    its work passes -- research's `research_runtime._frozen`, X's
    `book_x_post` and `x_work_scope`, a document stage, a crawl's every page
    and its resume, a swarm dispatch, a scheduled fire, a feature's socket
    -- and each asks `work_refusal` for the person the work is for (a
    booked post records its `booker`; a crawl its `asker`).
    `features.NO_ADMISSION` says why the rest have none. Work that cannot
    run waits (`FeatureOff`): a booked or legacy X post stays due, a crawl
    stops `interrupted` (`feature_off`) for a Resume, nothing held or
    failed; a document job fails with Retry, and an identity outage in its
    stage is retried as `metadata_unavailable`. A new door passes an
    admission or is a new one. A record that names no account (Kazma's
    own, "operator") is left to its space's rules. A feature off keeps the
    person's data.
  - The root conftest gives every test's people -- real accounts only --
    every feature (the admin's Development kept); a test of the features
    themselves is marked `real_features`. `create_app()` reads the stored Spaces switch into the
    process: a test that sets `scope._enforced` imports what builds the app
    at collection, never mid-test.
  - The precondition of a second account (`features.precondition`, S1-33)
    holds while every stored switch names a feature of the table.
  - Gates: `tests/test_feature_grants.py` (the table against the real app,
    the registry, the commands and the loops; X Studio on for Y and off for
    G through routes, the offer, the call, a scheduled job's executor, a
    real swarm worker, `/x` and X's background work; a grant that only hides
    the menu entry as the control), `tests/test_feature_admissions.py` (the
    admission gate with a planted admission and the document stage without
    its call as controls; the intent path through the real supervisor graph;
    research's admission; X booked through Scheduled, the booker, a post that
    waits; a crawl through the real replayed crawl; the real document
    worker; live voice's handshake; every chat-app handler; pages and
    refusals in both languages; Knowledge through Documents -- each with
    its control), `tests/test_feature_grants_in_tests.py`,
    `tests/e2e/test_feature_grants_browser.py` (by the sidebar, EN/AR).
- **Shared spaces come in two kinds (S2-12, piece 1, 2026-11-22; plan 4.11,
  N29).** Only once Spaces is enforced (`spaces_off` otherwise), and only
  the admin makes one (`people.create_shared_space`, `POST
  /api/people/spaces`, Settings -> People -> Shared spaces; recorded
  `space_created`, the admin its owner). A plain space (`sandboxed`, the
  default) never has a host tool, for anyone, the admin too. A space with a
  project folder (`host`) works in that folder (its first workspace row,
  made before the space is recorded and dropped if the record fails).
  - **The folder's rules are one module** (`kazma_core/spaces/project_folder.py`,
    codes `PROBLEMS`, worded `settings.people_err.folder_<code>`): an
    existing absolute local folder (a share or device path refused on its
    text); never Kazma's install folder, data folder or home, the owner's
    machine workspace (the owner's rows, `KAZMA_WORKSPACE`) or another
    space's root, nor inside or holding one. Compared by real path AND by
    identity (`kazma_core/workspace/folder_identity.py`, the backup folder's
    rule, now one home: `backup.folder_copy` aliases it).
  - **Checked again at use**: `resolve_active_root` asks
    `project_folder.check_at_use` for a shared host space's active row every
    time, never swallowed; a folder that became a junction or link into
    Kazma's data after the space was made raises `RefusedBeforeEffect`
    before anything reads or writes through it. The per-task rung too (the
    S2-12 review, finding 10): a swarm task's workspace row and an approval
    resume's root, so another space's root is refused there.
  - **Kazma's folders come from one list** (finding 9):
    `store_registry.kazma_owned_paths` -- the data folder, the install,
    Kazma's home, every store wherever its own variable puts it, the vector
    store, the document store, an absolute research folder, what the setup
    record names (the data folder, Postgres's data, archive and base
    backups, before and after an upgrade), the engine's disk, the backup
    folder copy and the admin's extra folders. A source that cannot be read
    makes the folder `unreachable`, never one that overlaps nothing.
  - **A create is atomic** (finding 10): one at a time from the folder check
    to the record (`people._CREATE_LOCK`), so two creates never take one
    folder; a workspace row of a space the identity store does not hold (a
    create a stop cut off) is dropped before the next create
    (`WorkspaceStore.drop_rows_of_unknown_spaces`) and never counts as a
    space's root (`project_folder._roots_of_spaces`). Gate:
    `tests/test_project_folder_owned_paths.py` (the list, the per-task rung
    and the creates of before as the controls).
  - Gates: `tests/test_shared_spaces.py` (each refusal; the junction made
    after creation, with the check taken out as the control; a loopback name
    of Kazma's data, with the identity taken out as the control; a failed
    record leaves no workspace row), `tests/e2e/test_shared_spaces_browser.py`
    (by the sidebar, EN/AR).
  - **Who is in one (piece 2).** The admin adds a person
    (`people.add_member`, `POST /api/spaces/{space_id}/members`, People);
    they are told at their next page load (`member_added`, with the space's
    name). A member leaves (`people.leave_space`, `POST .../leave`, Settings
    -> This space's data -> Who is in this space); its owner or the admin
    takes one out (`people.remove_member`, `DELETE .../members/{account_id}`;
    told, `member_removed`); the last owner stays (`last_owner`). Each is an
    event of the People record.
  - **What goes with a member (N36)**, leaving, taken out, or their account
    deleted (`delete_person`, every shared space they were in): after the
    membership is gone, `memory.forget.forget_entry` forgets every fact under
    their own entry there (journaled first; their messages stay, the others'
    entries and the space's shared facts too), and their share of its
    documents is taken back (`documents.principal.take_back_access`,
    `revoke_member_access` on both document stores, audited `revoke_member`;
    their own documents stay theirs). A forget that fails is `forget_failed`
    (503), never silent. The confirm dialogs say this first, EN/AR.
  - **The forget is never left unfinished** (the S2-12 review, finding 4).
    It is journaled BEFORE the membership changes (`people._journal_then`:
    the change tried on a copy first, so a refused one journals nothing;
    `forget_entry(journal_seq=)` marks that entry applied), so a stop or a
    failure after the change leaves an entry the forget convergence applies.
    The convergence also forgets every `member_*` entry whose account is no
    longer a member of its space (`forget._forget_departed_entries`: a forget
    never journaled, a deleted account), and a replay never forgets a current
    member's entry (`forget_journal._still_a_member`). The removed member's
    notice says the facts were forgotten only once they were
    (`notices_for` `forgotten`, `forget.entry_forgotten`; else the pending
    wording). Gate: `tests/test_member_forget_converges.py` (the flow of
    before as the control).

- **The S2-05/06 review's fixes (2026-11-22).** Only where Spaces is
  enforced.
  - **Whose card it is comes from the live interrupt**: the approve route
    and the timeout watchdog ask `whose_card` with the live interrupt's id
    and payload, never an id the request names, and the card's `asker`
    wins over a row's. Two people's identical cards are two gate rows
    (`hitl_gates._askers_differ`: the hash id and the arguments' twin match
    never merge across askers), and claiming one never supersedes the other
    (`_supersede_pending_twins`, the second review: Omar's identical card
    was dropped unanswered when Reem's was claimed). A clarify or confirm
    card's tools are its `items[].tool` (N21 holds when it is answered).
  - **An MCP server's sampling request is a card**: it names its asker
    (`spec_client._sampling_card_who`), the approve route asks the rule
    before `resolve_sampling_hitl`, and the pending list keeps the
    process-wide requests to the space and the person who may answer
    (`hitl_answerers.cards_of_this_space`).
  - **N4: nobody skips their own cards for their approvers**
    (`spaces.approvals.standing_grant_refusal`, asked by `enable_yolo`,
    `grant_tool`, `grant_task` and `/unrestricted`): a person whose cards
    the admin sent to approvers gets `approvers_decide`; an approver's
    grant from the card they answered passes. A chat app's swarm button
    asks the whole rule for the owner (`shared_approvals._a_chat_button_may_decide`).
    Cancel and Retry of one's own swarm task ask whose task it is
    (`single_operator.task_is_callers`), Approve and Reject who answers it
    (`task_actions.caller_may_act_on(answering=)`). With Spaces off the
    Swarm decide route reads no request before deciding. **A standing
    approval reads the approvers when it is used** (the second review: YOLO
    or a grant a person made before the admin set approvers kept skipping
    their cards): every grant records who made it (`granted_by`,
    `approvals.made_by_a_person`), and `hitl.standing_approval` lets one
    hold for a person with approvers only when an approver made it
    (`approvals.approvers_now`; an identity store that cannot be read holds
    none). Gate: `tests/test_standing_approvals_read_approvers.py` (the
    supersede by arguments and the grant read alone as the controls).
  - **The watchdog**: once enforced, whose card it is and its chat-app
    route are read before the timeout is recorded (a read that fails leaves
    the card pending and claimed by nobody; the next pass tries again). The
    third pass that cannot read it records the timeout anyway and closes the
    turn with a line, resumed as nobody (`hitl_timeout._close_turn_unread`,
    `_READS_BEFORE_GIVING_UP`): a card never stays pending for good. With
    Spaces off the watchdog records first and reads the route after, as
    before (the full suite's three watchdog tests). A card whose asker left
    its space ends the turn with a line saying why
    (`turn_budget.write_turn_end`), resumed as nobody.
  - **Every resume runs as the turn's asker**: a turn a restart cut off
    continues as the author of the message that OPENED the turn
    (`hitl_answerers.whose_turn`, `_turn_author`: the newest user row before
    the open turn's reply row, never a steer's row -- marked `steer` -- nor a
    later row; read in the chat's own space), not at all when they left.
    Gate, per call site (the second review: a binding anywhere in a
    function passed every resume in it, and a chat app's continue and the
    watchdog's chat-app resume ran unbound): every call that runs a resume
    -- a resume command, a function that builds one, or a turn continued
    from its checkpoint, given to what runs a turn or handed to a chat app's
    resumer -- sits inside `with as_the_asker(...)`/`bind_scope(...)`, or
    its function is declared (`tests/test_resumes_run_as_the_asker.py`,
    planted unbound resumes, one beside a binding, as the controls).
  - **Another member's message never drops a card**: a new message or
    voice utterance in a chat whose pending card waits on someone else is
    refused with a line naming them (`sse_chat._card_waits_on_someone_else`),
    nothing saved; the asker's own message goes on as before.
  - **Nobody else ends or steers a member's turn** (the second review): one
    rule, `hitl_answerers.turn_control_refusal`, asked by the routes through
    `sse_chat._turn_control` before anything is saved, queued or cancelled.
    A steer (`/api/chat/steer`, soft or hard, running or paused) is its
    asker's only; stop and abort (`/api/chat/stop`, `/api/chat/abort`) its
    asker's or an owner of the space; `/reset` and `/compact` the chat's
    opener's or an owner's, never while another member's turn runs or
    waits; a new message or voice utterance while another member's turn
    runs is refused with a line saying the chat is answering them (it would
    cancel the turn; the same person's message supersedes as before). Each
    refusal is a line in the person's language (`sse_chat._TURN_LINES`) the
