    thread (S3-02), so the next message and button press are refused at the
    adapter, and one already queued is not run (`chat_place`).
  - **What waits for them is dropped**: `chat_links.address_revoked(target)`
    (memory only, any thread) is true for the chats of an unlinked or deleted
    chat-app account and of a disabled account's links, never a chat still
    linked to an enabled account. `GatewayManager.send` drops a reply to such
    a chat (`gateway._dropped_for_its_person`), and the outbox's retry pass
    settles a waiting one `dropped` (`ChatOutbox.finish`, no notice owed):
    an expired card's notice from the watchdog, a swarm result, a reply that
    was not taken -- never sent. A disabled person's chats are answered
    again once enabled.
  - Gates: `tests/test_unlink_stops_everything.py` (the outbox, a queued
    message, a press, a pending card's expiry; disabled, deleted, linked
    again; a waiting reply still sent as the control),
    `tests/e2e/test_chat_unlink_browser.py` (by the sidebar, EN/AR).
- **A chat app's admin is the admin's linked account (S3-08, 2026-11-23).**
  Once Spaces is enforced `allowlists.is_gateway_admin` -- the one admin rule
  of the chat apps: admin-only commands (`changes_global_config`), install
  buttons, a swarm bus card's press -- asks
  `chat_links.linked_admin(platform, user)` (memory: a link to an enabled
  account whose install role is admin; a Discord sender's user, never its
  channel). `KAZMA_GATEWAY_ADMINS` and the allowlists grant nothing then
  (its `platform:id` entries became the owner's links when Spaces was
  switched on, S3-02); before Spaces they decide, as always
  (`_admin_by_lists`). Every admin-only refusal says how one becomes able
  to through `allowlists.admin_hint` (the handler's in the sender's
  language, `graph._admin_only_text`), never the retired list once
  enforced. Gate: `tests/test_chat_admin_is_an_account.py` (the rule, a
  listed member refused through the real handler in English and Arabic,
  the owner's linked chat passing; the environment list as the control).
- **The stage 3 review's fixes (2026-11-23).** Only where Spaces is
  enforced, unless said.
  - **A link is made from a person's own sign-in** (H1,
    `chat_links_api._own_sign_in`): the chat-link routes answer a browser
    session, or a credential with the admin role (the shared secret, an
    admin token); a token of any other role is refused, 403
    `own_sign_in_only`. Every API token is the owner's account
    (`space_binding.account_of`), and an operator token's code made its
    holder the chat apps' admin. Gate: `tests/test_chat_links_own_sign_in.py`.
  - **No API token acts as the owner on the person's own routes** (the
    account-route class, `auth.token_acts_for_the_owner`, asked by
    `auth.principal_allows`, the middleware's one role rule): once Spaces is
    enforced every route `route_scopes` classes ACCOUNT refuses an API token
    below admin (403 `own_sign_in_only`) -- My account's notices, chat links
    and model keys, Web Push's subscribe, the bell, the problems list.
    `auth.TOKEN_MAY_ASK` declares the few that describe the credential or
    the install, with why; the chat-link and notices routes ask the rule
    again (`people_api._own_caller`). An operator token read and dismissed
    the owner's notices and could subscribe its endpoint to the owner's
    answers. Gate: `tests/test_account_routes_own_sign_in.py` (every
    ACCOUNT route of the built app; the rule taken out as the control).
  - **The switch adopts only what was the owner** (M1,
    `chat_links.owner_link_plan`, `_was_the_owner`): a known id passes the
    sender rule of before (on the allowlist; with none set, the known ids
    or the open switch -- a set allowlist decides alone) and the admin rule
    of before (`KAZMA_GATEWAY_ADMINS` when
    set, else the allowlist, else the known ids); a Telegram group (a
    negative id) is never adopted; `--check` names every id adopted and
    every one left, with why. The core restates the gateway's rules (it does
    not import the gateway). Gate: `tests/test_switch_on_adopts_the_owner_only.py`.
  - **Codes** (L1, L2, `sender_rule.link_attempted`, `chat_links.prefixed_code`,
    `bare_code`, `live_codes_in`, `is_live_code`): a code alone from a
    linked sender counts only when it is live (a "next-week" is their
    message, never a guess counted against them); a live code anywhere in
    a message, its own word, is burned in a group and redeemed in a direct
    chat, never handed to the agent; the live codes are kept in memory (this
    process's issues and uses at once, another's through the store's change
    notice). A redemption is a `chat_linked` event by the chat-app account
    that sent the code, told to the account at its next page load
    (`people._TOLD`, `account_notices.js`), with Unlink and "It was me".
  - **The links in memory fail closed** (L3, L4): a read that fails forgets
    them (`chat_links._forget_snapshot`: no stale admin); `linked_admin`
    reads again past `LINKS_TTL_S`; before the links were read a reply waits
    in the outbox (`gateway._links_unknown`). A native command's unlinked
    sender is told how to link (L5); `--check` reads a list-typed allowlist
    as ids (`chat_links.split_ids`, L6). Gate:
    `tests/test_chat_link_codes_review.py` (each with the rule of before as
    its control), `tests/e2e/test_chat_unlink_browser.py` (EN/AR).
  - **An answer from another chat never sends the asker's work to the
    presser** (M2): `hitl_answerers.as_the_asker` clears the delivery target
    and platform when it binds someone else (the tool worker then takes the
    turn's own `_gateway` route); a card answered for someone else
    (`hitl._answered_for_someone_else`) resumes into the asker's chat only
    when `chat_is_the_askers` says the chat is theirs -- a group of their
    space, or their own chat (`chat_links.is_own_chat`) -- else nowhere, and
    the presser's chat gets only a receipt. Gate:
    `tests/test_hitl_resume_never_reaches_the_presser.py`.
  - **A press keeps the chat it was pressed in** (M5): a Discord press
    carries its `guild_id`, so a press in a server channel is not a direct
    chat; each adapter's press message says which kind of chat it is in
    (gate in `tests/test_press_keeps_its_chat.py`).
  - **No fallback to the owner's chat for someone else's work** (M6):
    `send_file`'s and the document handler's fallbacks answer
    `send_message.own_address`; every product function reading a
    configured chat id asks it or is declared (`tests/test_chat_fallbacks_ask_the_person.py`).
  - **A member sends only to their own chat or this conversation** (M7,
    `call_preflight._outbound_refusal`): every tool of
    `side_effects.OUTBOUND_TARGET_FIELDS` but those `OUTBOUND_NOT_CHECKED`
    names (the space's own mailbox; `send_file`, no recipient) is checked
    before the card and at the call (`PREFLIGHT_TOOLS`); the admin keeps the
    allowlist rule of before. Gate: `tests/test_member_outbound_targets.py`.
  - **A dropped reminder ends quietly** (L8): the scheduler's delivery pass
    asks `chat_links.address_revoked` first, and `finish_delivery(dropped=True)`
    ends the delivery `dropped`, the job done, no retry, no alert
    (`scheduled.delivery_dropped`; the digest counts it, not as a problem).
    Gate: `tests/test_cron_dropped_reminder_ends_quietly.py`.
  - **A waiting card is checked again under the thread lock, in every
    chat** (M3): another member's message that waited on the lock behind
    the turn that paused never drops its card (`graph._waits_on_someone_else`,
    asked before the lock and again before `cancel_pending_hitl`). Gate:
    `tests/test_card_wait_checked_under_the_lock.py`.
  - **`/undo`, `/edit` and `/replay <step>` are the chat's opener's or an
    owner's** (M4): action `rewind` of `hitl_answerers.turn_control_refusal`,
    the rule of `reset`, in groups and direct chats; the S3-06 command
    matrix runs in a group too. Gates: `tests/test_chat_rewind_per_person.py`,
    `tests/test_chat_commands_act_as_the_account.py`.
  - **A card is decided in the space it lives in** (L7,
    `hitl._card_space_for_presser`): after a `/space` switch, a member of
    the card's space presses it there, as themself; whose card it is is
    still asked on the live card. Gate: `tests/test_card_press_after_a_space_switch.py`.
  - **A group's binding holds while its binder is a member**
    (L9, `chat_apps._group_space`); **a forum topic is the group's**, named
    by the group, never the member who wrote (L11,
    `graph._resolve_thread_in_place`); **`/reset` clears the chat's own
    pointer in its space** (L10). Gate:
    `tests/test_chat_group_bindings_and_pointers.py`.
  - **A change to a member's fact is decided by them or an owner** (L13,
    `changes._not_theirs_to_decide`, code `not_theirs`): in a shared space
    a change filed under `member_<account>` is confirmed, undone or
    dismissed only by that member or an owner of the space, on the Memory
    page and with `/memory` alike. Gate:
    `tests/test_memory_changes_decided_by_their_person.py`. Asked before
    the memory mutation lock (`changes._decided_before_the_lock`: the
    identity store is no call to wait on under it, §15 D2), and an identity
    store that cannot answer is the refusal `identity_unavailable`, never a
    500: 503 with `Retry-After`, as the other outages are. Gate:
    `tests/test_memory_change_decided_before_the_lock.py`.
  - **Time Travel restores, forks and clears a chat of its opener or an
    owner** (`thread_rewind._theirs_to_change`, once Spaces is enforced):
    `rewind_thread`, `fork_thread` and `clear_thread_snapshots` -- the one
    service the page, the terminal app and the chat apps call -- and the
    web chat's and the chat apps' `/replay clear` ask the rule a chat app's
    `/replay` asks (`turn_control_refusal`, action `rewind`): 403
    `not_your_chat`, worded on the page (EN/AR) and in the chats. The space
    check alone let any member of a shared space take back, copy or delete
    another member's turns. Gate: `tests/test_time_travel_restore_per_person.py`
    (the real routes behind the real tenant middleware; the space-only
    check as the control).
  - **A whole chat is changed by its opener or an owner** (the review of
    3da533662): once Spaces is enforced the web routes that change a whole
    chat ask the rule `/reset` asks (`turn_control_refusal`, action
    `reset`): delete (`DELETE /api/chat/sessions/{id}`, through
    `sse_chat._turn_control`: never while another member's turn runs or
    waits), rename, archive, unarchive, pin and unpin
    (`sse_chat._whole_chat_refusal_sync`), and the Dashboard's delete
    (`DELETE /api/sessions/{thread_id}`; whether a turn waits read from the
    gate registry, `dashboard._turn_runs_or_waits`). 403 `not_your_chat`;
    503 with `Retry-After` when who it is cannot be read. The Dashboard's
    "Clear saved steps" clears every member's chats of the space: an owner
    of the space only (`dashboard._clear_all_refusal`, 403 `not_an_owner`).
    The space check alone let a member delete another member's whole chat,
    its steps and its record.
    The memory route that keeps a chat out and forgets its past asked
    S1-11's rule already (`speakers.may_keep_chat_out`). A new web route
    that changes a whole chat asks the same rule. Gate:
    `tests/test_whole_chat_routes_per_person.py` (the space-only check as
    the control).
- **Once a second account exists, no switch opens the install (S4-03,
  2026-11-23).** The boot refuses sign-in off (`KAZMA_AUTH_DISABLED`,
  `KAZMA_DEV_WS_BYPASS`, `KAZMA_LOOPBACK_AUTOLOGIN`, `KAZMA_TRUST_LAN`:
  the last two hand a peer the owner's auto-login, refused though S4-02's
  rule already ends it, so a lab is told at start), demo mode
  (`KAZMA_DEMO_MODE`) and the chat apps' open switch
  (`KAZMA_GATEWAY_OPEN_TO_EVERYONE`, unless
  `KAZMA_GATEWAY_STRICT_ALLOWLIST` overrides it) and the open season
  take-over (`KAZMA_SESSION_OPEN_TAKEOVER`). One list,
  `boot_guard.OPEN_SWITCHES`, read through `boot_guard.open_switches_on`
  (the strict override is there) by this refusal and by the cloud profile
  (S4-08) alike: a new switch that lets anyone in goes there. `boot_guard.open_switches_refusal` is asked by
  `KazmaAppBuilder._bootstrap_services` once the settings store answers:
  exit 1 before anything serves, the refusal on stderr and in the log,
  naming the accounts it counted. It counts accounts, not Spaces: an install
  still on the older multi-user mode refuses too. With no switch on it reads
  nothing; an identity store that cannot answer refuses. Gate:
  `tests/test_open_switches_refused_with_members.py` (each switch through
  the real `create_app`; the boot guard without the rule as the control).
- **Stronger sign-in (S4-02, 2026-11-23).**
  - **A second factor** (`kazma_core/security/totp.py`, RFC 6238 on the
    standard library; `kazma_core/security/second_factor.py`): turned on in
    My account (`kazma_ui/sign_in_api.py`, `static/js/sign_in_settings.js`),
    in every mode. The secret and the recovery codes' digests are kept in
    the vault, install-scoped (`account.2fa.<account id>`: sign-in reads it
    before any space is bound), never in settings. A right password -- or,
    for the owner, the install's secret -- answers 401
    `second_factor_required` for an account with one
    (`routes_direct.auth._second_factor_verdict`), and the sign-in page
    asks for the code; a code is taken once (the last step kept per
    account, `second_factor.STEPS_KEY`), a recovery code used once. No API
    token, whatever its role, turns it on or off. Whether an account has
    one is `second_factor.factor_on`: a plain marker in settings
    (`second_factor.ON_KEY`, no secret), or the vault's copy when the
    marker is off (a settings restore from before the factor took the
    marker away; the marker is put back). With the marker on, a vault that
    cannot be read refuses (503); with it off, an unreadable vault is no
    factor, so a vault that failed to open stops no account without one. An
    install with no vault at all has none (`vault.vault_disabled`). Turning
    it on ends the account's other sessions (this one stays). **Wrong codes
    pause** an account's code checks in every mode, from every address, a
    known one too: `second_factor.WRONG_CODES` in a row, then `PAUSE_S`,
    doubling to `PAUSE_MAX_S` (`PAUSES_KEY`), counted under
    `second_factor._lock` so wrong codes at once make one pause; sign-in answers 429
    `second_factor_paused`, My account shows it, and the person is told
    where Spaces is enforced. The admin resets a person's from People
    (told), only from a signed-in admin's session (never the install's
    secret or a token: `session_only`) and never their own
    (`own_in_my_account`); deleting a person forgets it. **The way back
    with no code** is on the machine only: `kazma account second-factor off
    --account <id>` (`kazma_cli/account.py`, `second_factor.break_glass`)
    holds the runtime lock (refused while a server holds it), reads the
    vault itself, takes the factor off even when the vault lost it, and is
    an event of the People record.
  - **The install's secret is a key for programs once the owner has a
    second factor** (`auth._owner_second_factor_on`): it never mints a
    browser session (`auth._auto_cookie_via`), and a browser-style request
    that sends it (`Accept: text/html` or `Sec-Fetch-*`, or the legacy
    secret cookie) is refused 401 `secret_in_browser`
    (`auth._secret_refused_in_a_browser`), and so is the legacy
    `kazma-secret` cookie on a chat socket (`auth.get_websocket_principal`).
    The CLI (`local_api`), the guard and `scripts/deploy_live.py` keep it.
    The local network's auto-login (`KAZMA_TRUST_LAN`) ends then too
    (`auth._lan_auto_login`); this computer keeps its own. My account says
    the second factor does not cover the secret, and that the auto-login on
    this computer asks no code (by design, before Spaces or with one
    account).
  - **Sign-in limits per account** (only where Spaces is enforced): wrong
    passwords for one name from every address together, past
    `routes_direct.auth.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILS` in `ACCOUNT_WINDOW_S`, pause
    sign-ins to it, but from an address it signed in from in the last 30
    days (`KNOWN_ADDRESSES_KEY`, hashed); the person is told
    (`sign_in_paused`).
  - **Invitation links that expire** (`kazma_core/spaces/invitations.py`):
    the admin makes one on People (one use, at most `invitations.HOURS`
    hours, only its digest kept). The link is `/invite#<token>`: the token
    after the '#' never reaches a server or its log (the page reads it,
    takes it out of the address bar and asks `POST /api/invitations/lookup`);
    the access log cuts any `/invite/<x>` path
    (`observability.log_noise.NoTokensInPaths`). `/invite`, the lookup and
    `POST /api/invitations/accept` are open before sign-in and make the
    account through `people.create_person` (S1-33's preconditions too),
    claiming the link first so it makes one account. Revoked at will.
  - **Each person's sessions**: People lists a person's and ends one
    (`web_sessions.end_one_session`, told); My account ends one of one's
    own. The owner's are every kind it has (`web_sessions.sessions_of_account`:
    a sign-in with the secret, the auto-login, a browser that sent the
    secret's header), each named by how it came (the session's `via`).
  - **No auto-login once a second person has an account**
    (`auth.everyone_signs_in`, asked by `_peer_trust_allowed`): with Spaces
    enforced and an account besides the owner's, the peer address is no
    credential, so this machine gets no session for nothing and its sockets
    are refused; the owner signs in like anyone and the session lasts as any
    does. The same rule ends `KAZMA_TRUST_LAN`'s auto-login for a private
    network peer (a Docker bridge included): it is peer trust too, on HTTP
    and on sockets. The sign-in page says why (`#everyone-signs-in`). When
    the rule first holds -- `people.create_person` while enforced, and
    `preconditions.switch_on` with an account besides the owner's -- the
    auto-login sessions already made end
    (`web_sessions.end_peer_trust_sessions`: those of `via`
    `this_computer` or `local_network`; one signed in with the secret
    stays). Before Spaces, or with one account, nothing changes. The root conftest keeps today's
    auto-login for other tests; a test of sign-in is marked `real_sign_in`.
  - Gates: `tests/test_sign_in_hardening.py` (a password alone signing in,
    a link spent never, and today's auto-login as controls),
    `tests/test_sign_in_review_fixes.py` (the review's eight items, each with
    today's behaviour as its control), `tests/test_sign_in_recheck.py` (the
    re-check's seven, each with today's behaviour as its control),
    `tests/e2e/test_sign_in_hardening_browser.py` (by the sidebar, EN/AR).

## UI Conventions (Web)

- **Dialogs:** use the unified Promise-based helpers, never native browser
  dialogs. `window.kazmaConfirm(opts)` (→ `Promise<boolean>`; with a
  `checkbox` label it shows that box unticked and answers `{ok, checked}`),
  `window.kazmaAlert(opts)` (→ `Promise<void>`), `window.kazmaPrompt(opts)`
  (→ `Promise<string|null>`). All backed by `$store.modal`
  (`static/js/modules/stores.js`) + `components/modal.html`. Each has a
  native fallback if Alpine hasn't booted. The modal is single-instance:
  `close()` clears its content 200 ms later (after the leave transition)
  only if no dialog opened meanwhile -- it cleared regardless, and an alert
  shown right after a confirm sat open with no text and no buttons
  (`tests/js/test_modal_store.js`, 2026-09-27).
- **Every interface word comes from the catalog; content is marked
  `translate="no"`** (2026-09-28). Templates use `{{ t('key') }}`; scripts
  use `window.kazmaT(key, english, vars)` (or the page's own helper that
  calls it; chat.js and agentStore.js use `ti`/`tiFmt` through
  `CHAT_I18N`). Never read `window.KAZMA_I18N[key]` yourself: an entry is
  `{en, ar}`, and research.js printed "[object Object]" that way. Dates and
  numbers go through `window.KazmaFormat` (Latin digits in Arabic). What
  stays as written -- the user's words and chat titles, the model's replies,
  names, a tool's or skill's own documentation, server diagnostics -- is
  marked `translate="no"`. Gates: `tests/test_i18n_keys_exist.py` (every key
  a page names exists in both languages), `tests/test_templates_have_no_english.py`
  (no English literal in a template), `tests/e2e/test_pages_read_in_arabic.py`
  (every page, and a chat turn, rendered in Arabic). Names that are the same
  in every language live in `tests/_ui_names.py`.
  **Scripts are gated too** (`tests/test_scripts_have_no_english.py`,
  2026-10-01): a toast, a dialog, a modal or a title a script sets after a
  click is on no page the browser tour reads, and 57 were English in every
  language (the chat's steer messages, "Read aloud", pinned/unpinned,
  "Rebuild started", the Workspace's pull-request viewer...). The gate lexes
  every script and every template's inline script and fails on English words
  at those sinks outside a translation helper (found from the source: a
  function whose first parameter is the key and whose body reads the
  catalog). HTML a script builds (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`,
  `insertAdjacentHTML`) is read too: the expression's literals are joined in
  order and only what the browser shows is checked -- text between tags and
  the `title`/`aria-label`/`placeholder`/`alt` values, never a tag, a style,
  a class or a data attribute -- so markup split across literals is not
  English; on the old scripts it found 19 strings and no markup. In the same file: every option a page passes to
  `kazmaConfirm`/`kazmaPrompt`/`kazmaAlert` is one `stores.js` reads (the
  Workspace passed `confirmLabel`, so "Delete files too" read "Confirm"); no
  template quotes `{{ ... }}` inside a script -- write `{{ value | tojson }}`
  (Jinja's HTML escaping is not JavaScript escaping: a newline in a value
  ended the script, `&` arrived as `&amp;`); and the strings tables
  `__KB_STRINGS`/`__MEM_STRINGS` hold every `S.<key>` their scripts read.
- **A modal's body is HTML; what came from outside goes in escaped.**
  `$store.modal.body` is rendered with `x-html`. The Workspace's pull-request
  viewer put the PR's title, the reviewers' names and GitHub's merge state in
  as they came, so a PR titled `<img src=x onerror=...>` ran script in the
  operator's page when it was opened (fixed 2026-10-01,
  `tests/js/test_workspace_pr_modal.js`). `kazmaConfirm`/`kazmaPrompt`/
  `kazmaAlert` escape their message themselves; `showModal({body})` does not.
- **A script's table of labels is catalog keys, not words** (2026-09-29):
  chat.js named every step's tool in English ("Read file") on Arabic pages.
  A table read as `ti(pair[0], pair[1])` (`_HEADER_PHASE_LABELS`,
  `_TOOL_FRIENDLY`) is read by `tests/test_chat_i18n_bridge.py` like any
  `ti()` key. **Mixed-direction content sits in a `<bdi>`** -- a tool call, an
  id, a date inside Arabic text is reordered by the bidi algorithm otherwise
  (`dir="ltr"` for code-like content, automatic for a date).
- **Text follows its own language, whatever the UI's** (the owner's rule,
  2026-10-02): the UI language lays out the page and its own labels; English
  text runs and aligns left-to-right and Arabic right-to-left in BOTH UIs.
  Alignment is logical (`text-align: start`); a `left`/`right` keyed to the
  page's `dir` is declared with its reason (`DECLARED` in
  `tests/test_text_follows_its_language.py`) -- the Arabic UI right-aligned
  English replies, tool output, tables and cards. Markdown blocks get their
  direction from their own words (`KazmaBidi.blockDir`: the language most of
  the words are in, a URL/path/identifier one word; a word with an Arabic
  letter or Arabic punctuation is Arabic ("وDOCX"); a name-like Latin word
  -- acronym, CamelCase, a digit, a capital mid-sentence -- counts a
  quarter, or Arabic technical prose reads as English; a tie to the first
  letter; no letters -> the container's, so a number column stays put),
  never from `dir="auto"`'s first letter; the bidi helper isolates a run
  against ITS paragraph, never the message (an English-first reply's Arabic
  paragraph ran left-to-right in both UIs). Data a page shows is content
  (`translate="no"`; the global `unicode-bidi: plaintext` rule gives it and
  its blocks their text's direction, except an element whose `dir` a script
  set -- the renderer's paragraph, a `<bdi dir="ltr">` tool call -- and an
  interface word inside content (`translate="yes"`: an isolate in the page's
  direction); never mark a number, which then reads left-to-right). Content
  shown in a row of interface text is its own block, or it sits on the
  row's start in the page's direction. A line mixing a page label and content is split (the
  memory row). No page-`dir` rule aligns a chat bubble: a reply looks the
  same in either UI. Python asks `i18n.current_language()`; only the
  middleware reads the `kazma-lang` cookie (four routes defaulted to English
  on an Arabic install). Gates: `tests/test_text_follows_its_language.py`,
  `tests/e2e/test_text_follows_its_language.py` (real turns in both UIs,
  live and reloaded, the two compared line for line; old rules as the
  negative controls), `tests/js/test_block_direction.js`.
- **The TUI names its pages from one table, in the web UI's words**
  (`kazma_tui/nav_rail.py` `TAB_LABELS`, 2026-10-01): the tabs and the
  navigation rail read it. The tabs' Arabic labels were never applied --
  `update_localization` called `TabbedContent.tabs`, which does not exist, and
  a catch-all logged it at DEBUG -- and the rail stayed English. A tab the web
  UI also has takes its `nav.<tab>` word, or is declared with its reason
  (`tests/test_tui_labels.py`, through the real app in both languages).
  **Ctrl+L** (`action_toggle_language`, also in the command palette) switches
  and saves the language; nothing called `set_language` before.
  `update_localization` works on the MAIN screen (`screen_stack[0]`), never
  `self.screen`: a switch from the palette runs with a modal on top.
  **A handler reads only what its event carries** (`tests/test_tui_event_attributes.py`,
  from Textual's own source): the Traces tab read `event.coordinate` from
  `DataTable.RowHighlighted` and crashed the TUI whenever a trace existed.
  Text in a RichLog or a DataTable cell is Rich markup: escape what comes
  from data (`rich.markup.escape`) and never put a Textual `$variable` in it
  (`App.get_css_variables()` gives the colour).
- **A save the server accepted never reports failure.** Only the request
  sits in the save's `try`; applying the result to the page is a separate
  step (`tests/js/test_settings_saves_report_truth.js` runs every Settings
  save against an accepting server).
- **Toasts:** use `window.showToast(msg, type, duration)` or
  `Alpine.store('toast').add(...)`. `streaming.js`'s `KazmaStream.toast`
  delegates to `$store.toast` — there is one toast system. `add(message,
  type, duration, action)` takes an optional `{label, run}` button (the
  toast closes after it); `duration` 0 stays until answered.
- **An open tab is told when Kazma was updated** (`modules/build_watch.js`,
  2026-10-16): the page carries the build that rendered it
  (`<meta name="kazma-build">`, the `build_commit()` template global,
  resolved at process start) and, when visible and every 5 minutes, compares
  it with `/health/live`'s build through `kazmaGetJson`; another build shows
  ONE "Kazma was updated -- Refresh" toast per tab. An unknown build, a
  restart of the same build or a server not answering shows nothing. Never
  scan the asset files on `/health/live`: it is the guard's probe, on the
  loop. Gates: `tests/js/test_build_watch.js`, `tests/e2e/test_update_notice.py`
  (EN/AR, after a sidebar navigation, Refresh reloads).
- **Kazma's mark has a face per theme** (2026-11-20, the owner's logo,
  `scripts/make_app_icons.py`, from `static/img/brand/kazma-logo-master.webp`):
  the dark theme shows the artwork as drawn (`kazma-logo-dark-theme.png`,
  `kazma-icon-dark-theme.png`), the light theme a two-tone mark whose white
  strokes are navy ink and blue strokes as drawn (`kazma-logo.png`,
  `kazma-icon.png`; the plain names are the one that reads on either page,
  so a place with one image uses it). Every place that shows it holds both
  `<img>`s, classed `brand-on-dark` / `brand-on-light`, and `kazma.css` hides
  the other theme's; chat.js draws it only through `_kazmaMarkHtml`. The
  website's first light mark recoloured every stroke blue, and the owner
  asked why the logo was one solid blue. The favicon and app icons are the
  artwork on the dark rounded square. Gates: `tests/test_logo_by_theme.py`
  (the website's recolour and the artwork as negative controls),
  `tests/e2e/test_sidebar_brand_and_build.py` (by the sidebar, EN/AR, both
  themes; also the sidebar card's release, build and start time, and the
  hover backdrop).
- **One colour system: a card is one step above the wall** (2026-11-09, the
  owner's refresh, `docs/plans/UI_DESIGN_REFRESH.md`; raised 2026-11-17 to
  the look kazma.ai took the day before). Every colour is a token in
  `kazma.css` (dark in `:root`, light in `[data-theme="light"]`): the surface
  scale -- the wall is the page (`#080d18` dark, `#f4f7fd` light) and the
  chrome (sidebar, header) is the wall; `--surface-card` is one step above it
  (`#101a2e`, white), and `--bg-panel` / `--bg-card` / `--bg-primary` /
  `--card-bg` are the card; overlays (menus, popovers, toasts) are the card's
  surface with a deeper shadow; `--surface-sunken`, the well (code, table
  heads, an inset block), is below the wall in both themes; inputs are
  transparent, so they take the surface they sit on -- status colours with
  `-subtle` and `-border` variants and `--on-*` inks for fills, `--cat-1..6`,
  and the card shape (`--card-radius` 14px, `--card-padding`, a layered
  `--card-shadow` per theme with a top highlight, `--card-hairline`). One
  grouped card rule paints `.card` and every card family with the card
  surface and shadow, and no family paints itself. Only a card is the card
  colour: a column or band of chrome (the chat page's session list, a
  drawer) is `--surface-chrome` with a hairline -- the session list read
  `--bg-panel` and showed as a lighter column; on a phone both drawers and
  their backdrop sit above the sticky chat composer (it covered the session
  list's footer). Gate: `tests/e2e/test_chrome_is_the_page.py` (every page
  and Settings tab, desktop and phone, both themes; the old session-list
  rule and the old stacking as controls). The dark accent is
  measured against the card (`accent_colors.DARK_CARD`): it must stand 3:1
  off the brightest dark surface it sits on. The accent is six `--accent-chosen-*`
  seeds (a dark and a light variant, each with its own readable ink,
  `kazma_ui/accent_colors.py` and `components.js` share
  `tests/fixtures/accent_variants.json`), rendered on `<html>` by the server;
  CSS derives every accent shade with `color-mix()`, and Settings applies or
  saves an accent only when the owner chose one (the retired indigo is a
  `RetiredDefault`). Gate: `tests/test_ui_color_tokens.py` (every `var(--x)`
  defined, both themes, the surface order, the card rule, 4.5:1 text in both
  themes, no selector coloured differently in the two stylesheets; each with
  its negative control) and `tests/js/test_accent_family.js`.
- **The shell and the shared components are defined once, in `kazma.css`**
  (2026-11-09, the refresh's stage 2). The shell: the sidebar is the wall
  with a hairline on its inner edge; menu items are 45px pills, hover takes
  the accent ink and moves 4px along the reading direction, the active item
  is a filled accent pill with the `--on-accent` ink; the header is
  chrome (the wall) with a hairline along its bottom edge that meets the
  menu's (transparent with no border, it ran into the page once the page
  darkened), with round 40px icon buttons, a search field
  that opens the Ctrl+K palette, and menus (the bell, the account) that are
  the overlay surface with the overlay shadow, rows leading with an icon tile. The
  shared classes a page uses and never redefines (nor `kazma.v5.css`, which
  loads last): `.btn` with `.btn-primary` (filled), `.btn-secondary` /
  `-success` / `-warning` / `-danger` (soft: the colour's 12% tint and its
  ink), `.btn-danger-solid` (a destructive confirm), `.btn-outline`,
  `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-icon`; `.badge-*` pills (an error is `.badge-danger`;
  the legacy names are aliases); `.tone-*` for `.icon-tile`, `.stat-tile` and
  `.notice` (`.alert` is the same thing: tinted, never a stripe);
  `.page-banner`; `.card-header` / `.card-title` / `.card-sub` /
  `.card-nested`; the 40px form fields, `.form-label`; `.toggle`; `.tabs`
  pills; `.segmented`; `.data-table`; `.dropdown`; `.empty-state`;
  `.progress` (the track) with `.progress-bar` (the fill). A soft button or
  a badge on another tinted surface (an approval card, a notice, the page
  banner, a stat tile) lays its wash over the card's colour
  (`--surface-card`), never over the tinted surface's: two washes stacked put
  its ink under 4.5:1. A card does not
  lift on hover, and titles and numbers are plain ink. Every
  `--accent-chosen-*` seed falls back to the theme's accent (an install
  with no chosen accent has no seeds). Logical properties only: the shell mirrors in Arabic with no
  `[dir="rtl"]` override. Canvas and SVG drawings that read tokens redraw on
  `kazma:themechange` (on `document`, detail `{theme, reason}`), dispatched
  by `syncDocumentColorScheme` when the theme changes and `applyAccentColor`
  when the accent does (Auto follows the OS while the page is open). Gates:
  `tests/test_ui_shared_components.py` (every shared class defined, none in
  v5, the active item and the chosen tab filled pills, soft buttons, no lift,
  no gradient text, soft buttons and badges 4.5:1 on every tinted surface,
  no literal colour outside the token blocks but the declared brand marks, a
  ratchet at 0; each with its negative control),
  `tests/test_ui_color_tokens.py::test_no_chosen_accent_renders_the_theme_accent`
  and `tests/js/test_theme_change_event.js`.
- **`x-cloak` is GLOBAL — do not re-introduce the blink.** The rule
  `[x-cloak] { display: none !important; }` lives once in `kazma.css`
  (`base.html` then loads `kazma.v5.css` — last-wins for overlapping
  selectors; do not duplicate HITL/card rules). Any `x-show`-gated panel
  MUST also carry `x-cloak`. Never put `display:flex` (or any `display`) in
  an inline `style` on an `x-show` element — the inline declaration wins
  over Alpine's `display:none` toggle; put flex layout in a CSS class
  instead (see `.system-alerts-banner`).
- **A boolean binding is a boolean** (2026-11-23, found building S2-04;
  corrected the same day). The vendored Alpine (3.14.8) sets a boolean
  attribute (`disabled`, `hidden`, `required`, `readonly`, `open`...) for
  every value but `null`, `undefined` and `false` (`0` and `""` set it), and
  turns an `undefined` into `""` when the expression's text holds a `.`
  (measured in Chromium): `:disabled="busy[p.provider]"` or
  `:disabled="e.protected"` DISABLES the control while the value is missing,
  and a bare `:disabled="busy"` does not. Bind `!!value`, a comparison or a
  value that is always `true` or `false`. Gate:
  `tests/test_alpine_boolean_bindings.py` (every dotted binding of an
  attribute on Alpine's own list, read from the vendored file, is provably a
  boolean or declared; 20 were not, all latent; planted shapes as controls),
  `tests/e2e/test_alpine_boolean_binding_trap.py` (the gate flags exactly
  what the browser disables).
- **Responsive grids:** use `class="two-col-grid"` (collapses to one column
  ≤768px via `kazma.css`) on any inline `grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;` —
  bare inline 2-col grids don't collapse and crush on mobile.
- **Every page loads clean — four did not (2026-09-26).** Touring the live
  install page by page found the IDE, workspace, knowledge and settings pages
  throwing on every load; no test had opened them. The rules that broke:
  - **No markup inside a double-quoted directive.** `x-text="a ? '<span
    class="ki">' : b"` ends the attribute at `class=` (a SyntaxError per
    row). Build markup in a component method and bind it with `x-html`.
  - **Icons inserted after load come from `KazmaIcons.span(name)`**, which
    returns them filled. `icons.js` hydrates `[data-icon]` only on DOM ready,
    so a bare `<span data-icon>` inserted later stays empty. A page reached
    by the sidebar is such an insert: soft navigation fills the swapped-in
    body and the header title (`hydrateIcons` in `nav.js`, after the swap
    and after Alpine renders the page); without it 32 of the Workspace's
    icons were blank by the sidebar and none on a load (2026-11-09,
    `tests/e2e/test_soft_nav_icons.py`, the old soft navigation as its
    control).
  - **A `<template x-for>` carries only `x-for` and `:key`.** Any other
    binding on it runs OUTSIDE the loop ("s is not defined").
  - **Declare every field a template reads in the component's initial
    data**, and expose a closure constant the template uses (`kb.js`'s `S`).
    A field set only by a loader throws until the loader runs.
  - **Never `x-init="init()"` beside `x-data`.** Alpine 3 calls the
    component's `init()` itself; eleven templates called it again, the app
    shell in `base.html` among them, so every page ran its init twice —
    every load fetched twice and every `setInterval` poller ran twice.
  - **One poller per endpoint per page.** The system-alerts banner reads
    `$store.notifications` (which polls `/api/alerts/recent`) instead of a
    10 s poller of its own (`tests/js/test_alert_banner_link.js`).
  - **Settings mixins compose by descriptor** (`settings.js`):
    `Object.assign` evaluated every getter once and froze it, so the
    Packages, Skills and Tools filters never worked.
  - **The CodeMirror bundle checks its own load order**
    (`scripts/vendor_codemirror.py`: every `require()` bundled earlier, or
    the build fails). One missing addon stopped nine editor modes loading.
  Gates: `tests/e2e/test_pages_load_clean.py` (every nav page in its own
  tab: no uncaught error, every directive compiles, every bundled mode
  registered), `tests/test_alpine_templates.py` (every directive in every
  template compiles in node; `<template x-for>` scope; no second `init()`),
  `tests/js/test_settings_mixins.js`, `tests/test_vendor_codemirror.py` —
  each with a negative control.
- **A page reads its deep link from the page, not the address** (2026-11-08).
  Soft navigation runs the incoming page's scripts BEFORE it pushes the new
  address, so `location.search` at start is the page before: the bell's link
  to `/settings?tab=agent` opened Settings on its first tab, as did every
  in-app link to a Settings tab, Chat's `?s=`/`?new=1` and Replay's
  `?thread=`. Each page's root element carries what it was asked for
  (`data-*` from the request: `settings-root` `data-tab`, `chat-root`
  `data-s`/`data-new`, `replay-root` `data-thread`, as Research, Knowledge and
  the Dashboard's incident already did), read first; an address rewrite
  (`replaceState`) runs only on the page's own path, or it rewrote the page
  before. Gate: `tests/test_deep_links_survive_soft_navigation.py` (a planted
  bare read as the control); behaviour: `tests/e2e/test_bell_opens_the_page.py`
  (the old Replay script fails it).
- **A notification opens the page it is about** (2026-11-08, the owner). Every
  item `/api/alerts/recent` returns carries `link`
  (`observability.alerts.alert_link`): its own `link:/...` callback, else its
  subsystem's page (`SUBSYSTEM_PAGES`, `SUBSYSTEM_PREFIX_PAGES`), else the
  Dashboard, whose open-problems card lists every alert; always a path of this
  site. The bell's rows are links to it (`$store.notifications.href`, which
  refuses another site), closing the bell. A new subsystem put in the bell
  needs a page or a link: `tests/test_bell_notifications_open_their_page.py`
  (a planted one as the control), `tests/js/test_bell_links.js`. **Opening
  one marks it read** (the owner: "the notification still there with a bell
  badge showing"): `POST /api/alerts/read` records the ids in
  `observability.notification_reads` (`system.notifications.read`, runtime,
  at most 500, the oldest read dropped), the list says `read` per item, the
  badge counts the unread, read news (a success or information) leaves the
  bell and a read problem stays dimmed until it is fixed; "Mark all as read"
  marks the rest. Gates: `tests/test_notification_reads.py`, the store's half
  in `tests/js/test_bell_links.js` (the old count as the control), the
  browser walk in `tests/e2e/test_bell_opens_the_page.py`.
- **A page reached by soft navigation has every script it includes**
  (`modules/nav.js`, 2026-10-03). A sidebar link swaps the page and runs its
  scripts; each is one of three kinds: the base shell's (`GLOBAL_LIB_PATHS`,
  run once by the page load: every classic script base.html loads), a shared
  one (`isSoftNavSharedScript`: a classic script in `static/js/modules/`,
  loaded once per version, `scriptKey`), or the page's own
  (`isSoftNavPageScript`, run on every visit). The shared kind did not
  exist: the folder was skipped as "modules", and Chat keeps its turn
  machinery there (`turn_document.js`, `turn_view.js`,
  `turn_presentation.js`, `delivery_cursor.js`...). On live, a Chat opened
  from the Memory page painted no turn -- no header, no steps, no approval
  card -- until a refresh, and `chat.js` declines quietly without those
  modules, so no error said why. A shared script that binds a document
  listener binds it once (`turn_visibility.js`). Gates:
  `tests/test_soft_nav_page_scripts.py` (every template's scripts, none
  dropped; the old rule as the negative control) and
  `tests/e2e/test_soft_nav_into_chat.py` (Memory, then Chat by the sidebar,
  then a turn that must paint; away and back runs each module once).
  **The page's scripts run in the order the page has them**
  (`runPageScripts`, 2026-11-22), external and inline alike, as a page
  load runs them: an inline script inside the swapped root runs where it
  stands, one elsewhere in the body is added to the body. Pages define their
  words inline before the script that reads them (chat.html's `CHAT_I18N`,
  the Dashboard's `__DASH_I18N`, Knowledge's `__KB_STRINGS`, Memory's
  `__MEM_STRINGS`); every script file used to run first, so whatever
  `chat.js` painted before the inline scripts ran was English on an Arabic
  page reached by the sidebar. No inline script ahead of a page script may
  wait for the page's load (soft navigation would run it at once). Gate:
  `tests/e2e/test_soft_nav_page_data_first.py` (Arabic, a tab opened on
  Memory, Chat by the sidebar with the script after `chat.js` held back:
  every text the turn header shows; the words moved after the page's last
  script, today's order, as the control). **A page's own merge into
  `KAZMA_I18N` runs again** (the second review): soft navigation skipped
  every inline script naming `window.KAZMA_I18N` -- meant for the shell's
  bootstrap -- so research.html's merge never ran again, the refresh wiped
  it and the Research page reached by the sidebar was English. The shell's
  bootstrap is marked `data-kazma-i18n-bootstrap` and skipped by that mark
  alone. Gate: `tests/e2e/test_research_words_on_soft_nav.py` (nav.js's
  text rule put back as the control).
- **Every `KazmaX.member` a page reads exists** (2026-09-28). The Swarm
  Templates tab called `KazmaUtils.esc` (the helper is `escapeHtml`), the
  render threw, and its fetch's `catch` showed "Failed to load templates"
  over three good ones. `tests/js/test_namespace_members.js` loads every
  script that defines a namespace in a sandbox where no page is ready and
  checks every member reference in the static JS and the templates.
- **A control changes something, or is not shown** (2026-09-28). The Agents
  page's Start/Stop flipped `agent.is_running`, which nothing else read: the
  page said "Stopped" over an agent answering chats. It now shows whether the
  server is serving and says how a reply or the server is stopped; the
  `POST /api/agents/{start,stop}` route that answered 409 with that text is
  gone since 2026-10-01 (nothing called it). Built-in skills'
  "Uninstall" and the skill switch were the same shape (§22G), and so was
  Settings → Skills until 2026-10-01. `DELETE /api/settings/{key:path}` is
  gone the same day: nothing called it, and it deleted whatever key the path
  named -- the provider list, the platform users, a secret's vault pointer --
  with no check; the route inventory missed it because a page called other
  `/api/settings/...` paths and the inventory matched paths, not methods.
  So did six more a method-level reading found the same day: a DELETE twin
  of the clear-approvals POST, GET and PATCH of one bookmark, a second MCP
  server list (`GET /api/settings/mcp`), a swarm "metrics" stub and the
  Agents start/stop -- all removed.
- **A button reaches what it names** (2026-09-28). The calendar card
  ("Google / Outlook") had one "Connect Calendar" that only started Google's
  sign-in. `tests/test_button_label_matches_action.py` follows every
  template button's click into the scripts its page loads and fails when
  the label names a provider its routes never reach, or names none inside a
  section for several while it serves one (negative control: the old card).
- **What the owner can change has a control** (2026-09-28): a route that
  changes something the owner decides gets a control on its page, or a
  reason it has none. Found with no control at all: removing a document from
  a Knowledge library, protecting a memory entity, resetting a swarm
  breaker, Outlook Calendar's disconnect, folders outside the workspace.
  Every one is now on its page. **The route inventory is a gate**
  (`tests/test_api_route_callers.py`, 2026-09-30): every `/api` route the
  built app serves has a caller -- a string in a page script, a template, the
  TUI, the CLI or a script (server-side Python is not a caller: an error text
  once made a dead route look called) -- or is declared in
  `NOT_CALLED_BY_A_PAGE` with its reason (OAuth redirects, the documented
  Document API, operator reports...). A declaration fails the day its route
  gains a caller or disappears. The first pass removed three dead routes
  (the typing-telemetry stubs and `/api/system/flush`, which reset live
  registry singletons) and found the Settings backup had no restore control;
  it has one since 2026-10-01 (§47), with runtime state and credentials kept
  out of both the file and the restore. **Since 2026-10-01 it reads methods**:
  each method of a route needs a caller WITH that method (read from the call
  around the literal -- `fetch`'s `method:`, `hx-post`, a Python client's
  `.delete(` / `_request(..., "DELETE", ...)`; a call it cannot read counts
  for every method), or a `"METHOD /path"` declaration. Matching paths only
  had let the delete-any-setting route and six other uncalled methods pass
  because a page called the same path with another method. **A prefix built
  by concatenation** (`'/api/research/' + id`) reaches only a route whose next
  segment is a parameter or a word quoted in its file or in a template that
  loads it (`'/api/x/reply/' + kind`, the page passing `'retry'`): any route
  under the prefix used to count, and `/api/research/eval` passed that way.
  **Every route exists when the app is built**
  (`tests/test_routes_exist_when_built.py`, the real lifespan run, route
  table compared): mount a router in `KazmaAppBuilder._setup_routers`, and
  read what startup makes per request (the replay API's getters). The
  research and replay APIs were mounted in `_on_startup` until 2026-10-01,
  so none of these gates had ever seen their 29 routes. The first look
  found a paper export that read any file the server could (served by
  `/download`), a report scorer that measured any file on disk -- one rule
  now, `research_pipeline.resolve_report_file` (a request names a path inside
  a `research/reports` folder) -- a DAG workflow validator for workflows
  nothing could run (removed), the task-history export and the memory
  graph's move and tier with no control (Swarm → Task History **Export
  CSV**; **Group under→** on a grouped node moves it, **Tier…**), and a
  create route that failed on its primary key for a node with a parent.
- **A panel lays out by its own width** (`@container`), not the window's:
  with the sidebar open a 918px window left the IDE editor ~40px and
  clipped the providers panel. `tests/e2e/test_layout_widths.py` (each with
  the container switched off as its control). A narrower panel moves the
  least important region first: the IDE puts its AI chat below the editor
  at 1000px and stacks the file tree only below 560px, capped in height --
  stacking everything at once put the editor 2,400px down the page.
- **Kazma installs as an app** (2026-11-14, REMAINING 4.1,
  `kazma_ui/web_app.py`): every page (and the login page) links
  `/manifest.webmanifest` (name, `start_url` `/chat`, standalone, the icons
  `scripts/make_app_icons.py` makes, shortcuts, `lang`/`dir` in the page's
  language), served before sign-in. `/sw.js` -- Web Push's worker, registered
  by every page at load -- answers a failed NAVIGATION with the one page it
  caches, `/static/offline.html` (bilingual, retries `/health/live`); it never
  answers or caches anything else. Gates: `tests/test_web_app_manifest.py`,
  `tests/e2e/test_web_app_install_browser.py` (Chrome's own
  `Page.getInstallabilityErrors` empty on a page reached by the sidebar; the
  offline page with the network gone).
- **Dates, times and numbers go through `window.KazmaFormat`**
  (`static/js/locale_format.js`, loaded by `base.html`): `Intl` in the page's
  language (`<html lang>`), Latin digits in Arabic like every other number
  the interface shows. Pages used the browser's own locale and wrote "ago"
  by hand, so Arabic pages showed English dates (`tests/js/test_locale_format.js`).
  **A count is said in its plural form**: `{{ t_plural('key', n) }}` in a
  template, `window.kazmaCount('key', n, vars)` in a script (`base.html`: the
  catalog's `<key>.zero` ... `<key>.other`, six in Arabic), never a number
  beside a word in one form -- "1 أدوات" on the MCP card and in Settings.
  `vars.n` shows the number another way ("12.3K") while the form follows
  the number; the chat's own scripts read their forms through the
  `plural` bridge (`tiCount`). Gates: `tests/test_count_labels.py` (no glued
  count in a template or an Alpine expression; no catalog count label in
  one form -- the last 34 were converted on 2026-10-02 -- whether the noun
  comes right after the count or after a word or two, "(s)" included; and
  the ARABIC of every entry checked on its own, because the English cannot
  show it: "Cleared {n} failed" was "مُسحت {n} مهام فاشلة". An Arabic word
  that does not change with the count, such as a preposition, a stat line's
  adjective or a unit, is declared there; a placeholder that is not a count
  (a name, a path) is skipped by both),
  `tests/test_kazma_count.py` (every `kazmaCount` key has every form).
  The English-only surfaces, which are the TUI, the CLI and the chat-app
  replies, say a count through `kazma_core.english_count.count_noun(n,
  'message')`: they printed "(1 msgs)" and "0/1 requests available".
  `tests/test_english_counts.py` reads every f-string in those packages,
  and a value that is not a count is declared there with why.
  A page-level helper for catalog strings must not be named after an
  element tag: the Dashboard's `tr()` was shadowed by `var tr =
  createElement('tr')` in its row loop and rendered no rows (caught by
  `tests/e2e/test_dashboard_session_table.py`). **No script declares the
  name of a translation helper it calls**, as a parameter or a variable
  (`tests/test_scripts_keep_their_translator.py`, 2026-10-02): the Swarm
  page's active-task loop `function(t)` hid `t()`, and the first translated
  word threw inside an empty `catch` -- a running task the page had not
  started never appeared.
- **The Dashboard's session table reads the chat store** for a thread's
  title, platform and message count, and the checkpoints for its saved steps
  and last activity (`list_checkpoints`: newest per thread, time from the
  uuid6 id via `checkpoint_retention.checkpoint_time`). It read a
  five-minute gateway cache and the Postgres checkpoint row (which holds no
  messages), so every live row said "unknown / anonymous / 0". Delete removes
  the chat; "Clear saved steps" removes every chat's checkpoints and keeps
  the chats (they carry on from their messages, `fallback_history`).
- **A control is wired once** (2026-09-28): never an inline `on<event>` in a
  template and a script listener for the same element and event -- Start
  All and Stop All sent every click twice. A handler that only prevents the
  default (`onsubmit="return false;"`) is not an action.
  `tests/test_ui_double_wiring.py`.
- **A list shows its empty state only after it has loaded.** The chat
  sidebar painted "No sessions yet" for a second on every visit (an early
  re-render replaced the "Loading…" placeholder).
  `tests/e2e/test_session_list_loading.py`. Every template empty state
  (length vs zero, `!list.length`, `!list.some(...)`) names a flag its loader
  sets on SUCCESS (`xLoaded`), or loading AND error flags -- `!loading` alone
  says "none" over a failed read -- or is declared with why in
  `tests/test_empty_states_after_load.py` (2026-10-15: Documents said "No
  documents yet." for seconds over five, and 39 other empty states had the shape;
  `tests/e2e/test_documents_list_loading.py`). A failed read says it failed:
  no `catch` in a page script paints an empty list, an empty-state text or
  made-up rows (the same gate; the Workspace showed a fake `kazma-core/`
  listing when its file read failed).
- **A poller reads through `window.kazmaGetJson`** (`auth-guard.js`): the
  parsed body of a 2xx JSON response, else null (an error status, a proxy's
  HTML page, no network); it never throws or logs. While the server restarts
  Cloudflare answers 502 HTML, and the Memory and Swarm pollers parsed it as
  JSON, logging "Unexpected token '<'" on every restart (2026-09-27). Gate:
  `test_every_page_survives_a_restart` (every nav page and Settings tab, every
  API GET answered 502 HTML, the page's clock run 65 s; negative control).
- **Every translation key the chat page's scripts use is bridged.** chat.js
  and agentStore.js read `window.CHAT_I18N`, which `chat.html` fills line by
  line; 15 keys had no line and showed English in every language. Gate:
  `tests/test_chat_i18n_bridge.py` (each `ti`/`tiFmt`/`tiCount` key has a
  line, each line's catalog key exists in English and Arabic, all six plural
  forms for a count).
- **A polled route never calls a rate-limited API per poll.**
  `/api/github/status` spent ~2,000 GitHub calls an hour per open Workspace
  tab (10 s poll, fetched twice per tick, three calls each). It now keeps one
  status per (owner, repo, token fingerprint) for 30 s, fetched once at a time
  (`_status_once`: single-flight), reads its stores in a thread, and the page
  refreshes on a new connection only. `tests/test_github_status_cache.py`.

## Server Management

### Persisted deployment policies (2026-10-07)

`safety/deployment_policy.py` owns `security.workspace_roots` (explicit existing
absolute directories) and `security.execution.container_required` (strict bool).
The authenticated admin Settings API validates these, including parent mapping
saves, before its atomic write. Agent `config_save` cannot write `security.*`.
The workspace root environment is an additional floor; a stored list cannot
expand it. Policy failures deny access. A strict profile wins over legacy
ALLOW_LOCAL / HOST_SHELL flags, requires Docker, skips E2B and never falls back.
Health must check Docker for that profile. Tests: `test_production_qualification.py`.

The Docker Python runner pipes the sandbox script through stdin (`run -i`,
`python -I -`), including the Windows Selector-loop fallback. Never restore a
bind mount of its private temporary directory: the scheduled S4U/Highest service
can create containers and mount workspaces, but Docker Desktop cannot read that
service-created temporary folder (live diagnostic, 2026-10-07). The workspace
mount stays read-only and all container restrictions remain. Temporary folders
retain their private permissions. Gate: `test_docker_stdin_avoids_private_temp_mount`.

`agent/approval_facts.py` reports the tool worker's actual decisions, including
single, selective and denied batches. Never build approval truth from tool
content or infer success from authorization. `ide/env_context.py` distinguishes
the global MCP binding from a per-task scoped instance. Scoped outside-root
prohibitions and mount descriptions are not global audit-only requests; a
separate explicit global restriction still wins.

> **RULE (user directive, 2026-08-15, amended 2026-09-26): never start the
> Kazma server and never kill it by hand.** Code reaches the running server
> only through the guard's reload, below.

> **RULE (user directive, 2026-09-02): NEVER edit the live install at
> `C:\Users\balfa\kazma`.** The dev repo (`G:\GitHubRepos\kazma`) is where all
> work happens. Do not write, copy, patch, or revert ANY file there (not even
> static assets that the server would pick up "without a restart", and not
> even to verify a fix), and do not change its git config or history.

> **Deploys (operator's standing order, 2026-09-26).** The agent may deploy
> the live install itself: push to `origin/main`, then
> `git -C C:/Users/balfa/kazma pull` (a plain merge -- the clone keeps a
> local `kazma.yaml` delta, so it is never a fast-forward; pull only a tree
> with no modified tracked files), then reload with the LIVE install's guard,
> then verify the new commit is serving and test through the UI.

```powershell
# The RUNNING GUARD carries out the reload: it stops the server gracefully
# (the app's shutdown hooks run) and starts the code on disk (§39). Run the
# guard script OF THE INSTALL BEING RELOADED -- the request lands in
# <that install>/.kazma. --when-idle waits until no chat turn is running
# (GET /health/activity, local callers only); exit 3 = still busy at
# --idle-timeout, nothing was touched.
& 'C:\Users\balfa\kazma\.venv\Scripts\python.exe' 'C:\Users\balfa\kazma\scripts\service\kazma_guard.py' --reload --when-idle
& 'C:\Users\balfa\kazma\.venv\Scripts\python.exe' 'C:\Users\balfa\kazma\scripts\service\kazma_guard.py' --status
```

`--status` says `guard : running` or `NOT RUNNING`, from the guard's
heartbeat. With no guard running, `--reload` starts the `KazmaAgent` task and
the new guard clears the old server with its own rights, so a reload never
needs an elevated shell.

**A deploy whose pull changed `pyproject.toml` runs the update before the
reload** (2026-11, FA-258: live ran 26 packages below the build's floors
because a pull installs nothing): `<live python> -m kazma_cli update
--reinstall -y` (it pauses the guard when idle, installs, resumes; §50). A
pull that changed document code also rebuilds the worker image:
`<live python> scripts/document_worker_image.py build` (§19 E1).

`--reload` also picks up a tool added to PATH while Kazma ran (§38). A
new *guard* (its own code, or other OS-level variables) still needs the
`KazmaAgent` task restarted.

**`scripts/deploy_live.py` keeps each step's whole output in `.kazma/deploy/`
of the dev checkout and names the error lines (`essential`); its revert of a
`pyproject.toml` change puts the reverted code's packages back
(`put_packages_back`: the update, else `repair_packages`, every package
rewritten with uv while the guard holds Kazma, which stays held if that
fails) instead of a reload, which lifted a failed update's hold and left
live crash-looping (2026-11-13).** **`scripts/deploy_live.py` does all of the above and checks it** (resilience
plan C2): pull (refused over modified tracked files), the update and image
build when their files changed, reload when idle, then the new commit on
`/health/live`, ready and deep health, one test turn ("Reply with the word
OK", kept out of memory, the chat deleted) and no ERROR/CRITICAL line since
the boot. A failed check reverts what `origin/main` gained (the live pull is
a merge, so never the live HEAD range) on `main` here, pushes, pulls the
revert into the live install, reloads and pages the owner naming the check
(`--no-revert` pages only). Gate: `tests/test_deploy_live.py` (real git
repositories, a stub server; a live checkout with its own commit).

## Testing & Validation

**Answer-quality observations (2026-10-09):**
`observability/answer_quality.py` records at `graph_respond.respond_node`, after
terminal formatting, on a worker thread. A bounded 30-day/10,000-turn SQLite
ledger holds flags and turn/chat identity only; never add prompts, answers,
tool arguments, model reasoning or credentials. Rechecks and plan blocks are
review signals, not accuracy failures (requested JSON/plans may be valid).
Paragraph signals share `answer_format`'s narrow EN/AR predicate and exclude
protected layouts and failed turns. Pauses, cancellations and usage commands
do not pass this terminal node. The quality API is administrator-only; a
storage failure is unavailable, not zero healthy. No external messages are
sent. Gate: `tests/test_answer_quality_monitor.py`.

- **Runtime ownership:** `KazmaAppBuilder` acquires `RuntimeOwnership` before
  services construct and releases only after complete shutdown. Its local
  OS fence is always on. `KAZMA_RUNTIME_HA=1` additionally holds a dedicated
  Postgres session, paired to the complete volume's `.runtime-state-id`.
  Never reconnect that lease or release it while workers still run: session
  loss stops the process. Keep one runtime and qualify CSI storage fencing;
  advisory ownership alone cannot fence a partitioned host's effects.
  Drills: `tests/test_runtime_ownership.py` (marked real Postgres tests),
  deployment contract: `tests/test_kubernetes_runtime_contract.py`.
  **The Kubernetes root filesystem is read-only** (2026-11-11,
  `deploy/kubernetes/runtime.yaml`): every container's security context
  makes its root read-only, and every place Kazma writes is a mount -- the
  `/state` volume (with `KAZMA_ENV_FILE` and `HF_HOME` on it) or an emptyDir
  (`/tmp`, `/home/kazma`, ClamAV's three folders; an init container seeds
  the signatures). The contract test resolves the write locations with
  Kazma's own code in a child under the manifest's environment (every
  zero-argument function of `kazma_core.paths`, the temp folder, the home
  and its caches, the Hugging Face cache, `env_files._install_env_file`, a
  shell tool's home, the skills home, the OCR models) and fails on one
  outside every mount; a planted write, the manifest without its emptyDirs
  and without `KAZMA_ENV_FILE` are the negative controls. A new write
  location outside them needs a mount. Unverified on a cluster.

- **A finished run leaves nothing in the temp folder** (2026-11-14: about
  5 GB from five days of runs). The root conftest's five folders carry their
  process id (`kazma-test-<kind>-<pid>-`), and each run first removes those
  of processes that have ended (`_remove_ended_test_temp`; a folder whose
  process still runs, a soak under pytest, is kept; `KAZMA_TEST_KEEP_TEMP=1`
  keeps all); `scripts/fast_test.py` does the same with its run folders
  (`remove_ended_run_folders`); a helper making a store in a test uses the
  test's `tmp_path`; a soak script removes its scratch folder when the run
  passes (`_scratch` / `_end`, kept and named when it fails); the vault drill
  closes the vault before removing its copy (an open connection left an
  encrypted vault copy per drill on Windows); the git tools' empty hooks
  folder is removed at exit. Gate: `tests/test_test_temp_folders.py` (two real
  runs leave one run's folders; `KAZMA_TEST_KEEP_TEMP=1` as the control), the
  drill's `test_the_drill_leaves_no_copy_of_the_vault`.
- **A test run never touches an install's data** (2026-09-27). The root
  `conftest.py` pins `KAZMA_DATA_DIR` and `KAZMA_USER_HOME` to fresh temp
  folders before any product module is imported and clears the per-store
  path overrides: a live install IS a checkout, and a run inside it (Kazma's
  agent tests its own workspace) wrote test gates, a test chat store and
  test swarm tasks into the live stores. A test that needs a folder of its
  own still sets the variable. Gate: `tests/test_install_data_shield.py`
  (every location `paths.py` resolves, from its source). Since 2026-10-01 it
  pins `KAZMA_SKILLS_HOME` too: the skill folders in the user's home, which
  the live install, running as the same user, reads (§22H).
- **No test reaches the network or loads the real embedder** (2026-10-15,
  `tests/_egress_guard.py`, registered by the root `conftest.py`). Swarm
  pipeline tests loaded bge-m3 from this machine's Hugging Face cache (it
  starved the live server) and built real provider calls. A DNS lookup of
  another host, a connection or UDP send to one (sync sockets and both
  asyncio loops), and the import of the real `sentence_transformers` are
  refused where they are made, and the test FAILS with the call site even
  when the code under test swallowed the refusal. Loopback stays open
  (local servers, the suite's Postgres, Playwright). A test that truly
  needs the real model or a provider is `@pytest.mark.real_model`
  (`KAZMA_TEST_REAL_MODEL=1` runs it), one that needs the internet
  `@pytest.mark.network` (`KAZMA_TEST_NETWORK=1`); `KAZMA_TEST_EGRESS_GUARD=0`
  turns the guard off for debugging. Stub instead:
  `tests/_no_models.keep_models_out` (no embedder, the model package absent,
  self-improvement off, a registry client that refuses like a keyless
  provider) and `finish_turn_memory` (a turn's post-turn memory thread ends
  inside its test), a fake LLM client, `ssrf._resolve_host_ips` answered
  locally. The root conftest sets `KAZMA_EMBEDDER_PREWARM=0` (every app a
  test built loaded the model at boot) and the Hugging Face offline
  switches. Gate: `tests/test_egress_guard.py` (planted tests in a child
  pytest as the negative control).
- **No test reaches the Kazma running on this machine** (2026-11-13). The
  terminal app's tests mount the real app, and its polling went to
  `127.0.0.1:9090`: the live install's log held 33-44 unauthenticated
  requests a dozen times a day, a `PUT /api/settings/single` among them,
  refused only because live asks for a sign-in. The local API asks only the
  configured port (`runtime.local_api.candidate_api_bases`: `server_port`,
  then `KAZMA_BASE_URL`; it also guessed 9090 and 8000, which on a machine
  with two installs reached the other one; the Docker image sets
  `KAZMA_PORT=8000` for commands run inside it). The root conftest gives the
  suite a port nothing listens on, and the egress guard refuses a loopback
  connection to a Kazma outside the run (`KAZMA_TEST_OUTSIDE_PORTS`: 9090
  and the port the environment named before), unless the test bound that
  port itself. Gates: `tests/test_suite_reaches_no_running_kazma.py`,
  `tests/test_egress_guard.py` (a planted test as the negative control),
  `tests/test_agent_turn.py`.
- **A test that runs real containers is marked `real_docker`** (2026-11-13).
  `tests/conftest.py`'s `_isolated_docker_config` points `DOCKER_CONFIG` at
  an empty folder for every other test (which engine a developer's machine
  uses never decides a test); its `default` context is the platform's own
  Docker address, which on a machine whose engine is Kazma's (no Docker
  Desktop) answers nothing: every container test failed there and the
  sandbox's real run skipped without a word. A marked test keeps the
  developer's settings. A test's own `docker run -v` names the folder as the
  engine in force mounts it (`docker_cli.engine_host_path`). The same fixture
  hides the machine's own Kazma engine folder (`docker_cli.kazma_engine_dir`:
  once this PC's setup installed Kazma's docker CLI there, every lookup test
  found it, 2026-11-14); a test that sets its own `LOCALAPPDATA` gets that
  folder. Gate: `tests/test_real_docker_marker.py` (the marked and unmarked
  tests are each other's control).
- **A file a child process publishes is renamed into place and read with
  `tests/_published_files.read_published_text`** (2026-11-14): a child that
  wrote in place was read empty, and on Windows a file just renamed can be
  held for a moment by the scanner (`PermissionError`); both failed only on a
  loaded machine.
- **Every docs diagram parses** with the docs site's own Mermaid
  (`tests/test_docs_mermaid_diagrams_parse.py`, in a blank Chromium page; it
  needs `cd docs && npm install`, as building the site does). The site draws
  diagrams in the browser, so a broken one is only a console error: the
  Commitment Layer page's had never drawn.
- **Compile check (Python):** `& '.venv\Scripts\python.exe' -c "import py_compile; py_compile.compile(r'<file>', doraise=True); print('OK')"`
- **Syntax check (JS):** `node --check "<file>"`
- **Run tests (single file):** `& '.venv\Scripts\python.exe' -m pytest <path> -v`
- **Fast FULL suite (use this — ~10 min, not 40):**
  `python scripts/fast_test.py`
  Crash-tolerant chunked runner: file-chunks run as independent serial pytest
  processes; crashed/empty chunks are retried per-file; poison files are
  reported. One chunk per CPU, at most 8 (`DEFAULT_MAX_CHUNKS`: 32 chunks
  each loading torch crashed 12 of them, 2026-09-25); CI passes
  `--chunks 4` and no budget (a fixed 1500 s was below what ~400 files need
  on CI's runner: every chunk ran out of time in November 2026 and was
  re-run whole, 60-75 minutes a run). Locally, pass NO `--chunks`. **A
  pytest process runs at most `--files-per-process` files** (2026-11-23;
  default `DEFAULT_FILES_PER_PROCESS`, 60; CI's Tests job and the coverage
  run pass it): a chunk runs its files as consecutive pytest processes
  (`split_into_pieces`: even, in the chunk's order), one after another
  (`run_chunk_in_pieces`), so as many processes run at once as before; each
  has its own budget (its own files, 10 s each, floor 900 s; an explicit
  `--chunk-timeout` is every process's), its own tally, its own line in the
  log as it ends ("chunk 00, process 3/8") and its own recovery -- a process
  that crashes or runs out of time costs the chunk's other processes
  nothing. `0` is one process per chunk, the runner before (the control in
  `tests/test_fast_test_runner.py`, real processes). Why: CI's runner (4
  vCPUs, 16 GB, ~470 files a process) was ended from outside 30-40 minutes
  in, run after run; every chunk process grew for the whole run (3.8, 3.6,
  3.5 and 2.8 GB at 40 minutes, 14.6 of 16 GB used; 5.1 GB at 52 on an
  earlier run), and `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` changed nothing: what a test
  leaves reachable stays until its process ends. Measured on chunk 00 of
  the 4-chunk layout (471 files, Windows, private bytes, one test thread):
  one process 5.53 GB at its end; at most 120 files a process 1.43-2.34 GB;
  at most 60, 0.77-1.72 GB; the same 7,033 passed and 54 skipped all three
  ways, 2,953 / 2,962 / 2,966 s (about 6 s of start-up for each extra
  process). The worst process at any size holds `tests/test_settings_scope.py`
  (about 710 MB kept, building the app several times) and
  `tests/test_static_gates.py` (about 400 MB) -- the next thing to shrink.
  **Every
  pytest run is one killable unit** (2026-09-30: a `--chunks 4` run took
  1 h 22 min): a chunk's budget scales with its files (10 s each, floor 900 s)
  unless given; a timeout kills the whole tree -- a kill-on-close Job Object on
  Windows, where the venv's `python.exe` is a launcher and killing it left the
  interpreter running tests while CPython's post-timeout `communicate()` waited
  with no timeout; a process group on POSIX -- and the drain after it is
  bounded; a finished run's leftovers are reaped (Windows); and a chunk that
  ran out of TIME is re-run as parallel pieces, not one process per file,
  serially (`tests/test_fast_test_runner.py`, real processes, with the old
  direct-child kill as the negative control). Every pytest process it starts first lowers itself below a
  normal program (`pytest_command`: Windows CPU class below normal and
  memory priority low; `nice` elsewhere; `--foreground` opts out), and gets
  its share of math-library threads (CPUs / chunks, `OMP_NUM_THREADS` & co.
  unless already set): the live install runs on the machine the suite runs
  on, and two minutes into a 4-chunk run its event loop froze for 18.5 s
  (2026-09-29). The DISK priority is left alone, measured: low I/O priority
  took 476 SQLite-heavy tests from 80 s to 147-199 s, and a full run with
  it timed out every chunk; Windows' background mode made `import torch`
  take 244 s instead of 4.4 (`tests/test_fast_test_runner.py`). It PRINTS the per-chunk FAILURES tracebacks (deep-audit
  2026-08-19 — they used to be captured and discarded, leaving CI-only
  failures undiagnosable) and treats pytest exit 5 ("no tests collected",
  i.e. module-level importorskip like the Playwright e2e suite on a
  `.[test]`-only install) as a benign skip, not POISON. Per-file exit 0/1
  without a terminal tally is unmeasured: pytest-timeout exits 1 without that
  summary. Both isolation retries require a parsed tally (exit 5 remains an
  explicit no-tests skip), otherwise the file is POISON. A timed-out/crashed
  chunk's parsed tally is not added before recovery: pytest may print its
  summary and hang during shutdown. Count the recovered files once, retaining
  observed failure identities so a clean retry never erases them. The original
  double-count boundary is covered in `tests/test_fast_test_runner.py`.
  Both isolation retries require a parsed tally (exit 5 remains an
  explicit no-tests skip), otherwise the file is POISON. The original boundary
  is a negative control in `tests/test_fast_test_runner.py`. Do NOT use
  pytest-xdist here — worker segfaults (native lib) make
  it silently drop ~half the suite. The serial monolithic run intermittently
  segfaults and takes 20+ min.
  **Quiet hours** (2026-11-17, the owner: "My pc is whining because of the
  test suite"): `--cores N` holds a run to N cores (0: all), and a schedule
  kept beside the checkout, `.kazma/fast_test.json` (git ignores it), holds
  every run to its cores at the hours it names, in its own time zone
  (`scheduled_cores`); the owner's: 8 cores from 01:00 to 13:00 Kuwait time,
  all cores the rest of the day. The cap is the runner's CPU affinity, which
  every process it starts inherits; a held run's chunk budget grows with it.
  Gates in `tests/test_fast_test_runner.py` (a real grandchild's cores, the
  uncapped run as the control).
- **Manual verification:** reload through the guard (Server Management
  above — never a hand restart), then test via Telegram and the Web UI

- `docs/plans/HITL_GATE_REGISTRY_PLAN.md` — Gate registry (P6)
- `docs/plans/TURN_DELIVERY_V2_CURSOR_RESUME_PLAN.md` — Turn Delivery V2
- `docs/plans/CONTEXT_INTEGRITY_HARDENING_PLAN.md` — Context integrity
- `docs/plans/GUARD_OPS_ALERTING_CAUSE_QUALITY.md` — Deferred Guard/ops alerting sprint
- `docs/plans/done/DOCS_CONSOLIDATION_PLAN.md` — Docs consolidation plan (completed)
- `docs/docs/reference/benchmarks.md` — the public benchmarks page, WRITTEN by `scripts/benchmarks_page.py` from the committed result files (memory, Knowledge, document fidelity); never edit it by hand: a lock that changes a score re-runs the script in the same commit (`tests/test_benchmarks_page.py`)
- `docs/docs/security/safety-design.md` — how the safeguards are built (the public write-up; the threat model says what they do not stop). A safeguard added or removed is described there in the same commit
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Sprint history
- Live docs only under `docs/docs/` (Docusaurus). Do not resurrect retired `docs-v2` / loose handover trees. A page added, moved or deleted there (or directly in `docs/`) changes `docs/website-pages.json` and `docs/sidebars.js` in the same commit (`tests/test_website_pages.py`, `tests/test_docs_sidebar.py`). Every `#anchor` a docs link names is a heading of its page -- a `{#id}` or the id Docusaurus derives -- because Docusaurus only warns and CI does not build the docs (`tests/test_docs_anchors.py`; five pointed at removed sections on 2026-10-01). kazma.ai honours `{#id}`, and its build fails on a missing anchor and on an Arabic page linking to an English page that has an Arabic one (docs/docs/ops/website-sync.md). Every file a published page names in a code span is a tracked file, or declared with its reason -- runtime, example, another repository, a removal the page states (`tests/test_docs_file_refs.py`; 39 pointed at nothing on 2026-10-01, one of them a security protection whose code had been deleted).
- The docs site's build packages (`docs/package-lock.json`) are fixed with `npm audit fix`, never `--force`, and checked with `npm run build`; `docs/package.json` names Mermaid's major in `overrides` (12 since 2026-11-13) and `uuid` 11 (the dev server's sockjs asks for 8); every docs diagram parses with the site's own Mermaid (`tests/test_docs_mermaid_diagrams_parse.py`: the site draws diagrams in the browser, so a broken one is only a console error, and the Commitment Layer page's had never drawn). Each package the 2026-11 fix moved past its advisories has its first fixed release as a floor (`tests/test_docs_site_packages.py`, the old lock's versions as the negative control); what is left needs a major version Docusaurus 3.10.2 holds back (`docs/docs/contributing/development-setup.md`).
